DARS-NIC-00574-V2H1F.summary: Southampton City Council uses pseudonymised hospital data, including inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care records, in its public health work. It uses them to analyse local health needs, inequalities and service demand, supporting needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The data have already informed drug and alcohol needs assessments, falls analysis, and neighbourhood health profiles used by clinicians to set priorities.

DARS-NIC-00747-G8G0Z.summary: Cheshire East Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to meet its public health duties. It uses them to produce needs assessments, strategies and advice for NHS commissioners, helping it find and respond to local health challenges, especially for disadvantaged groups. The council reports that the data informed its Crewe needs assessment, published in August 2023.

DARS-NIC-01207-V9G9P.summary: Compufile Systems Limited, a consultancy, uses pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) to provide analysis to NHS organisations and NHS suppliers, partly through its ESPRiT tool. The analysis covers care pathways, benchmarking and service evaluation, aiming to help clients improve services and patient outcomes. Reported results include regular heart attack benchmarking for NHS RightCare, and a London workshop that led an NHS organisation to improve communication with GP practices about discharge coding.

DARS-NIC-02292-T4P9N.summary: Herefordshire Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital data, covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care records. It uses this data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that admissions data has already identified hotspots for targeted action, such as falls and cardiovascular disease.

DARS-NIC-02544-M7M7G.summary: The University of Birmingham, an academic organisation, is using hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and critical care to carry out health services research. This covers hospital use and outcomes in the West Midlands, including maternity and child health, and the link between weekend specialist staffing and hospital deaths. The aim is to improve care and inform service planning. Published papers and a local emergency care report have already been used in discussions and decisions.

DARS-NIC-03075-X3M3H.summary: Somerset Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will analyse local health needs and inequalities to support needs assessments, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported uses so far include informing the council's response to violent crime and COVID, and a Director of Public Health report on COVID's impact on other conditions.

DARS-NIC-03398-N1D2C.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using pseudonymised hospital records covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients. It is studying how air and noise pollution near airports, especially Heathrow, affect local people's health, so that airport policy and NHS planning can be better informed. A newspaper article reported that during a 2012 trial flight ban at Heathrow, spending on prescriptions for conditions such as insomnia and depression fell by 5.8% in the no-fly zones.

DARS-NIC-03422-Y7Y0Z.summary: University College London (UCL), through the Cancer Research UK and UCL Cancer Trials Centre, uses mortality data (date and cause of death) for patients in the GALA-5 pilot trial who have been lost to follow-up. It uses the data to calculate survival in a trial testing 5-ALA and carmustine (Gliadel) wafers alongside standard glioblastoma treatment. The results are expected to guide a future phase III trial and inform a review of NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-03429-L9Y1D.summary: Wirral Borough Council uses pseudonymised hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. It uses them to plan and assess local services, produce needs assessments and strategies, and advise NHS commissioners, with the aim of identifying and addressing local health inequalities. It reports using the data to evaluate a local alcohol-sales scheme, inform drug and alcohol commissioning, and support NHS pathway redesign.

DARS-NIC-03519-X1P5B.summary: Northumberland County Council, a local authority, uses hospital records covering admitted patients, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported results include detailed needs assessments, ward and primary care network profiles, and support for a falls pilot scheme.

DARS-NIC-03716-R3W8Q.summary: The University of Exeter is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, giving admission counts for cardiovascular disease, diabetes and obesity by small area, age band and gender. It is analysing whether rural location and area deprivation affect hospital admissions for these conditions, alone or combined. The aim is to help clinicians and policymakers plan services for local needs. So far, the data has been used to validate the university's small-area model of comorbidity, which matched the observed pattern of admissions.

DARS-NIC-05206-L1V6D.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit uses pseudonymised hospital, mental health, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, death registration and patient-reported outcome data. It uses them to benchmark services, model activity and support planning and commissioning for NHS and partner organisations, aiming to improve decisions about care. Reported results include a national report, "Making the Case for Integrating Mental and Physical Health Care", for NHS England, and work that informed responses to the 2021 spending review.

DARS-NIC-05429-H7X6R.summary: Device Access UK Ltd, a commercial company, uses Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and Emergency Care Data Set records to produce bespoke, aggregated analysis of current NHS patient pathways for medical technology companies and NHS organisations. The analysis supports their submissions to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), helping new devices be assessed and adopted by the NHS. Its analysis has been used in NICE applications that resulted in positive NICE guidance in 2022-2023.

DARS-NIC-05934-M7V9K.summary: Harvey Walsh Ltd, a commercial health data analysis company, holds pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mortality, medicines and COVID-19 data from NHS England. It uses the data to give NHS bodies, universities, charities and life science companies services such as benchmarking, service evaluation and health economics studies. The aim is to help clients improve patient care and services. Reported results include published studies, conference presentations and a dashboard used to train clinicians.

DARS-NIC-06303-H3G5G.summary: The London Borough of Southwark, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data covering admitted patients, outpatients, critical care and A&E. It is using the data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to give locally focused analyses of health and inequalities. So far, it has analysed smoking and substance misuse admissions by ward, and winter pressures.

DARS-NIC-06381-N2B8J.summary: The University of Hertfordshire is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It is using them to build simulation tools that help NHS Trusts test changes to care pathways, such as for COPD, and assess their costs and effectiveness. The aim is faster, better-evidenced service planning. At Leicester Royal Infirmary, the cataract model led to approved changes and more surgeries each month.

DARS-NIC-06527-J1Q6T.summary: University College London (UCL) is using linked hospital records and death registration data for England. It is carrying out four studies on healthy life expectancy, meaning how long people live without significant ill health, and how this varies by factors such as deprivation, ethnicity and sex. The aim is to give policy makers and service commissioners evidence to address disparities. So far, UCL reports published analysis tools, public training on using the data, and a research paper under resubmission to a journal.

DARS-NIC-06587-S1Q6N.summary: Wiltshire Council, a local authority, is using pseudonymised hospital data covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, and critical care records. It uses the data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that the data was used for the 2022 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and analyses of alcohol-related and falls admissions.

DARS-NIC-06605-X1L9Z.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust uses national hospital, emergency care and death registration data to run an online benchmarking platform and produce bespoke reports for NHS organisations. These help them monitor clinical quality, patient safety and efficiency, so they can improve services for patients. Reported results include one trust moving from special measures to a "Good" Care Quality Commission rating, and a new one-stop orthopaedic outpatient service.

DARS-NIC-06759-X5V7P.summary: The University of York uses linked NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer registration, death and demographic records for a matched comparison group of people without blood cancers. It compares their healthcare use, survival and other health conditions with those of patients with blood cancers in the Yorkshire and Humber region. The aim is to improve understanding of blood cancers and inform care and policy. Published papers so far include one on rheumatological disorders and lymphoma.

DARS-NIC-07093-K5N3D.summary: Buckinghamshire Council, a local authority, uses hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It uses them in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. The council reports using the data to build analysis tools and to produce the annual public health report, needs assessments and local area profiles.

DARS-NIC-07141-L2S0B.summary: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust, through its hosted quality improvement body AQuA, uses hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care). It uses the data to analyse and benchmark hospital quality and safety, including mortality and re-admissions, for its member organisations. The aim is to reduce mortality and improve patient safety. Reported results include lower SHMI values at all six trusts given an in-depth mortality review, and a 2017 Greater Manchester stroke pathway review.

DARS-NIC-07233-W1M2Q.summary: Neil Wilson Associates LLP, a consultancy, uses Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care data in its Financial Benchmarking System. NHS organisations use it to compare their costs and activity with national or similar-organisation averages and to plan service and financial changes. The intended benefit is more efficient, better-quality care. One CCG negotiated an invoice reduction of over £1 million with its local acute trust after using this evidence.

DARS-NIC-07289-G8J6C.summary: The Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership (HQIP) uses hospital admission, death registration and patient reported outcome data to run the National Joint Registry, which tracks the results of joint replacement surgery. It uses the data to monitor outcomes by implant, hospital and surgeon, and to give early warning of patient safety issues. Reported benefits include outcomes data that led the MHRA to withdraw some devices, and changes to clinical practice such as guidance on hip implants.

DARS-NIC-07360-K4R9R.summary: The University of Southampton is using hospital, mental health, accident and emergency, and death registration records. It is studying Community Treatment Orders, which let patients detained in hospital continue compulsory treatment in the community. The research looks at how their use varies between people and places, how they relate to outcomes such as readmission and deaths, and what they cost. It aims to give a stronger evidence base on whether and for whom they work. An advance summary of the research was cited by the Wessely Independent Review of the Mental Health Act.

DARS-NIC-07763-M5K6S.summary: Cambridgeshire County Council is using pseudonymised hospital data, including admitted patient care, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care records. It uses them for its public health work, such as producing needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Since February 2021, the data has been used to assess mental health admissions.

DARS-NIC-07787-Z1W1X.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using national hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics) linked to death registration records. It is using them to examine whether reducing antibiotic use in acute and general medical inpatients is linked to higher death rates or other poorer outcomes. The aim is to help design ways of safely cutting antibiotic use, and so reduce antibiotic resistance. The analysis has already contributed to developing an intervention now being tested in a large trial.

DARS-NIC-08472-V9S6K.summary: UK Biobank, a charity, uses NHS England health records, including hospital, cancer, mental health, death and medicines data, linked to its research participants. It uses them to follow participants' health over time so researchers can study the genetic, social and economic causes of illnesses, with the aim of improving prevention, diagnosis and treatment. Published research has already used UK Biobank data, including around 400 COVID-19 papers and a study linking blood proteins to cancer diagnosis years earlier.

DARS-NIC-09122-R1S1D.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care uses non-identifiable Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, accessed through the NHS Digital Portal. It analyses them to support policy development, commissioning decisions, benchmarking, publications and answers to parliamentary questions. The main benefit is fast analysis of recent data when ministers need it. The department reports the data has informed national policy, including 7-day services policy, and ministerial briefings.

DARS-NIC-09519-D5G0R.summary: Methods Analytics Ltd, a supplier, uses pseudonymised national patient-level hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data. It uses them to produce analysis, tools and reports that help NHS organisations and the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) programme understand variation in care and improve quality, safety and efficiency. Reported results include a GIRFT review that identified over £1bn of NHS savings, and an NHS Trust's improved patient flow.

DARS-NIC-09637-Y8T1N.summary: The University of Oxford is using a pseudonymised extract of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) that has been linked to birth registration records. Its researchers are studying how gestational age affects children's health and economic outcomes up to age 11. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines, services and support for families of babies born before full term.

DARS-NIC-09901-F6V6M.summary: Bracknell Forest Council uses pseudonymised hospital data, including admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency records, for its public health work. It uses the data to analyse the local population's health and to support needs assessments, health strategies, public health advice and commissioning of services. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that needs are identified and acted on. So far, the council has built a data warehouse, and in 2022 hospital admissions data informed the relaunch of local Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-10029-G5R2H.summary: The Northern Ireland Clinical Trials Unit holds pseudonymised mortality data for people with acute lung injury who took part in the HARP2 trial. The data is kept securely for archiving, and the trial itself is complete. The trial tested whether simvastatin improves outcomes in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and informed a Scandinavian clinical guideline and two systematic reviews, which recommended against statins for ARDS.

DARS-NIC-100629-M8Y8B.summary: Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, support suicide audits and prevention work, and produce aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics for needs assessments and public health reports. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported uses include producing the JSNA and PNA, a suicide audit and local life expectancy profiles.

DARS-NIC-10094-P6P4B.summary: City, St George's University of London holds a research database linking hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) with birth registration and notification records. It is used to study how the day and time of birth relate to outcomes, to help inform maternity staffing and service planning. Reported results include a final report published by NIHR in 2019 and a 2023 BMJ Open paper finding that higher out-of-hours neonatal mortality was limited to babies born by emergency caesarean section without labour.

DARS-NIC-10123-M5K5H.summary: The University of Oxford uses identifiable death records and demographic data for 470 English participants in ACST-2, an international trial comparing two stroke-prevention procedures: carotid surgery and carotid stenting. The data supports long-term follow-up of stroke outcomes, including disabling or fatal strokes, with a final report due in 2026-27. The intended benefit is to show whether the procedures give comparable results, so patients and doctors can choose between them. A major report was published in The Lancet in 2021.

DARS-NIC-10328-S0H5J.summary: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust, through its North East Quality Observatory Service, uses pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, A&E and emergency care data. It uses them to measure care quality, benchmark services and evaluate service changes, producing aggregated reports for NHS and public-sector clients. The aim is to help organisations spot unwarranted variation and improve care. Reported results include reduced hospital stays and readmissions at several Trusts, and reports used in regional discussions on hospice services and children's asthma pathways.

DARS-NIC-103333-G9P5T.summary: London Borough of Sutton, a local authority, uses hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data. It uses them in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and planning of local services. The aim is to understand local health and inequalities better. The data has already informed the Sutton Health and Care Plan and the Annual Public Health Report.

DARS-NIC-10343-Z3M1B.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London uses Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, linked to audit records on people treated for hip fracture in England and Wales. It uses the data to compare hospital performance fairly, track outcomes such as readmission and return to independent living, and estimate how many cases the audit captures. The aim is better care and outcomes for patients. An independent evaluation has reported that the database has reduced deaths in the month after hip fracture.

DARS-NIC-10459-G9T3P.summary: The London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. Reported work so far includes analyses of violence-related A&E visits, preventable admissions, Covid inequalities and leading causes of death.

DARS-NIC-10620-V9D8R.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, which hosts the East Midlands Academic Health Science Network, is using Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency care, along with the Emergency Care Data Set. The network uses it to produce aggregated reports on demand for services, variations in care and the impact of innovations. The intended benefit is better, safer and more efficient care for East Midlands residents.

DARS-NIC-107979-X3R6Q.summary: Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council uses identifiable birth and death registration data, plus primary care mortality data, to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. Results are published only as aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. So far, the data has been used to produce community profiles and to monitor mortality rates ahead of national monitoring.

DARS-NIC-108067-P1C4R.summary: Worcestershire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. It reports using deaths data during the Covid pandemic to target services, and working with the integrated care board (ICB) on ongoing health issues.

DARS-NIC-108098-D2L3V.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) is using linked health data, with identifying details removed, from GP records and NHS Digital sources. It is carrying out two studies for Cancer Research UK on bowel cancer screening. One looks at how people who do not respond to screening use primary care. The other looks at how patients and GPs respond to symptoms after a negative screening test. The aim is to help target support and promote earlier diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-10891-M2Y6Z.summary: CHKS Limited, a supplier, uses Hospital Episode Statistics, Emergency Care Data Set and Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator data to provide benchmarking and analysis services to NHS providers, commissioners and some commercial organisations working with the NHS. The data supports performance comparison, mortality review and reports, with small numbers suppressed. The aim is to help improve patient care and efficiency. Reported benefits include Barnsley and Barts Health using mortality reports to guide action plans and reviews.

DARS-NIC-10912-D5Y1L.summary: Newcastle City Council's public health team uses hospital inpatient, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data, plus emergency care data. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. So far, the data has fed into a Drug Market Profile, alcohol admissions mapping and completed needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-10929-K8H5K.summary: The Royal Borough of Greenwich, a local authority, is using hospital records from NHS England's Secure Environment: Hospital Episode Statistics covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and A&E, plus the Emergency Care Data Set. Its public health team uses them to produce needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported use so far includes analyses of COVID-19, maternity, alcohol and falls admissions that fed into reports and service performance reporting.

DARS-NIC-10932-H7Y6B.summary: Suffolk County Council, a local authority, uses hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care, outpatients and A&E attendances. It uses them for public health work, such as producing needs assessments and the Director of Public Health's annual report, advising NHS commissioners and planning services. The aim is local analysis of health inequalities, including for disadvantaged groups. Analyses already produced cover areas such as self-harm, falls and asthma admissions, and demand projections.

DARS-NIC-109867-M8S6B.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics), death records and cohort tracking reports for women in the UK Women's Cohort Study. It links them with diet and lifestyle information to study how diet and lifestyle relate to cancer and other chronic diseases, with the aim of informing public health advice. The register reports published research from the study, such as papers on cancer risk and hip fracture, which it says has informed policy and NHS programmes.

DARS-NIC-10994-B8M6V.summary: Cheshire West and Chester Council's public health team uses hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and emergency care data. It uses them to produce analyses that support its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported results include published Starting Well and falls needs assessments and annual Children's Centre profiles.

DARS-NIC-110660-G9W6M.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former NHS Stockport CCG, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and primary care activity data, with some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target their care, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better planned for local people.

DARS-NIC-11114-J5C4Q.summary: Devon County Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital records, covering admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care data. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported benefits include the data informing the 2025 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment refresh and its new chapter on inequalities.

DARS-NIC-11221-X6Y6N.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust uses Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E through the NHS Digital Portal. It uses the data to study acute kidney injury (AKI) in England and to support quality improvement, with the aim of improving length of stay, mortality and services. Earlier access led to published research papers on AKI and to changes in coding and AKI recognition at Queens Hospital, Burton.

DARS-NIC-112374-X0T4S.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Patient Reported Outcome Measures linked to them. It is independently evaluating the Getting it Right First Time (GIRFT) programme, which aims to reduce variation in NHS orthopaedic surgery, focusing on hip and knee replacements. The intended benefit is evidence on what worked, so the programme and future improvement programmes can be refined.

DARS-NIC-112633-G0C0H.summary: The University of Ulster, an academic body, is using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 data on adults in England. It is carrying out more detailed analysis of hazardous, harmful and dependent drinking, including how harm differs by social class. The aim is to give policy makers and health planners stronger evidence for targeting services at the drinkers at greatest risk of alcohol-related harm.

DARS-NIC-112910-R4X9X.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital admission records and death registration data to follow up patients hospitalised with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (a type of heart attack or unstable angina). The study tests whether using the GRACE risk score increases use of guideline-recommended treatments and reduces cardiovascular deaths and hospital readmissions at twelve months, compared with standard care. Data received so far went to the trial's Data Monitoring and Ethics Committee in 2019, which used it to decide that the study should continue.

DARS-NIC-11302-Q1L1F.summary: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) uses Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency. It uses them to scope and review guidance and standards, develop indicators and build tools that estimate the cost of putting guidance into practice. The aim is guidance based on the best available evidence. In 2021, the data informed a published resource impact report and template for prostate cancer guidance.

DARS-NIC-113025-X7Z3L.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) is using linked health records, supplied through bespoke Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) datasets, to support the PEARL study. The study looks at long-term health outcomes for women who have had assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment and for their children, linking GP data with fertility treatment registry data. The main intended benefit is better evidence for couples considering fertility treatment, for families and for clinicians, and for NHS planning.

DARS-NIC-113611-X2Y3H.summary: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust is using Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency attendances and hospital admissions for patients with specialist palliative care needs. It aims to find out why these patients end up in emergency departments and acute hospitals. The findings are meant to help design services that support them at home and reduce hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-113855-M5G7Q.summary: Isle of Wight Council's public health team is using hospital records on admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and accident and emergency attendances. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that the data has informed health needs assessments, prioritisation work and early analysis of COVID's impact.

DARS-NIC-113964-G3J0C.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised, record-level hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data about people taking part in The HOME Study. The data will help show whether adding a new psychological care approach for older hospital patients reduces the time they spend in hospital, and what it costs the NHS. The results are expected to inform decisions about NHS investment in liaison psychiatry services.

DARS-NIC-113980-R8Z8K.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB uses pseudonymised health, social care and civil registration data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services, to support commissioning. It analyses the data to plan services around local needs, understand patient flows and risk, and manage contracts. The main intended benefit is better planning and quality of services for the local population.

DARS-NIC-114531-J1Q9G.summary: Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, is using civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data. It uses the data to understand local health needs, support public health work such as suicide audits, and produce summary statistics for health strategies and reports. The aim is to tailor local services, reduce premature deaths and tackle health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-114652-L3R2T.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant is using civil registrations of death data to find out whether recruited trial patients were still alive one year after major trauma bleeding. It supports the CRYOSTAT 2 trial, run with Queen Mary University of London, which tests whether early high-dose cryoprecipitate, a fibrinogen-rich blood component, reduces deaths. The aim is to show whether it improves survival and is cost effective. So far, short-term results have been shared with the trial team and a manuscript is being prepared.

DARS-NIC-115298-L5X4V.summary: GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited, a commercial company, is keeping hospital records data (Hospital Episode Statistics covering A&E, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients) for people in the Extended Salford Lung Study. It will use the data to answer peer review comments on its asthma studies before they are published. The main intended benefit is helping doctors identify asthma patients with poor control or frequent moderate flare-ups. Findings have already been presented as abstracts at the ISPOR 2022 and CHEST 2022 conferences.

DARS-NIC-115405-P6X6Q.summary: The University of Nottingham is using hospital records from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) for people with familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH), an inherited cause of high cholesterol. The study will examine treatment patterns, heart-related outcomes and NHS costs over the long term, and use them to build economic models of testing relatives of people with FH. The aim is to show which testing approach offers the best value for money, to inform NHS commissioners and national guidance.

DARS-NIC-11544-S1L0R.summary: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust uses pseudonymised (non-identifiable) Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, accessed through an online portal. It uses them to benchmark care, plan services across the local health system and assess future population need for children and women. The aim is well-planned paediatric care. Reported benefits include data informing orthopaedic service planning in business cases and the placement of community maternity hubs.

DARS-NIC-115590-Q1C7Z.summary: The University of Surrey is using hospital records for children in England, including admissions, outpatient and A&E visits, critical care and death registrations. It is using them for one part of the EU-funded MOCHA study, which looks at how individual and health service factors affect outcomes in eight childhood conditions, including asthma, epilepsy and rickets prevention, between 2003 and 2017. The aim is to show which structural factors matter for child health outcomes in England, and to help identify the best models of primary care for children.

DARS-NIC-115892-Y2C6D.summary: Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties. It uses the data to analyse health needs, inequalities and service use, and to produce documents such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments and the annual public health report. The aim is more locally targeted and responsive services. Reported uses include supporting commissioning of young people's health and drug and alcohol services, and informing violence reduction work.

DARS-NIC-115934-P8P0X.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, acting for the former Hartlepool and Stockton-on-Tees clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payments and better patient care.

DARS-NIC-11613-B4J8Z.summary: Blackpool Borough Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to meet its public health duties. It uses them to plan and commission services, advise NHS commissioners and produce needs assessments and strategies. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Work so far on children's dental extractions, falls, alcohol-related admissions and urgent care use has supported needs assessments and influenced commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-116377-L5J9M.summary: The University of Sheffield is using hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and a bespoke MRIS (Medical Research Information Service) dataset. It is linking them with dental data to study whether invasive dental procedures are connected to infective endocarditis, heart attack, stroke, pulmonary embolus and spontaneous pre-term birth. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence for guidelines on antibiotic prophylaxis before dental and medical procedures.

DARS-NIC-116548-M7Z5F.summary: NHS Frimley ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and other local provider activity data, including NHS-number-level data for some uses. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned to match local needs. The register says services have been delivered to match population requirements, but gives no specific example.

DARS-NIC-116560-R7F9J.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners), which can be identified by NHS number, supported by NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit. It is used to check provider invoices so that only patients the ICB is responsible for are paid for. It is also linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and earlier, better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-116582-F2F2J.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB, working with Oxfordshire County Council, uses pseudonymised health and adult social care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, prescribing and death records. They use it to plan and commission health services for Oxfordshire's population, including population health management and service redesign. The main intended benefit is better decisions and improved quality of services and health outcomes. Reported results include a diabetes dashboard used to improve diabetes care and a new community gynaecology service.

DARS-NIC-116738-W8J8Q.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, which can be identified by NHS number, and links it with GP data. It uses the data to check provider invoices before payment and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, so that care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for treatment and that at-risk patients receive earlier, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-116829-C2B8N.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB, as a sub-ICB location, uses Secondary User Services (SUS) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. It is used to check hospital and service invoices so that only activity for patients the organisation is responsible for is paid. It is also used for risk stratification, which links SUS data with GP data to identify patients at high risk so that care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care.

DARS-NIC-116883-L8W9Q.summary: Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, working with University College London, is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for about 550,000 patients who had retinal scans. It is studying how changes in the retina relate to dementia and other neurodegenerative diseases, with the aim of developing a tool to detect dementia early. Published work so far includes a 2022 BMJ Open paper, research finding retinal changes in Parkinson disease about seven years before clinical presentation, and a dementia prediction model.

DARS-NIC-117514-V5D2N.summary: Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will analyse local health patterns and needs to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of better targeting local health challenges and inequalities. It has already used the data in a Family Hubs needs assessment to identify areas with birth-related issues, so support could be targeted there.

DARS-NIC-11809-H1Y3W.summary: The University of Leeds uses cancer registration, hospital, mental health, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data to run the Yorkshire Specialist Register of Cancer in Children and Young People. The data supports research on hospital use, diagnosis pathways and long-term health risks among cancer survivors aged 0 to 39. It aims to improve care and treatment decisions. Reported results include peer-reviewed publications and evidence that supported risk-stratified follow-up care in Yorkshire and beyond.

DARS-NIC-118232-Z8V8B.summary: Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council is using identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work. The main intended benefit is local services that are better targeted at areas of greatest need, helping to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported uses so far include analysis feeding into the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and Annual Report, and the data has been used extensively in the council's suicide prevention work.

DARS-NIC-119910-K6W9Q.summary: The University of Bristol is using NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and diagnostic imaging records for men in the CAP trial, which compares inviting men aged 50 to 69 for a PSA test for prostate cancer with standard NHS care. The data are used to follow up deaths and cancer diagnoses over the long term, to assess whether PSA testing reduces prostate cancer deaths and whether it is cost-effective. The results are intended to inform UK screening policy. Findings have already been published in JAMA, and results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and used in the National Screening Committee's review.

DARS-NIC-120105-F0K2L.summary: The University of Leicester is using linked, pseudonymised hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care) and civil registration death records, alongside audit data on children's intensive care. It is studying whether delays in reaching paediatric intensive care, and the care given during transport, affect critically ill children's survival, and it is also analysing the costs and value for money of different transport team models. The intended benefit is evidence to guide future standards of care and national policy for transporting critically ill children.

DARS-NIC-120519-J7H0T.summary: Bolton Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is to tailor services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported uses include Bolton's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, its serious violence needs assessment and strategy, and a licensing decisions tool.

DARS-NIC-120848-R6V4C.summary: The University of Warwick is using hospital admission and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for patients who had total knee replacement surgery in 2003, linked to National Joint Registry records of tourniquet use. The research looks at whether using a tourniquet during surgery is linked to complications such as blood clots in the leg or lung and stroke in the year afterwards. The main intended benefit is evidence on the safety of tourniquets, which could inform surgical practice and NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-121483-R8P9F.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust manages the database for the Baby Biome Study, using hospital, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care and death records for consenting mothers and their babies. The feasibility stage tests whether these records can be linked to the study's own data and checks their quality, to see whether early gut bacteria relate to later childhood health. The main aim is to support funding to expand the study and, longer term, to inform child health practice.

DARS-NIC-121849-W0T5C.summary: The University of Birmingham is using pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for mothers and babies from births between 2005 and 2018. It is studying whether giving antibiotics before skin incision, rather than after cord clamping, in caesarean births is linked to children's later hospital admissions, mainly for asthma and eczema. The aim is to inform national guidance. The team reports finding no evidence of an association between the change in antibiotic timing and early-life illnesses in children.

DARS-NIC-121996-T2R7B.summary: The University of Bristol is using civil registrations of death data, linked to information on people with learning disabilities who have died in England. It aims to identify their exact causes of death, which cannot currently be seen in national mortality statistics, so that services can be improved and early deaths reduced. Benefits reported so far include a national NHS England "Learning into Action" group, a March 2019 conference and a 2018 annual report.

DARS-NIC-123200-J0L4T.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital records (admitted patient and critical care) and death and follow-up records for 1,615 people aged 65 to 84 who took part in a vitamin D trial. The study tests whether a larger trial of vitamin D supplementation, to see if it reduces illness and extends life, would be feasible. It aims to set the procedures, costs and design for that main trial. A paper on the feasibility study has been accepted by the NIHR Health Technology Assessment journal.

DARS-NIC-125012-S7Z6Y.summary: The London Borough of Hounslow, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported benefits are information supplied to the Public Health team, such as deaths by cause and births by ward.

DARS-NIC-125031-Z3D7S.summary: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust is using hospital admission, critical care, outpatient and death records for babies born at 27 to 31 weeks of gestation in England. It is studying the cost of care up to age two, comparing neonatal intensive care units with local neonatal units, to help decide the best place of care. The aim is to guide neonatal service provision. The study team report finding more serious brain injury in 27-week babies at local units, which is informing discussions on service delivery.

DARS-NIC-125783-W2W3P.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, working with Wakefield Council, uses linked health and care data covering hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and death records. It is used to evaluate Population Health Management work with care home residents in Wakefield and to plan services, with the aim of reducing hospital admissions and emergency demand. Reported benefits so far include a clearer picture of deaths moving from community settings into hospital, and of causes of in-hospital deaths.

DARS-NIC-126117-S3Y1K.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which is pseudonymised but identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that hospital and other provider invoices are the commissioner's responsibility and recovers overpayments. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted earlier.

DARS-NIC-12629-B4N5K.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using NHS England cancer registration, hospital, emergency care and death records for the long-term follow-up of women in the IBIS-I breast cancer prevention trial. It is studying how well and how safely tamoxifen prevents breast cancer, aiming to give women at high risk and bodies such as NICE better information. Results from this data have already been published, including a 2015 paper on the main trial outcome that was used to inform NICE's recommendations on tamoxifen.

DARS-NIC-126676-G1X4M.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable NHS England data, including hospital records, cancer registrations and death registrations, for 382 women who took part in the TARGIT-A breast cancer radiotherapy trial. It is extending the trial's follow-up and checking whether collecting outcomes directly from patients is complete and accurate compared with NHS England data. The main intended benefit is a better way to gather long-term follow-up data in clinical trials.

DARS-NIC-12706-T1K2Q.summary: Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council is using hospital data covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) attendances. It uses the data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. So far, the council has used the data to monitor flu admissions by age group and to look at emergency admission trends.

DARS-NIC-127189-R2K8F.summary: St. George's Hospital Medical School, an academic organisation, is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, supplied as tabulated counts of hospital admissions. It will use them with air pollution estimates to study how long-term and short-term exposure to outdoor air pollution relate to hospital admissions for respiratory and cardiovascular disease. The aim is to give UK policy makers useful information for assessing health impacts and planning measures to reduce air pollution.

DARS-NIC-127332-G0J1N.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), linked to GP data for risk scoring. It uses the data to check that provider invoices are valid and payable, and to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are accurate payment and budget control, and earlier support that reduces avoidable hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-12784-R8W7V.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, uses linked NHS hospital, cancer, mental health, diagnostic imaging and death registration data in its National Genomics Research Library, a secure environment holding genomic and health data. Researchers use it to understand diseases, find disease-causing gene variants and develop new treatments. Reported results include new diagnoses for 25% of participants in the 100,000 Genomes Project using whole genome sequencing.

DARS-NIC-12828-M0K2D.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit, an academic research group, uses hospital records (inpatient, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and civil registration death data. It develops measures of healthcare quality and safety, including monthly hospital mortality alerts and studies of how COVID-19 affected care. The aim is to show variation between hospitals and help improve care. Its mortality alerts helped identify problems at Mid Staffordshire NHS Foundation Trust, and its work has appeared in NICE clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-12881-L1H2B.summary: The University of York runs the National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation and uses hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to count patients with heart conditions who should have received cardiac rehabilitation. This helps it report on how well services are performing, so commissioners and clinical teams can improve them. The audit has produced over 25 research articles and led to national certification of programmes and inclusion in NHS England quality reporting.

DARS-NIC-129507-J0H0D.summary: NHS North East London ICB (a sub-ICB location covering seven former CCGs in the area) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care and civil registration data, including clinical and financial information. It uses this to plan and commission health services for the local population, including population health management, needs assessment, demand management and contract monitoring. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions, improving the quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-129819-V5P5Z.summary: The University of Sheffield is using NHS list cleaning data (mortality checks, current addresses and type 2 objection removals) for patients with bladder cancer in Yorkshire, Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees. It supports a survey of patients' health-related quality of life, to understand variation in outcomes and identify unmet needs. The list cleaning aims to improve survey coverage and avoid mailing people who have died.

DARS-NIC-12983-Y3L3K.summary: The University of Sheffield is using de-identified hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to compare the safety and quality of care across English hospitals. The aim is to give policy makers and hospital administrators evidence on which hospitals may need further investigation. So far, the university has developed two new mortality indices, one for safety and one for quality, and used them to compare 136 acute general hospitals between 2010 and 2015.

DARS-NIC-129836-D5F3W.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies receives demographic data, in the form of updated addresses, for members of the 1970 British Cohort Study. It uses them to invite participants to the age 51 survey and to keep in touch between surveys. The aim is to re-contact people it has lost touch with and avoid contacting those who have died. In the 2012 survey, almost 800 interviews were achieved with participants newly traced through addresses supplied by NHS England.

DARS-NIC-130731-T6N7C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former NHS Eastern Cheshire CCG area, uses pseudonymised (personal details removed) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information. Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit analyses it to plan and commission health services, assess population needs and redesign services. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow for the local population.

DARS-NIC-130735-P4Q6M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former Southport and Formby CCG area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and births and deaths data. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including population health analysis, spotting patients at risk of admission, and managing demand and contracts. The aim is for services to better match local needs, with Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit doing the processing.

DARS-NIC-130743-V5C9T.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former NHS Halton CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, with some identifiable at NHS number level for risk stratification. It uses the data to identify patients at high risk, and to plan, monitor and redesign health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-130761-H9V5V.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (for the former Vale Royal CCG area) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and civil registration data, with clinical and financial detail. Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit analyses it to plan and commission health services, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-130779-P1H2C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former South Sefton clinical commissioning group (CCG) area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and births and deaths data. The Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit analyses it to plan and monitor health services, understand local health needs and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and improved quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-130789-T3F8P.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for its Knowsley area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and death and birth records, covering both clinical and financial information. It uses them to plan and commission health services for the local population, including studying needs, predicting demand and reviewing provider performance. The main intended benefit is better-planned services that improve quality and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-130796-T8T5F.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former St Helens CCG area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and births and deaths data. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, understand local needs, model demand and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes. Reported benefits include supporting the Covid-19 vaccination and testing programmes, hospital discharges and care home support.

DARS-NIC-13133-B7B3K.summary: The University of Bristol is using NHS hospital records (including accident and emergency, inpatient, outpatient and critical care), mental health data sets and death and tracing records for about 5,000 adults enrolled in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children as babies. It uses them to trace participants, update records and study adolescent mental health, substance use, self-harm and sexual health. The main intended benefit is better evidence for public health policy. Studies using the wider ALSPAC data have already informed policy and guidance, including on fish consumption in pregnancy.

DARS-NIC-13172-S1S3F.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admission records and death and status-tracking records for people who took part in the SHARP kidney disease trial. It is comparing events recorded in these routine datasets with the outcomes that trial clinicians confirmed by reviewing hospital notes. The aim is to show whether routine healthcare data could replace costly manual checking, making future clinical trials cheaper and less demanding for participants.

DARS-NIC-132001-W7C3H.summary: Derby City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan public health services, and carry out work such as suicide audits and prevention. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local need, to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include death data being used to frame a new inequalities agenda, and birth data informing school placement planning.

DARS-NIC-132395-Q4W9P.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB, working with other clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in the Hampshire and Isle of Wight partnership, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and related data containing clinical and financial information. It is used to plan and commission health services, including reporting, demand planning and identifying patients and groups with particular needs. The stated benefits include better planning of patient pathways, improved access and quality, and fewer avoidable emergency readmissions.

DARS-NIC-132869-R0D7F.summary: Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council is using hospital data covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It will use the data in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report, and advice to NHS commissioners. The intended benefit is local analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups. Outputs will be aggregated, with small numbers suppressed.

DARS-NIC-134460-X5B7B.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, which is identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that provider invoices are the commissioner's responsibility and supports budget control. Risk stratification links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and offered earlier, with the aim of improving commissioning and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-134552-B5T6B.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses a wide range of hospital, community, mental health, primary care medicines and population datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to validate provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better patient care and avoided payment losses. The CCG has published an annual report describing developments supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-134558-G9L9K.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, through a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, with both clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the population of the former Hambleton, Richmondshire and Whitby CCG area. This includes analysing patient needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services, with improved patient flow and access.

DARS-NIC-134613-G2M6G.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (for the former Northumberland CCG area) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at risk of poor health, and plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient care and accurate payment of providers. The CCG has produced an annual report describing developments and achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-134630-K0M4D.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, for the former South Tyneside CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health datasets, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support the planning and commissioning of local health services. The main aim is accurate payment and more effective, better-targeted care. The CCG's annual report includes case studies that used this data.

DARS-NIC-134638-Z3C2N.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, for the Newcastle Gateshead area, uses hospital activity, community, mental health, maternity and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and plan and monitor commissioned health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is planned and targeted more effectively.

DARS-NIC-134656-N8S3W.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, acting for the former North Tyneside CCG, uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor health services. The main aim is to pay providers accurately and to target care more effectively. The CCG has published an annual report on its achievements.

DARS-NIC-134666-G5H1F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (North Durham area) uses hospital, ambulance, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices and recover overpayments, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be prioritised, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned more effectively.

DARS-NIC-134719-D5W2Y.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration records for the CIPHER study, which involves people who have had a stoma formed during bowel surgery. The study looks at how often parastomal hernia develops within two years and whether surgical techniques, such as the use of mesh, affect that risk. It aims to inform future research and guidance that could reduce hernias and improve patients' quality of life.

DARS-NIC-135277-R8M3G.summary: The Regional Drug and Therapeutics Centre at Newcastle uses pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and primary care dispensing data. It links them to produce prescribing reports for NHS areas, comparing medicine use with hospital admissions. The aim is to help local NHS teams benchmark prescribing and use medicines more cost-effectively. In Greater Manchester, the reports led to a diabetes pathway being developed and formulary changes.

DARS-NIC-135294-P7L0F.summary: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using NHS England mortality data, including death registrations and cause of death reports, for the OxValve cohort of people aged 65 and over screened for valvular heart disease in primary care. It is reporting how long people with and without the condition survive and what they die from. This aims to help patients, clinicians and commissioners understand outlook and plan care. The findings have been published in the journal Heart and in a blog advising GPs that mild disease is unlikely to affect long-term outcome.

DARS-NIC-136400-H5Y3X.summary: Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council uses hospital data, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) or emergency care attendances. It uses this data for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. The council reports using the data to inform its clean air strategy, a falls needs assessment and a learning disability needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-136916-B7D5C.summary: University College London is using linked hospital, death registration and cohort-tracking records to compare outcomes for first-time teenage mothers who joined the Family Nurse Partnership home visiting programme with similar families who did not. The aim is to show how well the programme works for different groups of families, helping commissioners and policymakers target support. Reported results include published papers on enrolment and data linkage, and findings shared with the Family Nurse Partnership National Unit.

DARS-NIC-137718-T4D1S.summary: Bedford Borough Council's core public health team uses identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, on behalf of itself, Central Bedfordshire Council and Milton Keynes Council. It uses them to assess local health needs, run public health work such as suicide audits, and produce aggregated statistics for plans and reports. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce mortality and health inequalities. So far, the data has produced a mortality dashboard for each of the three councils as part of the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-137864-T1P9B.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable NHS England demographic data, mainly current addresses, for the National Child Development Study, which follows people born in one week in 1958. The addresses let its Centre for Longitudinal Studies contact participants who have moved and invite them to take part in future surveys. Reported benefits include newly traced participants being interviewed in the age 55 survey, and the age 55 data being available to researchers through the UK Data Service.

DARS-NIC-138652-J2Q4S.summary: The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses the data to measure local health needs, plan public health work such as immunisation programmes, and produce reports such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, with only aggregated statistics published. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. It reports that the data helped identify suicide hotspots and risk factors, which informed the local suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-139035-X4B7K.summary: NHS England uses pseudonymised health data, including hospital, mental health, community, ambulance and clinical registry records, in its NHS England & Improvement Data Platform. It uses the data to manage commissioned services, support quality and productivity programmes, check data quality and evaluate service changes. The aim is to help it meet its statutory duties and commission effective services. Reported benefits include a service moved to a more accessible location, dashboards and reports, and data supporting a published paediatric critical care review.

DARS-NIC-13906-G0F3F.summary: The Private Healthcare Information Network (PHIN), appointed by the Competition and Markets Authority as the "Information Organisation", uses pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on planned hospital care. It uses the data to publish hospital and consultant performance measures and to compare NHS-funded and private care. The aim is to help patients make better-informed choices of provider. PHIN reports published analyses, consultant data reviews and GPs using its website to support patient choice.

DARS-NIC-139091-F3T3H.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, together with the other clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in the Greater Manchester partnership, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care, prescribing and death and birth records. They use it to plan and monitor health services, track provider performance and costs, and understand demand across the area. The main intended benefit is better-planned, higher-quality care that meets the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-139146-W7C3P.summary: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission and civil registration of death data to follow up patients with chronic thoracic aortic aneurysm in the ETTAA study. The data will check that deaths, hospital admissions and resources used are recorded accurately. The aim is to give reliable evidence on the clinical and cost-effectiveness of treatments, to guide decisions and NHS policy. Published papers in 2022 have already reported findings on treatment and monitoring.

DARS-NIC-13925-Q7R2D.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, holds hospital data from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics, Emergency Care Data Set and data quality reports) that feeds its Hospital Treatment Insights database on diagnoses, treatments and drug use in hospitals. Under this agreement it may only keep the data securely, not process it further. Earlier work produced published studies and conference presentations on high-cost drugs, plus drug-use feedback reports that hospital chief pharmacists used to benchmark their prescribing.

DARS-NIC-139741-D9Y1C.summary: Bangor University, an academic organisation, is using Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions and outpatient visits for the NERVES trial, which involved 163 patients with sciatica. It is using the data to cost hospital care in the trial and compare the cost-effectiveness of surgery with steroid injections. The main intended benefit is to help the NHS and commissioners decide which treatment is most clinically and cost-effective.

DARS-NIC-140037-T3W0M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former Knowsley CCG area, uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better-targeted support for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-140059-P1J9L.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, with the local CCGs and councils in the Cheshire and Merseyside partnership, uses pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, prescribing and death records. They use it to plan, monitor and improve commissioned services for their population, including demand, costs and patient pathways. Liverpool CCG reports using it to meet national data collection and 2-hour crisis response requirements, improve ethnicity coding, and support diabetes and Telehealth services.

DARS-NIC-140981-R5N6Z.summary: University College London (UCL) is using a pseudonymised extract from the Mental Health Services Data Set, linked with Child Outcomes Research Consortium data, on young people aged 2 to 25 in child mental health services. It is studying how young people's characteristics relate to treatment outcomes and resource use, so care can be better tailored. UCL reports that a region has already used its findings in its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-141410-W6H4Y.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient and death registration records for children and young people aged 0 to 24 in England. The research looks at why the UK's child and youth death rate is higher than in many comparable countries, including how health service use relates to this. It aims to inform health policy and service reform. Findings have already been published in Archives of Disease in Childhood and contributed to the RCPCH Paediatrics 2040 report.

DARS-NIC-141755-M8J2J.summary: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that providers' invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, where the data is linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-142633-S5G3Q.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB, working with the former Erewash, Hardwick, North Derbyshire and Southern Derbyshire CCGs, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care activity data, with financial information and birth and death records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs and redesign services. The main intended benefit is better planning of care, so services meet the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-142790-C1J9J.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using survey data on adult psychiatric morbidity and data from Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) services. It is comparing the mental health, needs and treatment outcomes of veterans and non-veterans in England. The intended benefit is to help NHS England and service providers identify effective, timely treatments for ex-service personnel with mental health problems.

DARS-NIC-14340-R7G1F.summary: Meditrends Ltd, a consultancy, uses Hospital Episode Statistics hospital records and linked death registration data. It runs a web portal of aggregated, small-number-suppressed analytics and produces custom analyses for NHS-led projects. The aim is to help plan services, compare care pathways and estimate the budget impact of new technologies.
