Reported results include a NICE multiple sclerosis appraisal analysis and a heart valve tariff guide.

DARS-NIC-14342-Q8W0X.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) linked to the ATTOM study of people in England with kidney disease who are on dialysis or have a kidney transplant. It will examine how health literacy, socioeconomic status and other health conditions relate to hospital use, costs and survival. The aim is to build evidence for reducing inequity in access to kidney transplantation.

DARS-NIC-14360-S9G2Y.summary: Imperial College London Business School is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care records to study how new surgical techniques spread among consultants. It looks at colorectal and breast cancer surgery, and cardiac surgery, asking whether formal hospital cancer networks or consultants' professional networks have more influence on following national guidelines. The aim is to help policy makers target funding to speed up proven, cost-effective treatments. Two peer-reviewed papers, published in 2021 and 2025, have so far come from the work.

DARS-NIC-143888-H0W2N.summary: The University of Leicester is using national hospital admission and death records, linked with other health datasets, to study how heart disease and cancer affect each other. The research looks at questions such as whether heart attack patients with cancer are treated differently and how cancer treatments affect long-term heart health. The main intended benefit is better evidence on managing patients who have both conditions, which could improve treatment and clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-144057-G4S0Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised hospital admission records and death registration data for about 900,000 people over 60 who had hip fracture surgery. It is evaluating all-cause and cause-specific deaths after hip fracture, including how rates vary between hospitals, to show where and in whom mortality could be reduced. Benefits reported so far: the work supported the justification and planning for the DIRECT trial, which is now fully funded by NIHR.

DARS-NIC-14440-Q2G4W.summary: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust uses Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care data for the Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) programme. It calculates hospital and Clinical Commissioning Group level metrics to support clinician review meetings, research and coding quality checks. The aim is to reduce variation in surgical practice and deliver efficiency savings. It reports measured changes in practice, such as shorter hospital stays and fewer readmissions in orthopaedics, and estimated savings already realised.

DARS-NIC-144568-D7G6V.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, through Royal Brompton Hospital, is using hospital admission, death registration and COVID-19 surveillance data. It is studying trends in acute myocarditis (heart muscle inflammation) and related conditions over 23 years, including patient outcomes and links with COVID-19. The aim is to show the real burden of the disease. Findings have been presented, published in 'Circulation', cited on a UK government website and used in the 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines.

DARS-NIC-144761-Y3X9Y.summary: King's College London, an academic organisation, is using hospital admission, A&E and death registration data. It is studying end of life care for adults with serious mental illness, looking at hospital use in the last year of life and place of death, and which demographic and clinical factors are linked to them. The intended benefit is evidence on whether these patients face inequalities in care, to inform practice and policy.

DARS-NIC-145260-G4Y0G.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to study asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and coronary heart disease. The research looks at how respiratory viruses and environmental factors such as air pollution affect the timing of hospital admissions for flare-ups of these conditions. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of these triggers, to help design preventive strategies and reduce the burden of flare-ups.

DARS-NIC-146909-L9Q3C.summary: Thurrock Council, a local authority, is using pseudonymised (identifying details removed) hospital, mental health, psychological therapy and maternity data, processed by MedeAnalytics International Limited. It uses the data to support commissioning of health and social care services, including population health analysis, service redesign and contract management. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient experience. So far, the council has used the data to complete the first phase of an evaluation of an alternative approach to adult social care.

DARS-NIC-147034-XH3H2.summary: The University of Cambridge holds date and cause of death records and related demographic data for participants in the CFAS II and CFAS Wales studies of people aged over 65. They use it to work out survival and life expectancy, including for people who develop cognitive impairment, to support research on dementia and healthy ageing. The findings help plan services. Welsh Government now uses CFAS dementia prevalence findings to calculate diagnosis rates across Health Boards.

DARS-NIC-14709-Z2H2R.summary: i5 Health Limited, a consultancy, uses hospital, emergency care and community services data from NHS England to produce aggregated reports and data models for NHS bodies, local authorities and voluntary organisations. These support commissioning decisions, such as identifying out-of-hospital services, care gaps and the value of community nursing. The aim is better use of resources and improved patient care. Reported results include a £500,000 rise in NHS investment in nurse prescribing training, and 76 more patients identified for atrial fibrillation registers in Haringey.

DARS-NIC-147747-KRTQ8.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and cohort follow-up records for about 2.7 million women eligible for NHS breast screening invitations between 1988 and 1994. It is evaluating how the NHS Breast Screening Programme affects breast cancer deaths and overdiagnosis. The aim is to give decision makers precise estimates to inform screening policy, such as age groups and intervals between screens. Earlier analysis of about 40% of the cohort has been published in two papers.

DARS-NIC-147748-XD18S.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on people with insulin-treated diabetes, and is keeping it securely, with no other processing, so it can run updated analyses in 2028 for a long-running national cohort study of cancer and mortality. The aim is better information on long-term health risks, to support patient advice, follow-up and screening. Papers from the study have already been used in international clinical guidelines on cholesterol disorders, heart disease and complications in children with diabetes.

DARS-NIC-147749-3SSRF.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds cancer registration, death and demographic records for about 27,000 patients with chromosome or childhood hormone disorders. The data is kept only for a long-running cohort study of cancer and death risks, with updated analyses planned for 2028. The aim is better information for patients, families and clinicians on long-term risks and follow-up. Published papers from the study have already been used in clinical practice guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147750-8GS7S.summary: The University of Cambridge is using mortality and demographic records for about 39,000 people screened for type 2 diabetes in the ADDITION study. It is following them up to see how screening, and early intensive treatment of risk factors, affect long-term death rates and cardiovascular risk. The aim is to inform NHS policy on whether population diabetes screening should be offered. So far, the study has produced over 80 published papers, and its findings have been cited in international screening guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147755-C5H4X.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, death and demographic records to follow up patients in the Arterial Revascularisation Trial (ART) for 15 years. The trial compares bilateral with single internal thoracic artery grafting in coronary artery bypass surgery. The aim is to provide long-term evidence on survival and cardiovascular events to guide the best treatment. Earlier results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019, and a cost-effectiveness analysis followed in 2022.

DARS-NIC-147756-SMGHS.summary: Nuvia Ltd, a commercial organisation, is using mortality and cancer follow-up data on about 22,000 people employed at the Atomic Weapons Establishment between 1951 and 1982. It uses the data to study the health effects of low-dose occupational radiation exposure, with the aim of informing the regulation of exposure limits. A 2017 published paper has already reported a significant effect of inhaled plutonium and uranium on lung cancer rates.

DARS-NIC-147757-8SVGP.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, death, cancer registration, demographic, prescribing and diabetes audit data on UK participants in the REVEAL trial of the cholesterol-modifying drug anacetrapib. It is extending follow-up for at least 15 years to study long-term effects on cardiovascular events, deaths, cancers and other serious adverse events. The aim is to improve understanding of treatments for vascular disease. The main trial has already shown a 9% reduction in major coronary events.

DARS-NIC-147774-MZT95.summary: The University of Manchester is using cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its study of children with rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis, who take biologic therapies. It will combine this with study data to check whether these drugs raise the long-term risk of cancer or early death. The aim is to help choose the best treatments in future. Study data has already been cited in a 2015 NHS England commissioning policy, which led to more consistent prescribing.

DARS-NIC-147776-69CX7.summary: The University of Manchester is keeping mortality and cohort tracking records (from the Medical Research Information Service) for adults with myositis who took part in the UKMYONET study and agreed to data linkage. The research looks at which cancers these people develop, why, and their causes of death. It aims to support evidence-based cancer screening recommendations for earlier detection. Published papers and conference abstracts have already informed the 2023 international cancer screening guideline.

DARS-NIC-147782-0D7TX.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admission records and mortality and status information from NHS England for 1,759 surviving participants in the SHARP trial, a large study of people with chronic kidney disease. It will analyse this data to see the longer-term effects of a cholesterol-lowering combination tablet (simvastatin plus ezetimibe). The aim is to clarify long-term effects, which could inform kidney treatment guidelines and clinical care.

DARS-NIC-147783-6T2MW.summary: The University of Nottingham, an academic organisation, holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events, flagging status and cohort membership for the Gedling Lung Health Study. The agreement allows secure retention only, with no other processing, while a later extension is prepared. The cohort studies how diet and other factors affect lung disease, cancer and survival. Reported benefits include at least 10 peer-reviewed papers, student dissertations and 3 local dietary intervention trials.

DARS-NIC-147788-X0G5L.summary: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and death and cause of death information for people with stage 3 chronic kidney disease who were recruited from GP surgeries. It is studying their survival, cardiovascular events and acute kidney injury, aiming to inform national guidance on managing the condition in primary care. The study has already produced peer-reviewed papers, including a five-year outcomes paper in PLOS Medicine in 2016.

DARS-NIC-147793-R05H3.summary: University College London (UCL) is using personal demographics and Scottish NHS registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the INFANT study. The study tests whether intelligent decision-support software can help staff interpret heart rate monitoring (cardiotocograph, or CTG) during labour and improve how labour is managed. It also looks at whether using the software affects the longer-term neurodevelopment of children born to women in the study.

DARS-NIC-147794-JDPT1.summary: Public Health England is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and personal demographics records. The data relates to patients admitted to Addenbrooke's Hospital between 2005 and 2007, some with Clostridium difficile infection and some without. The aim is a survival analysis to determine whether C. difficile infection is associated with excess deaths from all causes.

DARS-NIC-147797-45YHZ.summary: The University of Birmingham is using NHS mortality and cancer registration data (from the Medical Research Information Service, MRIS), including cause of death and demographic records. It is building a database of about 170,000 to 200,000 people in England and Wales who were diagnosed with cancer aged 15 to 39 between 1971 and 2006 and survived at least five years. The database will be used to study risks of specific causes of death, later cancers and other health conditions, and to assess evidence for cure. It aims to identify groups of survivors at much higher risk of poor health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-147805-HDHWM.summary: University of Warwick holds pseudonymised NHS England mortality and cohort records for 75,143 people who worked in the UK electricity supply industry between 1973 and 1982. It uses them to monitor long-term health among these workers, including any effects of exposure to extremely low frequency electric and magnetic fields. The aim is to inform bodies such as the Health and Safety Executive in setting exposure levels. Study findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals, including papers in 2019 and 2022.

DARS-NIC-147806-M11MB.summary: The University of Bristol is using mortality records and related personal and registration data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) to evaluate the Integrated Drug Treatment System in English prisons. The study compares deaths, engagement with community drug services and re-offending between 10,000 people released from prison on opiate substitution treatment and 10,000 released after detoxification. It aims to show how effective increased use of opiate substitution treatment is at reducing overdose deaths and disengagement from services after release.

DARS-NIC-147809-M6YZK.summary: The University of Birmingham is using personal demographics data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the ASTRAL trial. The trial looks at whether opening narrowed kidney arteries with balloon angioplasty or stents can safely prevent worsening kidney failure in people with atherosclerotic renovascular disease. The text does not state a specific intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-147809-X5N8G.summary: Manchester City Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, and support work such as suicide prevention, with only aggregated figures published. The intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include use of the data in the Manchester Reducing Infant Mortality Strategy and the Manchester Suicide Prevention Plan.

DARS-NIC-147811-YTH88.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic organisation, holds mortality data from NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, including cause of death and cohort event notifications. The data was originally supplied for the Norfolk Arthritis Register, a long-term community study of inflammatory arthritis. This agreement only allows the data to be stored securely for an interim period, with no other use and no new outputs.

DARS-NIC-147814-86GS4.summary: The University of Bristol uses identifiable NHS England Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events and current status for men in the Speedwell heart disease study. It uses them to follow the men's health and deaths over time and study the causes of heart disease and other chronic illnesses. The aim is to improve understanding of risk factors and prevention. A published risk prediction algorithm, SCORE2, has already come from related collaborative work.

DARS-NIC-147815-X5CHM.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant, a special health authority of the NHS, holds mortality data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), covering cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and members and postings. The agreement only lets it keep this data securely for an interim period, with no other use, while it prepares a new application. The original study used the data to check that dates and causes of death on the UK Transplant Registry are accurate, to support organ allocation.

DARS-NIC-147827-NC2TC.summary: Imperial College London is using NHS England mortality records (the Medical Research Information Service) and National Disease Registration Service cancer registrations, linked to hospital colonoscopy data. It is studying how often patients with low-, intermediate- and high-risk bowel adenomas need follow-up colonoscopies, to show who can safely avoid surveillance. The results contributed evidence to the 2020 UK surveillance guidelines and were published in journals including Gut.

DARS-NIC-147829-5K4QP.summary: The University of Cambridge, an academic body, uses death records, demographic data and mortality-related reports for people in the long-running Cognitive Function and Ageing Study (CFAS) and the ALPHA study of older people. They use it to confirm dates and causes of death so they can estimate survival and life expectancy in people with cognitive impairment. This supports dementia planning. Published findings on dementia prevalence and incidence are already used by NHS England for GP dementia targets.

DARS-NIC-147834-LHQ2R.summary: Nuvia Ltd, a commercial company, uses mortality and cohort records from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the long-running MR110 study of UK Atomic Energy Authority employees. The study examines deaths and cancer in the workforce to understand the health effects of low-dose occupational radiation exposure, helping inform exposure limits in regulations. A 2017 paper from the study reported a significant effect of inhaled plutonium and uranium on lung cancer rates.

DARS-NIC-147837-RJMRN.summary: The University of Bristol uses mortality and cancer records, linked to school growth records, questionnaires and blood samples, for a study of former Christ's Hospital School pupils born between 1927 and 1956. It is testing whether growth and puberty timing are linked to later conditions such as cancer and heart disease. The aim is to improve understanding of how childhood development affects chronic disease risk. Reported findings include that earlier puberty is associated with higher IGF-I levels, a hormone linked to cancer risk.

DARS-NIC-147839-Y4RRC.summary: The Health and Safety Executive uses NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging status, demographics and Scottish registration records. It uses them to maintain its Mesothelioma and Asbestosis Registers and to produce statistics on how common these diseases are. The aim is to inform workplace asbestos control policy and to model future mesothelioma deaths in Great Britain.

DARS-NIC-147841-1G36R.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, current status and demographic details, for patients with amyloidosis. It aims to establish cause of death and prognosis, and to see how treatments affect survival. Being kept up to date on deaths also means staff can avoid distressing relatives by chasing follow-up for patients who have died.

DARS-NIC-147843-8NKTW.summary: City St George's, University of London is using cancer registration, death record, demographic and flagging data about people who joined a screening trial between 1997 and 2006. The study tests whether screening for H. pylori infection and treating it reduces the later risk of stomach cancer. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether population screening would prevent stomach cancers.

DARS-NIC-147847-P6MMR.summary: King's College London's Centre for Military Health Research is using cancer registration, death registration, demographic and military cohort tracking data on UK Armed Forces personnel who served in Bosnia between 1992 and 1996. It is studying whether their rates of cancer and death are higher than expected. The main intended benefit is evidence that could either reassure veterans or lead to earlier diagnosis and better protection from harmful exposures.

DARS-NIC-147852-RV70L.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using cancer registration, death registration and MRIS (Medical Research Information Service) cohort tracking data. It is studying whether radiation from CT scans and heart procedures in childhood affects later cancer risk. The aim is to inform guidance on safer scanning of children. Published results have already led some clinical groups to change practice, and most children's hospitals now have dedicated paediatric CT protocols.

DARS-NIC-147858-KGYSS.summary: Saving Faces - The Facial Surgery Research Foundation, a charity, is using identifiable NHS England death registration, cancer and demographic data for 609 consenting patients in its SEND trial. The research tests whether removing neck lymph glands as a precaution (elective neck dissection) improves survival and cancer control in early mouth cancer. It aims to help patients and clinicians choose treatments using high-quality evidence. A published paper has already been cited in international guidelines and by other researchers, and has been linked to a change in surgical practice.

DARS-NIC-147860-0RSHN.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses civil registration death records, demographic details and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) mortality reports for about 19,000 members of the Millennium Cohort Study. It uses them to update contact details, avoid contacting people who have died or emigrated, and study causes of death, with sub-licensed access for wider research. Published MCS research has shown, for example, how breastfeeding and smoking in pregnancy relate to children's health, and has reported rates of teenage depression and obesity.

DARS-NIC-147863-CCGZN.summary: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust uses death registration, demographic and cause-of-death data to follow up participants in the Diabetes Alliance for Research in England (DARE) study in the Exeter region. The data helps researchers study how diabetes develops and leads to complications, including mortality. It also keeps participant records accurate so the Trust does not contact families of people who have died. So far, DARE data helped develop a urine test for insulin production, and mortality data fed a published study on arm blood pressure differences.

DARS-NIC-147867-D8128.summary: The University of Aberdeen is using cancer registration, death and demographic data to continue following women in the Royal College of General Practitioners' Oral Contraception Study, which began in 1968. The aim is to understand the long-term health effects of oral contraceptives, including on mortality and cancer, so the public can be given informed advice on their safety. The study has produced over 100 publications and has informed national and international clinical guidelines on prescribing combined oral contraceptives.

DARS-NIC-147875-00SJY.summary: The Institute of Child Health is holding mortality and cancer data, supplied through the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, about around 1,800 people treated with pituitary-derived growth hormone between 1959 and 1985. The agreement covers secure retention only, while a longer-term application is prepared. The wider study tracks deaths and illness in this group to monitor the risk of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) and to support public health advice. Reported results include showing that the CJD incubation period exceeds 37 years.

DARS-NIC-147876-YSQFX.summary: Public Health England is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and demographic records, for a register of healthcare and laboratory workers who have reported occupational exposure to CJD and other transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs). The register will standardise reporting, hold the information in a central database and allow long-term follow-up to monitor the risk of CJD in these workers. It is intended to help develop guidance for healthcare and laboratory workers.

DARS-NIC-147877-QXH0L.summary: West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic records. It is using them for a long-term observational study of how patients with early rheumatoid arthritis are treated and how they fare across the UK. The study aims to build a database that could contribute to good clinical practice, guidelines and clinical governance, and help design further studies.

DARS-NIC-147884-R7CBN.summary: The University of York is using linked hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records to study the long-term health of people diagnosed with cancer as children, comparing them with people of the same age and sex who were not. It aims to examine hospital activity, reasons for admission and survival, to inform future healthcare planning. The study has already published papers on health outcomes of childhood leukaemia survivors and on the follow-up study's design.

DARS-NIC-147885-0TV66.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable hospital, mental health, cancer registration and death records to follow up people who took part in the HPS2-THRIVE cholesterol trial. It aims to study the long-term effects of lowering LDL cholesterol on health, including dementia, so patients and guideline bodies can better judge medicines. Reported results include the trial's findings that niacin/laropiprant brought no significant reduction in major vascular events, and its withdrawal from the European market.

DARS-NIC-147887-RJFZH.summary: Cardiff University School of Medicine holds pseudonymised death records, obtained through the Medical Research Information Service, for about 200 people in the SCOPE 1 oesophageal cancer trial. It keeps them so the trial analysis can be recreated and audited if needed. The trial tested adding cetuximab (Erbitux) to chemoradiotherapy. Findings from the trial have been published in journal papers, and it stopped recruiting in 2012 after cetuximab seemed unlikely to improve outcomes, so funds were reallocated.

DARS-NIC-147901-2XMLG.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust is using cancer registration, death and demographic records, plus cohort tracking reports, for the Head and Neck 5000 study, which follows 5,511 people diagnosed with head and neck cancer. The data support a 10-year follow-up, comparing outcomes and identifying factors that predict survival and long-term side effects. The aim is to improve outcomes and care for patients. The study has published peer-reviewed papers and contributed to the largest genetic study of head and neck cancer risk to date.

DARS-NIC-147907-MLK7R.summary: Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital records of people who attended the Royal Derby Hospital Emergency Department after self-harm, linked with death registration and cause of death data. It uses them to monitor self-harm and to identify risk factors for early death, including suicide, so that care and suicide prevention strategies rest on better evidence. The register reports that the findings supported the commissioning of a 24/7 Liaison Psychiatry service at the hospital and a liaison team for under 18s.

DARS-NIC-147908-CPCPG.summary: The University of Leeds holds mortality and cohort tracking reports for people in the CE-MARC study, which tested cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) scans for suspected coronary heart disease. This agreement lets the university keep data already received while it prepares a further application. The study's long-term follow-up aims to show whether CMR predicts later heart problems better than SPECT. Reported results include papers in the Lancet and Annals of Internal Medicine, and the study is said to be changing how suspected angina is investigated.

DARS-NIC-147910-HHGGZ.summary: University of Oxford is using cancer registration, death registration and demographic data, which is identifiable at first, for about 7,000 women treated for subfertility in Oxfordshire and West Berkshire between 1970 and 1990. The research looks at their long-term cancer and death risks, and at how treatments and pregnancies relate to these. It also looks at twinning, sex ratio and birthweight in the babies born. The main intended benefit is better evidence on the long-term effects of fertility treatments, some still in use today.

DARS-NIC-147912-5CDTL.summary: Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic information, for a randomised trial of people with Barrett's Oesophagus. The trial tests whether offering an endoscopy every two years improves overall survival compared with endoscopy only when symptoms arise. Participants are followed for 10 years. The trial aims to inform future NHS and international surveillance policy.

DARS-NIC-147916-DPQ3Q.summary: The University of Manchester is using death registration and demographic data, including mortality records, linked to hospital self-harm records. It uses them to study the risk of suicide and early death after self-harm and to identify groups at higher risk. The aim is to inform suicide prevention strategies and the allocation of healthcare resources. Its findings have already been reported as informing NICE self-harm guidelines and national suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-147922-T7W2F.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses identifiable death registration and demographic data on about 18,500 members of the National Child Development Study 1958 cohort. It uses the data to update participant records, study mortality outcomes and support further research. The aim is to inform health policy and healthy ageing. Death notifications have already stopped the study contacting relatives of people who had died, and research has fed into government briefing papers.

DARS-NIC-147923-P5DTX.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds cancer registration, death record, demographic and NHS-linked tracking data for a national study of cancer in twins. This agreement only allows the data to be stored securely until updated analyses in 2028. The aim is to give patients, families and clinicians better information about cancer risks. Published papers from the study have already added to scientific knowledge about the causes of some cancers.

DARS-NIC-147927-8K193.summary: The University of Birmingham is using hospital, cancer registration, death and related records for people with Parkinson's disease who took part in the PD MED trial. It is using them to complete a 20-year analysis of which classes of Parkinson's medicine work best and are most cost-effective, including effects on care home admission and survival. The aim is to guide which medicines clinicians use. Earlier trial results were published in the Lancet and led to a 2017 NICE guideline update on treating early Parkinson's.

DARS-NIC-147931-DT25Y.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS England data on cancer registrations, hospital admissions, deaths, cancer treatments and demographics for 4,553,604 women in the AgeX trial. It is using the data to assess the benefits and harms of extra breast screening invitations at ages 47-49 and 71-73. The findings are intended to inform UK breast screening policy through the UK National Screening Committee.

DARS-NIC-147932-B9FG1.summary: The University of Birmingham is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer and current status records, for a study of rubber factory employees. It aims to describe deaths and cancer among recent entrants to the UK rubber industry. It will also check whether measures to reduce dust and fume exposure have removed the excess of lung and stomach cancer seen in recent years.

DARS-NIC-147936-1L3FD.summary: University College London (UCL) holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on deaths, cancer events and patient status for the HiLo thyroid cancer trial. This agreement lets UCL keep the data securely, with no other use, while it prepares a further application. The trial compared a low and a standard dose of radioiodine, and a later follow-up paper is planned. The trial's published results led to the low dose becoming standard care and being recommended in the 2014 British Thyroid Association guidelines.

DARS-NIC-147936-X6M4N.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, for the former NHS Lincolnshire East CCG, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data about hospital and other care activity, identifiable by NHS number, in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, so that the CCG pays only for activity that is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-147940-WVXJF.summary: The University of Oxford holds identifiable NHS England data on deaths, cancer registrations and demographics for 1,405,340 women born in England or Wales between 1945 and 1948. It is used for a study of whether the age at which women are first invited for a routine breast screening mammogram affects their risk of dying from breast cancer. The findings are expected to inform national breast screening policy.

DARS-NIC-147941-XX4JP.summary: The University of Manchester uses linked cancer registrations, death records and hospital admissions data for the British Association of Dermatologists' register of people with psoriasis taking biologic treatments. It uses them to track long-term safety, such as cancer, serious infections and death. The aim is to help clinicians and patients make better-informed treatment decisions. Published papers have already reported on drug survival, serious infection risk, cardiovascular events and skin cancer risk.

DARS-NIC-147942-N8J6Y.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB is using Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for commissioners. Liaison Financial Services will use it to check invoices and review past payments for Continuing Healthcare, looking for overpayments and working with providers to recover the money. The main intended benefit is finding and recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping control of the budget.

DARS-NIC-147944-KJQBS.summary: Imperial College London is using NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, demographic and cohort tracking reports, for the European Community Respiratory Health Survey III, a long-running study of about 10,000 adults. The data will help trace participants, send them questionnaires, work out accurate response rates and describe deaths in the cohort. The study aims to show how respiratory symptoms, allergy and lung function change as adults age.

DARS-NIC-147947-CGW0Y.summary: The Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and membership reports. The agreement allows the Trust only to keep this data securely for an interim period while it prepares a later application to extend it. The original study aimed to identify risk factors for heart disease in people with rheumatoid arthritis. The data has already led to published papers, theses, changes to national and international guidelines, and patient education material.

DARS-NIC-147948-6MSGP.summary: University College London is keeping cancer and death registry records, including cancer type, diagnosis date and cause of death, for people who took part in the Lung-SEARCH lung cancer screening trial. The data will support further analyses of the trial's results, which could inform a national lung cancer screening programme for people who smoke and have COPD. Trial findings have been published, including the main trial paper in the European Respiratory Journal.

DARS-NIC-147955-M8D2Q.summary: King's College London's TwinsUK research registry is using NHS hospital, cancer, death, emergency care and mental health records, linked to its long-running study of twins. The aim is to study how genes and environment affect health and disease over a lifetime, and to track outcomes more completely, including for people who find it hard to attend clinics. It is hoped this will improve disease prediction, diagnosis and prevention. Earlier linkage work identified clinical and genomic risk factors for cancers.

DARS-NIC-147957-4444C.summary: The University of Oxford uses hospital records of people who presented at Oxford's John Radcliffe Hospital after self-harm, linked to death registration and cause-of-death data. It uses them to study risk factors for death, including suicide, and how hospital care relates to it. The aim is to help design better services that reduce self-harm and early death. Its findings have already informed NICE guidelines and national suicide prevention strategies.

DARS-NIC-147970-M0H6Z.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, maternity and other health service data, containing clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the population across the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland partnership area. The main intended benefit is better-designed services and patient pathways, with improved access and quality.

DARS-NIC-147978-LZDFC.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission, accident and emergency, death registration and demographic data to follow people in the ERICA study of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It is examining how heart, muscle and inflammation markers relate to later hospital admissions and deaths. The aim is to identify biomarkers that help predict outcomes and support more personalised COPD treatments.

DARS-NIC-147982-J7KGV.summary: The University of Liverpool is using NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for the Liverpool Lung Project, a long-running lung cancer study. It aims to build risk models and biomarkers that identify people at high risk of lung cancer, so that diagnosis can happen earlier and screening can be better targeted. The reported benefits include the risk model being used to select people for lung cancer screening, and over 160 research publications.

DARS-NIC-147997-R8B9S.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital records covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. It is using them in a research project funded by the National Institute for Health Research, called UK-SAFE. The project looks at when, which and how patients present for revision surgery after joint replacement. The aim is to give evidence-based recommendations on how and when follow-up care should happen, reducing unnecessary appointments and tests.

DARS-NIC-148022-1MQBH.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne holds mortality and cancer registration data for the Newcastle Heart Project, a study of heart disease, diabetes and risk factors in White and South Asian adults in Newcastle. The agreement only allows the data to be kept for an interim period, with no other use. The aim is to update earlier analysis of how risk factors relate to mortality in the two groups, to help inform targeted health interventions. Earlier work has been published in 2017 in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health.

DARS-NIC-148023-KVWYZ.summary: Royal Brompton Hospital is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, event notification, current status and demographic records, for a pilot trial in patients treated with primary PCI after a ST elevation heart attack. It is building a registry of these patients and comparing complete revascularisation with treating only the infarct-related artery in those who also have multi-vessel disease. It will track deaths and major cardiovascular events for up to 12 months.

DARS-NIC-148024-P8GSC.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds mortality data on UK Gulf War veterans from 1990-1991, covering cause of death, postings and status reports. Under this agreement it can only keep the data securely for an interim period, while it prepares a further application. The original study looked at whether veterans' death rates, including suicide, were higher than the UK population's. Earlier analysis produced annual National Statistics and found no excess in deaths among the Gulf cohort.

DARS-NIC-148030-Q5N4D.summary: The UK Haemophilia Centre Doctors' Organisation, a society, uses identifiable death registration and cause-of-death data for people with haemophilia and other inherited bleeding disorders. It uses the data to keep the National Haemophilia Database up to date and to study causes of death and life expectancy. The aim is to show which treatments are most beneficial and cost effective. Its annual reports to NHS England, Scotland and Wales have supported national healthcare planning, and its findings helped justify prophylactic therapy.

DARS-NIC-148034-SCKLL.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) death and flagging reports linked to records held by the UK Barrett's Oesophagus Registry. It aims to establish all causes of death among people with Barrett's oesophagus, a change in the cells lining the lower oesophagus. The hoped-for benefit is better management of patients and prevention of progression to cancer. A 2012 paper in Endoscopy has already been published and used in British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148044-RGS7W.summary: The University of Oxford, working with University College London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, uses pseudonymised cancer registration, death and demographic data on 19,019 London civil servants in the Whitehall Study. They are studying how lifestyle, social circumstances and cardiovascular risk factors relate to cancer and causes of death in old age. Reported benefits include results published in peer-reviewed journals and findings that have guided public health policy and clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148056-T6T5Z.summary: Imperial College London is using linked NHS England data, including hospital, mental health, cancer, death, COVID-19 test and vaccination records, to follow the health of police force members in the Airwave Health Monitoring Study. It aims to examine whether use of the TETRA police radio system, and other lifestyle and workplace factors, affect their risk of cancer and other conditions. The main intended benefit is better evidence for health policy and for working conditions in police forces. The study has already supported over 80 publications.

DARS-NIC-148063-6YT63.summary: The University of Birmingham is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status, membership and postings, and personal demographics reports. It is using this data to study and improve the acute care of people with TIA (transient ischaemic attack) and stroke in Birmingham. The work aims to identify and reduce barriers to timely, effective treatment, so that patients reach specialist care sooner and care improves overall.

DARS-NIC-148069-ZB4GM.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital records, cancer registrations, death records and mental health data on people who took part in the Heart Protection Study, a large trial of simvastatin and antioxidant vitamins. It will continue long-term follow-up of these participants to assess the lasting effects of lowering LDL cholesterol on major health outcomes. The intended benefit is better evidence to guide decisions about statin treatment. The trial's results have already influenced NICE guidelines and changed clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-148071-QHNM8.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using cancer registration, death registration and demographic data. It is extending follow-up of the UK Flexible Sigmoidoscopy Screening Trial to test whether a single bowel screening test at age 55–64 keeps reducing bowel cancer cases and deaths into older age. The aim is to inform future screening policy. Findings have already been published in The Lancet in 2010, 2017 and 2024, and supported flexible sigmoidoscopy's inclusion in the English Bowel Cancer Screening Programme.

DARS-NIC-148077-M9HG5.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging current status, members and postings, and Personal Demographics Service records. It is using them to evaluate the clinical outcomes of patients who had percutaneous coronary intervention to the left main coronary artery at the Yorkshire Heart Centre.

DARS-NIC-148096-PT589.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and hospital records for 113,766 women in the Generations Study. It is studying genetic and environmental risk factors for cancer, especially breast cancer, and for death, with the aim of supporting prevention and risk prediction. The study has produced over 190 peer-reviewed publications, including six in 2024, and has contributed to improved breast cancer risk models.

DARS-NIC-148100-6RFK9.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for members of the 1946 National Survey of Health and Development, a long-running British birth cohort study. It links these to the study's own data to understand how factors across life affect ageing, including heart health, physical and cognitive capability. The aim is to inform health and social care policy. Published papers include one showing that early childhood chest infections were linked to premature adult death from respiratory disease.

DARS-NIC-148101-R7RSL.summary: University College London (UCL) holds mortality, cancer registration and demographic data for the British Women's Heart & Health Study, which follows women aged over 60 in England, Scotland and Wales. This agreement only allows UCL to keep the data securely for an interim period, with no new processing. The study aims to understand risk factors for heart disease and stroke. Its publications have contributed to fifteen clinical care and public health guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148106-PP9LS.summary: The University of Oxford is using death and cohort follow-up records for 24 people with Apert syndrome who took part in an earlier study. It will reanalyse them to improve the estimates of mortality in a manuscript that has been waiting to be published, and keep the data securely so the published findings can be checked. The main intended benefit is better knowledge of long-term outlook and causes of death in adults with Apert syndrome.

DARS-NIC-148118-VCXW9.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using identifiable NHS England death registration and cohort tracking data about men in the UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study, who have prostate cancer or a family history of it. It uses the data to study survival and to find genetic changes linked to prostate cancer risk. The aim is to help screen relatives and develop new treatments. So far, the data has helped build a genetic risk model that gives personalised predicted prostate cancer risks.

DARS-NIC-148119-WLQ4M.summary: Public Health England is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notifications, flagging status and demographic details. The aim is to follow people identified by the CJD Incidents Panel as being at increased risk of CJD, and to find any CJD-related deaths among them. The work is intended to improve assessment of the risks these individuals face and to inform and evaluate public health measures.

DARS-NIC-148128-815J1.summary: University College London uses mortality and cancer registration reports to follow up children born in England and Wales to women living with HIV. It is keeping previously supplied data for an interim period while it prepares a further application. The long-term surveillance monitors cancer and survival in children exposed to HIV and antiretroviral drugs before birth. So far, flagging methods have been established and 100 death and cancer notifications received for 8,877 children.

DARS-NIC-148129-FK1JJ.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with the University of Birmingham, is using cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on a cohort of families of people with ataxia telangiectasia. It is following them up to estimate cancer risks for people who carry an ATM gene mutation, so that their care can be better managed. A 2005 paper from earlier data led to breast screening starting at age 40 rather than 50 for obligate carriers.

DARS-NIC-148130-46N08.summary: The University of Oxford holds NHS England mortality follow-up records (cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and members and postings reports) for UK patients in the ISIS-2 heart attack trial. The agreement covers only secure storage and back-up, so the trial results can be checked or recreated if challenged. Published results showed that streptokinase and aspirin cut deaths, and a survey reported that these findings changed clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-148144-69CQ0.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using civil registration death records (age and cause of death) linked to the Wynn Database, a collection of metabolic health records from thousands of volunteers and clinic patients. It will study how metabolic risk factors relate to survival time and cause of death, particularly for diabetes, heart disease and cancer. The main hoped-for benefit is a better understanding of chronic disease, which could inform prevention. The database has previously contributed to knowledge of diabetes and cardiovascular risk.

DARS-NIC-148150-D5TDH.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne holds pseudonymised mortality and flagging records for participants in the Newcastle Heart Project, a study of White and South Asian residents of Newcastle. It uses them to study how cardiovascular and diabetes risk factors relate to death rates in the two groups, including the "healthy migrant effect". The aim is to inform targeted interventions. A 2017 paper in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health has already been published.

DARS-NIC-148155-K7P19.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research holds NHS mortality and cancer flagging reports (cause of death and current status) for people treated with growth hormone as children. The agreement only allows the data to be kept securely while the study moves to the University of Manchester, and in case questions arise about a paper under review. The study looks at long-term cancer and death risks after treatment, to reassure patients and the public about its safety.

DARS-NIC-148161-XXPS5.summary: The UK Health Security Agency uses identifiable NHS England demographic data and cancer registration data for about 43,690 servicemen, including those who attended UK atmospheric nuclear weapons tests between 1952 and 1967 and a control group. It uses them in a long-term study of whether test participants have had higher rates of cancer or other fatal diseases than controls and the general population. The study aims to give veterans evidence about their health. Four analyses have been published in scientific journals, and the Ministry of Defence uses the findings when considering veterans' concerns, such as War pensions.

DARS-NIC-148164-9PRJ0.summary: The University of Westminster, an academic organisation, is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status flagging, demographics and Scottish NHS registration data. It is studying whether changes in biochemicals (oligosaccharides) on breast cancer cells relate to how aggressive the cancer is, measured by the development of secondary cancers. It also aims to assess whether patients who survive for long periods have natural immunity to these biochemicals.

DARS-NIC-148175-1MJ42.summary: The University of Bristol uses mortality, cancer registration and demographic data from the Medical Research Council's Boyd Orr cohort follow-up, which tracks 4,999 children surveyed in 1937–1939. It uses the data to study how early-life factors, such as childhood diet and family circumstances, affect adult heart disease, cancer and death. The aim is to provide evidence for health guidelines and policy. Research from the cohort has produced over 50 peer-reviewed publications and has informed national and international guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148194-QYCWF.summary: Barts and the London School of Medicine and Dentistry, an academic organisation, is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data covering cause of death, current status flagging and personal demographics. It is using this data to work out the current life expectancy of babies born in England and Wales with trisomy 13 or trisomy 18, a chromosomal condition.

DARS-NIC-148196-4WQRP.summary: The University of Southampton is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for historical cohorts of workers exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. It aims to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals.

DARS-NIC-148202-4LQ9V.summary: Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic data. The study looks at life expectancy and leading causes of death in people with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) in the UK, and extends earlier UK research. It also examines trends over time and compares UK and USA results. The intended benefit is better preventative and therapeutic care, and better planning for life-long care.

DARS-NIC-148204-7B1XT.summary: University of Oxford's Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group uses identifiable cancer registration, death registration and related mortality tracking data on women in early breast cancer trials. It combines long-term follow-up from many randomised trials to assess the benefits and risks of breast cancer treatments, so clinicians, patients and policy makers can make better-informed decisions. Its published analyses have already changed practice, including wider use of aromatase inhibitors and bisphosphonates, and have been cited in guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148215-CQWFM.summary: The University of Nottingham is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data covering cause of death, cohort event notifications, current status flagging, members and postings, and personal demographics. It is studying whether thrombophilia, an increased tendency of the blood to clot, raises the risk of developing idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). It also asks whether thrombophilia changes the effect of environmental risk factors for IPF and whether it worsens prognosis for people with IPF.

DARS-NIC-148219-ZHB4Z.summary: The UK Health Security Agency uses identifiable demographic data and cancer registration data on past and present UK radiation workers in the National Registry for Radiation Workers study. It combines them with workers' radiation dose records to investigate how long-term occupational radiation exposure affects health, including cancer and death rates. The aim is to give public health planners more precise evidence on radiation risks. Results from earlier analyses have been published in peer-reviewed journals and found risk estimates consistent with those used by international bodies.

DARS-NIC-148227-4H7DT.summary: The University of Bristol is using NHS Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, current status and demographic details, to trace 951 people. They were born to women enrolled in a dietary supplementation trial in South Wales between 1972 and 1974. The project will invite them to a follow-up clinical examination and questionnaire. It aims to understand how factors in pregnancy, infancy and early childhood relate to insulin resistance syndrome in early adulthood.

DARS-NIC-148232-CPHLL.summary: The National CJD Surveillance Unit, part of the University of Edinburgh, is using death records and cause-of-death data for blood donors and recipients linked to CJD and variant CJD (vCJD) cases in England and Wales. It uses them to check whether CJD or vCJD can pass on through blood transfusion, with the aim of informing policy on risk. The project has already identified four instances of probable transfusion-transmitted vCJD, and its findings have informed blood safety precautions.

DARS-NIC-148239-M8RTP.summary: The University of Oxford holds mortality and event-notification data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) and NHS Digital, linked to a register of children in four counties with cerebral palsy, vision loss or hearing loss. The register was used to monitor how common these conditions are, support research and help plan services. The data is now kept as a unique resource for possible future survival analysis. Over 90 peer-reviewed papers were published, and annual prevalence reports were given to clinicians and service planners.

DARS-NIC-148247-CH0Z6.summary: The University of Manchester is using cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its long-running study of newer biologic therapies for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). It will link the data to existing study records to check whether these drugs raise the risk of cancer or early death compared with similar patients not taking them. The aim is to give a complete picture of long-term safety. The study's register was named as a condition for NHS England funding of rituximab in 2013 and for NICE guidance on belimumab in 2016.

DARS-NIC-148267-W26RZ.summary: The University of Oxford is using cause of death and cancer notification records, which include identifiable details, for around 10,626 people in the Oxford Vegetarian Study. It is examining how vegetarian and non-vegetarian diets affect long-term cancer risk and death rates, to inform dietary guidance. The study's evidence has already been used in UK Government Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition reports on saturated fat and dietary fibre.

DARS-NIC-148269-0WSH2.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust is using NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death reports, flagging status and demographic details, for the London Life Sciences Population (LOLIPOP) Study. The study follows about 30,000 Indian Asian and European white adults in West London to identify heart and circulatory events and deaths over 20 or more years. It aims to identify the genetic and environmental factors behind the higher cardiovascular disease risk among UK Indian Asians.

DARS-NIC-148284-T2GPT.summary: The University of Southampton uses hospital admission records, death registration records and demographic data for people in the Hertfordshire Cohort Study, which follows men and women born in Hertfordshire between 1911 and 1939. It uses them to study how factors across a person's life affect hospital admission, death and chronic diseases of ageing. The aim is to build evidence on risk factors that could later inform ways to reduce hospital admissions among older people. Earlier work from the study has been published widely and cited in national and international health policy.

DARS-NIC-148286-3RWRG.summary: University of Birmingham is using identifiable cancer registration, death registration, demographic and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data on the 8,861 women who joined the aTTom breast cancer trial. It is following them over the long term to see whether taking tamoxifen for 10 years rather than 5 improves survival and what side effects it causes. The aim is to help clinicians give individualised advice on extended treatment. Results have already appeared in published papers, and USA and European guidelines now recommend the Breast Cancer Index test.

DARS-NIC-148313-G56YY.summary: The University of Birmingham's Centre for Childhood Cancer Survivor Studies is using linked health records, including cancer registrations, deaths and hospital data, for people who survived cancer diagnosed in childhood, teenage or young adult years. It is monitoring their risks of serious health problems and healthcare costs compared with the general population. The aim is to identify higher-risk survivors so follow-up care can match need. Its earlier published findings were used as key evidence in NHS England's review of its service specifications.

DARS-NIC-148321-ZPHJ3.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable civil registration of death records (date and cause of death) for patients treated for ocular melanoma and other eye tumours. It is using them for a service evaluation and audit of survival, vision and eye retention after treatments such as proton beam radiotherapy. The main hoped-for benefit is better information on prognosis and treatment choices, to improve patient counselling and care.

DARS-NIC-148322-TMFVQ.summary: The University of Oxford uses NHS England cancer registration, hospital admission, death and demographic records, linked to its EPIC-Oxford study of about 65,000 mainly vegetarian men and women. It uses them to examine how diet affects the risk of cancer and other long-term diseases. The aim is to give reliable evidence to inform dietary advice. Findings have been published in journals and used by the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition in its reports.

DARS-NIC-148331-5F2FS.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School, an academic organisation, holds pseudonymised death, cancer registration and demographic records for about 22,000 men who attended a London BUPA medical centre between 1975 and 1982. It uses them to study risk factors for cancer and death, especially smoking-related risks. The data is kept so past analyses can be recreated and future research can continue. Reported results include over 30 published papers, a 2022 prostate cancer screening study, and work that led the MRC to fund a pilot trial on aortic stenosis.

DARS-NIC-148334-51PXR.summary: The University of Southampton is using identifiable NHS England data on a cohort of 2,888 breast cancer patients, including cancer registrations, hospital admissions and death records. It is used for long-term follow-up in the POSH study, which compares outcomes and recurrence in patients with and without BRCA1 or BRCA2 gene mutations. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed treatment decisions. Published findings have already contributed to changes in NICE testing guidance and in how often immediate bilateral mastectomy is recommended.

DARS-NIC-148336-V4SL1.summary: The University of Bristol is using cancer registration, death registration, demographic and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and cohort event data. The data will be linked to the Caerphilly Prospective Study, a long-running health cohort, to follow its participants until death and study the causes of chronic disease, including heart disease and dementia. Approved researchers may also use the linked data to help prevent disease. CaPS data has contributed to published work, including World Health Organization cardiovascular risk charts.

DARS-NIC-148341-TC6TD.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable hospital, cancer registration, death and mental health records for people who took part in the SEARCH trial of cholesterol and homocysteine lowering after heart attacks. It is following them up over the long term to study how lowering LDL cholesterol affects chronic conditions such as dementia. The aim is to help guideline bodies and patients judge the effects of medicines like statins. Published results have already influenced statin labelling, treatment guidelines and recommendations on folic acid.

DARS-NIC-148348-XTNPJ.summary: University College London (UCL) is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cohort event notification, current status and demographic records. It is used in a randomised trial of women with screen-detected ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). The trial compares surgical removal alone with surgery followed by radiotherapy and/or tamoxifen. It looks at how often invasive breast cancer later develops.

DARS-NIC-148353-G88Q7.summary: The University of Manchester, working with the British Society for Rheumatology, is using NHS England cancer registration, death and demographic data. It links them to the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register for Rheumatoid Arthritis to study whether newer rheumatoid arthritis drugs raise the risk of cancer or early death. Findings from the register have been used in NICE appraisals, clinical guidelines and patient information leaflets, and in published studies on biosimilar switching and JAK inhibitor use.

DARS-NIC-148364-RHMHS.summary: The Society for Endocrinology, working with the University of Sheffield, is using cancer registration, death registration, demographic and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on UK adults with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH). It will study causes of illness and death in these patients and how other conditions and treatments affect outcomes. The aim is to improve day-to-day management of CAH. Earlier results from the study have been published, and centres report improved follow-up and transition care.

DARS-NIC-148369-8PPWK.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, cancer registrations, deaths and demographics for around 11,940 participants of the Oxford Vascular Study in Oxfordshire. The study follows people over the long term after stroke, mini-stroke and heart events, to measure outcomes and costs and to improve prevention and treatment. Study findings have already informed national stroke strategy and clinical guidelines on treating TIA and minor stroke.

DARS-NIC-148376-YBRWP.summary: Addenbrooke's Hospital holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event and demographic details, for participants in a study of how arteries stiffen with age. This agreement only allows the hospital to keep the data securely for an interim period while it prepares a new application. The original study followed about 1,200 healthy volunteers and kidney disease patients to measure how quickly arterial stiffness changes.

DARS-NIC-148382-7KTF1.summary: The University of Southampton is using NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, which covers cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status flagging and demographic details. It is following up groups of workers who were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The aim is to describe patterns of death and cancer over time. The findings are intended to inform regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals in the UK and internationally.

DARS-NIC-148386-78PDC.summary: The University of Southampton is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for people in historical worker groups. These workers were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The aim is to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international risk assessment and management of these chemicals.

DARS-NIC-148399-BJ7GR.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds cause of death report data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for a study checking how deaths among UK Armed Forces personnel are coded. The study compares the Ministry's coding with national coding so that death rates can be compared fairly, and looks at how accurately suicides and related deaths are identified. This version of the agreement allows the data to be kept for an interim period only, with no other use. The main intended benefit is more accurate identification of suicides and related deaths.

DARS-NIC-148406-2YXPR.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust's Family Cancer Clinic uses death and cancer-notification records from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for patients with a family history of colorectal and other cancers. It uses them to keep clinic records accurate and to evaluate the outcomes of colonoscopic surveillance. The intended benefit is surveillance tailored to each person's genetic and family risk. Published studies have already changed surveillance ages and intervals and are cited in national and European guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148407-LRP3M.summary: University College London is using identifiable hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for 960 consenting participants in the Southall and Brent Revisited (SABRE) study. It is studying why heart disease, diabetes and physical and cognitive function in older age differ between ethnic groups and between sexes. The aim is to inform better prevention and treatment. Published papers have already used this data, and its findings on diabetes and obesity informed NICE's BMI thresholds.

DARS-NIC-148411-Q64H8.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable NHS England cancer registration, death registration and demographic data, plus Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports, for about 8,000 men in the British Regional Heart Study. The study follows disease outcomes to research prevention of cardiovascular disease, heart failure, dementia and disability in older age. So far, the study has published over 600 peer-reviewed papers, which have contributed to UK and international clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-148413-JDKYG.summary: The University of Southampton is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status flagging and personal demographics, for people in historical groups of workers. The workers were exposed to styrene, phenoxy herbicides and formaldehyde. The aim is to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform UK and international regulatory risk assessment of these chemicals, so workers are protected without unwarranted restrictions.

DARS-NIC-148417-FT2KY.summary: The University of Southampton is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer-related event notifications, current status and demographic records, for historical groups of workers exposed to formaldehyde, styrene and phenoxy herbicides. It aims to describe patterns of death and cancer over a longer follow-up period. The findings are intended to inform regulatory risk assessment and management of these chemicals in the UK and internationally, so workers are protected without unwarranted restrictions.

DARS-NIC-148425-R38F2.summary: The University of Birmingham holds NHS mortality and cancer-related records for people who agreed to join the National Register of Radiofrequency (RF) Workers. Under this agreement it may only store and back up the data for an interim period while it informs those people how their data is used. The data was originally used to study long-term health effects of workplace RF exposure, which could lead to new exposure limits.

DARS-NIC-148437-C9YSC.summary: The University of Leicester is using identifiable death registration, demographic and hospital admission records for men recruited to the United Kingdom Aneurysm Growth Study after abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) screening. It is following their health events and causes of death over the long term to understand what influences AAA progression and whether screening can improve wider health. The main intended benefit is better clinical management of men with small AAA. Data received earlier was used to avoid sending study materials to men who had died.

DARS-NIC-148465-PJQ4L.summary: The UK Health Security Agency uses cancer registration, death registration and mortality follow-up data on people in the national hepatitis C register, mostly people infected through blood transfusions. It uses them to study how hepatitis C infection and liver disease develop and to model future demand on health services. The aim is to inform efforts to eliminate hepatitis C by 2030. Its analyses have already fed into the Infected Blood Inquiry, compensation decisions and published annual England reports.

DARS-NIC-148468-KFJZ5.summary: The Ministry of Defence holds mortality data on UK Armed Forces personnel who deployed to the 1982 Falklands campaign. This agreement lets it keep that data for an interim period, with no other processing. The data was originally used to check claims of higher suicide rates among Falklands veterans by comparing death rates with other groups. Earlier data led to two Official Statistics, the last in 2014, which reported risks of dying lower than or the same as the UK general population for all causes, except transport accident deaths in 1989.

DARS-NIC-148471-FR43L.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using mortality and cohort tracking data (MRIS reports, including cause of death) for the Newcastle 85+ Study, which follows people from age 85 to 97 in the North-East of England. It aims to identify factors linked to healthy ageing, disability, frailty and use of health and social care, so that care for the very old can be planned better. The study has contributed evidence to government reviews and parliamentary inquiries, and over 90 articles have been published.

DARS-NIC-148484-PSL6Q.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine, an academic body, is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on causes of death, cohort events, flagging status and members and postings, previously supplied for the UK Breast Screening Age Trial. They are analysing how screening from age 40-41 affects breast cancer survival and mortality, by cancer type and grade, to explain why the benefit seems shorter-lived. The aim is to inform screening policy for women under 50. The trial has already published results showing reduced breast cancer mortality.

DARS-NIC-149576-G6M4B.summary: The University of Edinburgh is using hospital admission records linked to death registration records for the RESTART trial, which tests whether people who survived a brain haemorrhage should restart antiplatelet drugs. The data will help find trial outcomes missed by other follow-up and check how accurate each method is. This could show whether linked data alone could track outcomes in a larger future trial. Published trial results have already influenced guidelines in Canada, China and the USA.

DARS-NIC-149784-H9K6B.summary: The University of Oxford, an academic organisation, is using pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) linked with National Hip Fracture Database data. It is for a PhD project to build a better way of adjusting hip fracture outcomes for patients' existing health conditions, and to compare outcomes between the UK, US and Australia. The main intended benefit is fairer identification of hospitals with better or worse hip fracture outcomes.

DARS-NIC-150201-T3G7X.summary: London Borough of Tower Hamlets, a local authority, is using pseudonymised NHS hospital, ambulance, community, mental health and children's data, linked with council and GP data. It will use the data to understand health inequalities and service use across local communities, and to produce a one-off summary report. The stated aim is to inform local commissioning so the right services reach the right people in the right places.

DARS-NIC-150435-R7X1Q.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission and outpatient records, plus death registration data, to support an evaluation of stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) for patients with cancer. The data will be added to the information collected for NHS England's Commissioning through Evaluation programme, which is analysed by King's Technology Evaluation Centre. The aim is to assess whether SABR improves survival, side effects, quality of life and cost-effectiveness, and so informs future NHS commissioning.

DARS-NIC-150521-F2Q1V.summary: The University of Liverpool is using hospital accident and emergency attendance records (Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency) for people with epilepsy who took part in the SAFE pilot trial of seizure first aid training. The researchers will estimate the training's effect on emergency department use and compare the records with participants' own reports of their visits. The main intended benefit is better design of a possible larger future trial.
