DARS-NIC-150780-W6W3Z.summary: The University of Sheffield is using hospital admitted patient care and accident and emergency records to evaluate shared haemodialysis care, in which patients having dialysis at a centre learn to carry out some of their own treatment tasks. The study covers 12 dialysis centres in England and assesses the programme's effectiveness and costs to the NHS. It aims to show the benefits and savings so patients, clinicians and policy makers can decide whether to adopt it. A report to the funders found no significant quality of life benefit but potential cost savings.

DARS-NIC-150856-G6P5R.summary: The University of Warwick is using NHS hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and death registration data for 182 consenting participants in the PARAMEDIC2 trial. The trial tests how safe and effective adrenaline is for people who have a cardiac arrest outside hospital. The data give survival, hospital and intensive care stays, and costs. The main results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2018.

DARS-NIC-150908-B9F4C.summary: The London Borough of Lambeth uses hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for public health analysis, such as needs assessments, health strategies and the Director of Public Health's annual report, to understand local health and inequalities. Reported benefits include informing a suicide prevention plan, oral health services for young children and the serious youth violence strategy.

DARS-NIC-151212-B5Z3R.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust, through its National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (NICOR), holds linked hospital admission and death registration records for about 1,965 patients who had MitraClip mitral valve repair, left atrial appendage occlusion or patent foramen ovale closure. The data supported an NHS England evaluation of these procedures, and is now kept for archiving only. The intended benefit was better evidence for commissioning policy. A report on patent foramen ovale closure was published in July 2018.

DARS-NIC-152228-DL5MK.summary: University College London holds mortality data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the Clinical Cohorts in Coronary Disease Collaboration (4C), a study of 3,345 patients investigated for new-onset chest pain. The agreement only lets UCL keep the data for an interim period, with no other processing. The original study aimed to improve understanding of heart disease outcomes and to inform policy on stable coronary disease. The benefits section reports no benefits from earlier outputs.

DARS-NIC-15226-X7Z9R.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies is using demographic data and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) reports to trace members of the Next Steps cohort, who were born in 1989/90. The data helps it find addresses so it can invite people to its surveys and keep the study sample representative. The age 32 survey data is now available to researchers through the UK Data Service.

DARS-NIC-152414-W3P6Q.summary: The University of Bristol uses linked NHS England health records, including hospital, mental health, maternity, medicines and death data, for the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), which follows families recruited in pregnancy. The data are added to a research database so approved researchers can study health and wellbeing across generations. The aim is to improve understanding of health and care needs. Reported results include published papers and an earlier ALSPAC study that contributed to UK policy change on infant sleep positioning.

DARS-NIC-15283-X7W4K.summary: North Northamptonshire Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records from NHS England (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reports using the data for a cancer deep dive, self-harm and substance misuse analyses, and work for Local Area Partnerships.

DARS-NIC-15293-R6V2H.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial company, uses NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health data. It uses the data to produce benchmarking, service analysis and disease burden reports, and to run its Vantage dashboard, which shows aggregate figures with small numbers suppressed. The aim is to give health organisations evidence on regional differences in access to treatment. Its analysis has already featured in a published journal paper on aortic valve replacement and in a regulatory submission.

DARS-NIC-15335-H0D1F.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England uses hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and A&E) and linked death registration data to study how care and outcomes differ across NHS providers, regions and over time. The work covers national clinical audits and academic research, aiming to help the NHS benchmark services and improve patient outcomes. Reported results include national audit reports used in Care Quality Commission inspections, and peer-reviewed papers on vascular surgery outcomes.

DARS-NIC-15336-S8W9K.summary: NHS England uses pseudonymised, record-level Diagnostic Imaging Data Set records, covering NHS imaging tests such as X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI, from 2012 onwards. It uses them to produce official statistics, answer parliamentary and media questions, and analyse access, waiting times and cancer pathways. The aim is to monitor and improve imaging services and support earlier cancer diagnosis. The published statistics have been used by the Care Quality Commission, Public Health England and NHS Improvement in their work.

DARS-NIC-153720-N8K6X.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death registration data, covering both clinical and financial information. It uses this to plan and monitor health services for the population of the former Ashford CCG area, including population health management, risk stratification and service redesign. The main intended benefit is better planned, higher-quality services that meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-15411-C9Z9L.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, uses Hospital Episode Statistics (covering admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency and critical care) linked to civil death registrations. It uses them for two projects: modelling future NHS funding pressures and how service changes could ease them, and an international comparison of the care, costs and quality for patients with long-term, complex conditions. The aim is to help policymakers target changes to cost and care quality. Work so far includes a published joint report with the Institute for Fiscal Studies and papers on readmission rates.

DARS-NIC-154880-M7G5Z.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS service data, which includes both clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the population of the former Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CCG area. This covers analysing local needs, monitoring services and budgets, and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planned, more accessible services.

DARS-NIC-154892-N5F9Z.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, with clinical and financial information. It is used to plan and commission health services for the population of the West Kent CCG area, including population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient flow, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-155188-V0V7L.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, with clinical and financial details. It uses them to plan and commission health services for the Medway population, including analysing needs, service redesign and identifying people at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow. The agreement reports the data has helped check the quality and efficiency of commissioned services.

DARS-NIC-155197-S3L3V.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for the former Swale clinical commissioning group (CCG) area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus births and deaths records. It uses this to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs, and manage costs and demand. The stated aim is to match services to the needs of the local population. Reported results include business cases presented, a forecast £3.3m of savings, and analysis behind changes to eye and skin services and an Urgent Treatment Centre.

DARS-NIC-155254-Y1H0S.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, acting for the former South Kent Coast clinical commissioning group (CCG), uses hospital, community, mental health and other NHS activity data, including birth and death records. It uses the data to check provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility and to plan and commission local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned around the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-155278-D1D1J.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, births and deaths data, among others, covering the former Canterbury and Coastal CCG area. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including population health management, service redesign and identifying people at risk of hospital admission. The stated aim is to direct health and social care resources more effectively and improve patient experience.

DARS-NIC-155287-C4K4G.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, a sub-ICB location covering the former Thanet CCG area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, diagnostic and civil registration data, including births and deaths. It uses this to analyse health needs, plan and redesign services, manage contracts, and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-155843-0MQMK.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital admission and mental health records for the general population of Yorkshire under 65. It compares them with a register of people diagnosed with cancer as children or young adults. The aim is to understand their hospital use and long-term health effects, so that follow-up care and services can be better tailored. So far, the work has contributed to a completed University of Leeds PhD thesis on the long-term mental health of survivors.

DARS-NIC-15625-T8K6L.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), part of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, uses NHS England hospital, mental health, cancer, maternity, death and other secondary care records linked to GP records. It provides these linked data to researchers for public health research and drug safety work, aiming to improve clinical care and public health policy. Published studies have already shown higher flu risks for cancer survivors, supporting UK COVID-19 vaccine priority groups.

DARS-NIC-156334-711SX.summary: The University of Cambridge is using linked NHS England health records, including hospital, cancer, death, GP and COVID-19 data, for blood donors in the INTERVAL, COMPARE and STRIDES studies. It is following their long-term health and how it relates to genetic, biological and lifestyle traits. The aim is to improve blood donation services and donor health, and to support wider research on chronic diseases and COVID-19. Results have already led NHS Blood and Transplant to change its haemoglobin screening test and to use reminders to help donors keep appointments.

DARS-NIC-156407-5KJ0Y.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging current status, members and postings, personal demographics and Scottish NHS registration data. It is studying whether the very small amount of heart muscle damage that can occur during angioplasty affects patients' long-term health, and whether the patients most at risk can be predicted. The aim is to allow steps before, during and after the procedure to reduce risk and improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-156409-W056Z.summary: University College London is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, including cause of death, cohort event notification, flagging status and demographic data. It uses them for the SCORAD III trial, which compares one dose of radiotherapy with five doses in patients with metastatic spinal cord compression. The trial looks at whether patients keep or regain the ability to walk, along with quality of life, side effects and survival. The text says single-dose treatment could need fewer NHS resources and shorten hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-156412-QY9WM.summary: The University of Birmingham is keeping death registration and cause-of-death records linked to participants in the ECHOES heart failure study. The study aims to estimate long-term survival after a heart failure diagnosis, identify the main causes of death and find factors linked to survival. The main intended benefit is better information for patients and doctors about likely outlook. Earlier 5 and 10-year survival papers were published, and clinicians have used the figures when talking with patients.

DARS-NIC-15721-Y4V1G.summary: Warwickshire County Council, a local authority, uses hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients, including Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, health reports and advice to NHS commissioners, to better understand local health and inequalities. Reported results include a report on childhood injuries and analyses used in two Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-157211-T8B2M.summary: University College London is using hospital, mental health, Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) and death registration records to study whether psychological therapies in IAPT services affect the later risk of dementia. It also examines access to and outcomes from therapy for people with dementia and other groups, aiming to inform policy, commissioning and clinical care. So far, it has published peer-reviewed papers, discussed findings with IAPT services and commissioners, and contributed to an Alzheimer's Society report.

DARS-NIC-15741-J6Y4L.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using pseudonymised civil registrations mortality (death) data, linked to cervical screening records. The study examines whether women in poorer health are less likely to attend cervical screening, and by how much, by comparing women who died with women of the same age. The aim is to show whether current estimates of screening effectiveness need adjusting, so that screening programmes and health inequalities can be improved.

DARS-NIC-157431-T3M4X.summary: Liverpool City Council uses hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and accident and emergency data, including Emergency Care Data Set records. It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning of services and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. So far, the data has supported monitoring of hospital admissions for conditions including cancers, and helped identify health disparities in child injuries across the city.

DARS-NIC-158112-L0R5C.summary: University of Northumbria at Newcastle is using Diagnostic Imaging Data Set records to study GP direct access to radiology tests for suspected brain, lung, pancreatic and sarcoma cancers in the North East and Cumbria. It will compare the costs and clinical process measures, such as time to diagnosis, of direct access with the urgent two-week-wait referral route. The main intended benefit is evidence on cost-effectiveness to inform commissioning decisions, service planning and guidance on referral routes for suspected cancer.

DARS-NIC-15814-C6W9R.summary: Monitor, which works alongside NHS England and NHS Improvement, uses hospital, mental health, community, diagnostic imaging, cost and death registration data. It uses them to set national tariff prices, oversee NHS providers and support programmes such as Model Hospital and Getting It Right First Time. The aim is to improve productivity, quality of care and payment. Reported benefits include Kettering Hospital releasing about £400,000 after reviewing its medicine stock.

DARS-NIC-158283-T2Q2D.summary: Cardiff University is using National Diabetes Audit data, including HbA1c blood glucose measures, linked with schools and higher education records. It is studying how diabetes-related health and educational outcomes such as attendance and attainment affect each other. The aim is to give clinicians evidence to help them support people with diabetes. So far, the team has published a study on variation in outcomes for children with type 1 diabetes and presented findings to practitioners, patients and researchers.

DARS-NIC-158754-R5T3V.summary: The Brain Tumour Charity is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics), diagnostic imaging data and civil registration death data for people in England with a brain tumour. It is building BRIAN, a research database and patient information system, to produce reports and research data extracts on diagnosis times, treatments and survival. The aim is to help patients make better-informed decisions and to support research. The Charity has already published three reports, on comorbidities, tumour incidence and surgeries per hospital, in its patient portal in September 2019.

DARS-NIC-159225-C9N9P.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS). The study looks at how smokers with mental health problems can be helped to try quitting more often and to succeed. The researchers hope the findings will inform policy and clinical practice on stopping smoking for this group, and will publish the results in peer-reviewed journals.

DARS-NIC-159251-K4Y6Q.summary: King's College London (an academic organisation) is using the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS) to study ethnic inequalities in health and in the use of health services. The aim is to produce evidence for guidelines on training, practice and policy that reduce health disparities. Findings have already gone to policymakers and healthcare bodies, and a report produced with the Welsh Government informs its Race Equality Action Plan.

DARS-NIC-159399-K2M6H.summary: The National Centre for Social Research is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS) 2014, which covers mental illness, treatment and service use in the adult population. It will analyse the circumstances of adults with a learning impairment compared with everyone else, including physical health conditions and unmet needs for treatment and services. The findings will go into a short report for the Department of Health. The report aims to inform decisions on the design and targeting of services.

DARS-NIC-159523-F1C1P.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners), linked with pseudonymised social care data, on behalf of Kirklees Council and the local NHS commissioners. It aims to understand how social care and hospital use interact, and to produce reports and dashboards on falls, Better Care Fund measures and intermediate care. The intended benefits include fewer A&E attendances and emergency admissions, especially for older people.

DARS-NIC-159576-C0V1M.summary: University College London (UCL) is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults under 65 in England. It is comparing rates of mental disorders and help seeking between sexual minority and heterosexual people in 2007 and 2014, and looking at what predicts mental distress and wellbeing. The aim is to help address health inequalities. A first paper in Psychological Medicine has been published and received significant media attention.

DARS-NIC-16016-Y9H1D.summary: HSJ Information Ltd, a non-NHS provider, uses hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health data from NHS England. It analyses this data to raise awareness of diseases, support commissioning and service improvement, and produce long-term analysis of rare diseases. The main intended benefit is better diagnosis and patient outcomes. Its work has already produced a respiratory disease dashboard that a charity used to evidence health inequalities in discussions with NHS England, and it was covered in national press.

DARS-NIC-160361-NDZKG.summary: The University of Nottingham holds mortality and cancer registration records for about 550 consenting people with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), taking part in the PROFILE study. The study uses them to link survival with blood and other biomarkers, aiming to predict disease progression and guide treatment. Reported results include several peer-reviewed papers, biomarkers used as endpoints in a clinical trial, and a successful NIHR Research Professorship application.

DARS-NIC-16068-V9H0M.summary: North East Lincolnshire Council uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to analyse local health needs and inequalities, and to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The council reports using admissions figures to understand local demand and geographic inequalities over time, such as for self-harm and substance misuse.

DARS-NIC-160958-K3J4W.summary: NHS North West London ICB, through its Brent sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and death and birth records, including clinical and financial information. It uses them to plan and commission health services for local people across the North West London Sustainable Transformation Partnership. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways, capacity and quality, based on a fuller understanding of the population's needs.

DARS-NIC-160981-S2D3K.summary: NHS North Central London ICB, acting as a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer, diabetes, and birth and death records, including clinical and financial information. It uses them to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways. North East London Commissioning Support Unit carries out the processing.

DARS-NIC-161143-S2S3Z.summary: NHS South West London ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death records, including clinical and financial information. North East London Commissioning Support Unit processes it. The data is used to plan and commission health services, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of care pathways and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-161352-L1M9W.summary: NHS South East London ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former Bexley CCG area) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, diagnostic, cancer waiting times, diabetes, and births and deaths data. It uses the data to plan and manage health services, understand local health needs, identify patients at risk and monitor costs and quality. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways for the local population.

DARS-NIC-161422-Q0K1M.summary: Royal Liverpool University Hospital is using hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration records for patients treated for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms, a complex type of aneurysm near the kidney arteries. The study compares open surgery, endovascular repair and non-operative care to see which works best and costs the NHS least. It aims to inform national guidelines and commissioning. Results have been published in the European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery and have informed European aneurysm treatment guidelines.

DARS-NIC-162677-S1D8W.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB uses pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer waiting times and births and deaths records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health management, service redesign, budget monitoring and identifying people at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flows, with fewer avoidable emergency readmissions.

DARS-NIC-16274-J8H5T.summary: The University of Sheffield is using pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and linked death registration data to study vascular services in England. This extension examines socioeconomic, geographical and ethnic differences in who receives vascular surgery and how well they do, so policy makers can reduce those disparities. The project's findings on hospital surgical volumes contributed to the Vascular Society's 2021 revised policy document on vascular services.

DARS-NIC-162895-N9K8S.summary: NHS North Central London ICB (Camden area) is using Secondary Uses Service (SUS) hospital data for commissioners, identifiable only by an encrypted NHS number. It is used for risk stratification, which forecasts future demand and identifies people at high risk of hospital admission or A&E attendance so GPs and commissioners can offer earlier support. The intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning of services, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-164024-C3N9T.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey as a nationally representative comparison group. The aim is to study alcohol misuse and dependence among UK Members of Parliament, and the main intended benefit is better mental healthcare and support for MPs. The study has already produced a published paper, which was widely shared and prompted national discussion.

DARS-NIC-164594-K4C5N.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to study how sensory and cognitive impairments relate to mental health, abuse and discrimination. It aims to build scientific understanding so clinicians and organisations can make better decisions about care for affected people. Several papers from this work have already been published in journals, including on sensory impairment and common mental illness, psychotic symptoms and suicidal ideation.

DARS-NIC-164830-L7L7C.summary: King's College London is using hospital admission records and death registration data, linked to National Hip Fracture Database records, for people admitted with a hip fracture. The research looks at whether getting out of bed within 36 hours of surgery affects survival and recovery, and which patients are at higher risk of poor outcomes. The aim is to inform better, more tailored rehabilitation. One paper has been accepted in Age and Ageing, finding early mobilisation was linked to better survival on discharge.

DARS-NIC-165460-G2C3R.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 for a PhD project. It is examining whether psychotic experiences, such as hallucinations or delusional beliefs, are risk markers for suicidal thoughts and behaviour in high-risk groups, including people with certain physical or mental health conditions. The aim is to improve understanding of suicide risk and inform clinical practice and suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-165970-Q4Q8P.summary: West Sussex County Council, a local authority, uses Hospital Episode Statistics data covering emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It uses the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and commissioning. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported benefits include analyses of mental health admissions that fed into a mental health needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-166391-W1S0Y.summary: Sunderland City Council, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will analyse them to support statutory duties such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Reported uses so far include ward-level analysis for needs assessments, new birth visits analysis for contract monitoring, and Covid-19 admissions analysis.

DARS-NIC-16656-D9B5T.summary: The University of Liverpool's Place-based Longitudinal Data Resource uses Hospital Episode Statistics (hospital admissions, outpatient and A&E records) and Emergency Care Data Set records for the whole of England. It uses them to build neighbourhood-level health indicators and to study how social, economic, environmental and policy changes affect health and use of health services. The aim is to help local agencies target resources at the neighbourhoods most affected. Reported results include published papers, a tool used by GPs across Cheshire and Merseyside, and evidence that informed government funding and welfare policy.

DARS-NIC-166879-K4Z0S.summary: The University of Bristol is using NHS hospital records (admissions, critical care and outpatient care) and civil death registration data for a randomised trial of adults with end-stage kidney disease on dialysis. The trial compares high-volume haemodiafiltration with high-flux haemodialysis, mainly to see whether it affects non-cancer mortality. The intended benefit is stronger evidence on whether haemodiafiltration should be offered to patients.

DARS-NIC-167122-G6W8K.summary: King's College London researchers are using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014 data, which covers mental health in adults in England, in an Economic and Social Research Council funded project. They are studying how employment status relates to common mental disorders such as anxiety and depression, and how this has changed over time and by age group. The aim is to build the evidence base for public health policy. A paper from earlier survey years has already been published, and the researchers have presented findings at conferences.

DARS-NIC-167186-V7J4F.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital accident and emergency, admitted patient and mental health services data. It is examining how differences in local health and care services and in population needs relate to variation between clinical commissioning groups in A&E attendances and potentially avoidable emergency admissions, for people in contact with mental health services and those not. The aim is to show decision-makers where improvements could reduce avoidable emergency hospital use.

DARS-NIC-167794-K1P8H.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to study whether patient choice of GP and hospital provider has affected fairness of access to planned operations such as hip and knee replacements and cataract surgery. It aims to give NHS planners and policy makers evidence to reduce inequalities. A paper on private sector expansion and the NHS treatment gap between rich and poor has been published in Health Policy.

DARS-NIC-168692-Y5S4C.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), through its South Warwickshire area, uses pseudonymised health and care data, including clinical and financial information from hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services, along with birth and death records. It uses this to plan and commission health services, assess population needs and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefit is a more joined up, efficient and higher quality care service. It reports that adding primary care data has allowed more targeted commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-168879-K2N8Q.summary: University College London is using NHS England hospital, emergency care and children's mental health survey data to study how genetic disorders linked to intellectual disability affect the mental health of children and young people. The aim is to map how risks develop for people with different types of intellectual disability. The study hopes to give clinicians and families better evidence for care decisions and help healthcare resources be targeted more efficiently.

DARS-NIC-169866-G4Z6F.summary: NHS Frimley Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health service data, plus birth and death records, covering three former clinical commissioning groups (CCGs). It uses them to plan and commission health services for the local population, including analysing demand, service use and health needs. The main intended benefit is better planning of patient pathways and services, with care delivered in the right place.

DARS-NIC-169879-V6R4L.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death registration data, with clinical and financial detail. It uses this to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health analysis, service redesign and budget reporting. The stated aim is to improve planning, patient flow and access to services.

DARS-NIC-169933-S9N9J.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, maternity, social care and civil registration data, with both clinical and financial information. It uses the data to analyse and plan health services across the Sussex and East Surrey partnership, supporting commissioning and the redesign of services across boundaries. Reported results include a hospital discharge wellbeing checks pilot, which completed 1,441 follow-up checks, and health checks delivered with GP practices.

DARS-NIC-169971-Z9M1C.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine, a research organisation, is using cancer registration, death registration and demographic data for about 1,800 UK workers from the glass-reinforced plastics industry. It is studying whether workplace exposure to styrene, a chemical used in plastics and rubber, raises the risk of cancer or death, by comparing these workers with the general population and with each other by exposure level. The study aims to clarify whether styrene increases cancer risk, which could inform exposure limits and workplace practice.

DARS-NIC-170100-T1Q8C.summary: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital inpatient, outpatient, A&E and death records, linked to its research database, to study people with dementia with Lewy bodies compared with other types of dementia. The aim is to understand how the condition presents and which modifiable factors affect survival, and to help develop a language-processing app that supports earlier diagnosis. The Trust reports that its first paper on mortality in this condition has been cited 49 times since 2017.

DARS-NIC-170211-Z1B4J.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital episode, emergency care and civil registration (death) records, which are pseudonymised (identifying details replaced). Its Northern Medical Physics and Clinical Engineering team uses them for not-for-profit research on the safety, effectiveness and uptake of medical devices and procedures, and on patient pathways. The aim is to inform national guidance such as NICE's. Published studies have already contributed to updated NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-170430-D2S8V.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB), for the former Ashford area, uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data about hospital and other care activity, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, with Optum Health Solutions advising whether each should be paid. The main intended benefit is making sure providers are paid accurately and that the commissioner pays only for patients it is responsible for.

DARS-NIC-170444-L5Z2P.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (Sub ICB Location, for the former Canterbury and Coastal CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for invoice validation. A processor, Optum Health Solutions UK Limited, analyses it in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance to check that invoiced care is the commissioner's responsibility and to advise whether invoices can be paid. The intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is properly controlled.

DARS-NIC-170552-H5Q2X.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (for the former Thanet CCG area) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses this data for invoice validation, checking that care providers' invoices relate to patients the commissioner is responsible for. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is spent appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170564-P9F0D.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using linked hospital records (admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and civil registration death data, combined with National Chronic Kidney Disease Audit data. It is studying long-term outcomes, care pathways and the accuracy of GP coding for people with chronic kidney disease, aiming to improve diagnosis and care. Published results include a BMJ Open paper linking accurate GP coding of the condition to fewer hospitalisations.

DARS-NIC-170580-K3W3H.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, for the former Dartford, Gravesham and Swanley CCG area, uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation. Optum Health Solutions checks invoices from care providers in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance, so the commissioner can confirm that the patients billed for are its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public money is spent appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170589-L2W0Y.summary: The University of Glasgow is using linked hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. It is following up patients in the FAMOUS-NSTEMI trial, which tested whether a pressure test during angiography (fractional flow reserve) should guide treatment after a type of heart attack called NSTEMI. The aim is to show whether this approach improves long-term outcomes, such as death or further heart attacks, and so inform NHS practice and guidelines.

DARS-NIC-170593-N0R4N.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB, for the former NHS Swale CCG area, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, which is identifiable by NHS number. It is used in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance, where Optum Health Solutions LTD checks provider invoices to confirm that the commissioner is responsible for the care claimed. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public funds are used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-170647-Z0B6H.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration data for the Sunflower Study, a clinical trial run with the University of Bristol and Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. The study tests whether imaging the common bile duct before gallbladder surgery is needed for patients at low or moderate risk of stones there. It aims to inform national guidance and reduce unnecessary imaging. So far, the data have reassured the independent data monitoring and safety committee that the trial is safe for participants.

DARS-NIC-170867-M5Q6W.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using civil registration death data, linked to National Vascular Registry records of patients who had elective repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm. It is using the data to develop and externally validate a clinical decision tool based on the Aneurysm Repair Decision Aid (ARDA). The aim is to help patients and surgeons make informed decisions about the best time to repair an aneurysm, or whether to keep observing it.

DARS-NIC-171083-Q8R4B.summary: The University of East Anglia, working with Public Health England, is using names-free records of addresses and ages for randomly selected GP-registered people in England. They will be invited to join a case-control study as healthy comparison participants, to find which routes spread Shiga-toxin E. coli (STEC) infection. The aim is to identify the most common sources so infections can be reduced. Recruitment has begun, with over 250 controls recruited.

DARS-NIC-172121-G0Z1H.summary: The University of Oxford's Big Health Data Group is using linked hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Patient Reported Outcome Measures data, alongside National Joint Registry data, for two studies of hip and knee replacement surgery. One compares partial and total knee replacement for patients with several health conditions. The other looks at follow-up care after joint replacement. The aim is evidence to guide patient decisions, NHS commissioning and surgeons' practice.

DARS-NIC-17218-B0W9X.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses identifiable death registration, demographic and cause-of-death data on the 15,976 people in the 1970 British Cohort Study. It uses the data to update participant records, avoid contacting people who have died or emigrated, and research mortality and its links to health, behaviour and early life. The text says this should help inform preventative health policies. It reports that study research has already informed government briefing papers and gained media coverage.

DARS-NIC-172240-R4R0L.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS England hospital admission records, demographic details and list-cleaning data to find and invite people with existing cardiovascular disease to join the ORION-4 trial. The trial tests whether inclisiran, a cholesterol-lowering drug, safely reduces heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths. Reported results so far: recruitment exceeded its target, with 13,190 UK participants, and a preliminary analysis of the invitation process was presented at a conference in October 2024.

DARS-NIC-172334-W0G2L.summary: Imperial College London is using pseudonymised hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency, and critical care) from 2012/13 to 2018/19. It is evaluating whether NHS England's Commissioning for Quality and Innovation (CQUIN) incentive payments for specialised services improve care and give value for money. The aim is to inform how future incentive schemes are designed. Findings have been reported to NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care, and a journal paper has been published.

DARS-NIC-173508-F4X6P.summary: The Isle of Man Department of Health & Social Care, with Manx Care, uses pseudonymised hospital activity and cost data (Secondary Uses Service data) for patients treated in England and Wales. It uses this to plan and commission health services, with the aim of providing more care on the island and reducing travel for patients. The data has already helped justify a full-time plastics consultant for dermatology, bring the macular degeneration service back to the island, and support new CT scanning on the island.

DARS-NIC-174209-R8G8N.summary: King's College London is using five years of pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care), linked with NICOR heart disease registry data. The research aims to find how many heart failure patients are repeatedly readmitted and which risk factors are involved. The intended benefit is to help clinicians avoid readmissions, improving patient experience and reducing costs for the NHS.

DARS-NIC-174337-X0N1L.summary: Kent County Council, a local authority, is using pseudonymised health data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity, diagnostic imaging and children's services data, together with data from local providers. It uses this to analyse the health and social care needs of people in its area and to support commissioning, service redesign and its statutory Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and annual public health report. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-174486-Q8J1B.summary: University College London holds mortality, cancer registration and demographic data on women taking part in the British Women's Heart and Health Study, a long-running study of heart disease and stroke in older women. This agreement only allows the data to be securely kept while a further application is prepared. The wider study aims to identify risk factors for cardiovascular disease and support prevention. It has produced 218 peer-reviewed publications, fourteen of which contributed to fifteen clinical care and public health guidelines.

DARS-NIC-174557-H6J6Y.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, covering the former NHS Rotherham Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other patient data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-174740-C0H0L.summary: King's College London is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which is hospital admissions data, for a PhD research project. The project studies how rates of self-harm differ between neighbourhoods and populations in London. The intended benefit is to help public health teams and mental health services target preventative support for self-harm in the areas that need it.

DARS-NIC-175120-W5G2X.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) uses NHS England hospital, emergency care, psychological therapy and birth notification data to produce official statistics and statistical research. It uses them to develop and improve statistics on births, population and migration, and health. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions by government, local authorities and others. ONS has published analyses using these data, including articles on suicides, climate-related hospital admissions and carers' health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-175693-L5Y4K.summary: The University of Liverpool is using the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a national survey dataset, for a PhD research project. It will examine how social adversity, such as discrimination, bullying and trauma, helps explain the link between belonging to an ethnic or sexual minority group and psychosis, including paranoia. The intended benefit is better understanding, diagnosis and care for minority groups experiencing psychotic symptoms.

DARS-NIC-175989-M9T7B.summary: The National Centre for Social Research is using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data, which covers mental health among adults in England. It is analysing trends, inequalities and risk factors in mental illness and self-harm, particularly for women and men, so government can plan services. It has already published papers, including one in Lancet Psychiatry on rising self-harm that received media coverage and was cited in policy briefings.

DARS-NIC-17649-G0X4B.summary: The University of Leeds is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which are hospital admission records. Its Cardiovascular Epidemiology research group is studying hospital stays and survival in people who survive a heart attack in England, including differences between areas. The main intended benefit is evidence to help NHS commissioners plan services and help clinicians improve care. The benefits have not yet been realised, so none have been reported.

DARS-NIC-176695-S5L5T.summary: The University of Birmingham is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a general population household survey. It is analysing mood disorders and personality disorders to understand their causes, access to health services, inequalities and links to other disorders. The aim is to improve mental health care. A 2021 paper in the Journal of Affective Disorders has already been published, covering how common bipolar disorder is and who gets support.

DARS-NIC-177114-Y6W8J.summary: The University of Leicester is using anonymised data from the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a nationally representative mental health survey. It is studying how ADHD and autism relate to other psychiatric conditions and risk factors, checking an ADHD assessment tool, and looking at diabetes in autistic adults and trends in mental and physical health. The aim is to inform clinical understanding, health service planning and policy. The ADHD assessment validation has been carried out, but it has not yet been written up or published.

DARS-NIC-177392-B8T1Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital records (admissions, A&E, outpatient and critical care) linked to death registration data. The aim is to study whether reorganising trauma care into Regional Trauma Networks and Major Trauma Centres has improved outcomes and cost-effectiveness, using open fractures of the lower limb as an example. The intended benefit is evidence to guide commissioning and service design. Reported findings so far show the burden of disease and the effect of the policy change and national standards on the process of care.

DARS-NIC-177523-N8J2S.summary: University College London (UCL) is using the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a survey of adults' mental health. It is studying mental illness, loneliness and service use in people with borderline intellectual functioning compared with the general population. The aim is to improve understanding of this group's needs and help the planning of mental health services. A paper on loneliness and common mental disorders in this group has already been published in the Journal of Affective Disorders.

DARS-NIC-178123-C4W3G.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB is using pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer and other health service data, with its analytics supplier Optum Health Solutions Limited. They are analysing it to plan Milton Keynes health services around local needs, including population health management and service redesign. The aim is to understand population needs and unwarranted variation in care. Reported results include insights delivered to the CCG, local clinician workshops, and a noted change in clinical behaviour.

DARS-NIC-178135-HJSFF.summary: University of Birmingham's Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit holds identifiable data on date and cause of death, and cancer outcomes, for participants in the CReST colorectal stenting trial. It is being kept for archiving only, with no further processing, so the trial results can support evidence-based treatment of patients with bowel obstruction caused by colorectal cancer. The data has already helped change European guidelines on stenting as a bridge to surgery.

DARS-NIC-17824-V9F2B.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies, a research organisation, uses pseudonymised NHS hospital records (admitted patient care, A&E, outpatients), death registrations and patient-reported outcomes for joint replacement. It uses them for economics research on the health and care system, to give policymakers evidence for better health policy. Reported results include published journal articles, and Sure Start findings that informed a decision in Northern Ireland to continue funding.

DARS-NIC-17875-X7K1V.summary: University of Bristol's Bristol Medical School is using pseudonymised hospital admitted patient and outpatient records, diagnostic imaging data and death registrations. It aims to measure and explain geographic variation in hospital care and procedure use across England. The aim is to help the NHS use limited resources more effectively. Research using earlier data has produced published evidence on admission-reduction services, treatment costs and the effects of paused services.

DARS-NIC-178836-V1G3V.summary: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admissions records and death registration data, linked with National Joint Registry data. It is studying how many total and revision ankle replacements fail within five years, including through further surgery, fusion or amputation, and what complications follow. The main intended benefit is that surgeons and patients get more accurate information on likely outcomes when deciding about ankle replacement.

DARS-NIC-178855-W0G7Z.summary: Oxfordshire County Council uses birth and death registration data, including identifiable details, and primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, and support work such as suicide prevention and immunisation programmes, with published outputs aggregated and small numbers suppressed. The intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports that mortality data has supported suicide surveillance and helped plan its COVID response.

DARS-NIC-179115-S0R1W.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is using Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS) records to analyse trends and regional differences in mental health activity in England. It will build an economic model to estimate how spending pressures on mental health services may grow over the next 15 to 20 years, and how policies might reduce them. The main intended benefit is to help policymakers, commissioners and providers plan funding and workforce.

DARS-NIC-179285-7RS6G.summary: The University of Manchester is using NHS Digital cancer registration, death and demographic data to add to its study of children and young people with juvenile idiopathic arthritis who take etanercept. It aims to check whether etanercept raises the risk of cancer or early death compared with the standard treatment, methotrexate. Published papers from the study have influenced NICE appraisals, clinical guidelines and a 2015 NHS England commissioning policy.

DARS-NIC-17931-M2B4J.summary: North Yorkshire Council, a local authority, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. It reports using the data to inform targeted work on older people's acute care, guide community service redesign, and contribute to the Director of Public Health's annual report.

DARS-NIC-179549-L8L1P.summary: The London Borough of Hounslow is using pseudonymised hospital data, including Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care, outpatients, accident and emergency and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set. The council will analyse it to carry out its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that the needs of the most disadvantaged residents are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-179596-N1Q8X.summary: The London Borough of Tower Hamlets uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to produce needs assessments, health strategies and advice, so it can better understand and respond to local health needs and inequalities. It reports using the data in a diabetes needs assessment, locality profiles, and violence and mental health needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-180025-W6S0Z.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for the former NHS Tameside and Glossop Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which is identifiable by NHS number, in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, so the CCG can confirm it is responsible for the activity claimed and challenge any discrepancies. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and commissioners pay appropriately for the patients they are responsible for.

DARS-NIC-180665-GJMW5.summary: University College London is using linked NHS birth registration, hospital and mortality records, including maternal age at birth, for children conceived through assisted reproductive technology (ART), their spontaneously conceived siblings and matched unrelated controls. It is studying whether ART-conceived children face higher risks of specific diagnoses, such as prematurity complications and cerebral palsy, to inform families, clinicians and health service planning. Findings have been published in BMJ Open and the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology, which reported that ART-conceived children were more likely to be hospitalised.

DARS-NIC-18089-C7M8J.summary: Torbay Council, a local authority, uses pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported benefits include admissions analysis underpinning the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and a two-page A&E profile that aided commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-181948-L5P9K.summary: The London Borough of Barnet is using hospital records, covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, through NHS England's secure environment. The council uses them for public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to understand local health needs and inequalities. The analyses have already fed into its updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, joint projects with local hospitals on children's A&E admissions, and council strategies on child poverty and dementia care.

DARS-NIC-182098-Y4H0W.summary: The University of Cambridge is using hospital, emergency care and death registration records, linked to its own clinical data on 152 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) recruited from primary care. It is studying hospital admissions and deaths in this group to understand outcomes and the factors affecting them. The aim is to improve how HFpEF is diagnosed and managed. So far the project has produced published papers and a research briefing, though these do not yet use the linked data.

DARS-NIC-182332-B2F4M.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location formerly a clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including pseudonymised and NHS-number-identifiable records. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-182736-Q2K7Y.summary: King's College London, working with Lancaster University, is using NHS England cause of death, current status and postings records for veterans who took part in chemical warfare agent experiments at Porton Down. It is updating earlier analyses of deaths and cancer with at least ten more years of data, to see whether exposure to nerve agents, vesicants or riot control agents is linked to long-term health risks. The aim is to improve understanding of low-dose exposure. A published cohort profile paper has already prompted contact from veterans and their families.

DARS-NIC-182801-H6R6R.summary: Bristol City Council uses civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details such as postcode. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with only aggregated figures published. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports that its analysis fed into the city's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, a commended maternity care review and local suicide prevention policy.

DARS-NIC-183359-N7P0D.summary: King's College London researchers are using the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to study the mental health and wellbeing of military veterans and serving personnel compared with the general population. The studies cover employment, dementia, women's mental health, health service use and domestic violence and abuse. The aim is to inform health services, support for veterans and charities' spending. Reported results include findings on veterans' job outcomes, higher rates of musculoskeletal disorders and a higher risk of homelessness among short-service veterans.

DARS-NIC-183465-X4D2Z.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB), acting for the former East Surrey Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including NHS-number-level Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk, and plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-planned, more effective services for patients.

DARS-NIC-183742-Z1J1B.summary: Oxfordshire County Council, a local authority, is using Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-183842-H8L1J.summary: The Health and Safety Executive is using identifiable death, cancer registration and demographic data about asbestos workers who joined its survey after 2006 and gave consent. It is tracking their deaths and cancers over time and comparing them with the general population and between types of asbestos work. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether tighter asbestos regulation is reducing asbestos-related disease. Findings have already been published in HSE research reports and peer-reviewed journal articles.

DARS-NIC-184951-D1G8R.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) holds pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for a completed study of anticoagulant treatment used in kidney replacement therapy in intensive care. The data is now kept for secure storage and for re-checking published findings. The study compared the clinical and cost-effectiveness of citrate and heparin anticoagulation. Its final report has been published in the NIHR Health Technology Assessment journal, and the NIHR selected it for an NIHR Alert.

DARS-NIC-184980-J5B6C.summary: Cardiff University, an academic organisation, holds identifiable NHS England mortality, cancer registration and demographic data from the AML15 acute myeloid leukaemia trial. It is kept for secure storage, backup and regulatory audit, and previous analyses may be repeated only to verify published findings. The trial aimed to improve leukaemia treatment. Its results were published, informed later trial designs, and led to a change in the standard of care for a subgroup called APL.

DARS-NIC-185179-V0B0T.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care and civil registration (deaths) data. It is comparing emergency surgery with non-operative care for people admitted as emergencies with common acute conditions, looking at effectiveness and cost. The aim is to inform changes to emergency general surgery across the NHS. Results already published include a final report to funders (January 2023) and papers, which found no overall difference in outcomes, but a benefit from non-operative care in very frail patients.

DARS-NIC-185897-R6T5S.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, run by Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, which checks that care providers' invoices are the commissioner's responsibility. The second is risk stratification, run by Prescribing Service Ltd, which links SUS+ data with GP data to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefit is better planning and more targeted care.

DARS-NIC-185910-D9W1Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The checks are carried out by Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit in a secure finance environment. They confirm that the activity claimed is the commissioner's responsibility before payment. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public funds are used appropriately.

DARS-NIC-185930-B6N0H.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, through its former South Norfolk CCG area, uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses this data to check invoices from care providers, so it can confirm that the activity claimed is its responsibility before payment. Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit carries out the checks. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for patients' treatment.

DARS-NIC-185937-D7J1Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), including NHS numbers, to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor outcomes, and understand local population health needs. Invoice checking and risk scoring are carried out by external organisations. The stated aim is accurate payment of providers and earlier, better-targeted care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-185940-J1W0Y.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, through Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data that can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data in a secure Controlled Environment for Finance to check provider invoices and confirm that the care claimed for is the commissioner's responsibility. This lets it challenge invoices, control its budget and ensure providers are paid accurately for patients' treatment.

DARS-NIC-186860-T7H5K.summary: The University of Manchester is using hospital admission records and death registration data for people aged 75 and over in Greater Manchester care homes. It is studying how different kinds of healthcare support for care home residents relate to emergency hospital admissions and place of death. The aim is to help commissioners and care providers plan more appropriate care and reduce avoidable admissions. Early findings have already been presented at local care home forums in 2019.

DARS-NIC-186881-Z9P9B.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West Integrated Care Board uses hospital, community, mental health and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and commission health services. The aim is services that match local needs. The agreement reports that services have been delivered to match the population's requirements and that integrated care has been delivered.

DARS-NIC-186883-L6C8Y.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull ICB is using hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can target care, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with providers paid accurately and care better matched to local needs.

DARS-NIC-186885-Q1T3D.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, to validate provider invoices, identify patients at risk of poor health, and plan and monitor commissioned services. The aim is to pay providers accurately and to plan care that better meets the population's needs. It reports around £28.5m of savings identified and data used to monitor the overnight closure of an A&E department.

DARS-NIC-186888-X2K6T.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, some of it identifiable and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services better match local needs. The CCG reports it has used the data to monitor in-year projects and publish an annual report.

DARS-NIC-186893-W6V1H.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, acting for the former East Berkshire clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other provider activity data, including NHS-number-level and pseudonymised records. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target their care, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-186896-Q5Q2G.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (covering the former NHS Leeds CCG) uses hospital, community, mental health, GP-linked and other health and social care data to check invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support the planning of health services. Some data is identifiable by NHS number, and some is pseudonymised. The aim is to ensure providers are paid correctly, target care for vulnerable patients and plan services around local needs. Benefits reported so far are contributions to the organisation's annual reports.

DARS-NIC-187228-X8C4G.summary: Derby City Council, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. This includes needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that the data helped it show the need to change its urgent care system and supported its Discharge to Assess model.

DARS-NIC-18798-V2J6C.summary: NHS England uses Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data on hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E, plus the Emergency Care Data Set, which it downloads through the NHS Digital portal. It uses them for commissioning, policy, finance and analysis, such as monitoring services and planning future care. The aim is to improve the quality and efficiency of NHS services. Published examples include a mixed sex accommodation breach rate and the Diagnostic Atlas of Variation.

DARS-NIC-188499-K4G0M.summary: King's College London is using pseudonymised data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey 2014, a national survey of adults in England and Wales. The researchers are studying how mental disorders relate to experiencing sexual violence and to carrying out domestic violence. They aim to give clearer evidence on how common and how likely these experiences are among people with mental disorders, to inform future research, practice and policy.

DARS-NIC-188901-P9M0S.summary: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission, death registration and maternity records for children admitted to paediatric intensive care units (PICUs). The research, part of a doctoral fellowship, examines why girls admitted as infants have had higher death rates than boys, unlike in the general population. It aims to inform care and a possible revision of the Paediatric Index of Mortality score. So far, one systematic review is in peer review.

DARS-NIC-189166-R0Y9Y.summary: The University of Southampton, an academic body, holds cause of death report data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for the New EPOC cancer trial. The trial tested whether adding cetuximab to chemotherapy helps patients with operable colorectal liver metastases. The data is now kept only for back-up and storage, to meet research standards. Results from the trial have already been presented at cancer conferences and published in the Lancet in 2014.

DARS-NIC-189627-R3N8Y.summary: Sunderland City Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand local public health needs, including suicide and drug-related death audits, and to produce aggregated statistics for needs assessments and health strategies. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. So far, the council has built internal Power BI reports showing births and deaths trends by ward.

DARS-NIC-190086-F5Z7B.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School, an academic organisation, is using hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and accident and emergency), death registration data and a list cleaning report. The data covers about 120,000 young people who had voluntary heart screening through Cardiac Risk in the Young. The study will look at outcomes for the whole screened group, including those with normal results, to estimate how often sudden cardiac death occurs. The aim is a more reliable estimate that could inform decisions on screening programmes and guidelines.

DARS-NIC-190996-C4P8G.summary: RM Partners, a cancer alliance hosted by The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust, is using the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records cancer patients' waits from referral to treatment. It will analyse waiting times and patient flows across North West and South West London to find variation and delays. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Earlier analysis compared provider performance, so support could be targeted at providers facing challenges.

DARS-NIC-191209-G3Z6Z.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for the former NHS Bolton CCG area, is using pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital provider data and civil registrations of death. It supports the Greater Manchester and Eastern Cheshire Cancer Vanguard's evaluation of cancer care and outcomes, and helps commissioners plan health services, including population health management and contract management. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-191964-Y3Z1L.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, for the former North Kirklees area, uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services, SUS+) that can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices before payment and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately for the care they deliver, and that patients at risk can be offered earlier, better-targeted care.

DARS-NIC-192032-K0J3X.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location covering former Calderdale, Greater Huddersfield and North Kirklees CCGs, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other health and care activity and financial data, plus birth and death records. It uses this to plan and commission health services across the West Yorkshire and Harrogate partnership area, including population health analysis, demand planning and contract management. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-192218-L8R4C.summary: London Borough of Waltham Forest, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, annual public health reports and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. It has already produced JSNA chapters on cardiovascular disease, respiratory diseases and air quality, and informed council projects such as road improvements for air quality.

DARS-NIC-192305-X3T0Y.summary: NHS England uses national, patient-level cancer waiting times data, with identifying details removed, along with aggregate figures. It uses them to produce official statistics, monitor performance against NHS Constitution standards, support policy and service improvement, and give Cancer Alliances local performance reports. The main intended benefit is to focus improvements on the areas that will best improve cancer waiting times.
