Reported benefits include published monthly and quarterly statistics, funding allocated to Cancer Alliances using them as a benchmark, and national timed pathways developed from them.

DARS-NIC-19237-R3T6S.summary: The University of Liverpool is using cancer registration, death registration, demographic and mortality-flagging data for people who consented to join the UK Lung Cancer Screening Trial. It uses them to follow participants' cancer diagnoses, whether they are alive, and their dates and causes of death. The aim is to show whether low-dose CT screening reduces lung cancer deaths, to inform the UK National Screening Committee. Results have already been published in Thorax and The Lancet Regional Health - Europe.

DARS-NIC-192767-R0S9V.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and primary care data, along with birth and death records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the local population, including analysing demand, finding patients at risk of admission, monitoring providers and redesigning services. The main intended benefit is that commissioners can make better decisions and improve the quality of services and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-193456-W3M0H.summary: NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board, working with three other ICBs, uses pseudonymised hospital activity, local acute provider and death registration data. It is used to plan and commission health services and to produce aggregate quality reports through the Advancing Quality Alliance. The aim is more equal, consistent care across trusts. Two published papers (2012 and 2020) report reduced mortality, and one trust changed its antibiotic process after analysis of the data.

DARS-NIC-193518-T5K7C.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office is using the pseudonymised 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to estimate how many children live in households where an adult has physical or mental health problems, or alcohol, substance or domestic abuse issues. It will publish aggregated statistics so local authorities and government can plan services for families with complex needs. Its earlier estimates have been used in central government dashboards and in local authorities' Joint Strategic Needs Assessments.

DARS-NIC-194340-D6F3B.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) holds linked census and life events data on about 1% of the population of England and Wales, and this agreement is a short-term extension to keep that data. It maintains the ONS Longitudinal Study research database and gives approved researchers controlled access to it, so they can study topics such as health inequality and ageing. Its data has already supported government reports on health inequalities, National Statistics on life expectancy, and evidence submitted to the Dilnot Commission.

DARS-NIC-194387-K3H5K.summary: The University of Sheffield is using demographic data and NHS mortality list-cleaning reports to check whether bladder cancer patients in Yorkshire, the Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees have died or moved address. This supports a survey of patients' own reports of their quality of life during the first year after diagnosis. The aim is to understand outcomes, identify unmet need and shape clinical care. The checks also help surveys reach the right people and avoid distressing bereaved families.

DARS-NIC-194629-S4F9X.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services, a research charity, uses NHS hospital, emergency care and community services data. It uses the data for the NIHR Rapid Service Evaluation Team's evaluations of new ways of providing care, so that findings reach decision makers quickly. Reported results include influence on the Care Quality Commission's special measures regime, national Covid oximetry at home services, and a final maternity advocate report shared with government.

DARS-NIC-195235-Q0B5T.summary: The University of East Anglia is using hospital records on accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care for care home residents in England who took part in the FinCH trial. The data will help work out the costs of a falls prevention programme for care homes, compared with usual care, as part of a cost-effectiveness analysis. The aim is to give decision makers evidence on whether the programme reduces falls and offers value for money. The team's findings are submitted for publication but not yet published.

DARS-NIC-195377-M9L8Z.summary: The Nuffield Trust, a health research charity, is using hospital data covering A&E, inpatient and outpatient care to study how prisoners use secondary care services and how their care compares with non-prisoners. It aims to help fill a gap in evidence on healthcare quality in prisons. The Trust reports that its findings were cited in a Prisons and Probation Ombudsman report and used in a review that led the Ministry of Justice to publish figures on pregnant women in custody.

DARS-NIC-195618-N6T1R.summary: King's College London is using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data in a doctoral research project, with support from the National Centre for Social Research. The project looks at common mental disorders and access to psychological treatments among ethnic minority groups in the UK, including the reasons for the treatment gap. It aims to build the evidence base on mental health inequalities to support better access to services. A presentation based on the analysis has already been delivered at a UK Data Service conference in July 2021.

DARS-NIC-195793-R5Y3H.summary: The University of Surrey, working with the Royal College of General Practitioners, is using hospital admission records linked to death registration data. It is studying how mandatory risk assessment for venous thromboembolism (VTE, blood clots) has affected VTE rates and outcomes after surgery in England. The aim is to help target preventive treatment to the patients most at risk. The team has developed a prediction model for VTE after hip and knee surgery, and an abstract on it was accepted for a 2022 international conference.

DARS-NIC-196211-N2W0D.summary: The University of Aberdeen is using hospital, emergency care, outpatient and death registration records for patients in the UK-REBOA trial. The trial compares standard major trauma centre care with and without REBOA, a balloon placed in the main artery to stop life-threatening bleeding after severe injury. The data will help measure 90-day mortality and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to show clinicians how best to treat major trauma and whether REBOA offers value for money to the NHS.

DARS-NIC-196221-K4K3Y.summary: The University of Manchester is using National Diabetes Audit data, including records of people at risk of type 2 diabetes, linked to NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme participation records. It is using them to evaluate how well the programme works and whether it is a good use of NHS funds, so that commissioning decisions can be informed. Several research papers and conference presentations based on the data have already been published.

DARS-NIC-196263-J9Q7Z.summary: University College London is using hospital records (admissions, outpatient and A&E), civil registration death records and cohort-tracing data on women who gave birth. These are linked to Cafcass family court records on care proceedings. The research looks at the health needs of mothers involved in care proceedings, comparing them with other women who gave birth. It aims to give policy makers and services evidence to guide support for vulnerable families.

DARS-NIC-197669-K8J6D.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health and care data covering five local CCG areas. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including demand planning, reporting and identifying people at risk. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways. Reported results include an urgent community response service and a single bed bureau for hospital discharge, plus published 2020/21 annual reports.

DARS-NIC-198066-F4H9X.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that provider invoices relate to patients it is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, linking the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of poor health. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-198104-H9N9N.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB, through the former NHS Castle Point and Rochford CCG, uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+) for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices before payment and, with Prescribing Services Ltd, to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aims are accurate payment for care and more targeted, effective care.

DARS-NIC-198111-C2W4W.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. With Liaison Financial Services, it confirms that the activity billed is the commissioner's responsibility and reviews past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.

DARS-NIC-198119-X9P3J.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB (Thurrock area) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. It checks provider invoices to confirm that the CCG is responsible for the activity claimed, and, through Prescribing Services Ltd, links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted, more effective care planning.

DARS-NIC-198958-C9G0C.summary: Leicestershire County Council, working with other Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland health and care partners, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners). They use it to analyse local needs and service use, and to plan, commission and redesign health and care services under the Better Care Together partnership. The main intended benefit is a more sustainable, better-integrated system, with improved patient flow, quality and access to services.

DARS-NIC-199574-S1W3N.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, linked to GP data for one purpose. It is used to check that provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for, and to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned and managed. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment for care and better targeted support for at-risk patients.

DARS-NIC-199584-M8L6H.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, checking that the care providers bill for is the commissioner's responsibility. The second is risk stratification, linking the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted, planned care.

DARS-NIC-199599-S0T5M.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses mental health and hospital activity data (Mental Health Services Data Set and SUS for Commissioners). It uses them to check that provider invoices are for patients it is responsible for, and to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can plan their care. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment and more targeted, effective care that improves patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-199682-T1L7Z.summary: The University of Cambridge's MRC Epidemiology Unit is using address details for participants in the WRAP weight management trial, taken from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) list cleaning report. It will use them to update contact records, trace participants who have moved and avoid contacting those who have died, so it can invite them to 5- and 10-year follow-up studies. The aim is to give policy makers and commissioners stronger evidence on which weight management programmes offer value for money.

DARS-NIC-199726-F4V3C.summary: King's College London is using hospital admission and outpatient records, together with civil registration death data, for the National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit. The audit assesses how well rheumatology units in England and Wales follow NICE quality standards, aiming to reduce variation in care and improve outcomes. Reported results include the Care Quality Commission using audit-based metrics in its reviews, and a Best Practice Tariff linked to audit data.

DARS-NIC-200139-H2X2Y.summary: Kingston University's Institute for Leadership and Management in Health is using pseudonymised hospital inpatient and outpatient records from 2015 to 2018. It is using them to estimate the direct medical cost to the NHS of nine major diseases caused by HPV (human papillomavirus) across the UK. The aim is to give policy makers evidence on resource use and possible savings as the HPV vaccination programme extends to boys.

DARS-NIC-201243-R7L2M.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care is using pseudonymised NHS Health Check records for adults aged 40-74, linked to hospital admission and death records. It is using them to evaluate and monitor the programme and to see how patients' health outcomes differ. The aim is to help local services improve delivery and target support. Findings have already informed the 2021 NHS Health Check review, published papers and an interactive dashboard, and the announced inclusion of menopause in NHS Health Checks.

DARS-NIC-202004-C5F6G.summary: Bedford Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. It will analyse them to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and addressed. No benefits have been reported yet.

DARS-NIC-203509-L9P1P.summary: Health Innovation Network - South London, an Academic Health Science Network, uses Hospital Episode Statistics data on accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It uses the data to produce aggregated reports on demand for services, variations in care and the impact of service improvements. The intended benefit is better, safer and more efficient care, with investment decisions informed by evidence about what works.

DARS-NIC-203730-Y4V0Z.summary: The University of Bristol, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital admission and death registration data for about 40,890 patients who had lower limb vascular surgery in the National Vascular Registry between 2014 and 2016. It is evaluating patient outcomes, including re-admissions and deaths, in the 12 months after surgery. The aim is to give clinicians and patients better information to guide treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-204228-D8J4D.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services, an independent health research charity, is using hospital records for children and young people. These cover accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. It is studying the causes of variation in emergency admissions for under 5s and of poor child health outcomes. The aim is to give national and local decision makers evidence to improve services and outcomes for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-204376-Y0V5Y.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using linked hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care and death records for patients with remotely monitored heart devices. It is evaluating the Triage-HF Plus pathway, in which patients with a high heart failure risk score are phoned to check for symptoms. The aim is to assess hospital admissions, deaths and healthcare use, and to guide improvements to care. A 2024 paper reported an association with fewer hospital admissions, and the data were submitted to a NICE review.

DARS-NIC-204512-H4R8C.summary: The Northern Cancer Alliance, a network whose staff are employed by NHS England, uses National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records on the time from referral to cancer diagnosis and treatment. It uses them to compare waiting-time performance across hospital trusts and CCGs, spot delays and outliers, and inform discussions on improving cancer pathways. The aim is to help meet national waiting-time standards and improve survival and patient experience. Earlier use of this data has already supported monthly provider reports, funding bids and clinical group discussions.

DARS-NIC-204517-W3N5Z.summary: West Midlands Cancer Alliance, a network hosted by NHS England (West Midlands), is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times across hospitals and clinical commissioning groups to find variation and delays in cancer pathways, aiming to improve survival and patient experience. It reports that earlier access has already informed performance reporting, executive advisory group discussions and work on 104-day breaches.

DARS-NIC-204520-B1V2G.summary: West Yorkshire and Harrogate Cancer Alliance, a network hosted by NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. It will analyse waiting times across cancer pathways, identify variation and long waits, and inform discussions with hospitals and commissioners. The aim is to help meet waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience. The Alliance reports it has already built dashboards and tumour-specific data packs that were used to drive targeted improvement work with trusts.

DARS-NIC-204531-P5L8G.summary: Humber, Coast and Vale Cancer Alliance, with NHS East Riding of Yorkshire Clinical Commissioning Group as the legal data controller, uses patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data. It analyses waiting times and variation across hospital trusts and CCGs, to help improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. Reported results include performance dashboards, and analysis used in bids that secured £780k of 62 day recovery funding.

DARS-NIC-204535-L4S1P.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, which employs the East Midland Cancer Alliance's staff, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from NHS England. It is analysing cancer waiting times by trust, clinical commissioning group (CCG) and tumour site, to find variation and long waits and to work with providers on improving patient pathways. The intended benefit is better survival and patient experience through meeting national waiting time standards. Earlier access has already supported regional analyses of 2 week, 31 day and 62 day performance.

DARS-NIC-204544-H5L0S.summary: Peninsula Cancer Alliance, working with the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, uses National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data covering referral to cancer treatment. They use it to compare waiting-time performance, find variation and long waits, and inform cancer pathway improvements. The main intended benefit is helping meet national cancer waiting times standards. Earlier access supported monthly provider reports, pathway mapping and funding bids.

DARS-NIC-204548-T8H8P.summary: Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance, with the Christie NHS Foundation Trust as the lead organisation, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times across providers and tumour types to find variation and delays, and to guide investment in cancer pathways. The main intended benefit is better performance against national cancer waiting standards, supporting survival and patient experience. Earlier work with similar data included reporting on waiting-time targets and evaluating a shorter referral-to-first-seen period for lung cancer.

DARS-NIC-204550-N7M4D.summary: Kent and Medway Cancer Alliance is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times for cancer diagnosis and treatment, identify variation between hospital trusts and areas, and look at patient flows and long waits. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping meet waiting time standards and improving survival and patient experience. Earlier analysis has already supported monthly reports for provider leaders, funding bids and clinical group discussions.

DARS-NIC-204554-Y7F3H.summary: South East London Cancer Alliance, hosted by Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, is using patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. It uses them to analyse waiting times, patient flows and variation between providers and areas. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. The alliance reports that the data has helped improve performance in Breast and Head and Neck pathways.

DARS-NIC-204557-F0N1T.summary: Thames Valley Cancer Alliance, whose staff are employed by NHS England, is using Cancer Waiting Times data covering referral to treatment for cancer patients across the Thames Valley. It will analyse waiting times, variation between hospitals and commissioners, and patient pathways to guide priorities and investment. The aim is better survival, patient experience and performance against national cancer standards. Earlier work included inter-trust referral analysis and a prostate cancer pathway analysis.

DARS-NIC-204559-J4H7T.summary: Lancashire & South Cumbria Cancer Alliance, whose staff are employed by NHS England, is using patient-level National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records. It is analysing waiting times by tumour type, trust and treatment to find variation and long waits, and to inform cancer pathway improvements and investment. The main aim is to help meet cancer waiting times standards and improve survival and patient experience. Earlier work has produced monthly performance reports and used breach reasons to identify capacity and demand issues at trusts.

DARS-NIC-204562-J5W0T.summary: South Yorkshire & Bassetlaw Cancer Alliance, whose staff are employed by NHS Doncaster Clinical Commissioning Group, is using aggregate Cancer Waiting Times data that includes small numbers. It uses the data to analyse local performance by hospital trust and tumour site, and to identify variation in waits. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping meet waiting time standards and improving patient survival and experience. Earlier access to similar data has been used to inform service improvement.

DARS-NIC-204565-L5J5F.summary: North Central London Cancer Alliance, a cancer services network, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times along cancer pathways, including variation between hospital trusts, to guide priorities and investment. The aim is to help meet national waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience. Earlier use of similar data supported funding bids, capacity and demand analysis, and service commissioning.

DARS-NIC-204571-R1F4T.summary: East of England - North Cancer Alliance, whose staff are mainly employed by NHS England, is using the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records patients' waits from referral to cancer diagnosis and treatment. It will analyse waiting times by hospital trust, tumour type and treatment, and look for delays and unusual cases. The aim is to help the alliance and local providers improve cancer patient pathways, survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-204575-V7X8H.summary: Wessex Cancer Alliance, hosted by NHS England, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times across Wessex providers and commissioners, identify variation and unusually long waits, and inform discussions on improving cancer pathways. The main intended benefit is better delivery of national cancer waiting time standards, supporting survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-204580-F5B0C.summary: The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre NHS Foundation Trust, on behalf of the Cheshire and Merseyside Cancer Alliance, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times and variation between providers and tumour sites, and look at waits beyond the national standards. The aim is to guide priorities and investment to improve cancer pathways and patient outcomes. Earlier access has already supported monthly reports for provider discussions and funding bids.

DARS-NIC-204646-B9G2N.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked to GP and Ways to Wellness records, to evaluate a social prescribing scheme in the West End of Newcastle. It compares secondary care use and costs for treated patients with those elsewhere in Newcastle. The aim is to provide evidence on whether social prescribing works and is cost-effective. The team has published a health outcomes paper in JAMA Network Open, presented results at a seminar, and won a further NIHR grant.

DARS-NIC-204903-P1J7Q.summary: Imperial College London's Small Area Health Statistics Unit (SAHSU) uses hospital, emergency care, death registration and GP data for pandemic planning and research, some of it identifiable. It uses the data for research, surveillance and investigation of environment and health questions, such as the health effects of air pollution. The aim is to provide evidence for public health policy. SAHSU reports 20 peer-reviewed papers in two years, and its reports informed the introduction of London's Ultra Low Emission Zone.

DARS-NIC-205004-D2F8N.summary: The NIHR (National Institute for Health Research) Bioresource, a research organisation, uses Personal Demographic Service data to check participants' identities and whether they have died. This supports Covid-related studies and helps avoid sending distressing messages to families. So far, it has found that 1 in 200 participants had died since last contact, so it can stop trying to contact them.

DARS-NIC-205466-T2F7N.summary: The University of York is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on coronary stenting procedures, linked by the General Medical Council to its records on doctors' characteristics. The study looks at how consultants who graduated in the UK and abroad changed their use of drug-eluting stents after new evidence and guidelines were published. It is a first step towards modelling clinical behaviour. If differences are found, it could support research on reducing unwarranted variation in medical practice.

DARS-NIC-206314-N1N7K.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital records covering accident and emergency attendances and admitted patient care for older people with implantable cardiac devices who have joined the PATTErn study. It will compare physical activity recorded by the devices with unplanned hospital attendances and admissions, to test whether activity falls before these events. The main intended benefit is better understanding of this link, which could help clinicians use device activity data and inform future research.

DARS-NIC-206496-N2C9M.summary: Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, with published outputs being aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. So far, the council has used the data in a place-of-death bulletin, its suicide strategy, an infant mortality needs assessment and strategy, and its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-206516-X1R9B.summary: London Borough of Barnet, a local authority, is using civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work, publishing only aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local service changes that reduce deaths and health inequalities. The council reports it has analysed ward-level mortality to help shape cross-council services.

DARS-NIC-207675-J4L7G.summary: King's College London is using the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a nationally representative survey of adults, to study whether mental illness is linked to perpetrating domestic violence. It also looks at whether prior trauma, alcohol or drug use, or socioeconomic position explain any link, and at differences between men and women. The aim is to inform how mental health services respond to perpetrators. A paper on intimate partner violence perpetration among secondary mental health service users has been published in BJPsych Open.

DARS-NIC-208561-Z1M7V.summary: Imperial College London's Small Area Health Statistics Unit (SAHSU) holds Birth Notification Data (NN4B), linked to birth registrations, and may keep it securely but not otherwise use it. The unit uses such data to study how environmental factors like air pollution and noise affect health, including birth outcomes, to inform public health policy. Its research has appeared in peer-reviewed papers, conference presentations and policy briefings to the UK Health Security Agency.

DARS-NIC-209174-W2H3G.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics) linked to Patient Reported Outcome Measures (patient questionnaires on quality of life after elective surgery). It is studying how patient safety incidents, such as pressure ulcers and infections, affect patients' quality of life, and the monetary value of that loss. The aim is to inform investment in safety improvements. Preliminary findings were cited in an OECD report, "The Economics of Patient Safety – from Analysis to Action" (2020).

DARS-NIC-209200-S9H5R.summary: The Royal College of Psychiatrists is using pseudonymised Mental Health Services Data Set records for people aged 65 and under with first episode psychosis who are cared for by Early Intervention in Psychosis teams. It uses them for the National Clinical Audit of Psychosis, checking the data against audit data and measuring care against national standards. The aim is to improve the quality of NHS care for people with psychosis while reducing the data collection burden on teams. A 2022 feasibility study gave a baseline for how reliably this routine data reflects audit performance.

DARS-NIC-20951-D2K6S.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using Personal Demographic Service data, which includes details such as name, address and date of birth. It uses them to produce census, population and migration statistics, including population estimates and projections. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions on funding and services, including health and social care. ONS published early analysis from its Refugee Integration Outcomes project in June 2023, covering health and housing outcomes for resettled refugees.

DARS-NIC-210151-K9C7G.summary: IQVIA Technology Services Ltd., a commercial supplier, uses Hospital Episode Statistics (inpatient, outpatient and A&E) and Emergency Care Data Set records. It uses them to identify hospital sites and estimate their patient numbers for clinical trials, with outputs aggregated and small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is faster site identification and patient recruitment. By September 2024, 16 ongoing trials referenced the data, with 230 patients enrolled and improved recruitment rates reported.

DARS-NIC-21083-B6C5J.summary: The University of Surrey is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil death registration data, linked to GP surveillance data from the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) Research and Surveillance Centre. It is using them to monitor infectious and respiratory diseases in England, including how well influenza vaccines work and how severe illness is. The main intended benefit is earlier public health action, better vaccine effectiveness and a health system better prepared for influenza outbreaks.

DARS-NIC-211082-P5V9W.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, working with the five Norfolk and Waveney clinical commissioning groups (CCGs), uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, linked with GP data. It is used to plan and commission health services across the area, including patient stratification and population health management. The main intended benefits are better planning of services and patient pathways, fewer avoidable emergency admissions and a better understanding of local population health.

DARS-NIC-212803-G8K5K.summary: Northumberland County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan services, support suicide audits and protect public health, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include an automatically updating mortality dashboard, a births dashboard, and analysis identifying clusters of disease and suicide.

DARS-NIC-212898-X4C9W.summary: NHS Arden and Greater East Midlands Commissioning Support Unit processes pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, cancer waiting times and diagnostic imaging data, including local provider flows, for NHS England. It uses the data to monitor contracts, reconcile activity and validate invoices for NHS England's direct commissioning, including care for Armed Forces members and people in the justice system. The main intended benefit is better commissioning, planning and financial control of these services.

DARS-NIC-213403-P3R8Q.summary: NHS Improvement uses pseudonymised hospital, outpatient, accident and emergency, imaging, patient-reported outcome and death registration data from English hospitals. It uses the data for the National Consultant Information Programme (NCIP), an online portal where consultants and speciality grade doctors review their own activity and patient outcomes, including deaths within 90 days of procedures, against local and national benchmarks. The aim is to improve patient care through learning and appraisal. Trusts using the portal report that it has helped with mortality and morbidity meetings, quality improvement and appraisal.

DARS-NIC-213806-J2X7K.summary: Medway Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health duties. It uses the data to produce needs assessments, health strategies and reports, aiming to help it respond to local health needs and inequalities. Reported benefits include updated health profiles for local areas and analysis presented to the Kent and Medway ICP Sub Committee.

DARS-NIC-215003-F6L3H.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB uses hospital activity data from SUS for Commissioners (Secondary User Services), linked with GP data, for risk stratification carried out by Prescribing Services Ltd. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy service use, so GPs can target care and commissioners can plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-215080-Y5K7C.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data, linked with GP data, to carry out risk stratification, which is carried out for it by Prescribing Services Ltd. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or of using many services, so that care can be planned and GPs can target support. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning of services, leading to improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-215114-S6J7P.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB (South Norfolk area) uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data, for risk stratification. Prescribing Services Ltd applies an algorithm to produce risk scores that identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or of using multiple services. This helps commissioners plan care and helps GPs target support, with the aim of improving patient experience through more effective commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-216638-L9N4N.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, with South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit and Care Unbound Ltd (trading as HERE), is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), which includes clinical and cost details. It is used to plan and manage health services for the population of the two clinical commissioning groups (CCGs), including the musculoskeletal (MSK) contract. The main intended benefit is effective contract management and financial reconciliation between commissioners and providers for planned MSK care.

DARS-NIC-216853-V1V1H.summary: Kingston University is using civil registration death records, linked to national heart attack audit data (MINAP) and supplied without identifying details. It is studying whether ambulance patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome who have a 12-lead electrocardiogram before reaching hospital differ in 30-day and one-year survival, and how its use has changed over time. The intended benefit is better use of this test, leading to improved outcomes after a heart attack.

DARS-NIC-217282-M3J8J.summary: Wakefield Metropolitan District Council's public health team is using the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a national survey on mental health. It will analyse the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, commissioning of services and advice to NHS commissioners, and to produce reports, dashboards and infographics on mental health in the local population. The main intended benefit is giving local partners better insight into mental health needs, to inform service provision.

DARS-NIC-218380-R8L2R.summary: Imperial College London's Business School is using demographic data on GP practice registrations, alongside online review data, to study why patients change GPs. It looks at whether star ratings on the NHS website influence which practice patients choose, and whether this differs between wealthier and poorer areas. The main intended benefit is evidence to help NHS England improve the information it gives patients. Initial findings have been presented at an NHS England economics seminar and at academic conferences, including the NBER summer meetings in 2022.

DARS-NIC-218736-V3S0Y.summary: Peterborough City Council, a local authority, uses Hospital Episode Statistics (inpatient, outpatient, critical care and A&E records) and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including the impact of and recovery from Covid-19.

DARS-NIC-218988-L5K0G.summary: NHS Black Country ICB uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service, containing clinical and financial information) for commissioning health services across the Black Country and West Birmingham area. The data is analysed to profile the population and to support joined-up health and social care, with the aim of identifying where services can be improved. Reported results include dashboards combining health and social care data, which Wolverhampton City Council uses to understand pressure points in the care system.

DARS-NIC-219055-K4F8R.summary: The University of York's Centre for Health Economics is using pseudonymised hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to calculate health deprivation indicators for every small area (LSOA) in England. These cover emergency hospitalisations and hospitalisations for anxiety or depression, and they feed into the English Indices of Deprivation 2019. The aim is to help public bodies plan targeted action on health inequalities. The reported benefits describe how the 2015 indices were used, for example in funding decisions and local health needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-219359-T5B0V.summary: Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Foundation Trust supports University College London, which is using pseudonymised civil registration of death data (life status and age) alongside national congenital heart disease audit records. The study examines whether ethnic group, deprivation, antenatal diagnosis and hospital case volume affect long-term survival and repeat operations in children with complex heart defects. It aims to give families and services better long-term outcome information. Findings have been published in two papers and used in a patient information leaflet.

DARS-NIC-219944-G9X4V.summary: The British Thoracic Society is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records, linked to its 2018-19 national audit of adults treated in hospital for community acquired pneumonia. It will use the linked data to measure outcomes such as deaths after discharge and readmissions, and to compare care between hospitals across the UK. The intended benefit is to help hospitals reduce unwarranted variation in care and lower pneumonia deaths.

DARS-NIC-220105-B3Z3S.summary: The University of Liverpool is analysing the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a nationally representative survey of adults in England. It is studying how alcohol misuse and mental disorder occur together across socioeconomic groups, and how this links to physical health conditions. The aim is to help target alcohol screening and support. Preliminary findings have been presented to a project steering group, at a Society for the Study of Addiction conference and to the Medical Research Council.

DARS-NIC-224512-Z9W0B.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, acting for four Lincolnshire clinical commissioning groups, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health and other health service data, linked with GP data. It uses this to plan and commission health services, identify patients and groups at higher risk, and manage demand across the Lincolnshire Sustainability and Transformation Partnership. The stated aim is to design better care pathways, improve patient flow and target early help to the people who need it most.

DARS-NIC-225591-Z2B1C.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB uses pseudonymised (identifying details removed) health and care data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer, births and deaths records, with clinical and financial information. NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit processes it to plan and commission health services for the local population, including understanding needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow.

DARS-NIC-225927-H5J7J.summary: Surrey and Sussex Cancer Alliance, through its lead employer Royal Surrey NHS Foundation Trust, uses national Cancer Waiting Times data covering referral to cancer treatment. It analyses waits and variation between trusts, clinical commissioning groups and tumour types to guide priorities and investment, aiming to improve cancer pathways, survival and patient experience. It reports producing monthly data packs and dashboards for trusts that have identified outliers and prompted local improvement work.

DARS-NIC-226185-B6C2J.summary: The University of Hull is using hospital records from England covering admissions and emergency department attendances. It is studying people with alcohol dependence and alcohol withdrawal, looking at what predicts readmission and repeat attendance, including length of stay. The aim is to inform better care pathways for people admitted with unplanned alcohol withdrawal. So far, the data has supported a successful funding bid for an Alcohol Care Team at Hull Royal Infirmary.

DARS-NIC-226261-M2T0Q.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent health research charity, uses hospital, emergency care and community services patient data from NHS England. It uses the data to research the quality and fairness of health and social care and to inform health policy, aiming to improve services and care for NHS patients. Its reported results include a report on ethnicity coding that the Race Disparity Unit adopted, and a children's health analysis presented to a national council.

DARS-NIC-226296-S7T2Y.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, linked with GP records, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy service use. Prescribing Services Limited carries out the risk scoring. The aim is to help GPs target care and help commissioners plan services, reducing avoidable emergency admissions and improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-226603-C7K2R.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses SUS for Commissioners data, which is hospital activity data linked to GP data at NHS number level. It uses this for risk stratification, which gives patients risk scores to identify who is likely to need high levels of care. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The stated aim is better case management in primary care and more effective commissioning.

DARS-NIC-226613-D8S2N.summary: NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data, to run risk stratification. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services, so GPs and commissioners can plan and target their care. Prescribing Services Limited carries out the processing. The main intended benefit is better planned and more effective care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-228637-P6N0L.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using hospital-level National Diabetes Audit data on young adults aged 16 to 25 with diabetes. It is part of the TOGETHER study, which is evaluating group clinics for young adults. The analysis will compare the study clinics with other services in England on patient make-up, treatment targets and care processes, and track changes over time. It aims to show whether clinical outcomes worsen where group clinics are introduced.

DARS-NIC-228903-Z0F4V.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust, for the Transforming Cancer Services Team (London), uses national cancer waiting times data. The team analyses it across London to compare performance, spot variation and support discussions on improving cancer patient pathways. The aim is shorter waits for diagnosis and treatment, and better survival and patient experience. Reported results include informing London recovery planning after COVID-19 and supporting a redesign of the sarcoma pathway.

DARS-NIC-230360-H3Y3C.summary: Erasmus University Rotterdam, an academic organisation, is using civil registration death data to find out whether UK patients from the SYNTAX heart trial are alive or have died. The SYNTAXES study uses this to assess survival of more than 10 years after patients had either a stent procedure (PCI) or bypass surgery (CABG) for coronary artery disease. The main intended benefit is long-term evidence to help doctors choose the best treatment.

DARS-NIC-230538-B9J9Z.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council is using death registration records and hospital activity data for commissioners. It will link these with local health and social care data to show what services people use, and what is spent, in the last year of life. The aim is to help local partners redesign services so more people have a good death at home or in their preferred place, while using money sustainably.

DARS-NIC-231737-J7C6H.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, acting for the Airedale and Wharfedale area, uses pseudonymised (identifying details removed) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and births and deaths data. It uses this to plan and commission health services, including studying population needs, redesigning services and identifying patients at risk of hospital admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient flow, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-233512-B7C4W.summary: NEC Software Solutions UK Limited, a commercial company acting for the Society of British Neurological Surgeons, uses pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for people who have had neurosurgery in England. It uses them to run the Neurosurgical National Audit Programme, which checks surgical outcomes, including deaths, and identifies trusts or surgeons with outlying performance. The aim is to improve patient safety and outcomes. Reported results include published papers and trust reports that helped GIRFT direct resources to the trusts most in need.

DARS-NIC-23410-W8N9L.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic organisation, used hospital records covering admissions, outpatient and A&E care, patient-reported outcomes and death registrations. It used them to study how the Care Quality Commission's inspection and rating system affects hospital performance and quality of care, so the Department of Health and Social Care can improve it. The final report went to the department and the Commission, five journal articles were published, and the findings were presented to the Commission's board.

DARS-NIC-234297-P4M5G.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is using linked hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and A&E) and death registration data. It is using them to study how people with congenital heart disease use NHS services and what outcomes they have. The aim is to build better measures of service quality and outcomes that can inform commissioning and improve services.

DARS-NIC-234656-C3J1D.summary: University College London (UCL) is using linked hospital admission records and demographic data for children born in England between 2005 and 2014, along with their mothers' delivery records. It is studying how air pollution, housing conditions, and family factors such as parents' country of birth affect children's hospital admissions, especially for respiratory infections and preventable conditions. The aim is to give local authorities and NHS bodies evidence to improve child health and access to care. So far, findings have been presented at two conferences, and a paper has been submitted to a journal.

DARS-NIC-234915-J3K4V.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB, working for six Staffordshire clinical commissioning groups, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and death and birth records, which include clinical and financial information. It uses them to plan and commission health services, such as reviewing patient pathways, forecasting demand and monitoring providers. The aim is to match services to the population's needs. The CCGs report that the data has helped them monitor in-year projects and deliver integrated care.

DARS-NIC-237669-T9W5N.summary: The University of Nottingham is using pseudonymised hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked to death registration data, for patients who had surgery between 2007 and 2017. The study looks at how earlier strokes and heart attacks affect outcomes after surgery, and how this varies by timing, treatment and type of operation. The intended benefit is better information to help patients and clinicians decide whether and when to operate.

DARS-NIC-238282-X0B6H.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other health service data, linked with GP data, covering the Coventry and Warwickshire area. It uses this to plan and commission health services, understand local health needs and identify patients at risk, with the aim of improving patient pathways and services. Under an earlier approval, South Warwickshire CCG used linked data to show which trialled services helped patients, supporting decisions to expand funding or adjust services.

DARS-NIC-238370-G8Z6V.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB is using hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient activity. It is using them to build statistical models that produce growth projections and length of stay estimates by specialty, supporting local operational planning. Using national data is intended to make these estimates more accurate and reliable than local data alone. Initial length of stay work by specialty has already been used to update a length of stay fitting tool in open source simulation software built by the team.

DARS-NIC-238613-D3W0L.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised hospital admission records, patient reported outcome measures and death registration data, linked to National Joint Registry data. It is studying how implant choice, surgical approach and patient frailty relate to results after a first knee replacement, such as quality of life, mortality and revision surgery. The intended benefit is better-informed shared decisions for patients, clinicians and NHS commissioners.

DARS-NIC-239092-Q9Q3X.summary: Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust is using pseudonymised maternity records from the Maternity Services Data Set, covering 2017/18 to 2021/22. It is studying maternal and fetal factors linked to stillbirths, especially term stillbirths, and differences between ethnic groups. The aim is to improve evidence on risk so that care for pregnant women and their babies, particularly from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, can be better tailored and stillbirths reduced.

DARS-NIC-240279-Y2V2N.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked hospital, emergency care and civil registration death records, which it links to the QResearch database of pseudonymised GP records. The data supports medical research into causes of disease, drug safety and risk prediction tools, including urgent COVID-19 research. The aim is to give patients, the NHS and researchers a better understanding of disease. Its research has already informed NICE guidelines, and QRISK3 was implemented in the NHS from 2018.

DARS-NIC-241634-Z3F2L.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, working with NHS North Kirklees and NHS Wakefield Clinical Commissioning Groups, uses pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care data that includes clinical and financial information. It is used to plan and commission health services, monitor contracts, and understand the needs of the local population. The main intended benefit is better planning of patient pathways and services.

DARS-NIC-242146-J2W3T.summary: The University of Birmingham is using hospital records from NHS England (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients), linked to GP data from The Health Improvement Network. It is used for epidemiology, health services, public health and health economics research, including studies of childbirth and maternal health. The aim is to produce findings that can change clinical practice and policy, for example by informing NICE guidance on antibiotics given during caesarean sections.

DARS-NIC-242415-V9T5D.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit is using pseudonymised hospital admissions and accident and emergency records (Hospital Episode Statistics). It is comparing heart and circulation events in these records with those collected in the PATCH prostate cancer trial. The aim is to test whether national electronic records could supplement or partly replace manual trial follow-up, which could reduce costs and workload and mean fewer hospital visits for participants.

DARS-NIC-242486-R1G4D.summary: The University of Sheffield is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults aged 16 or over. It is studying how psychosis overlaps with conditions such as bipolar disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder and autism, and how childhood trauma and social factors relate to psychotic symptoms. The aim is to improve understanding of mental illness and inform treatment and public mental health. A 2021 paper in Psychological Medicine reported a strong association between autistic traits and psychotic-like experiences.

DARS-NIC-243359-X4T5M.summary: The Cambridge Centre for Health Services Research is working with partner universities and RAND Europe on the BRACE NIHR Rapid Evaluation Centre. It uses pseudonymised, record-level hospital data: emergency care, admitted patient, A&E and outpatient records. The data support quick evaluations of new ways of organising and delivering health and care services. The main intended benefit is high-quality evidence that helps decide which innovations to adopt and which not to pursue.

DARS-NIC-243790-Y8K8C.summary: Carnall Farrar Limited, a consultancy, uses record-level hospital, emergency care, outpatient, community and mental health data from NHS England. It uses the data to build analysis tools and reports for NHS organisations and other clients, covering forecasting, capacity planning, benchmarking and population health. The aim is to help the NHS find where performance, efficiency and finances can improve. Reported results include a Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust elective recovery plan and a south-east London mental health bed capacity model.

DARS-NIC-24422-R3W3S.summary: The University of Cambridge is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer registration and death records for a randomised trial of vitamin D (colecalciferol) supplementation in people with kidney failure on dialysis. It will check the trial's main outcomes, including survival, and follow participants over the long term without further contact. The aim is to show whether colecalciferol is a safe, cheaper alternative that improves survival. So far, the data has supported safety reviews, and aggregated results have informed trial committee decisions.

DARS-NIC-244278-F3V4X.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB, acting for the former Corby clinical commissioning group (CCG) area, uses pseudonymised health and care data, including clinical and financial information from hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other services. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including population health analysis, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-245768-V0N2T.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using cancer registration, death registration and demographic data to study men with prostate cancer managed by watchful waiting. The aim is to build and test models that predict which cancers will progress, and to see whether biological markers improve on standard clinical factors. The main intended benefit is helping patients and clinicians decide who can safely avoid unnecessary radical treatment. Published papers, including a 2021 Cancer Reports validation of a cell cycle progression score, have already come from the study.

DARS-NIC-245962-Y6W3Z.summary: Walsall Metropolitan Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. These include needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of analysing local health inequalities. Reported results include informing its air quality and suicide prevention strategies, and sharing analysis of violence-related admissions with West Midlands Police.

DARS-NIC-24629-X6B6N.summary: IQVIA Solutions UK Limited, a supplier, uses hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) linked to The Health Improvement Network (THIN) GP records. It supports medical research, including drug safety, into how primary and hospital care relate. Published studies using the linked data include a smoking study featured in a NICE press release and a frailty index that NICE recommends in its multimorbidity guideline.

DARS-NIC-24688-J6W3F.summary: The Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them in its public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. A new joint strategic needs assessment released in 2023 focused on the "Top 5s" of ill health, risk factors, hospitalisation and wider determinants of health.

DARS-NIC-24810-Q6T3B.summary: The University of Birmingham holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering A&E, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and civil registration death data for people in its COPD cohort study. Under this agreement the data is only kept securely, with no new processing. The original study used it to build prognostic models predicting hospital admissions and death in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), to support better patient management and service planning.

DARS-NIC-248117-P2K4S.summary: St Helens Council's public health team uses hospital records from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and the Emergency Care Data Set, covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so that local health challenges are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-249035-R2Z5Y.summary: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission, accident and emergency, critical care and death registration records for patients ventilated during COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) flare-ups. It will use them to follow readmissions and deaths for a year after discharge and to validate a bedside tool that predicts death. The main intended benefit is wider use of lifesaving non-invasive ventilation through better clinical decisions.

DARS-NIC-250023-M6T9H.summary: Public Health Scotland is using hospital admissions data for England (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care), limited to alcohol-related conditions. It will compare alcohol-attributable hospital admissions and deaths in Scotland with England, to assess the impact of minimum unit pricing for alcohol, introduced in Scotland in May 2018. The findings could help the Scottish Parliament decide whether the policy should continue.

DARS-NIC-25007-J9M9P.summary: Birmingham City Council's public health team uses hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and mental health data from NHS England. It uses them to support its public health and commissioning duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, benchmarked against similar areas. Reported results include a substance misuse needs assessment that informed the commissioning of drug and alcohol treatment services.

DARS-NIC-250100-R3W1G.summary: Glasgow Caledonian University, an academic institution, is using a list cleaning report that gives current names, addresses and whether people have died, for women in the ProLong study originally recruited in Birmingham. It is using this to contact them accurately for ProLong20+, a follow-up study of pelvic floor problems after childbirth, such as incontinence and prolapse. The main intended benefit is a better response rate and better knowledge of how these problems change over time, helping to plan future NHS services.

DARS-NIC-250326-W3F1B.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (Sunderland area) uses pseudonymised hospital and mental health data, including clinical and financial information. It uses this to plan and commission health services, covering population health management, service redesign and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways. It reports that population segmentation now feeds into commissioning decisions and service transformation.

DARS-NIC-252024-D7R9W.summary: The Royal College of Paediatrics & Child Health (RCPCH) is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data for the National Paediatric Diabetes Audit. It will analyse hospital admissions of children and young people with diabetes in a five-year comparative report, to show admission trends and support efforts to reduce admissions. Earlier analysis under a previous agreement was used by commissioners when deciding how to fund diabetes-related technologies.

DARS-NIC-252496-Z7M8H.summary: NHS Dorset ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, identifiable by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers and to carry out risk stratification. Invoice validation, done by Liaison Financial Services Ltd, confirms that charges are the CCG's responsibility and identifies overpayments to recover. Risk stratification, done by Prescribing Services Limited, links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefits are recovering money that would otherwise be lost and improved, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-252902-C7C6P.summary: The University of Glasgow is using pseudonymised survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, which covers mental health in adults. A PhD project will study risk factors for suicidal thoughts and behaviour in men, and how these differ from those in women. The intended benefit is to help health and social care services recognise and respond to men experiencing suicidal thoughts.

DARS-NIC-253220-Q1X8H.summary: The University of Manchester is using pseudonymised patient-level hospital admission, critical care and death records, linked to GP records from the ResearchOne database. It is evaluating OptimiseRx, a software tool that alerts prescribers to possible prescribing errors, and its effect on hazardous prescribing, hospitalisations and deaths. It is also assessing the tool's cost-effectiveness for NHS England. The intended benefit is evidence to support recommendations for safer prescribing.

DARS-NIC-25634-T2Z1Z.summary: MedeAnalytics International Limited, a commercial supplier, uses monthly pseudonymised, non-sensitive Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and Emergency Care Data Set records covering admitted patient care, outpatients and A&E. It uses them in an online analytics service that gives NHS and social care customers national comparators to prioritise service redesign. Benchmarking has already led one provider to correct A&E coding, with a £90k credit to the commissioner, and helped a CCG win about £190k for diabetes services.

DARS-NIC-25780-T1F4G.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital admission records, death registration data and national COPD audit rehabilitation data. It is studying how pulmonary rehabilitation affects hospital readmissions and survival in people with COPD, and will publish only aggregated results. The aim is to improve how rehabilitation services are designed, commissioned and delivered. A national report on patient outcomes has been published, and local reports have been given to services and commissioners.

DARS-NIC-258079-G7W1Y.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised NHS Digital birth and civil registration records for children born after assisted reproductive technology (such as IVF), and for their naturally conceived siblings. These will be linked with national school records to compare educational outcomes. The aim is to show whether these children are at higher risk of learning problems, to inform fertility regulation, schools and families.

DARS-NIC-258494-J2Q5M.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using civil registrations of death data (fact, place and cause of death) for DETERMIND, a research study led by the University of Sussex that follows people recently diagnosed with dementia and their carers. The data will be added to the study's research datasets, used to manage participants' withdrawal from the study and to prompt a carer bereavement survey. The study aims to build evidence on inequalities in dementia care, costs and outcomes, to inform policy and practice.

DARS-NIC-258780-S9H7G.summary: The University of Cambridge, with the University of Edinburgh and Royal Brompton and Harefield NHS Trust, is using hospital admissions, diagnostic imaging and death registration data covering England. They are studying how the 2016 NICE guidelines on investigating stable chest pain changed the use of cardiac imaging tests, and what happened to patients afterwards. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide future clinical practice, service planning and research.

DARS-NIC-25945-T8Q0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge is keeping hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and patient tracking data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) for an interim period. It uses them to follow up consented BEST2 study participants, checking cancer outcomes to gather long-term safety and effectiveness data on the Cytosponge™ test for Barrett's oesophagus. The aim is to inform whether this less invasive test could replace some endoscopies. Reported benefits include informing the design of the BEST3 trial and a published paper on a methylation panel biomarker.

DARS-NIC-259538-Q4V0W.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is using the 2017 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey, which covers children and young people aged 2 to 19. The research team will study how common body dysmorphic disorder is, how it varies with age and sex, which other conditions and environmental factors go with it, and what impairment it causes. The aim is to improve detection and diagnosis and to inform the design and commissioning of child and adolescent mental health services.

DARS-NIC-260281-Y6X5N.summary: University College London (UCL), working with Barts Health NHS Trust, is using identifiable hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for people recruited to the MASTER study, who have had aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. It will track hospital stays for heart failure and abnormal heart rhythms, to see how heart muscle scarring relates to these outcomes. The intended benefit is better identification of patients at highest risk, so treatment can be targeted earlier.

DARS-NIC-261216-Q1L2Q.summary: The University of Sheffield is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, along with patient demographic linking data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS), in the PJI Study. The study examines whether invasive dental procedures cause late prosthetic joint infections, which occur three or more months after a joint replacement. Its results should give evidence to support or challenge current UK dental guidance on giving antibiotics before such procedures, as well as guidance used elsewhere in the world.

DARS-NIC-261326-F9S5D.summary: The University of Cambridge is using hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and a mortality list-cleaning report. These are linked to data from the Pregnancy Outcome Prediction Study, which followed 4,212 mothers and their children. The aim is to see whether pregnancy data can predict later health and educational outcomes, so that risks can be spotted and addressed early. Findings have already been published in peer-reviewed journals on children's long-term outcomes after common pregnancy complications.

DARS-NIC-262206-F1P5Z.summary: The University of Glasgow is using pseudonymised hospital admission, maternity and death records for women in England who had a pregnancy-related episode between 1997 and 2017. It is studying peripartum cardiomyopathy, a rare pregnancy-related type of heart failure, to describe how common it is and what outcomes follow in the UK. The main intended benefit is UK-specific evidence to help clinicians inform patients about their condition and about the risks of future pregnancies.

DARS-NIC-262908-X5F4Q.summary: The University of Leicester's cardiac surgery research group is using hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death records for patients with heart conditions in England. It is using them to model surgical trials on a computer before they run, testing whether they are feasible and how to design them. The aim is to produce trial proposals on priority heart surgery questions. So far, it has supported the design and funding applications of four trials and published its method in the European Heart Journal.

DARS-NIC-263738-V6V9N.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and outpatients) and Emergency Care Data Set data. It is using them to compare hospital and emergency service use and medication safety between GP practices testing an intervention for people taking multiple medicines (polypharmacy) and those giving usual care. The aim is to judge whether the intervention works and is cost effective, and to help improve medicines use in these patients.

DARS-NIC-264102-D2X7J.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using pseudonymised hospital admission records and cancer registration data for patients in England. The research compares the risk of developing cancer after X-ray guided endovascular repair of aortic aneurysms with the risk after open surgical repair. The main intended benefit is giving clinicians and patients clearer information about radiation-related risk when choosing a treatment.

DARS-NIC-264169-J6F6T.summary: NHS Devon ICB uses identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service data for commissioners) and Personal Demographic Service data. It uses them to check invoices from care providers, confirming that the CCG is the responsible commissioner before payment. It also links hospital data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aims are accurate payment of providers and earlier, better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-265261-W7P8W.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England hospital records (admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and death records for people who took part in the UK Prospective Diabetes Study, a trial of blood pressure and glucose-lowering treatments in type 2 diabetes. It is linking them to see how the treatments affected dementia, major vascular disease, health service use and costs over the long term. The aim is better evidence for clinical guidelines and funding decisions. The original study has led to 122 manuscripts as of October 2023.

DARS-NIC-266008-T3S9D.summary: NHS England's Operations and Information directorate is using national patient-level cancer waiting times data, linked to deprivation, age and gender information. It is a one-off internal analysis to see whether deprivation, age and gender are associated with cancer waiting times. The intended benefit is a better understanding of how deprivation affects access to and effectiveness of cancer pathways, and whether adding these details to the data set routinely would be worthwhile.

DARS-NIC-266178-B3W1S.summary: Hartlepool Borough Council, a local authority, is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatient visits. It uses them in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so the council and its partners can respond to the needs of local people, particularly the most disadvantaged.

DARS-NIC-26646-M9Q0J.summary: The Public Service Consultants Limited (trading as 2020 Delivery Ltd), a consultancy, is using a pseudonymised extract of Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data. It is researching patterns of frequent A&E attendance for the British Red Cross, including what leads people to become high intensity users and how they can reduce their use. The main intended benefit is better support for these patients, and less pressure on emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-267223-D4Q3F.summary: Swansea University, an academic organisation, holds pseudonymised hospital records from Accident and Emergency and Admitted Patient Care (Hospital Episode Statistics) for twelve English emergency departments between 2010/11 and 2018/19. It uses them in a study, funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, of how different models of GPs working in emergency departments affect care. The aim is to build stronger evidence on the effectiveness, safety and resource use of these models.

DARS-NIC-26815-F8H6B.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England is using linked hospital records, patient-reported outcome measures, and death registration data to study access to and outcomes of elective hip and knee replacement for patients with long-term conditions. The research aims to show how these conditions affect who gets surgery and how well it works, informing care for patients. So far, papers and a PhD thesis have been published, and the study contributed evidence to a NICE guideline scoping workshop.

DARS-NIC-268750-B3T4W.summary: The University of Bristol is using aggregate, non-identifying Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data on monthly attendances across Greater Manchester.
