It is evaluating whether the Communities in Charge of Alcohol programme, which trains local volunteers as alcohol health champions, reduces A&E attendances. The aim is to show whether the programme works. So far, the team has published open access journal articles, including in BMC Public Health.

DARS-NIC-27085-C5L5G.summary: Imperial College London is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mental health, cancer, birth and death records for the SCAMP study of adolescents. It is examining whether mobile phones and other radio wave technologies affect young people's cognition, behaviour and mental health. The aim is to inform a review of UK advice on children's phone use. The study team has published papers on cohort profile, exposure validation, night-time screen use and sleep, and social network use.

DARS-NIC-272253-P9X9Y.summary: King's College London researchers are using hospital, emergency care and mental health service records for people treated for anorexia nervosa. They are using them in the TRIANGLE trial, which tests whether online support for patients and carers after leaving inpatient care improves long-term wellbeing and affects the number of days spent in hospital. The researchers hope the findings will inform NHS care decisions and help address rising readmissions for the condition.

DARS-NIC-272668-H4M3S.summary: The Wolfson Institute of Preventive Medicine, an academic body working with Queen Mary University of London, holds survey data from the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey on mental disorder in the household population. It is using the data to study the link between mental disorder and violence in England and Wales, with the aim of informing policy and services. So far, the team has linked key variables across the 2000, 2007 and 2014 surveys, and has been invited to join a London violence reduction advisory group.

DARS-NIC-272984-V0C5X.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB (a sub-ICB location) is using pseudonymised hospital activity and cost data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS) for commissioners. It links this with GP and social care data to plan and commission health services, assess population needs, identify patients at risk and monitor contracts. The main intended benefit is better-planned, higher-quality services that meet local needs, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-27404-D5Z3F.summary: University College London (UCL) is using linked hospital, accident and emergency, critical care, outpatient and death records for children and young people in England, combined with school data. It is testing how well health and education records can be linked, and studying how school outcomes relate to emergency hospital use, including for children with chronic conditions. The aim is to inform NHS and local policy. Results so far include a peer-reviewed paper on linkage error, published in September 2021.

DARS-NIC-274251-H0G6M.summary: King's College London is using linked hospital admission and death registration data on patients aged 60 or over who had hip fracture surgery in England or Wales in 2017. It is studying whether more frequent, longer or more comprehensive physiotherapy leads to better recovery, including discharge, readmission and survival. The aim is to inform quality improvement and reduce unwarranted variation in rehabilitation care. A published paper found that more frequent physiotherapy was associated with earlier discharge, and the results have been shared with physiotherapists and the Royal College of Physicians.

DARS-NIC-274291-Q5T1S.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB, with NHS Bassetlaw CCG as joint data controller, uses pseudonymised health, social care, mortality and prescribing data covering clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and monitor commissioned health services for the local population, including reporting, demand planning and patient stratification. The stated aim is better decisions and improved service quality. Reported results include a "safe today" quality dashboard and an infection outbreak dashboard.

DARS-NIC-276970-B8Y4H.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is using linked Hospital Episode Statistics and civil death registration records that carry no direct identifiers. It is analysing them to understand demand for healthcare and how the quality of care can be improved, so that the NHS and policy makers can plan for the future. Outputs from this work were used with Imperial College London to model how to allocate elective care capacity during the COVID-19 pandemic, which helped NHS policy makers make resource decisions.

DARS-NIC-277499-D3D0X.summary: Optum Health Solutions UK Limited, a commercial health services company, uses national hospital activity and payment data (Secondary Uses Service Payment by Results) to build four analytics products for NHS commissioners. These produce benchmarks comparing organisations, to help them find where care or spending differs and where savings or better care are possible. Reported results include a changed heart bypass pathway at one hospital, with £150,000 of savings written into the hospital contract.

DARS-NIC-27803-W8G1B.summary: University College London is using Hospital Episode Statistics hospital admission and critical care data, linked to routine clinical data from patients in participating critical care units. It is building a research database to track the long-term outcomes of people who have survived critical illness. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians, patients and researchers make better-informed decisions. So far, the wider CC-HIC database has led to 2 published papers and 5 published abstracts.

DARS-NIC-279476-Y8N7J.summary: University of Bristol's medical school is using NHS hospital, emergency care and mental health records for children and young people with chronic fatigue syndrome or myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME). It is using them in a trial of FITNET-NHS, an online cognitive behavioural therapy, compared with activity management. The aim is to find out whether FITNET-NHS works and is good value for money in the NHS, so the findings can inform future NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-28051-Q3K7L.summary: University College London (UCL) is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to build a classification of health needs for small areas, broken down by patient ethnicity. The aim is to show how health needs differ between areas and how stable they are over time. The intended benefit is to help clinical commissioning groups, local authorities and care providers set budgeting, commissioning and screening priorities.

DARS-NIC-280606-N9Z7W.summary: King's College London, an academic organisation, is using hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in the UK arm of the STARRT-AKI trial and a linked observational study. The records will be used to work out the NHS costs and outcomes of starting kidney replacement therapy earlier rather than at the standard time in acute kidney injury. The aim is to inform UK decisions and clinical guidelines on timing. Preliminary results have been presented at a workshop in Paris in September 2023.

DARS-NIC-281073-Y5G3F.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and social care data, some identifiable and some pseudonymised, for invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning. This helps check that providers are paid correctly, identify patients at risk of poor health, and plan services to meet local needs. The register reports that the data has helped match services to population needs and monitor in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-281239-V4X7H.summary: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. The council uses it to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The main intended benefit is local services targeted at the greatest needs, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. So far, it has been used to examine COVID-19 coded deaths and improve understanding of local drug-related deaths and suicides.

DARS-NIC-283774-B9Z6K.summary: Imperial College London is using linked hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient, mental health and death registration data for very preterm and surgical babies born in England between 2007 and 2020. It is using the data to study long-term health and education outcomes and how care in neonatal units affects them, aiming to improve neonatal care and inform health and education planning. The register reports that the work has already informed and changed national guidance on survival of babies born extremely preterm.

DARS-NIC-284866-L7K4D.summary: The University of Sheffield is linking Yorkshire Ambulance Service patient records with pseudonymised Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency data for adults taken to emergency departments. It is using them for medical research to build risk prediction models showing whether an emergency department attendance was avoidable. The aim is a tool to help paramedics decide on scene whether to take a patient to hospital, so patients receive the most appropriate care first time.

DARS-NIC-28591-H5Q3X.summary: University College London (UCL), working with the University of Newcastle, uses identifiable NHS England hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and mental health records for 4,123 consenting men in the British Regional Heart Study. The records add detailed disease outcomes to the study, to research ways to prevent cardiovascular disease, heart failure, dementia and disability in older age. Findings from the linked data have already been published in peer-reviewed journals, including on healthy lifestyle, heart failure risk and dementia.

DARS-NIC-28604-N2L8W.summary: Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports using the data to support commissioning and service delivery, such as examining causes of accidental child hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-287049-F7M1P.summary: NHS England, working with its evaluation partner Ipsos, is using cancer waiting times, cancer registration and death registration data. These are held in a secure NHS England research environment. They are evaluating the Targeted Lung Health Check programme, which invites people at higher risk of lung cancer for checks and scans. The aim is to measure its impact on cancer outcomes, such as stage at diagnosis, and to inform whether and how the programme should be expanded across England.

DARS-NIC-287229-D6F9F.summary: University College London is using survey data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, covering adults in private households across the UK, for a PhD project. It examines whether the amount of alcohol people drink each week is linked to suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts and self-harm. The aim is to inform suicide prevention practice and policy. Initial findings were published in the journal BJPsych Open in November 2022.

DARS-NIC-28744-S4F8H.summary: The University of Cambridge is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted care, outpatients and A&E) for 867 people whose type 2 diabetes was found through screening. It is testing whether early, intensive treatment of several risk factors lowers the long-term risk of cardiovascular events and death over ten years, and informs the costs of care. The ten-year results have been published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, alongside several other papers.

DARS-NIC-287601-K4P2V.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is holding identifiable hospital admission and death registration data for about 20,000 patients from the CHARIOT study. It is using the data to examine whether raised high-sensitivity troponin blood test levels are linked to later deaths and hospital admissions. The aim is to help clinicians interpret the test. Results have been presented at cardiology conferences and published in the American Journal of Cardiology.

DARS-NIC-288807-P0R9B.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Exeter, is using pseudonymised hospital records (admissions, A&E, critical care and outpatients), emergency care data and death registrations for 5,409 people aged 65 and over. It is using them to study back and other musculoskeletal pain in older people and to calculate the cost of their NHS care. The main intended benefit is a prognostic tool to help GPs spot when back pain threatens an older person's mobility.

DARS-NIC-290527-P5C0Y.summary: Northwest Ehealth Limited holds hospital admission, outpatient and diagnostic imaging records for patients with refractory chronic cough who consented to their records being used. The records are now kept for archiving only, and other data has been destroyed. The study looked at how much healthcare these patients use and what it costs, to help understand earlier diagnosis. Its analysis found that healthcare use and costs fall within six months of diagnosis.

DARS-NIC-29100-R2S2F.summary: The University of Sheffield is using hospital accident and emergency (A&E) and admitted patient records from Hospital Episode Statistics. It is evaluating alcohol intoxication management services, sometimes called alcohol treatment centres, which treat intoxicated people who would otherwise go to emergency departments. The study compares six cities with these services against six without, looking at attendances, time spent in the emergency department and costs. It aims to give decision makers evidence on effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

DARS-NIC-291482-X5N6H.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data. It is used for risk stratification, which predicts which patients are at high risk of health deterioration so that care can be planned and GPs can target interventions. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency readmissions and better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-291863-S9M0X.summary: The University of Birmingham is using hospital admission records and death registration data for people taking part in the BASIL-2 trial, who have severe limb ischaemia caused by blocked arteries below the knee. The data will check the trial's main outcome, amputation-free survival, and extend follow-up without contacting participants again. The trial compares vein bypass first with endovascular treatment first, to find which works better and offers better value to the NHS and social care.

DARS-NIC-291938-R6V3V.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust is using demographic data and Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) death and flagging reports to keep up to date the database of the Diabetes Alliance for Research in England (DARE) study in north east London. The database lets the team invite people with diabetes to take part in research, with the aim of recruiting faster and speeding up evidence on diabetes care. So far, the database has helped recruit about 4,200 people to 32 approved studies, and the team has held a public event for members.

DARS-NIC-291940-S3D6R.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne, an academic organisation, is using data from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) and the Personal Demographics Service. It is using this to provide the register with statistical analysis from birth certificates, and to update and complete the registration of young people with a malignant disease in the North and North West regions of England. The text does not state an intended benefit.

DARS-NIC-291941-Z2Q1C.summary: Cardiff University, an academic organisation, holds NHS England Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records on cause of death, cohort event notification and current status for patients in the FRAGMATIC lung cancer trial. It keeps them for secure storage and to repeat earlier analyses if the published results are challenged. The trial tested whether adding dalteparin to standard treatment improved survival. The results have contributed to international guidelines on preventing blood clots in cancer patients, and led to a new trial.

DARS-NIC-291953-M8M9V.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) records, covering cause of death, current status, members and postings, and personal demographics, for a breast cancer study. It links these to trial data to analyse relapse-free and overall survival, and to test whether bone marrow micrometastases at diagnosis independently predict outcomes. The aim is to identify women at high risk of relapse after surgery. Main results have already been published in the British Medical Journal and The Lancet.

DARS-NIC-291981-Y7J2F.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, holds pseudonymised NHS England mortality and cohort tracking records (MRIS reports) for patients in the SIGGAR and SOCCER bowel cancer diagnosis studies, now kept for archiving only. The studies compared CT colonography with colonoscopy and barium enema, and examined which patients need a whole colon investigation. Results led the NHS Bowel Cancer Screening Programme to recommend only CT colonography as an alternative to colonoscopy, and symptom guidelines were updated.

DARS-NIC-292087-M7V9Q.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admitted patient and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for the FORECAST Trial. The trial involves adults referred to rapid access chest pain clinics. It compares a CT heart scan, with a computer-generated blood flow measurement (FFRct) where needed, against routine hospital tests. The main aim is to see whether this approach uses fewer NHS resources over nine months, which could inform national NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-292279-Z2S5T.summary: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital, emergency care, death registration and demographic records to enhance its de-identified clinical records research resource, CRIS. The data are used to study physical health, mortality and use of healthcare in people with mental health conditions, and to identify health inequalities. Published research has already informed government policy and the Trust's smoke-free policy.

DARS-NIC-294268-B3Q6J.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners), linked with GP data, to identify patients at high risk of poor health outcomes. This risk stratification, carried out by Prescribing Services Limited, helps GPs target care and helps commissioners plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294304-Q1M0X.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB, working with Prescribing Services Limited, uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data linked with GP data. It uses this for risk stratification: identifying patients at high risk, so GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294327-K1S3K.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Sub ICB Location, formerly NHS Bassetlaw CCG) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data, for risk stratification carried out by Prescribing Services Limited. This identifies patients at high risk, so GPs can target care and commissioners can plan services. The main intended benefit is better planning and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-294590-B6V3F.summary: The University of Manchester is using civil registration death records, covering whether patients have died and the dates and causes of death, for 151 patients diagnosed with naevoid melanoma, a type of skin cancer, at Royal Surrey County Hospital. The study will compare the outlook for two subtypes, papillomatous and maturing. The intended benefit is more precise diagnosis and better-tailored follow-up and treatment for each subtype.

DARS-NIC-295342-W3Z6L.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admissions records linked to death registration data to study surgery for upper limb injuries and infections, and the complications that follow. It aims to show trends, regional variation, outcomes and NHS costs, so that services can be better planned and patients and clinicians can make better-informed choices. Analysis of flexor tendon injuries of the hand has been presented internationally and used to support an NIHR-funded trial of surgical techniques.

DARS-NIC-296034-T4Y4K.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, is using hospital records covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient care. It is studying people in England with pulmonary hypertension and its subtypes, looking at the route to diagnosis, treatment patterns, outcomes and healthcare use. The aim is to fill knowledge gaps and support better diagnosis, treatment and care pathways. A study report has been produced, and a publication is being developed.

DARS-NIC-297783-V4P6H.summary: GlaxoSmithKline Research & Development Limited is using pseudonymised hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) for 629 participants in its INTREPID trial of COPD inhaler treatment. It is testing whether routine hospital data can record and cost hospital use, reducing the data collection burden on research sites. An abstract presented at the ISPOR Europe conference in November 2022 concluded that the linked data gave more detail than patient recall.

DARS-NIC-29785-Q4Y2T.summary: Leicestershire County Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports analyses already done on alcohol-related admissions, covid admissions and hip fractures.

DARS-NIC-29822-N0N7W.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using linked hospital, mental health service and death registration records for English participants with dementia in the IDEAL study. It aims to understand patterns of health service use and costs, and how these relate to people's ability to live well with dementia. The intended benefit is better evidence to help shape services, policy and support for people with dementia and their carers. So far, service use and cost variables have been calculated and linked to the study data, and manuscripts have been submitted for peer review.

DARS-NIC-29827-Q8Z7Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) linked to civil death registrations. It is studying how patient, surgical and hospital factors affect outcomes and NHS costs in treating upper limb conditions such as arthritis, shoulder injuries, Dupuytren's disease and nerve compression. The main aim is to give patients and the NHS evidence on outcomes and variation in care. Six peer-reviewed papers have already been published on complications and repeat surgery, and they are being used in clinical practice.

DARS-NIC-300282-G9Q0Q.summary: University College London holds a register of people with familial hypercholesterolaemia, an inherited cause of high cholesterol, and uses linked hospital and death records for the University of Nottingham and University of York study. The study evaluates ways of identifying and managing patients, to inform cost-effectiveness models of relative testing. So far, the work has produced long-term risk estimates that supported charity advocacy, and has shown lipid specialists inequalities in care.

DARS-NIC-301834-K0S2Y.summary: Certara UK, a commercial research consultancy, is using pseudonymised hospital, accident and emergency, critical care, outpatient and death records for adults with haematological cancers. It is studying the clinical characteristics of patients who develop veno-occlusive disease, a rare liver disorder, and the hospital resources and costs involved in their care in England. The aim is to improve detection and care, and to inform planning of NHS resources.

DARS-NIC-302473-K6R0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge is using cancer registration, death registration and mortality follow-up records to study people who carry BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations and their relatives (the EMBRACE study). It aims to estimate cancer risks and the effects of lifestyle factors and risk-reducing surgery, so that screening and counselling can be better guided. Published papers have already been incorporated into guidelines, including those from NICE (the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence).

DARS-NIC-302604-S7H2N.summary: Imperial College London is using identifiable NHS hospital records (inpatient, outpatient, and accident and emergency), mental health data sets and death and status reports for participants in the ASCOT heart trial. It is studying whether atorvastatin and different blood pressure treatments affect long-term risks of dementia, stroke and other vascular disease, and how blood pressure variability relates to them. Published findings have already fed into the QRISK3 risk model and hypertension guidelines.

DARS-NIC-302792-X4T6B.summary: The University of Warwick's Clinical Trials Unit holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) from the completed PreFIT falls prevention trial. It keeps them securely archived for 10 years, and may re-run earlier analyses only to check published results if they are challenged. The trial compared ways to prevent falls and fractures in people over 70. The findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and are being considered by NICE.

DARS-NIC-302994-C2Q2Y.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS hospital, death, cancer, mental health, medicines and diabetes audit records to follow people who took part in the ASCEND trial of people with diabetes. It aims to find out whether low-dose aspirin, and omega-3 supplements, affect long-term risks of cancer, dementia, heart failure, heart attacks and strokes. Published results have already been cited in updated guidelines, including the February 2023 NICE cardiovascular guideline update.

DARS-NIC-303379-H4C8H.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust and Liverpool Heart & Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust are keeping identifiable hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient, critical care, diagnostic imaging and death records for 1,100 participants in the RIPCORD 2 heart trial. They hold them for secure storage, so the trial analysis can be repeated if its findings are challenged. The trial's findings were published in the journal Circulation in 2022 and have helped guide clinicians on using pressure wire technology.

DARS-NIC-303785-L3K3Z.summary: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission, outpatient and civil registration (death) records for patients treated with percutaneous coronary intervention, a procedure to open narrowed heart arteries. It will compare drug coated balloons with drug eluting stents, including in different patient groups, and look at outcomes such as mortality and rehospitalisation. The aim is to publish the findings and present them at medical conferences. This could help show whether drug coated balloons are a suitable alternative to stents.

DARS-NIC-304146-M5F6Y.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil registration death records for patients who attended an emergency department. The aim is to update the T-MACS chest pain decision aid with machine learning so it stays accurate over time, and to test whether emergency department data can predict long-term cardiovascular outcomes, including death. The expected benefit is continued safe, accurate and quick diagnosis of heart attacks.

DARS-NIC-30493-Y0C0K.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and mortality data, with names, addresses and NHS numbers removed, linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. It uses them to research health, social care use and ageing in people aged 50 and over, helping to inform planning of services. Linked data have already contributed to the Centre for Ageing Better's "Boom and bust?" report (November 2021) and a World Health Organization review on arts and health.

DARS-NIC-305864-D0Y3W.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital admitted patient and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and death registration data for a long-term follow-up of men in the UPSTREAM trial, which tested whether invasive bladder pressure testing (urodynamics) helps decide on prostate surgery for urinary symptoms. It aims to establish whether surgery rates were lower with testing. Phase I results have been published, but the Phase II analyses are still in draft.

DARS-NIC-30645-Z2Z2K.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital admission records and death registration data to study hip fractures in England and Wales. It is examining how social deprivation and region affect how often hip fractures happen, and what follows: death, recovery, return home, readmissions and their costs. The aim is to inform commissioning and reduce health inequalities. Several peer-reviewed papers have been published, and the work helped win further funding for a follow-on study.

DARS-NIC-306651-W7L4C.summary: Keele University, an academic organisation, is using hospital admission, death registration and national heart attack audit data to study complications and unplanned readmissions after a heart attack. The aim is to understand how often these occur and what raises the risk, so that risk scores can help clinicians tailor treatment and reduce readmissions. Published papers so far include one finding that heart attack patients with cancer face higher short- and long-term risk of death.

DARS-NIC-306849-M2N0X.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital records (outpatient, admitted patient and accident and emergency) and death registration data. It is studying people who had a right heart catheter test at specialist centres between 2009 and 2016 and whose lung artery pressure was raised but below the current threshold for pulmonary hypertension. The study compares their deaths and hospital admissions with a control group. It aims to support earlier monitoring and updated guidance for this group.

DARS-NIC-307462-D6B9M.summary: Royal Surrey NHS Foundation Trust is using cause of death information from death certificates, held in the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death report, for about 250 patients who had prostate brachytherapy and were lost to follow-up. It will add the causes of death to its Brachybase database and audit prostate cancer specific survival after treatment. The main intended benefit is to show how effective the treatment is and allow comparison with results from other centres.

DARS-NIC-308166-T2Z1J.summary: Warrington Borough Council is using identifiable patient details from the Personal Demographic Service, including name, address, date of birth and GP practice code. The council will use them to invite residents to take part in a Health and Wellbeing Survey. The survey is meant to give up-to-date information on local health and lifestyle, so the council and NHS partners can plan services and target resources at areas and groups experiencing health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-309029-P7H1D.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which covers hospital births, together with a linking identifier dataset. It is studying whether the Health in Pregnancy Grant, paid to pregnant women in England from 2009 to 2011, affected birthweight and prematurity. The researchers hope to show whether the grant achieved its aims, to inform policy debates on public health and early intervention.

DARS-NIC-309034-C7M7W.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with NHS Blood and Transplant, holds pseudonymised hospital records (admitted patient care and outpatients) and death registration data for about 200,000 blood donors. It is using them to study the long-term health effects of whole blood and platelet donation, such as on heart disease and diabetes, and to test whether such linkage can support ongoing donor health monitoring. Findings so far include no link between platelet donation and health outcomes, and preliminary results presented at a European conference.

DARS-NIC-309246-L8C4C.summary: The University of Nottingham is using maternity, hospital inpatient, critical care, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for the GBS3 trial. The trial compares two ways of routinely testing pregnant women for Group B Streptococcus with the current approach based on risk factors, to see whether testing reduces serious infection in newborn babies. It also assesses costs. The main intended benefit is evidence for the UK National Screening Committee to decide whether routine testing should be introduced.

DARS-NIC-309500-F4X1B.summary: The University of Birmingham, through its Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit, holds cause of death and current status records for the 1,440 people in the original BAFTA trial. It uses them in the BAFTA 2 follow-up study to see who has died, from what cause, and the overall death rate, to understand the long-term effects of anticoagulation (blood-thinning) treatment in very elderly people. The aim is to help clinicians and patients decide whether to continue treatment. The original BAFTA trial has already led to published papers and been included in national guidelines.

DARS-NIC-309509-L2G1J.summary: University College London is using identifiable hospital inpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for about 16,720 infants in a randomised trial of a diagnostic aid, a video tool and checklist, for GPs' 6-week hip checks. The trial will test whether the aid reduces unnecessary referrals to hospital and late diagnoses of developmental dysplasia of the hip. The aim is for infants who truly have the condition to be treated sooner, and for fewer families to face needless appointments.

DARS-NIC-309751-G8D4H.summary: King's College London is using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data from 2007 and 2014 for a PhD research project. The study looks at how caregivers' reports of domestic violence relate to their health, compared with carers who report no violence and with people who are not carers. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of carers' experiences of violence, which could help inform support and future interventions.

DARS-NIC-311182-F5W4X.summary: The University of Oxford is using demographic data (name, address, gender and date of birth) for people aged 65 or over in the Thames Valley who have several long-term conditions. The data will be used to identify and invite people to join the ATEMPT pilot trial, which compares taking more with fewer blood pressure medicines. The intended benefit is to help plan a larger trial on managing blood pressure in older people with multiple health conditions.

DARS-NIC-311182-N0L1Y.summary: National Centre for Social Research holds hospital records and death-registration data linked to participants in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, a long-running study of people aged 50 and over. The data supports research on health, work, finances and social life in older age, and can be shared with study partners at UCL and the Institute for Fiscal Studies. Linked data has already fed into published analyses on dementia trends, loneliness and end-of-life hospital spending, and into a Centre for Ageing Better report.

DARS-NIC-313754-G6X4Z.summary: Cardiff University holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) from the completed Building Blocks study of the Family Nurse Partnership programme for first-time teenage mothers. The data is securely archived to meet good clinical practice rules and to allow published findings to be verified if challenged. Retaining it also preserves a database that could support future research on children's longer-term outcomes. The study's findings were published and used by the Department of Health to decide how best to support young families in England.

DARS-NIC-314399-K4J9S.summary: NHS Wales Informatics Service, on behalf of Wales's seven local health boards, is using identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service accident and emergency, episode and outpatient records) about Welsh residents treated in NHS England. It is used for planning and managing health services, direct care, and checking payments and quality of care. The main intended benefit is better management of patient pathways and care across the Wales–England border. The register reports general improvements in care, services and finances, but names no specific outputs.

DARS-NIC-31491-V6Z9Y.summary: Calderdale Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It uses them for its public health duties, including its Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, the annual report of the Director of Public Health, commissioning plans and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-315134-L9Z6B.summary: IQVIA Solutions UK Limited, a supplier, is using pseudonymised or anonymised hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps. It is analysing treatment pathways and the burden of nasal polyp surgery, including repeat operations, for Sanofi Genzyme. The intended benefit is to help the NHS understand where surgery burden is greatest and support service improvement.

DARS-NIC-315419-F3W7K.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised, population-level hospital admissions and death registration data to research hospital admission trends, cancer, maternal health and the effects of COVID-19. The aim is to produce evidence that helps improve NHS services, care and policy. Reported results include a study of Covid-19 deaths among clinically vulnerable patients, reported to the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation, which helped inform early vaccine roll-out.

DARS-NIC-315716-L0F4M.summary: Imperial College London, an academic institution, uses pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to research care for frail and elderly patients with chronic conditions and the effects of government health policies. The aim is to better plan spending and identify older people at risk of declining health. So far, a PhD thesis has been passed with minor corrections, and earlier work was presented to health leaders and used to evaluate a health information exchange.

DARS-NIC-315871-Z7S4M.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (South Cheshire area) uses pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer waiting times and death and birth records, with clinical and financial detail. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, understand local needs, model how services interact, and identify patients at risk of admission. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-315999-W2W4C.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for a sub-study of the LP-MAESTRO project. The study evaluates the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of different liaison psychiatry service set-ups, which provide mental health care in general hospitals, using routine NHS data. It aims to help commissioners evaluate such services. Preliminary results on effects on hospital length of stay were presented at a RAID network conference in April 2017.

DARS-NIC-316369-X4S6T.summary: The London Borough of Croydon is using Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records, covering hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and A&E activity. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. So far, self-harm admissions analysis informed a needs assessment and was presented to the local suicide prevention board.

DARS-NIC-316443-V5Z4Y.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admission, death registration and patient-reported outcome records for people identified from the National Joint Registry. It is comparing cemented and cementless knee replacements, overall and for different groups of patients, including their costs. The aim is to show which fixation method works best so care can be tailored to patients. Research already published shows cemented total knee replacements had better clinical outcomes, while cementless partial replacements did better.

DARS-NIC-316558-W0T8G.summary: Cardiff University holds NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, covering cause of death, status tracking and demographics, for the AML16 clinical trial in older patients with acute myeloid leukaemia and high risk myelodysplastic syndrome. It is used only for secure storage and back-up, so the trial analysis can be reconstructed if needed. Reported benefits include tracking patients lost to follow-up, and trial results informing NICE guidelines and later trials.

DARS-NIC-316704-Z1Z7T.summary: The University of Cambridge is using pseudonymised hospital admissions, death registration and National Diabetes Audit data for people who took part in long-running studies of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes. The research looks at how childhood and adolescent risk factors relate to later heart, kidney, eye and nerve complications in adult life. The main intended benefit is better understanding of early risk factors, to help prevent complications and guide future care.

DARS-NIC-317048-N8P0R.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit is using pseudonymised health and care data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other services, with clinical and financial details. It supports the four Worcestershire and Herefordshire clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) in planning and commissioning services for their local population. The data is used for reporting, population health analysis and demand planning. The stated aim is to improve patient pathways and the quality of services.

DARS-NIC-318632-T0N3M.summary: The University of Leeds is using pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records, linked with National Hip Fracture Database data. It is comparing outcomes after a neck of femur (hip) fracture across ethnic groups and looking at possible reasons for any differences. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether ethnicity data should be collected, so hospital trusts can allocate resources fairly. Preliminary analysis has shown variation in survival after this fracture by ethnicity.

DARS-NIC-31865-Z2Y1D.summary: Gateshead Metropolitan Borough Council uses hospital records covering admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and emergency department attendances. It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported work includes analysis of alcohol-related admissions, housing and health conditions, and Covid-19 vaccine support.

DARS-NIC-318886-M1B9L.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, uses hospital-level counts of admitted patient care records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for angioplasty (percutaneous coronary intervention). It compares them with the cases hospitals submit to the national audit, to check how complete the audit is. The main intended benefit is publishing case ascertainment rates, which encourages hospitals to submit more complete data. Reported results include identifying centres below national benchmarks, with letters sent to centres performing fewer than 200 procedures for three successive years.

DARS-NIC-31911-S3Y6M.summary: Newcastle University is using records of children born with congenital heart disease (CHD) in England and Wales between 1985 and 2012, linked to death registrations and area deprivation scores. The aim is to estimate survival up to 25 years and identify factors that predict it. The main intended benefit is better information for counselling parents after a diagnosis and for planning health services.

DARS-NIC-319171-G7H8K.summary: The University of Bristol uses NHS England hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for the CAP trial, which compares inviting men aged 50 to 69 for a PSA blood test for prostate cancer with standard NHS care. The data are used to follow up men who did not consent, to assess whether PSA testing reduces prostate cancer deaths and whether it is cost-effective. Published results have already been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and used by the National Screening Committee.

DARS-NIC-320147-M9K6K.summary: London Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using hospital and emergency care records, linked to its 999 call and patient records for women who called in April to July 2019. It is studying how accurately the ambulance triage system (MPDS Protocol 24) identifies maternity emergencies and which questions and factors predict them. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve telephone triage questions, so women needing urgent help are identified more reliably.

DARS-NIC-320217-X8P0W.summary: King's College London is using record-level data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey to study how having several physical and mental health conditions at once relates to social class and to social exclusion, such as homelessness. The aim is to inform NHS care, public health policy and research on inclusion health. So far, preliminary results have been shared at conferences and with clinicians, and a blog has been published.

DARS-NIC-321226-T4B8S.summary: NEC Software Solutions, a commercial organisation, uses Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care data for the National Joint Registry, which collects data on joint replacement surgery. It uses the data to check how fully NHS trusts and hospitals submit their joint replacement records, and to report on this. The aim is to keep data quality high so that patient safety and outcomes can be improved. Reported benefits include helping trusts monitor Best Practice Tariff targets and improving the recording of where surgery took place in HES.

DARS-NIC-321968-S4Q6L.summary: The University of Cambridge is using linked NHS records, including hospital, cancer registration, death, mental health and diabetes audit data, for 25,639 people in the EPIC-Norfolk health study. It uses them to follow participants' health over time and study how diet and lifestyle relate to disease and healthy ageing. The aim is to help prevent chronic disease and support good health in later life. Reported benefits include research that fed into a Department of Health public health campaign and into clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-322051-S8N9N.summary: The University of Aberdeen, with the University of Oxford, is using hospital admissions records, cause of death reports and cohort tracking reports for participants in the Knee Arthroplasty Trial. The data supports 20-year follow-up of how different knee replacement designs affect long-term safety, need for further surgery and cost-effectiveness. This should give stronger evidence for patients, clinicians and policy makers. Ten-year results have been published and are a key source for American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons clinical practice guidelines.

DARS-NIC-323026-N2R0B.summary: Hull City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. It reports using the data to analyse stillbirths, calculate ward-level mortality rates and life expectancy, and support the local alcohol and drugs needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-32317-W3C2K.summary: Telford & Wrekin Council, a local authority, is using hospital data covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It will use the data in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-323223-Q6C3D.summary: Hull City Council's public health team uses hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It uses them to support its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis that helps identify and respond to health inequalities. Reported benefits so far include improved statutory reports, support for substance misuse services and asthma hotspot work.

DARS-NIC-323925-K0B9S.summary: London Borough of Haringey, a local authority, uses identifiable birth and death records, along with primary care mortality data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide audits and prevention work. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. So far, it has analysed excess winter deaths, heatwave deaths, Covid-19 excess mortality and changes in birth rates.

DARS-NIC-324040-N7L9R.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and death registration data, including cause of death, for patients who had a cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) heart scan between June 2016 and May 2018. It is studying how well CMR findings, such as heart scarring, predict death and hospital admission for heart failure. The aim is to identify patients at risk earlier and guide treatment. So far it has developed a risk calculator, now informing a primary care programme.

DARS-NIC-324170-J4P1J.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Maternity Services Data Set records, linked to kidney disease registries. It is building a calculator to predict how far pregnancy may worsen kidney function in women with chronic kidney disease. The aim is to help women and clinicians make informed decisions about pregnancy. The team has nearly finished the tool, and a paper is about to be submitted.

DARS-NIC-324220-P6W9Y.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, cancer registration and death records for about 3,000 participants in the IBIS-II breast cancer prevention and DCIS trials. It is following them over the long term to study the effects of tamoxifen and anastrozole on breast cancer, other cancers, heart disease, fractures and deaths. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed treatment choices. Results have already been published and contributed to a licence variation for anastrozole in England.

DARS-NIC-324368-Q0H5T.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to check that its national study of children aged 5 to 16 with cerebral palsy who have multi-level orthopaedic surgery (SEMLS) has not missed any cases. The study aims to count how many children have this surgery across NHS Trusts in England and to show how surgeons choose which children to treat. The intended benefit is stronger evidence to help set standard guidance on care.

DARS-NIC-324388-L6C2Q.summary: The University of Birmingham is using mortality and cancer registration data on about 35-40,000 male UK oil refinery and petroleum distribution workers in England. It is checking whether these workers have higher rates of particular cancers and causes of death than the general population, which could point to workplace exposures such as benzene. The findings are intended to help regulators assess worker protection. Two reports have been published on the Energy Institute website.

DARS-NIC-324608-Q0G8L.summary: The University of Sheffield's School of Health and Related Research is using hospital records (admissions, A&E and critical care) and death registration data for adults taken to hospital by emergency ambulance with possible sepsis. The data will be linked to ambulance records to test how accurate and cost-effective early warning scores used by paramedics are for spotting sepsis. The aim is to identify the best score for the NHS, which could lead to better treatment and fewer deaths from sepsis.

DARS-NIC-325074-F0J3D.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital, mental health and mortality records for young people who took part in the SHIFT trial, which compared family therapy with usual treatment after self-harm. The data is linked to trial data to measure repeat hospital attendance and safety, and to describe services used. The intended benefit is to inform NHS practice and NICE guidance. Results have been published, and the trial helped lead to a commissioned meta-analysis of self-harm therapies.

DARS-NIC-32537-Y2H2L.summary: The University of Warwick is using hospital records covering accident and emergency visits, inpatient stays and outpatient appointments for people aged 65 and over. The aim is to map the routes older patients with complex needs take through hospital and how those routes relate to their health outcomes and use of resources. The intended benefit is to help services plan and redesign care for this group.

DARS-NIC-325899-B0C9B.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (Sub ICB Location) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, births and deaths data, including clinical and financial information. It uses this to plan and commission health services for its local population, including population health management, service redesign and demand forecasting. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and improved quality of care.

DARS-NIC-327369-T1M7M.summary: The University of Nottingham, which manages the ATTACK trial for the University of Southampton, is using hospital admissions, emergency care, death registration and cancer registration records. These are used to identify heart attacks, strokes and other outcomes in people with chronic kidney disease, so the trial can test whether low-dose aspirin prevents major vascular events. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether aspirin should be prescribed to these patients.

DARS-NIC-327960-M2P9M.summary: Swansea University, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital records (outpatient, inpatient and A&E) and death registration data. It is evaluating whether multi-disciplinary case management for people who frequently call 999 is safe and effective, including whether it shifts demand elsewhere in the NHS. The aim is to help ambulance services manage frequent callers better. A final report went to the funder in June 2023, and preliminary findings were presented at the EMS 999 Research Forum.

DARS-NIC-328464-Y5Y8F.summary: The University of Kent holds survey data from adult social care users and from carers of people receiving adult social care in England. The original study, by the university's Personal Social Services Research Unit, looked at variations in quality and outcomes and at the efficiency and productivity of social care services. The work was intended to inform social care policy and practice, including the Adult Social Care Outcomes Framework. This agreement only permits the data to be kept for an interim period.

DARS-NIC-32854-Y8P8B.summary: The Institute for Fiscal Studies is using hospital records (inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and mortality data, linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, which follows people aged 50 and over. It is studying the economics of health and social care use as the population ages, to help plan services and policy. So far, results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England, and a paper was published in the Milbank Quarterly in October 2020.

DARS-NIC-329869-Q9Z2Z.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, covering hospital admissions in England from 1997 onwards. It is studying how air pollution, heat, cold and pollen affect hospital admissions in small areas, and which groups are most vulnerable. The aim is to give policymakers detailed risk information to protect vulnerable people. So far, the team has linked the data to local environmental measures and submitted articles on admissions for conditions such as asthma.

DARS-NIC-331142-P5K6M.summary: The University of Bristol runs the National Child Mortality Database, using NHS hospital, maternity, mental health, community, cancer, medicines and death records on children who die in England before their 18th birthday. It links these to child death review data to study how and why children die and to support recommendations that reduce child deaths. It reports that its findings have contributed to policy change, guidance and safety notices, and that its Sudden Unexpected Death in Childhood report was debated in parliament.

DARS-NIC-331607-P4J8H.summary: The University of York is using hospital records (outpatient, inpatient, and accident and emergency) and death registration data. It is studying whether healthcare use, especially emergency care, rises when young people with life limiting conditions move from children's to adult services. The aim is to give commissioners and hospices evidence to adapt services and target support at the groups most affected.

DARS-NIC-331733-T2K1Z.summary: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust is using civil registration death records and demographic data for 1,487 people in the Birmingham and Black Country Atrial Fibrillation study cohort. It will link causes of death to blood test markers taken at recruitment, to build a model predicting which people with atrial fibrillation will develop heart failure. The intended benefit is helping doctors start preventive heart failure treatment earlier. Baseline study data has already contributed to combined analyses within a research consortium seeking new biomarkers and treatment targets.

DARS-NIC-331952-D8S2S.summary: Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, is using Hospital Episode Statistics data covering emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care, outpatients and accident and emergency. It will use the data in its public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups, so local health challenges are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-332338-X1N2G.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital admission records and civil registration death records, linked to its consented EMMACE study cohort of heart attack patients. It is studying how changes in health-related quality of life relate to later outcomes such as stroke, repeat heart attack, heart failure and death. The aim is to help design interventions that improve quality of life and survival. Results have already appeared in peer-reviewed journals and at conferences.

DARS-NIC-33234-C0V1D.summary: The University of Oxford is using mortality data (cause of death, cohort event notification and flagging status reports) for 290 people who had a transient ischaemic attack (TIA), a temporary interruption to the brain's blood supply. It is linking this to an existing study to estimate long-term survival, main causes of death and factors linked to survival. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand prognosis after a TIA. An earlier 2003 paper from the study has been downloaded 3,926 times and cited 177 times.

DARS-NIC-332870-B6Z4R.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records to evaluate community-based multi-disciplinary teams that join up health and social care. It compares patients who used these teams with matched patients who did not, to see whether outcomes differ between patients and between team models. The aim is to give policymakers better evidence on how to integrate services cost-effectively.

DARS-NIC-333021-B6W2C.summary: The University of Manchester, an academic body, holds pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and critical care records from 1999 to 2017. Under this agreement the data is only kept securely for an interim period, with no other processing and no new outputs. The data was originally supplied for the Norfolk Arthritis Register, a long-term community study of the causes and outcomes of inflammatory polyarthritis.

DARS-NIC-33318-X4Q1B.summary: The University of Manchester is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) to study whether dementia training for hospital staff affects outcomes for patients with dementia. The aim is to give evidence to inform national and hospital Trust policy on dementia care. Results presented so far show that poorer outcomes for people with dementia are mostly explained by patient characteristics, and that no beneficial impact of training was found. A paper has been submitted to BMC Medicine.

DARS-NIC-333498-D1K7G.summary: Cardiff University is using NHS England hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency) and death registration data for mothers and children from the Building Blocks trial of the Family Nurse Partnership home-visiting programme. It is evaluating the programme's long-term effectiveness, mainly in reducing child maltreatment, and its costs and consequences. Results were published in journals and shared with government and local authorities, and early results influenced decisions on funding the FNP National Unit.

DARS-NIC-333880-G4H3T.summary: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), through its Wakefield sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised health and care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and death records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services for the local population, with processing carried out by North of England Commissioning Support Unit. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes. So far, it has allowed benchmarking of performance across West Yorkshire and easier sharing of insight between CCGs.

DARS-NIC-334459-R9H4C.summary: The University of York is using linked hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient care and outpatient data) for 180 children in the "Your Tube" study who are fed through a gastrostomy tube. It will use them to compare healthcare use and gastrostomy complications between children fed formula and those fed home-blended meals. It will also check whether routine data could support longer-term follow-up. The aim is to provide evidence to inform clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-334549-B1Y6X.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital records (admissions, outpatient and A&E) and death registration data, linked to the National Hip Fracture Database. It is studying how differences between hospitals in organising hip fracture care affect patient outcomes such as death, hospital stay and readmission. The aim is to reduce avoidable variation and improve care quality. Published papers have already supported a free toolkit for hip fracture services, launched in February 2023.

DARS-NIC-334745-L4J6P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital, death registration, diagnostic imaging, maternity and demographic data to study unruptured brain aneurysms in England. The study aims to predict the risk of rupture, including during pregnancy and delivery, so treatment decisions can be better informed. Pilot results have already shown that hospital and death records identified ruptured aneurysms in a subgroup of patients with a detection rate above 98%.

DARS-NIC-334952-R5M7K.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable NHS hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records from women in the UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening. It uses them to identify cases for follow-on studies that draw on the trial's stored blood samples, aiming to improve early detection of disease, especially cancer. The trial's main results were published in 2023, and further studies and publications have followed from the trial's data and samples.

DARS-NIC-33499-F9N8F.summary: Plymouth City Council uses civil registration births and deaths data, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits, with published results only as aggregated figures. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports using the data to produce a 2020 to 2022 suicide audit summary and Joint Strategic Needs Assessment documents.

DARS-NIC-336478-Z7Q9F.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent health research charity, uses hospital data covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients (Hospital Episode Statistics). It uses them for QualityWatch, a programme that monitors changes in the quality of NHS care through reports, blogs and online indicators. The aim is to give independent analysis that prompts improvements. Earlier QualityWatch reports were cited in an NHS England mental health plan and used by a commissioning support unit to change its approach.

DARS-NIC-336857-P6C9Q.summary: The University of Bristol, jointly with the University of Manchester, is using hospital inpatient and outpatient records and death registration data for adults in England who were admitted with a severe pressure ulcer. The study describes the care these patients received and compares outcomes, such as returning to hospital and death, for those who did and did not have surgery. It aims to inform the design of a future randomised controlled trial of reconstructive surgery. So far, results have been presented at several conferences, including a poster at the International Clinical Trials Methodology Conference 2022.

DARS-NIC-337801-K2N5Y.summary: The Health and Safety Executive uses cancer registrations, death records and demographic data on about 79,700 asbestos workers recruited before 2006. It tracks their long-term deaths and cancers, comparing them with the general population and across types of asbestos work. The aim is to show whether tighter asbestos regulation is reducing disease and to inform future policy. Findings have already appeared in HSE research reports and peer-reviewed journals, and previously published articles have been cited over 160 times.

DARS-NIC-338242-C8Z8M.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant holds linked hospital admission and death registration data for people on the national kidney transplant waiting list. The research looks at what happens to patients suspended from the list, including their hospital admissions and causes of death. It aims to help build a model for allocating donor kidneys by clinical need, with the intended benefit of fewer waiting list deaths and a fairer allocation policy.

DARS-NIC-338303-P4G5Q.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for a clinical trial called the DIvO study. The trial tests whether digital imaging with the Neocam device is better than the standard ophthalmoscopic red-reflex test at detecting congenital cataract in newborns. The main intended benefit is earlier detection, which could lead to better long-term vision and may inform national screening policy.

DARS-NIC-338773-H5J5S.summary: The University of Manchester's Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN) uses Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care data and civil registration death data. It uses them to check how completely hospitals submit trauma cases, and to work out 30-day patient outcomes, so that it can improve the quality of its reports. The aim is to improve patient care. Hospitals that used the linked data reportedly improved case identification by 5 to 50%, averaging 20%.

DARS-NIC-338789-M0T3Q.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, including clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and redesign local health services, understand the needs of the population, and identify patients at risk of needing hospital care. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow, access and quality of care.

DARS-NIC-338864-B3Z3J.summary: Barts and the London School of Medicine and Dentistry, an academic organisation, uses linked NHS England hospital, mental health, community, maternity, cancer, death and diabetes audit records for the Genes & Health research programme. It combines these with genetic data to study health and disease in British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani people, aiming to improve their health. Reported results include 44 publications and 50 volunteers diagnosed with familial hypercholesterolaemia and referred for NHS treatment.

DARS-NIC-341768-K2T6V.summary: The University of Birmingham, as sponsor of the BASIL-3 trial, is using hospital admission and death records for 481 patients with severe leg ischaemia (blocked blood vessels between the hip and knee). The data will extend follow-up of trial participants and check main outcomes without contacting them again. The trial compares three treatments, with the aim of finding the most clinically and cost-effective one.

DARS-NIC-341915-Z7J0Y.summary: The University of Edinburgh is using hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensed medicines records for 733 consented participants in the DUAL-ACS clinical trial. It will link them to trial data to compare 3 and 12 months of dual anti-platelet therapy after a type 1 heart attack. The main intended benefit is clear evidence on the safest treatment duration, to guide clinical practice and reduce harm and costs.

DARS-NIC-342229-X7K0T.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses identifiable hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service for Commissioners) and the Personal Demographic Service. It uses them to check provider invoices and confirm it is the responsible commissioner, and to identify patients at high risk so GPs and commissioners can plan and target care. The aim is accurate payment and better, more effective commissioning. It has produced an annual report that references achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-342322-Q1N7M.summary: University College London is using linked health records for children, including hospital, emergency care, mental health, birth and death registration data, with the Office for National Statistics processing the data. The study compares health and educational outcomes of children who had a brain injury around the time of birth with two matched groups of children without one. It aims to give parents, clinicians, the NHS and policymakers better evidence to shape care, follow-up and educational support.

DARS-NIC-343042-X5T7Y.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised local provider flow data covering acute, ambulance, community, mental health, emergency care, primary care and other services. It uses the data, with support from South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit and Optum Health Solutions, to analyse clinical and financial activity so health services can be planned around the local population's needs. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and patient pathways.

DARS-NIC-343158-Z2L4D.summary: NHS Gloucestershire ICB is using pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and births and deaths data about people in the Gloucestershire area. It uses the data to plan and commission health and care services, understand local health needs and support population health management. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved health outcomes. The CCG has published an annual report that refers to key achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-343380-H5Q9K.summary: The UK Health Security Agency uses a wide range of NHS England data, including hospital, emergency care, maternity, prescribing, testing and death registration records. It uses them to monitor, prepare for and respond to infectious diseases and other health threats, producing statistics, surveillance reports, dashboards and guidance. The aim is to protect public health. Covid-19 test results have already been used to estimate infection levels and the reproduction number, informing government decisions on restrictions and public advice.

DARS-NIC-344271-Q5X0S.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital accident and emergency and admitted patient care records, linked with other primary care and death data, to study how the mix of staff in general practice teams relates to quality of care, effectiveness and staffing costs. The aim is to show which staffing combinations work best and where tasks can move between different practitioners. The intended benefit is to help practices and commissioners make staffing decisions that treat more patients effectively at the same or lower cost.

DARS-NIC-345789-L9Q7J.summary: The University of Surrey is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, mental health, patient-reported outcome and death registration data. It is studying what affects how well NHS hospitals and ambulance trusts keep their staff, and how staff retention affects patient outcomes such as mortality, readmissions and length of stay. The aim is to give policymakers evidence for improving retention and patient care. So far, the project has led to press coverage, presentations to NHS England, and funding extensions.

DARS-NIC-346693-F2X1G.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, uses linked NHS hospital, mental health, cancer, death and COVID-19 records for the Whitehall II study of ageing in a long-running group of participants. It examines how social, biological and behavioural factors affect late-life conditions such as dementia, chronic disease and physical functioning, aiming to inform health policy and prevention. Its findings have been cited in clinical guidelines, including a 2023 NICE guideline on cardiovascular disease.

DARS-NIC-346859-C9J6J.summary: The University of York, working with Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, is using linked NHS records, including hospital, cancer registration and death data, for patients with blood cancers in Yorkshire and Humberside. It aims to understand the causes of these cancers, their effect on later health and healthcare needs, and real-world treatment outcomes. This is intended to inform cancer policy and services. Its data have already been used in 49 NICE submissions on treatments.

DARS-NIC-347209-L2Q4S.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School (St George's, University of London) is using hospital and emergency care records from NHS England, covering admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and A&E attendances. It uses them in a randomised controlled trial of specialist physiotherapy for functional motor disorder, a condition causing symptoms such as weakness and tremor. The records will show whether the physiotherapy reduces health service use and costs compared with usual treatment. If it works, this could support rolling it out across the NHS.

DARS-NIC-348357-W0P1W.summary: NHS Devon ICB, working with NHS Kernow and Cornwall Council, uses pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care and death records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, support population health management and compare provider performance. The main intended benefit is services that match local population needs. The register reports that the data has already helped monitor in-year projects and shape service delivery.

DARS-NIC-34907-D9R3N.summary: The University of Cambridge is using NHS hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, inpatient and outpatient care) and a service that checks which participants are still alive. The data covers people with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes in the ADDITION-Plus trial. It is used to follow their heart and circulation outcomes and health service use over the long term, and to test whether a behaviour change programme helps. The aim is to inform NHS treatment decisions. So far, the study has published 10 peer-reviewed papers.

DARS-NIC-349273-T3L4K.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London is using pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for patients in the national COPD audit in England and Wales.
