It links this to audit records to examine readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days, aiming to show how hospital care affects outcomes and to improve COPD care. Reports published in 2023 and 2024 have been used by hospitals to compare their performance and plan improvements.

DARS-NIC-349486-Y3C3L.summary: Market and Opinion Research International Limited, a commercial research company, is using data from two national social care surveys: the Adult Social Care Survey of service users and the Survey of Adult Carers in England. It is analysing which groups are under-represented in the surveys, as part of a research project funded by the National Institute for Health Research. The aim is to help the Department of Health and Social Care, NHS Digital and local authorities improve how well the surveys represent people, so that their findings are less misleading.

DARS-NIC-349688-V6V0Q.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB uses pseudonymised health, social care and mortality data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity and prescribing records, to plan and commission health services for the population of the former East Riding of Yorkshire CCG area. It uses the data for population health management, service redesign, demand forecasting and contract management. The main aim is to match services to local needs. The register reports that services have been delivered to match population requirements.

DARS-NIC-349889-Q7R7K.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using civil registration death records to follow intensive care patients for one year after they had a high-sensitivity troponin blood test. It aims to find out whether raised troponin levels in critical illness predict longer-term death and cause of death. The expected benefit is a better understanding of how clinicians should interpret these results in intensive care. Two abstracts have been accepted for presentation at the European Society of Cardiology Congress.

DARS-NIC-350331-P9L1M.summary: Roehampton University, an academic institution, is using record-level hospital admission, maternity services and death registration data about women giving birth in selected London areas and hospitals. This pilot study will compare childbirth, interventions such as inductions, forceps and C-sections, and maternal deaths and illness across ethnic groups. It aims to test whether the standard model of "normal" labour, based largely on white women, contributes to the ethnic gap in maternal outcomes, with a longer-term aim of improving care for Black, Asian and minority ethnic women.

DARS-NIC-35140-S8F6W.summary: Halton Borough Council, a local authority, uses identifiable birth and death registration data, including primary care mortality data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. It reports using the data in 2023 to produce local life expectancy and mortality figures for ward profiles and council performance reporting.

DARS-NIC-35152-Y4T0D.summary: Devon County Council uses identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits and hotspot mapping. Results are published as summary statistics to guide local services and reduce health inequalities. The council reports that this has informed its Annual Public Health Report, Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-351522-Y6W3L.summary: The Health and Safety Executive uses cancer registrations, death records, demographic details and hospital admissions data for people who completed pesticide competence certificates between 1994 and 2003. It uses them to monitor long-term health, including cancer, deaths and hospital admissions for neurological, eye, respiratory and skin diseases. The aim is to inform policy on the health risks of working with pesticides. Earlier analyses of cancer and deaths have been published in HSE research reports and a 2011 peer-reviewed paper.

DARS-NIC-35166-B5Y7P.summary: Civil Eyes Research Ltd, a commercial research company, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (Hospital Episode Statistics, covering admitted care, outpatients, accident and emergency, and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses them to benchmark hospitals against their peers, with analysis shared in workshops, to improve efficiency and clinical quality. It reports that hospitals have used this to review children's testicular surgery, London neurology services and organ transplantation.

DARS-NIC-351722-W7D4N.summary: L2S2 Ltd, a commercial company, uses pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics for admitted patient care and critical care to develop and maintain CRAB, a tool that compares hospital quality and outcomes while accounting for patients' clinical risk. Its reports support Care Quality Commission inspections and help NHS Trusts benchmark their performance, with the aim of identifying avoidable harm early. Reported benefits include use in CQC inspection work, Trust improvements and inclusion in GIRFT guidance.

DARS-NIC-351761-F8Z6V.summary: NEC Software Solutions UK Limited, a commercial company, is using patient reported outcome measures (questionnaire responses from hip and knee replacement patients) that can be linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). It uses them in its Beyond Compliance service, which monitors new or modified implants and produces monthly summary reports for surgeons, manufacturers and independent assessors. The aim is to spot implant problems early and make patients safer. The service reports it has led to changes in product design, instructions for use and indications for use.

DARS-NIC-351810-N3G6N.summary: The University of Warwick is using civil registration death records, NHS demographic data and a mortality list-cleaning report. It is linking them to its Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Outcomes (OHCAO) registry to track long-term survival of people who survived cardiac arrest outside hospital. The aim is to fill a knowledge gap and support improvements to patient care and outcomes. Reported benefits include survival data informing NHS England policy and annual reports that ambulance services use for planning.

DARS-NIC-352298-S8K3P.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, through its Lincolnshire West sub-ICB location, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. Its contractor, Liaison Financial Services, uses it to validate invoices, including Continuing Healthcare invoices, and to review past payments back to 1 April 2013 for possible overpayments. The main intended benefit is finding and recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping patient confidentiality.

DARS-NIC-352725-V1X2R.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admission, accident and emergency, and death registration records, linked to detailed intensive care data. It aims to find which patients are at risk of heart attacks, strokes and related events after leaving intensive care, and whether treatments and events in intensive care add to that risk. The intended benefit is to identify risk factors that could be changed to prevent these events. So far, it reports building a research resource from two sites, supporting two PhD projects, and creating and testing two predictive models.

DARS-NIC-353126-Y1S5F.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient) and death registrations, linked to GP records for people aged 50 and over. It is studying how frailty develops and how it affects the use of health services, to help plan and commission services for older people. Two published papers have reported that service use and costs rise with frailty severity, and have described how frailty progresses with age.

DARS-NIC-35323-Y2N7J.summary: Thurrock Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to assess local health needs, plan services, support suicide audits and protect public health, with the aim of tailoring services to local needs and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include births data helping redesign the Brighter Futures children's services, and deaths data feeding into suicide audits.

DARS-NIC-353691-D9Z9G.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, through its South Lincolnshire sub-ICB location, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation. Liaison Financial Services checks Continuing Healthcare invoices and past payments back to April 2013 to find possible overpayments and recover the money from providers. The main intended benefit is recovering money that would otherwise be lost, while keeping budget control and protecting patient confidentiality.

DARS-NIC-353882-J5X9Q.summary: The University of Warwick is using pseudonymised hospital admission data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and Emergency Care Data Set records for a PhD study. It examines how patients use out-of-hours and urgent care services that use the Odyssey digital triage tool over the phone, and what happens to their health and later service use afterwards, before and after COVID-19. The main intended benefit is evidence on the safety of digital triage, to help improve the tool and services.

DARS-NIC-35389-P6P2F.summary: Buckinghamshire Council, a local authority, uses identifiable births and deaths registration data, including primary care mortality data. It uses this to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The council reports using the data in its Annual Public Health Report, Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, community board profiles and suicide and drug-related deaths audits.

DARS-NIC-354267-B4V2G.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office is using the 2017 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey, which holds anonymous information on the mental health and wellbeing of children aged 2 to 19 in England. It will analyse how mental health relates to social and economic factors, internet use and risky behaviour. The results will feed into its Vulnerability Framework and reports on children's needs. The aim is to give government and local authorities evidence on where children need more support.

DARS-NIC-354497-V2J9P.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using pseudonymised hospital, A&E, outpatient, patient-reported outcome and death registration records to study how NHS reforms since 2000 affected patient outcomes, waiting times and provider behaviour. It aims to give policymakers stronger evidence for health and social care decisions, including by using deaths in any location as a measure of care quality. Its work has been cited by a Prime Minister, used by NHS Monitor, and its Hospital Frailty Risk Score has been added to an NHS England data portal.

DARS-NIC-35519-S2R9Y.summary: Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. In 2023 the council produced outputs including small-area life expectancy estimates, monthly mortality tracking and excess winter mortality analysis.

DARS-NIC-35531-X3Y7Q.summary: The London Borough of Enfield is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to plan and assess local services, produce needs assessments and advise NHS commissioners. The aim is to understand local health and inequalities. It reports using the data to monitor COVID-19 hospital activity, and to commission falls prevention and frailty programmes.

DARS-NIC-35562-V6G5W.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital records (admitted patient care, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data for patients who had an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. It is using them in the AIRWAYS-2 trial, which compares tracheal intubation with the i-gel supraglottic airway device to find which is more clinically and cost effective. The aim is better evidence on how ambulance staff should treat cardiac arrest. Results have been published, and some UK ambulance trusts, including SWAST, have changed their resuscitation practices in line with guidelines influenced by the trial.

DARS-NIC-355818-H7T3C.summary: Cegedim Rx Ltd, a supplier, uses hospital episode statistics, emergency care data and civil registration death records. It maintains a large research data resource, used for commercial research on behalf of clients such as academia, pharmaceutical companies and public health bodies. Studies cover disease epidemiology, medication safety and healthcare use. The intended benefit is evidence to improve patient outcomes, care pathways and NHS service planning.

DARS-NIC-355855-R4G6G.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists uses linked hospital admission, critical care, demographic and death records for adults who have had emergency abdominal surgery (laparotomy) in England. It uses them for the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit, which produces annual reports comparing hospitals' care and outcomes, such as 30-day mortality, to drive quality improvement. Reported benefits include seven peer-reviewed publications and improvements in key care standards, such as shorter hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-356125-G9Z7Y.summary: Stoke-on-Trent City Council uses identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of people in its area. It uses them for public health planning, immunisation programmes, health protection work and suicide audits. Outputs are aggregated statistics that help tailor local services and reduce health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-356234-W2K8R.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust (CPFT), is using hospital, emergency care and death records linked to CPFT mental health records. It is using them to study physical health problems and deaths in people with mental disorders compared with a control population. The aim is to help narrow the health gap these people experience. Work so far has identified the immediate causes of death in subtypes of dementia (2023) and found that cholinesterase inhibitor use in Lewy body dementia was linked to lower mortality (2022).

DARS-NIC-35642-F6J4F.summary: Newcastle City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable information. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan services, protect public health and carry out suicide audits, publishing only aggregated statistics. The stated aim is to adjust local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include a Drug Market Profile, a Drug Related Death Audit, Covid-19 death analysis and a 0-19 Service Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-356980-Z5B9G.summary: MAC Clinical Research Finance Ltd, a research organisation, uses hospital records covering admitted patient care, outpatients and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for volunteers who have consented. It uses them to check whether volunteers are eligible for clinical trials, as part of recruiting people onto trials for its clients. The main intended benefit is faster, safer matching of volunteers to trials, and less record-request work for GPs.

DARS-NIC-35699-L3K3Q.summary: Hertfordshire County Council uses identifiable birth and death registration data, including primary care mortality data, to study the health needs of its local population. It uses the data for public health planning, suicide audits and hotspot mapping, and for reports such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports it has supplied aggregated births data for school forecasting and children's centres, and has analysed avoidable deaths and suicides.

DARS-NIC-357479-S6C7T.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London, working for the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership and NHS England, uses pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for adults admitted to hospital with asthma attacks. It links this to audit records to measure readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days, to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes. The aim is to improve asthma care and outcomes. A 2023 outcomes report has been used to inform recommendations on service resourcing after the COVID-19 pandemic.

DARS-NIC-359603-D2Q6M.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC) uses identifiable hospital, mental health, community, maternity, emergency care and death registration data. It uses them to monitor health and care providers, plan inspections, flag concerns such as high mortality, and support reviews and national reports. The aim is to protect people from harm and improve care quality. CQC reports that the data have informed inspection planning and published reports, including the 2025/26 State of Care report.

DARS-NIC-359651-H3R1P.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Leicester, uses birth notification data from NHS England for the MBRRACE-UK programme, which monitors maternal, perinatal and infant deaths in England and Wales. The data is used to calculate perinatal mortality rates adjusted for factors such as gestational age and ethnicity, so that trusts and health boards can be compared fairly. The aim is to improve care for women and babies and reduce deaths. Reported benefits include changes to national policy, clinical guidelines and maternity services.

DARS-NIC-359692-Q4X1C.summary: Lightfoot Solutions UK Ltd, a small company, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records in its Signals From Noise analytics platform. NHS clients use the platform to view aggregated charts of waiting times, length of stay and demand, helping them plan services and winter pressures and improve patient outcomes. Reported results include a Wakefield pilot where a targeted approach cut hospital bed days, equivalent to 35 beds a year.

DARS-NIC-359940-W1R7B.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, uses linked hospital admission, death registration and demographic data on patients in six national cardiac audits. It uses them to measure survival and compare hospital and clinician care against national standards, aiming to improve care quality. Audit data is already used by the NHS to support Best Practice Tariff, which rewards hospitals providing a high standard of care.

DARS-NIC-360208-K1T4F.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, with the University of Cambridge, is using hospital, emergency care, imaging, death registration and primary care dispensing records to check clinical data collected for the UK-PBC Genetics Study of primary biliary cholangitis, a rare chronic liver disease. The aim is to improve risk prediction and treatment choice for patients. Checking the data has already found discrepancies in the study database, and a preliminary study was published in the journal Gastroenterology in September 2022.

DARS-NIC-360432-Z1Q8K.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull ICB, with Birmingham City Council and Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council, uses pseudonymised health and social care data covering hospital, community, mental health, primary care prescribing and population records. They use it to commission and plan health and care services and to carry out public health duties, such as needs assessments and reports. The main intended benefit is better-planned services, improved quality and access, and reduced inequalities. The CCG's annual report describes developments supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-36151-L1R4H.summary: Wiltshire Council uses identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services, and run suicide audits and hotspot mapping, publishing only aggregated statistics. The intended benefit is local services targeted to areas of greatest need, with fewer premature deaths. The data has already supported Joint Strategic Needs Assessments (JSNAs) in 2022 and 2023, health needs assessments and local suicide monitoring.

DARS-NIC-361864-N8P1S.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in England in a trial comparing two heart operations to repair the mitral valve: a small cut on the side of the chest and a full breastbone cut. It aims to show which gives patients a better recovery, to inform NHS guidance. Initial trial results are already cited in the 2025 European guidelines for valvular heart disease.

DARS-NIC-362204-F4B2C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, with Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) linked with GP data, identifiable by NHS number, for risk stratification. This applies an algorithm to score which patients are at high risk of health deterioration, so GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-362208-G8K6D.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, GP and other health and social care data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor local health services. The aim is to ensure providers are paid correctly and services match the needs of the local population. It reports that the data has helped it monitor projects and deliver integrated care.

DARS-NIC-362209-B8N9J.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB uses health, social care and registration data, including hospital, mental health, community and GP-related records, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned. The CCG has also published an annual report on achievements the data has supported.

DARS-NIC-362234-W6M0T.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target their care, and plan and commission local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is planned more effectively, improving patient experience and outcomes.

DARS-NIC-362236-D7W4M.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care. The CCG says it has published an annual report describing achievements supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-362237-Y5K7L.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, including identifiable data for some tasks. It uses it to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and commission services. The aim is accurate payments and better-targeted care. Reported results include a model of hospital patient flow and GP-led support for specific at-risk patient groups.

DARS-NIC-362239-F6V0N.summary: NHS South West London ICB uses health and care data from hospitals, GPs, community, mental health, ambulance and social care services, plus births and deaths records. It uses the data to identify patients at high risk of poor health, plan and commission services, and understand local health needs. The aim is to target care better and reduce avoidable hospital admissions. It reports that an annual report describes how the data helped it monitor services during its COVID-19 response.

DARS-NIC-362240-M2L1B.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former East Sussex Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), uses identifiable hospital activity data (SUS+) and patient demographic data. It uses them to check provider invoices and confirm the CCG is the responsible commissioner, and to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better-targeted care. The CCG reports that the data has helped match services to the population's needs and supported delivery of integrated care.

DARS-NIC-362252-M1X0V.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB uses hospital, mental health, community, maternity and other NHS patient data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and commission local health services. The stated aim is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. The CCG also publishes an annual report summarising benefits realised.

DARS-NIC-362253-J5V8L.summary: NHS North Central London ICB uses patient-level health and social care data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and GP-linked records, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. It uses them to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of ill health, and plan and monitor health services. The aim is accurate payment, better targeted care and more effective commissioning. Reported results include funding secured for health inequalities projects, such as a bid expected to bring in £670k over two years.

DARS-NIC-362254-Q6S4W.summary: NHS South East London ICB (formerly the Clinical Commissioning Group, CCG) uses patient-level hospital, mental health, community, GP-linked and other NHS data. It uses this to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The aim is accurate payment and better targeted care. The CCG reports that the data helped it introduce services such as a hospital at home service for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-362255-K5D1H.summary: NHS Kent and Medway ICB (the successor to the Kent and Medway clinical commissioning group) uses patient-level hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data. It uses this to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and to improve care through better targeted, more effective commissioning. The group's 2020/21 annual report highlights achievements that relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-362259-K6L0L.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former West Sussex CCG, uses identifiable and pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community and other provider data to check invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan health services. The aim is to make sure providers are paid correctly and that care is better targeted to local needs. It reports that the data has helped match services to the population's needs and monitor in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-362263-B4Y6N.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (County Durham) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and to support the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-362265-C4M6N.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (formerly the CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. It uses the data to check that provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration by linking it with GP data. The main intended benefits are accurate payments and budget control, and earlier, better-targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-362267-P1W2X.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Bradford District and Craven clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data. It uses it to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of poor health using risk stratification, and to plan health services. The stated aim is to make sure providers are paid accurately and that services and care for vulnerable patients are better planned. The group's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements during the year, some of which relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-362273-D4H7T.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (formerly North Yorkshire CCG) uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices so that only activity it is responsible for is paid. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-362275-P4S4T.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health datasets, including NHS-number-level Secondary Uses Service data for some tasks. It uses them to check invoices from care providers, identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can plan their care, and plan and commission local health services. The main stated benefit is that providers are paid accurately while services are planned around the population's needs.

DARS-NIC-363140-V3X2W.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and outpatients data) together with demographic data about women who had a mastectomy or delayed breast reconstruction in NHS England in 2008 to 2009. It will use them to identify the study group and compare the long-term clinical and cost effectiveness of implant-based and autologous breast reconstruction. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help women, clinicians and commissioners choose between reconstruction options.

DARS-NIC-363464-J4F8N.summary: The King's Fund, a health charity, holds Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient appointments and accident and emergency attendances. It uses the data to give the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) analysis and advice on national health policy, aiming to improve the evidence behind policy decisions. It has delivered a report to DHSC comparing England's emergency admission rates with those of other countries.

DARS-NIC-36455-Y6H8W.summary: Kent County Council, a local authority, is using civil registration births and deaths data and Primary Care Mortality Data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide audits and prevention work. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include analysis of excess winter deaths, suicide patterns, and deaths during heat waves.

DARS-NIC-365132-V5S8H.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care is using pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics for outpatients, admitted patient care, accident and emergency, and critical care, plus the Emergency Care Data Set) through NHS Digital's Data Access Environment. It analyses them to support health and care policy decisions and ministerial requests, often at short notice. Reported results include analysis of 7-day hospital services that informed Ministerial decisions, and outpatient referral analysis that informed policy work.

DARS-NIC-365145-G2P9F.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care uses NHS England's Secondary Uses Service Payment By Results data on hospital episodes, outpatients and spells. It uses the data to analyse health and care activity, so that policy, briefings to ministers and responses to parliamentary questions are based on evidence. The expected benefit is better-informed decisions on planning services, allocating funding and understanding population needs. The reported benefits come from separate Hospital Episode Statistics data, which informed work on new models of care, outpatient referrals and 7-day services.

DARS-NIC-365354-R3M0Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS hospital, GP, death, testing, vaccination, cancer and prescribing data for the RECOVERY trial, which compares treatments for people in hospital with COVID-19. The data gives the trial reliable information on outcomes such as deaths, so it can show which treatments work and could change NHS standard care. Published results have shown that some treatments, such as dexamethasone and tocilizumab, improved survival, and the COVID-19 Public Inquiry cited the trial.

DARS-NIC-365492-H6D6V.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant is using civil registration of death data to follow up one-year mortality for patients recruited to the CRYOSTAT 2 trial, run with Queen Mary University of London. The trial tests whether giving high-dose cryoprecipitate, a fibrinogen-rich blood component, early to adults with major trauma bleeding reduces deaths. The main intended benefit is clear evidence on whether it improves survival, to inform treatment guidelines. Short-term results have been shared with the trial team, and a manuscript is in late preparation.

DARS-NIC-365602-V5H3Z.summary: King's College London is using linked hospital accident and emergency, admitted patient care and death registration records for people with dementia. The data will be used in a PhD study to examine how often people with dementia attend the Emergency Department in their last year of life, why they attend and which factors predict it. The intended benefit is evidence to help policy makers, commissioners and clinicians improve end of life care for people with dementia.

DARS-NIC-365804-B3N1K.summary: Perspectum Ltd, a non-NHS provider, is using NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, deaths, cancer registrations, dispensed medicines and the National Diabetes Audit. It is studying how liver fibroinflammation, MRI measures and the severity and age of onset of eye disease and type 2 diabetes affect heart and other diabetes-related outcomes. The findings are expected to inform evidence-based decisions on care and treatment for people with diabetes.

DARS-NIC-366210-V2H5M.summary: Imperial College London, an academic institution, is using hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient, accident and emergency and critical care), death registrations and patient-reported outcome data. It is researching how NHS staffing, local funding and cancer care pathways affect waiting lists, access to care and patient outcomes, to give policy makers evidence for workforce planning and funding decisions. Earlier work under the agreement produced a tool giving local authorities projections of NHS and social care costs from air pollution.

DARS-NIC-366216-Z9H9Q.summary: The University of Sheffield uses Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which records hospital admissions, to build models of alcohol and tobacco policy. These models estimate how policy changes could affect illness, hospital admissions and costs, to help policymakers reduce harm from smoking and drinking. Its modelling has already informed a Royal College of Physicians report on meeting England's 2030 smoke-free target, and evidence for a government consultation on alcohol duty reform.

DARS-NIC-36666-D1M2K.summary: Hampshire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable details, along with primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention and health protection monitoring. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. So far, the data has enabled small area life expectancy calculations and continues to inform the council's Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-366913-C2V5F.summary: The National Institute for Health Research uses identifiable demographic data from NHS England to find out which people on the Join Dementia Research register have died. It uses this to remove their records, keeping the register up to date and avoiding contact with bereaved families. It reports that several hundred deceased volunteers have been removed from the register so far.

DARS-NIC-36716-S2S3Q.summary: Hampshire County Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care data from NHS England, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. It uses the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reports using the data to inform health needs assessments and substance misuse commissioning, and to help define neighbourhoods with the Integrated Care Board (ICB).

DARS-NIC-36724-F3F7N.summary: North Northamptonshire Council is using birth and death registration records, including identifiable details, and primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan immunisation and public health work, and investigate local concerns such as suicide hotspots. The aim is to tailor health and care services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported uses include the annual public health report, needs assessments and community-level health outcomes for Local Area Partnerships.

DARS-NIC-36794-M9N3S.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, acting for the former NHS Darlington CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be prioritised, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned and targeted.

DARS-NIC-368020-R5L2K.summary: Dr Foster Limited, a supplier of healthcare analytics, uses pseudonymised Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data, which measures deaths in and after hospital at non-specialist acute trusts. It uses the data in dashboards and bespoke reports for NHS clients, comparing SHMI with its own mortality measure, HSMR, to help trusts investigate mortality and improve patient care. Reported benefits include a May 2023 analysis that helped an NHS Foundation Trust understand a SHMI outlier.

DARS-NIC-36808-C2G1F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, through its sub-ICB location covering Durham Dales, Easington and Sedgefield, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-368233-L2N0W.summary: McKinsey & Company, Inc. United Kingdom, a commercial consultancy, uses hospital, emergency care, community services and diagnostic imaging data. It uses them to help NHS clients benchmark performance, compare activity and spending, study trends and forecast future capacity. The aim is to improve the quality and efficiency of NHS services. Past work has included a business case for the National Hospital Programme that secured central government funding.

DARS-NIC-368477-C9Q1X.summary: University College London (UCL) is using NHS England cancer registration, death registration and demographic data, linked to records of young people living with perinatal HIV (HIV acquired before or during birth). The aim is to study the risk of cancer and death as they move into adulthood. The expected benefit is evidence that could help tailor future HIV care and inform clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-368543-C3J4B.summary: CHKS Limited, a supplier, uses pseudonymised Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data on deaths in and within 30 days of leaving hospital. It uses the data for benchmarking and mortality profiling services that help NHS healthcare providers and commissioners analyse mortality, with the aim of improving patient care. Reported benefits include Shrewsbury and Telford and East Cheshire trusts using CHKS reports in mortality review groups, and one organisation planning services around local needs.

DARS-NIC-36866-Q9F5W.summary: Derbyshire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work, with only aggregated outputs published. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include annual and quarterly suicide reports, a life expectancy report for the Director of Public Health and analysis of cancer mortality and birth rates.

DARS-NIC-36882-M3N5C.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, acting for the former South Tees Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area, is using hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It is used to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better planned and targeted.

DARS-NIC-36890-W8W7D.summary: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will analyse them to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners, aiming to give locally focused insight into health inequalities. The council reports it has used the data to shape its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and to support projects on falls prevention, children's injuries and harmful behaviours.

DARS-NIC-36892-P3B3F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (Sunderland area) uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and support the planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned. Reported so far, invoices were validated on time and reports fed into budget and contract management, and an annual report has been published.

DARS-NIC-369348-H6H8B.summary: The University of Dundee is using NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths, cancer registrations and demographics for the ALL-HEART trial. The trial tested whether adding allopurinol to usual treatment reduces strokes, heart attacks and cardiovascular deaths in people with ischaemic heart disease. The aim is to improve their treatment. The main results have been published in the Lancet and presented at international meetings.

DARS-NIC-37047-V8V0H.summary: Peterborough City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. So far, death data has been used to monitor local death rates and inform prioritisation, and births data has fed into a children and young people needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-370530-K6B9K.summary: Isle of Wight Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, protect public health, and support work such as suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported uses include updating JSNA briefings, informing suicide audits, and monitoring excess deaths during and after COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-37060-F5M7B.summary: Cambridgeshire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide prevention audits. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. So far, the data has been used to monitor local death rates and causes and to inform a children and young people needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-370641-K0J0T.summary: The University of Leicester holds linked hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil registration death data for men invited to the NHS Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Screening Programme. The agreement lets it keep the data only, so it can respond to journal requests to revise analyses. The research looked at cardiovascular risk and outcomes after screening to help improve the programme. So far, the work has produced three published conference abstracts and supported funded NIHR grant applications.

DARS-NIC-370843-R6V8T.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for UK participants in the COSMOS mobile phone study. It uses them to follow participants' long-term health and examine whether mobile phone use is linked to health problems. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform health policy and advice on mobile phones. A 2024 published paper on 264,574 participants found no association between cumulative phone use and brain tumours.

DARS-NIC-37123-L4W1M.summary: West Sussex County Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to measure local health needs, support immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, to reduce mortality and health inequalities. In 2023 it reviewed mortality in COVID and non-COVID years and reported this to the Sussex ICB board.

DARS-NIC-371243-H1P5T.summary: NHS North and East London Commissioning Support Unit uses national Hospital Episode Statistics, emergency care and diagnostic imaging data for NHS England's commissioning support units. They use it to benchmark hospital activity and outcomes, helping commissioners and local authorities compare areas and plan services. Reported benefits include analysis of GP referral rates across London CCGs, support for diabetes and respiratory improvements, and modelling of drivers of A&E attendance.

DARS-NIC-371828-D2W1R.summary: Norfolk County Council uses pseudonymised hospital data, covering admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care records, to support its public health duties. It uses the data to produce local health needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, with the aim of better targeting services and tackling health inequalities. Reported benefits include a falls dashboard, updated electoral division health profiles, and a tool to support alcohol licensing decisions.

DARS-NIC-371831-L7M1M.summary: Leeds City Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital data covering inpatient, outpatient, accident and emergency, and critical care records. It uses the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to understand local health inequalities and the burden on Leeds hospitals. The data already feeds an area profile tool, an alcohol harm matrix used in licensing objections, and a performance report.

DARS-NIC-371832-J2L9K.summary: Lincolnshire County Council, a local authority, uses pseudonymised hospital records covering admissions, outpatient visits, accident and emergency, critical care and emergency care. It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, the Director of Public Health's annual report, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Reported benefits include an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, profiles for Primary Care Networks and analyses of self-harm, which informed local strategy and services.

DARS-NIC-37191-P5S9S.summary: University College London (UCL) is using death registration, cancer registration, demographic and mortality flagging data to follow up men in the RADICALS prostate cancer trial. It is used to capture deaths and cancer events that trial sites may miss and to check causes of death, giving more accurate survival estimates. Linking the data identified 33 deaths that sites had not reported, and trial results have already changed practice, sparing some men unnecessary radiotherapy.

DARS-NIC-372269-N8D7Z.summary: University College London is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, death, COVID-19 test and vaccination records, linked to its Virus Watch household study of 58,490 people. The aim is to estimate community COVID-19 infections, hospital visits and deaths, and to see how social distancing affected routine health service use. It is intended to inform the NHS and public health response. Findings have been presented to national advisory groups and used in reports and briefings, including one referenced by Australia's Department of Health.

DARS-NIC-372677-H7S0S.summary: The University of Warwick holds Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) cause of death and flagging current status reports for a study of older people in residential and nursing homes. The study tested whether a programme to promote exercise and social interaction reduces depression among residents. Under this agreement the data may only be retained for an interim period, with no other use. The study has produced a final NIHR HTA report and a Lancet publication.

DARS-NIC-372684-X6Q3M.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using NHS England's Medical Research Information Service (MRIS) data, including cause of death, cancer event notifications, current status and demographic details, for women in a cohort of about 25,000 breast cancer cases. The study looks at treatment effects and endocrine, genetic and cellular risk factors for a second breast cancer in the other breast. It also aims to identify genes that affect breast cancer risk and assess their value in predicting it.

DARS-NIC-372791-X0H3Q.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) uses NHS Digital data on people who have had COVID-19, linked to its blood donor database, to find and contact people who might donate convalescent plasma. The plasma contains antibodies and is being tested as a treatment for patients with COVID-19, including in the REMAP-CAP and RECOVERY trials. It aims to widen the pool of potential donors. By 15 November 2020, 33,994 donor attendances had led to 24,530 plasma donations collected.

DARS-NIC-372865-W5X1R.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This produces risk scores that identify patients likely to need high levels of care, so GPs and commissioners can target support and plan services. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-373042-Y8N7D.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former West Suffolk CCG) uses hospital data from SUS for Commissioners, linked with GP data and identifiable by NHS number. Prescribing Services Ltd uses it for risk stratification, which applies an algorithm to predict which patients are at high risk of health deterioration and heavy use of services. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is fewer avoidable emergency admissions through earlier intervention.

DARS-NIC-373132-D3Y7P.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient, COVID-19 hospitalisation and death registration records for the PRINCIPLE trial, which tests treatments for COVID-19 in people over 50 with health conditions and those over 65. The data is used to measure how well treatments given early in the illness prevent hospital admission and help people recover. The trial reports twice weekly to Public Health England, and these reports feed into disease monitoring and help shape national policy.

DARS-NIC-373563-N8Z9J.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, uses hospital records, emergency care data, death registrations and hospital mortality indicators. It uses them to provide paid analysis services to health sector clients, including software dashboards, care pathway analysis, hospital benchmarking and clinical trial site identification. The intended benefit is helping clients find ways to improve patient care and experience. Reported results include an analysis of unequal access to CAR-T cancer therapy and a characterisation of Thyroid Eye Disease patients, both being used to engage with the healthcare system.

DARS-NIC-374190-D0N1M.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, is using NHS England hospital, primary care, cancer, death, vaccination and COVID-19 surveillance records. It links them to whole genome sequences from people severely affected by COVID-19 to study how genes affect response to the virus. The aim is to find genetic variants and biomarkers that could inform new treatments and tests. Results so far include published papers in Nature identifying genetic variants linked to severe COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-374223-P4P4L.summary: The NIHR Bioresource is keeping hospital, emergency care, death registration and COVID-19 hospitalisation records for over 30,000 people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who volunteered for research. The records were collected to study how IBD medicines such as immunosuppressants and anti-TNF therapies, and genetic risk factors, affect COVID-19 outcomes. The main intended benefit is to inform treatment recommendations and policy for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-374907-Q5W5W.summary: Cardiff University is using linked hospital records (admissions, outpatient and accident and emergency) and death registration data to study the Family Nurse Partnership, a home visiting programme for young first-time mothers. The work examines how the programme produces its effects, including on child maltreatment indicators. It aims to inform the future development of home visiting in England and Germany. Earlier findings have already informed national and local decisions on continuing the programme and changing its content and delivery.

DARS-NIC-374924-C8S5Y.summary: The University of Sheffield is using demographic data from NHS Digital's list cleaning service to check whether people with bladder cancer have died and to find their current addresses. This supports a longitudinal survey of patient reported outcomes, which follows newly diagnosed patients in Yorkshire, the Humber, North Derbyshire and South Tees over their first 12 months. The main intended benefit is to avoid sending surveys to bereaved families, improve response rates, and identify gaps in care.

DARS-NIC-375354-G8V1H.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked hospital records (admissions, A&E, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data, joined to the QResearch database of GP records. It is using them solely for COVID-19 research, including linking to intensive care data held by ICNARC. The main aim is to help patients and doctors reduce the risk of severe COVID-19, for example by finding out whether common long-term medicines make the illness worse or better.

DARS-NIC-375669-J7M7F.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust, working with Queen Mary University of London, is using pseudonymised, patient-level Hospital Episode Statistics covering inpatient admissions, critical care and outpatient appointments. It is studying how COVID-19 disrupted surgery and other hospital procedures in England, how they are restarting, and what future waves might mean for care. The aim is to give policy makers and NHS planners evidence to plan surgical care and resources.

DARS-NIC-376141-W5D3L.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using linked national hospital, mental health, psychological therapies and death records for women who gave birth. It is studying whether community perinatal mental health teams change mental health admissions, access to care, birth outcomes and costs. The aim is to inform how these services are commissioned. Results have been published in peer-reviewed papers, including findings that the teams' national roll-out reduced the risk of acute mental health episodes after birth.

DARS-NIC-376367-M5V9H.summary: The University of Nottingham uses linked hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) with the QResearch database of GP records. Researchers use it to study disease causes, medicine safety and treatment outcomes, aiming to give doctors and patients better evidence for decisions. Its risk tools, such as QRISK, are now used across NHS GP practices and are recommended in NICE guidance.

DARS-NIC-37647-J8W1M.summary: Leicestershire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration births and deaths data and Primary Care Mortality Data, including identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is for services to be tailored to local needs and to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported work so far includes the Director of Public Health's Annual Report and the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-376603-K2J9R.summary: NHS England, with the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership, uses patient-level hospital, outpatient, emergency care, death registration and demographic records for adults diagnosed with bowel cancer in England and Wales. The data supports the National Bowel Cancer Audit, which assesses the quality of NHS care and outcomes. The aim is to help services compare themselves and improve care. The audit reports a rise in stage III colon cancer patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy, from 54% to 61%.

DARS-NIC-37666-Z1C3M.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using NHS hospital, cancer registration, death and demographic records for women in the LATTE study, who took part in the earlier ATAC breast cancer trial. It is studying the long-term safety and effectiveness of anastrozole compared with tamoxifen, including recurrence and survival. The aim is to help patients and clinicians choose between the treatments. Data received so far has provided information on deaths and breast cancer recurrence for the study's main endpoints.

DARS-NIC-377038-J7G7X.summary: NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit is using pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care data, covering clinical and financial information, for four Black Country clinical commissioning groups (CCGs): Dudley, Sandwell and West Birmingham, Walsall and Wolverhampton. The data supports planning and commissioning of health services for the local population. The stated aim is to understand patient flows and population needs, so services can be redesigned and targeted more effectively.

DARS-NIC-377644-X9J4P.summary: The University of Sheffield, an academic organisation, is using linked health records for people with suspected COVID-19 who used emergency care. These include GP data for pandemic planning, emergency care and hospital admission records, critical care records and death registrations. The PRIEST study is evaluating how well 111, ambulance and emergency department triage worked, and developing risk tools to identify patients likely to deteriorate. The intended benefit is fewer patients wrongly advised to self-care and less strain on services.

DARS-NIC-37789-N6J1N.summary: Leeds City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to assess local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide audits and hotspot mapping. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The council reports using the data for its 2022 Director of Public Health annual report and a mortality dashboard.

DARS-NIC-378185-P4L5Z.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensing records for 1,615 adults with heart failure who consented to take part in a trial. It is testing the Medicines at Transitions Intervention (MaTI) toolkit, which aims to make medicines safer and more consistent when patients move from hospital to home. The data will show whether the toolkit reduces deaths and hospital readmissions within 12 months. The main intended benefit is better evidence for heart failure care and guidance.

DARS-NIC-378523-Y5Q9L.summary: The University of Leeds holds hospital admissions and accident and emergency records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for residents of 12 Yorkshire care homes taking part in a feasibility trial. The data is used to check hospital attendance for safety and to measure health service use for a physical activity programme called REACH. This supports a decision on whether to seek funding for a larger trial. This version only allows the data to be securely retained.

DARS-NIC-378657-B8F3K.summary: The University of Birmingham, an academic organisation, is using hospital, emergency care and death registration data, with the University of Oxford processing it. It is studying how hospitals' approaches to acute care affected their resilience for COVID-19 and for other conditions, such as heart failure and stroke. The aim is to inform policy and NHS acute services. The team has completed one study on how hospitals' recovery of elective activity after the pandemic varied, mainly by region.

DARS-NIC-37891-V3K0S.summary: London Borough of Sutton, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses this to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and support work such as suicide audits. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The figures have informed neighbourhood team locality profiles and the Sutton Suicide Prevention Strategy.

DARS-NIC-378964-S2X2T.summary: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to analyse local health needs. It uses them to support its statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies and commissioning, with the aim of targeting services to local residents, particularly the most disadvantaged. The council reports using the data to break down COPD and hip fracture admissions locally and to inform weight management work.

DARS-NIC-379653-W3G5Q.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London is using pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration records for children and young people admitted to hospital with asthma attacks. It links them to National Respiratory Audit Programme data to study readmissions and deaths within 30 and 90 days. The aim is to show whether care has led to good outcomes and to improve standards of care. Reported benefits include a 2023 outcomes report that informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-379681-D6L7G.summary: The University of York is using hospital admission records for children with life-limiting conditions, linked to death registration data, to study how long these children and young people survive and how common these conditions are in England. The aim is to help plan children's palliative care and hospice services. The final report was launched in April 2020 and is being used by regional children's palliative care networks and NHS England for service planning.

DARS-NIC-379807-P3R7Z.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) is using pseudonymised hospital admission, death registration and National Diabetes Audit data for patients in adult critical care or who had an in-hospital cardiac arrest. It is studying risk factors and longer-term outcomes of critical illness to improve the risk models behind national clinical audits. Results so far include a published report, journal papers on sepsis and atrial fibrillation, and a new Case Mix Programme dataset now used in all participating units.

DARS-NIC-380650-K4F6X.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked hospital admissions, patient-reported outcome, and death registration data, combined with National Joint Registry data, to study results of revision hip and knee replacements. The aim is to understand outcomes, how they vary over time and place, and which factors affect them, so patients and surgeons can make better-informed decisions. The research has so far led to published journal papers on revision knee and hip replacement and a web application to support shared decision making.

DARS-NIC-381078-Y9C5K.summary: Health Data Research UK, an academic organisation, is using linked NHS hospital, GP, prescribing, vaccination, testing, mental health, maternity and death records for the COVID-IMPACT-UK research consortium. The research looks at how existing health conditions affect COVID-19, and how COVID-19 and the response to it affect later health. It aims to inform public health policy and clinical care. Published papers have already informed vaccine safety reporting to national bodies and discussions with the Chief Medical Officer.

DARS-NIC-381383-Z9F2P.summary: The Department for Transport holds hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics admitted patient care and accident and emergency data) linked to police road accident data. This agreement only lets it keep that data for an interim period while it applies to extend the agreement. The data has been used to understand road injuries and to identify seriously injured casualties more accurately than police judgement allows. HES analysis has appeared in the Reported Road Casualties Great Britain reports from 2016 to 2019 and fed into the STATS19 review, which produced recommendations on injury-based reporting.

DARS-NIC-381632-M4D9L.summary: The University of Oxford is using the Shielded Patient List, which here means a pseudonymised NHS Number and a COVID-19 risk code (high or moderate) for each listed patient. It will use this to develop and validate a new tool that predicts which people in England are at high risk of severe outcomes from COVID-19. The aim is a widely used, validated tool that supports consistent shielding policy and clearer communication between policy makers, professionals and the public.

DARS-NIC-381633-K9Y2T.summary: The University of Oxford's Department of Paediatrics holds COVID-19 test results from non-hospital (Pillar 2) antigen testing. It uses them in a trial of the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine to assess its efficacy and safety, and it will keep the data so that regulators can audit the findings. The main aim is to show whether the vaccine protects people from COVID-19. Analyses have already looked at efficacy against asymptomatic disease, reduced likelihood of transmission after vaccination, and efficacy against new variants.

DARS-NIC-381634-X8H0H.summary: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is using linked, pseudonymised NHS and COVID-19 testing, vaccination and hospital data to study how COVID-19 spreads between household members. The aim is to improve national surveillance of infections in England and show how vaccination affects transmission. Reported results include analysis showing household transmission was 40% to 50% lower where the first case had been vaccinated, published in The New England Journal of Medicine and used by government advisory groups.

DARS-NIC-381683-R6R6K.summary: The University of Oxford, working for the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) Research and Surveillance Centre and Public Health England, uses pseudonymised GP records linked to hospital, emergency care, mental health, imaging and COVID-19 test data. It uses them for studies and monitoring of COVID-19 in England, including community spread and the effects of lockdown on other conditions. The main intended benefit is better information for the national public health response.

DARS-NIC-381719-L6D2H.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, with King's College Hospital, is using Hospital Episode Statistics Critical Care data linked to its research data warehouse of clinical, laboratory and demographic records for patients tested for COVID-19 and other respiratory pathogens. It is being used for research on disease progression, treatment and outcomes, including risk calculators and prediction tools. The stated aim is to support better-informed decisions about COVID-19 treatment and care.

DARS-NIC-381887-X5W2S.summary: The University of Warwick is using hospital inpatient and outpatient records and death registration data. The researchers are studying why GP practices in England differ in how often they refer patients with suspected bowel cancer. They are also looking at how this affects diagnosis and survival, and at the effect of the bowel screening programme. The aim is to help target care at the right groups and reduce inefficiency in primary care.

DARS-NIC-381948-L9M8Y.summary: Northumbria Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, which hosts the Bone and Joint Infection Registry (BAJIR), is using hospital admissions (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and demographics data. It will run a feasibility study with 250 consenting patients, comparing NHS England data with registry records to check they are complete and accurate. The main intended benefit is a more accurate registry, and patients' care teams may also learn of details they did not know.

DARS-NIC-38197-Z4J4Y.summary: Torbay Council uses identifiable births, deaths and Primary Care Mortality Data to understand local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, and protect public health, including through suicide audits. It produces aggregated statistics for reports such as the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. Reported benefits include the data informing the local suicide prevention strategy and the 2023 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-381972-Q5F0V.summary: University College London uses linked, de-identified NHS hospital, maternity, mental health, community services and birth and death records, held in the ECHILD Research Database, to study how children's health, education and social care connect from childhood into adulthood. The aim is to give policy-makers evidence on improving outcomes for children and families. Reported results include published papers and studies commissioned by the Department of Health and Social Care.

DARS-NIC-381984-B7X3S.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised patient-level Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator (SHMI) data, which covers deaths in hospital and within 30 days of discharge. It uses the data in its Healthcare Evaluation Data (HED) system so NHS organisations can monitor mortality, benchmark against peers and spot areas of concern or good practice. The aim is to support safer, better-quality care. Bolton NHS FT reported that its mortality metrics moved into the expected range after it used the analytics.

DARS-NIC-38231-Y7T5P.summary: The London Borough of Hillingdon, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. It reports that the data informed needs assessments, including work by its suicide awareness panel and on low birth weights, and was used to test a claim about stillbirths.

DARS-NIC-382333-M5J9W.summary: The University of Bristol is using linked NHS hospital, emergency care and mental health service records for children in State care in England. It is studying how common mental health concerns are, and how these children move through mental health services compared with other children, before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The intended benefit is new evidence to help policy makers and services identify the children most at risk and support them earlier.

DARS-NIC-382334-Y2B1C.summary: The National Audit Office uses hospital, emergency care, mental health and linked death registration data from NHS Digital to produce value-for-money audit reports for Parliament. It analyses this data to examine how the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS bodies spend public money, aiming to help Parliament hold them to account and help services improve. Its reports have led NHS England to change GP opening-hour payment rules, and cancer admissions analysis identified £9 million of savings.

DARS-NIC-382364-Y0F4F.summary: The University of York is using the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a national survey of adults' mental health. It will study whether socioeconomic factors are linked to psychiatric hospital admissions for people diagnosed with a personality disorder. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence to inform policy, clinical practice and interventions, with the aim of reducing hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-382794-T3L3M.summary: Queen Mary University of London uses linked GP, hospital, maternity, birth, death, cancer and COVID-19 records to support the QResearch database. Approved UK researchers use it for observational medical research on the causes, treatment and outcomes of disease, with results published in journals. The aim is better evidence for patient care and health policy. Its QRISK and QCOVID risk tools are already used in NHS care, and its vaccine safety studies informed regulators.

DARS-NIC-38314-C3P0Z.summary: The University of Cambridge is using NHS England mortality data (death registrations and cause-of-death, event notification and current status reports) for the Oesophageal Cancer Clinical and Molecular Stratification (OCCAMS) study. The study looks at clinical and genetic factors affecting oesophageal cancer, to help predict how it progresses and tailor treatment. Reported results include several published papers and a revised lymph node-based classification giving better prognostic information.

DARS-NIC-383203-Q8B9L.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit uses pseudonymised hospital records linked to civil registration death data to measure the quality and safety of healthcare. The aim is to show variations in outcomes between hospitals and to develop risk-adjusted indicators, supporting better quality and safety of care in England. Its mortality alerts helped identify problems at Mid Staffordshire NHS Foundation Trust, and its published research on junior doctor changeovers led to a new shadowing protocol.

DARS-NIC-383324-D6B8T.summary: The Nuffield Trust for Research and Policy Studies in Health Services is using linked hospital admissions, patient-reported outcome and death registration data to study the care of frail older people. It is developing measures to spot areas giving good care to people over 65, and evaluating Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA), a multidisciplinary assessment of frail patients. The aim is to help the NHS target services at those who would benefit most. So far, a frailty risk score paper has been submitted to a journal, with a decision pending.

DARS-NIC-383345-W2D3J.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England, an academic body, uses linked hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and A&E) and death registration data for mothers and their children. It is studying how maternal factors before and during pregnancy affect children's use of health services and their outcomes, with the aim of informing NHS and policy decisions on maternity and children's care. Three papers have been published so far, including work that has led to other studies linking mother and baby records.

DARS-NIC-383356-N8J6Z.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, with the University of Cambridge, holds civil registrations of death data from a completed clinical trial called PROTECT-V. The data is kept for secure storage and back-up, and so earlier analyses can be repeated to check published findings if they are questioned. The trial tested whether a niclosamide nasal spray can prevent COVID-19 in people on dialysis or taking immunosuppressive medicines. The main hoped-for benefit is a preventive option for immunocompromised people.
