DARS-NIC-38410-S7X7G.summary: Somerset Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with outputs published as aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include a suicide audit report, an infectious disease needs assessment and analysis of excess deaths during the COVID-19 pandemic.

DARS-NIC-384136-J3N8Z.summary: NHS North East London ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected during the COVID-19 emergency. It uses the data to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping manage demand and capacity and supporting better commissioning decisions for patients.

DARS-NIC-384137-V8F6H.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using Hospital Episode Statistics data on admitted patient care, outpatient and accident and emergency care for the BRIGHTLIGHT study of teenagers and young adults with cancer. It will refine a scale of how much specialist care they received, to test whether specialist services add value. The aim is to show which model of care is best for young people and cost-effective for the NHS. Published papers have already reported findings on care outcomes and on diagnosis timeliness.

DARS-NIC-384326-R9V7S.summary: The Nuffield Department of Primary Health Sciences, part of the University of Oxford, is using hospital admission, cancer registration and death records for 1,490 people aged 60 or over in the NewKI chronic kidney disease (CKD) study. It is studying which factors predict death, cardiovascular disease and other poor health outcomes, and whether screening for CKD in primary care is effective. The aim is to help doctors identify who needs closer monitoring. Publications from the study have already estimated how common CKD is in UK primary care.

DARS-NIC-384504-N2V5B.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses NHS hospital and emergency care records, linked to survey answers from the Millennium Cohort Study at age 17. It uses them to check and improve the survey data and to support health research. The aim is to help research that benefits health and social care. So far, a linked dataset and a user guide have been made available to researchers, and a webinar has been delivered.

DARS-NIC-384582-F4X9R.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health services for COVID-19, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions on demand, capacity and workforce. The CCG has published an annual report on its COVID-19 response, which this data helped to support.

DARS-NIC-384608-C9B4L.summary: NHS England uses a range of COVID-19 related health data, including GP records, test results, death registrations, NHS 111, prescribing and shielded patient list data. It uses them to analyse how COVID-19 is spreading, plan services and resources, and produce dashboards and reports. The main intended benefit is to help control the virus and reduce deaths. Reported results include letters and guidance sent to people at high risk, and analysis showing a fall in spirometry activity in general practice, which led to initiatives to restart it safely.

DARS-NIC-384618-N1H4Y.summary: The University of Sheffield, an academic organisation, holds NHS Digital cohort notification and current status reports from the Medical Research Information Service (MRIS). It used them to check whether children in the MERIDIAN fetal brain imaging study were still alive before inviting families to a 2-3 year follow-up. The data is now kept only for back-up and storage. The study's results were published, including a final report in December 2017, and were used to produce improved information leaflets for parents.

DARS-NIC-384653-L3N2Q.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital records covering admissions, outpatient visits and accident and emergency visits for patients who had bariatric (weight-loss) or other planned general surgery. The study compares how much healthcare these patients use over the medium term, to help show how safe bariatric surgery is. The intended benefit is to inform commissioners and policy makers, which may make bariatric surgery more accessible to suitable patients.

DARS-NIC-384661-Z9H3W.summary: NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) COVID-19 data from GP records, along with ethnic category and vaccination status data. It uses this to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-384771-T2D4G.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB is using pseudonymised GP record data (coded details such as diagnoses, medications, tests and vaccinations) collected for pandemic planning and research. It uses the data to plan local health care during COVID-19, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission as groups rather than individuals, and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is better management of demand, capacity and resources.

Reported benefits include published studies on a fat-based imaging marker for heart attack risk, which has been included in clinical guidance.

DARS-NIC-39315-W4J4J.summary: North Lincolnshire Council uses identifiable birth and death registration data, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local public health needs. It uses them for measuring health needs, planning services, and work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to target services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. The council reports using the data to produce population, ward, locality and health inequality profiles, and to inform its suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-393510-D6H1D.summary: University College London's Children and Families Policy Research Unit uses linked NHS hospital, community, maternity, mental health, birth, death and COVID-19 testing records to study how children and young people use health services and what outcomes follow. The aim is to inform policy and practice for children's health and reduce future pressure on the NHS. So far, the work has produced published papers, including one on hospital admissions as young people with learning disabilities or autism move to adult services, and a policy briefing.

DARS-NIC-393650-B7J6F.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care is using demographic data, including names and contact details of people aged 5 and over, so Ipsos MORI can invite a random sample to take part in the Imperial College London REACT-1 COVID-19 testing study. The study estimates infection rates and the R value across England, regionally and locally. Reported results include informing lockdown and tier decisions, and being used in government briefings.

DARS-NIC-393853-V6F2F.summary: Bristol City Council's public health team uses hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics covering admitted care, A&E, critical care and outpatients) and Emergency Care Data Set data. It uses them to analyse local health needs and inequalities, supporting its statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported uses so far include informing children's centre programmes, road traffic injury and self-harm work, and homelessness and school health profiles.

DARS-NIC-394183-K3Q7F.summary: Sefton Metropolitan Borough Council's public health team is using hospital records covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) or emergency care. It uses them to analyse local health needs and inequalities, and to support its statutory public health duties, including needs assessments, strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to make local services more targeted and responsive. So far, the data has fed ward-level figures for the Substance Use needs assessment and reporting to the Combatting Drug Partnership.

DARS-NIC-394285-D0L6M.summary: Suffolk County Council, a local authority, is using pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, along with ethnic category and vaccination status data. It uses them to support its local COVID-19 response, including outbreak management, spotting health inequalities and analysing vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is identifying people at highest risk and targeting action to control the spread of the virus.

DARS-NIC-395236-V3W9P.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care, through the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities, is using Cardiovascular Disease Prevention Audit data, linked with hospital admissions and death registration records. It is using them for detailed analysis to support government and NHS England policy, including the health mission to cut deaths from heart attack and stroke, and to support NICE guidance. It is expected to strengthen the evidence on preventing cardiovascular disease. Earlier work produced a national report, published annually, and an interactive dashboard, published quarterly.

DARS-NIC-39553-K5V4H.summary: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus Primary Care Mortality Data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported uses include Covid-19 death analysis for the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and end of life care monitoring.

DARS-NIC-396095-H1P1D.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board uses pseudonymised, person-level health data from hospital, community, mental health, primary care and registration sources. It uses the data for COVID-19 analytics, including dashboards and reports that support recovery planning and target care to vulnerable people. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient outcomes. Reported results include an enhanced case-finding tool for clinicians and an elective recovery waiting list tool.

DARS-NIC-396113-N9L4L.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using GP records for pandemic planning and research, death registration records and virtual ward pilot data. It is evaluating whether monitoring suspected COVID-19 patients at home with remote checks, such as oxygen levels, can improve outcomes and reduce hospital use. The evaluation informed NHS England's Covid Oximetry at Home programme, including its 14-day monitoring period and oxygen saturation thresholds, and a pre-print paper has been published.

DARS-NIC-396119-C8W3W.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS data on COVID-19 hospital admissions, first positive COVID-19 test results and civil registrations of death for its RAPTOR-C19 study. The study compares new rapid point-of-care COVID-19 tests with laboratory tests in GP practices, to see how accurate they are. Linking the data aims to give more accurate estimates of test accuracy. The university reports it has already used the linked hospital data to build this improved reference standard.

DARS-NIC-396423-H4Z6Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using details from NHS Digital's Permission to Contact service, which holds information given voluntarily by people who agreed to be contacted about COVID-19 vaccine trials. It will use this to invite potentially eligible people to take part in its COVID-19 vaccine trial. The main intended benefit is faster, more transparent recruitment, helping speed the development of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-39719-F8X6K.summary: Leicester City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support suicide prevention, with published results being aggregated statistics. The aim is to adjust local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include updated needs assessments, targeted Covid-19 messaging and vaccination, and input to the 0-19s Healthy Child Programme service specification.

DARS-NIC-397618-T8L8Z.summary: NHS England is using Community-Local Provider Flows data, linked to pseudonymised GP records inside the OpenSAFELY secure analytics platform, so approved researchers can study COVID-19. The aim is to examine how high cost drugs relate to COVID-19 outcomes and to help identify who is at highest risk. Reported results include informing policy on shielding and vaccine prioritisation, and adding to the evidence on how several drugs are associated with COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-39782-Z8J2T.summary: London Borough of Newham, a local authority, is using Hospital Episode Statistics data covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. It will use the data in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report, and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the needs of the most disadvantaged residents are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-39816-L3W3Z.summary: Nottinghamshire County Council uses civil registration births and deaths data, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan public health services, and support work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported results include monitoring excess deaths during COVID-19 and local analysis of life expectancy and avoidable deaths.

DARS-NIC-398405-S0M4K.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admission records and death registration data for about 5,000 older adults in the CRASH-4 trial. The trial tests whether an early tranexamic acid injection helps people with mild traumatic brain injury, by tracking deaths, dementia and other outcomes for one year after joining. The expected benefit is reliable evidence to inform clinical guidelines and the care of older adults with this injury.

DARS-NIC-39848-B4R9P.summary: Medway Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan public health services and support work such as suicide prevention, with published results kept to aggregated figures. The main aim is to tailor local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported results include local area and health inequalities profiles, which informed a population health needs assessment and the local Integrated Care Strategy.

DARS-NIC-398666-H2S4K.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB, with three local clinical commissioning groups (CCGs) and three councils, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health data. They use it to plan and commission health services for the local population and to support public health work. The stated benefits include better service planning, fewer avoidable emergency readmissions and reduced health inequalities. The CCGs have published 2020/21 annual reports describing achievements, some of which relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-399287-T3X7W.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) is using NHS England death registration, emergency care and hospital admission and outpatient records for children in two randomised trials. The trials compare two kinds of breathing support, high flow nasal cannula and continuous positive airway pressure, in critically ill children. The aim is to give evidence on which works better and costs less as first-line support. Results have been published in the Journal of the American Medical Association for both trials.

DARS-NIC-399787-Z7T4V.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB is using pseudonymised GP record data (coded health details, with no free text) collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research. It uses the data to support its local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-399791-K3C6F.summary: NHS North Central London ICB is using pseudonymised (identifying details removed) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health services, model which patients are at risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-399796-Z4Q9K.summary: NHS Northamptonshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health services, assess risk and allocate resources during the COVID-19 response. The aim is to help commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The organisation reports that the data improved its understanding of demand, capacity and COVID-19 risks, and supported content in its annual reports.

DARS-NIC-399802-C7Y9D.summary: NHS North West London ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. It uses this to plan local health care during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and deciding where to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping manage demand and capacity and supporting better commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-399806-Q4L9C.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data, covering GP record data, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, forecast demand, identify patients at risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and a more effective response to the outbreak. The CCG's annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-399808-H3X8Q.summary: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. It uses them to plan local health services during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine rollout. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-399820-P9V9S.summary: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses this to plan local health services, model which patients are at risk of hospital admission, allocate resources and monitor vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity in response to COVID-19. The CCGs' published annual reports describe pandemic response work that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-400071-X3M7N.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire ICB uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. It uses them to plan local health services, assess risk and allocate resources during the COVID-19 response, and to monitor vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and make better decisions for patients. The CCG has published an annual report describing its COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-400077-T4C4V.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West Integrated Care Board and Oxfordshire County Council use pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital, community, mental health, social care, prescribing and births and deaths data. They use it to plan and commission health services, understand local needs and monitor quality, with the aim of better decisions and services. Reported benefits include monitoring cancer waiting times, helping develop the C the Signs cancer-risk tool, and assessing a cancer care review scheme.

DARS-NIC-400304-S1P1B.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) uses identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, GP, mental health therapy, birth and demographic records. It links them to study how COVID-19 affected disadvantaged groups, including employment and benefits outcomes, and to answer COVID inquiry queries. The aim is to give government better evidence for its pandemic response. ONS reports a completed project on long-term conditions and employment outcomes, due to be published.

DARS-NIC-400790-V0Y8W.summary: The University of Leicester is using linked, pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for children in England and Wales. It is studying what happens to children in their first two years when they move between neonatal and paediatric care. The aim is to help prepare families for neonatal discharge and to inform discharge policy and service planning. So far, one paper on paediatric intensive care admission risk in very preterm babies has been published, and a national group is drafting discharge guidance using the findings.

DARS-NIC-400985-V3D1C.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust is using hospital, emergency care, death registration and COVID-19 surveillance records for surgical patients in England. It is studying how COVID-19 and delays to surgery have affected deaths and complications, including differences by region, ethnicity and deprivation. The aim is to help policymakers plan the recovery of surgical services. Published papers have already described a fall in surgical activity and a higher risk of death for surgical patients with COVID-19, informing national health policy.

DARS-NIC-401171-F9Z8T.summary: The National Institute for Health Research is using Permission to Contact data, which is contact and eligibility details from people who volunteered to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. It is used to invite potentially eligible people to join a Phase 3 trial of the Novavax vaccine run by St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping a vaccine become available sooner.

DARS-NIC-401890-W6Q8W.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients with compatible Medtronic implanted cardiac devices who have consented to take part. It is studying the workload of the Triage-HF Plus pathway, where remote device risk scores prompt phone calls to patients at high risk of worsening heart failure. The aim is to help providers judge the effects of changing clinical workflows. Preliminary results have appeared in a peer-reviewed paper and contributed to NICE guidance published in 2024.

DARS-NIC-401935-N9W7P.summary: East Anglian Air Ambulance is using pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care and emergency care records for about 1,600 patients it treated in 2021/22. It is linking these to its own patient records to evaluate its care across the whole patient pathway, including diagnoses and outcomes. The aim is to find ways to improve care for future patients. It reports that the linked data was used to quantify secondary hospital transfers, work that won a prize at the 999 EMS Research Forum in 2024, and to evaluate a new intracranial bleeding pathway.

DARS-NIC-402080-N3V5Z.summary: The University of Exeter, working with the University of Cambridge, is using the names and contact details of people who took part in the Mental Health of Children and Young People surveys in 2020 and 2021. They will invite parents and young people to follow-up interviews about how Covid-19 affected mental health, education, access to services, special educational needs and disabilities, and eating disorders. The aim is to produce reports and briefings to help plan services and prepare for any future pandemic. Early findings have been presented at talks and conferences and in a participant newsletter.

DARS-NIC-402116-G1T7V.summary: The Health & Social Care Information Centre is using ethnic category data drawn from GP records and hospital records (inpatient, outpatient and accident and emergency). It will link this data to existing systems to support the NHS England national call/recall flu vaccination programme. It will be used to identify COVID patients at high risk and to report on vaccine uptake by ethnic category, to address health inequalities. The aim is to reduce winter pressure on the NHS and help coordinate flu and COVID-19 vaccinations.

DARS-NIC-402414-Q5R7Y.summary: Public Health Scotland uses aggregated, small-number-suppressed English hospital and emergency care data (HES and the Emergency Care Data Set) in its Discovery dashboards. These let Scottish NHS Boards compare their performance with English peer hospitals, supporting service planning and quality improvement. Boards have used the comparisons to improve day case rates, reduce pre-operative stays and shorten lengths of stay, and to carry out bed modelling.

DARS-NIC-402417-N9Z5W.summary: The University of Leeds, an academic organisation, is using linked national health data on COVID-19, hospital care, cancer, medicines and deaths. It is studying how the pandemic affected cancer referrals, diagnosis, treatment, clinical trials and outcomes. The main intended benefit is to inform public health policy and clinical care for people with cancer. Work with NHS England on data quality and data dictionaries has already taken place, but no outputs have been published yet.

DARS-NIC-402494-Y1V5Z.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data, covering GP record data, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, model patient risk, allocate resources and find areas of low vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and respond to the outbreak. The CCG has published an annual report describing its COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-402684-K6V7T.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, a sub-ICB location, is using pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. It uses the data to support its local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-40296-L3N1D.summary: Cornwall Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan public health services and support work such as suicide prevention audits, with results published as aggregated statistics. The aim is to adjust local services to reduce deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include a Power BI tool for tracking mortality and births trends, and births data informing pupil number projections.

DARS-NIC-402963-P0Y5D.summary: The University of Liverpool, an academic organisation, uses pseudonymised NHS England data on hospital, emergency care, mental health, deaths, diabetes, COVID-19 and vaccination records for a cohort of about 275,000 people. It is used to study the clinical effects and longer-term outcomes of COVID-19 and other infectious diseases, to help plan care and vaccination. Reported results include papers in journals such as the Lancet, reports to SAGE and modelling by SPI-M.

DARS-NIC-402975-T8R3T.summary: The University of Bristol is using Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey data, a population survey that includes measures of autism and autistic traits. It is studying how often adults with autism or autistic traits also have conditions such as anxiety, depression, psychosis or self-harm, and which life factors are linked to this. The aim is to improve clinical training, services and prevention. Findings have been presented as an award-winning conference poster.

DARS-NIC-40319-H0N3V.summary: London Borough of Newham Council is using identifiable births and deaths records, including Primary Care Mortality Data, to understand local public health needs. It uses them to plan services, run immunisation programmes, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits, publishing only aggregated statistics. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports using the data to track trends in births and premature mortality, raising awareness and informing commissioners.

DARS-NIC-403356-Z0X1D.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) on women in England who had surgery or embolisation to treat uterine fibroids. It will compare readmissions, repeat treatments, pregnancies and leiomyosarcoma (a rare cancer) diagnoses over up to 10 years after myomectomy and uterine artery embolisation. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help clinicians and patients choose between these two treatments.

DARS-NIC-403429-N2X9B.summary: Medway NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised hospital admission, critical care, emergency care and death registration data for patients having surgery for ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease between March 2019 and February 2023. It is studying how surgical care and outcomes, including complications and readmissions, changed before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The main intended benefit is evidence to help clinicians and policy-makers plan surgical care for people with inflammatory bowel disease.

DARS-NIC-403870-H8L5B.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using pseudonymised patient-level data from the Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) dataset. It is studying how well IAPT treatment works, and why outcomes differ between patients, services and local areas. The aim is to inform policies that improve services and match patients to the most relevant treatment. LSE reports it has published a discussion paper (CEPDP1982) showing that treated patients were more likely to improve and recover, with differences between patient groups.

DARS-NIC-40395-P4F0P.summary: Luton Borough Council, a local authority, is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, run immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide audits. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local need, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-404670-D6W4M.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data: GP record data, ethnic category data and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, predict demand, allocate resources, identify patients at risk and find areas of low vaccine take-up. The aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and respond to the outbreak. The CCG has also published an annual report describing pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-404674-S3L8Y.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, covering missed appointments, patient risk stratification and resource allocation. The main intended benefit is better decisions on demand, capacity and resources. The CCGs have published annual reports describing their pandemic response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-404677-S1Z2D.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (not directly identifiable) COVID-19 data. This covers GP record data, ethnic category data and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan health care for its local population, including predicting demand, allocating resources, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and monitoring vaccine take-up. The stated aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and to respond to COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-404692-C3F7B.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) COVID-19 data: GP record data from the GDPPR, ethnic category data and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, predict demand on services, assess patient risk, allocate resources and track vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and respond to COVID-19 in their area.

DARS-NIC-404695-D4J5R.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health care, forecast demand, allocate resources, identify patients at risk of hospital admission and monitor vaccine uptake. The intended benefit is to help commissioners make better decisions and respond to the COVID-19 outbreak.

DARS-NIC-404696-M4N3F.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (not identifiable) COVID-19 data on GP records, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health services, allocate resources and identify patients at risk, so commissioners can make better decisions for patients. The organisation reports that the data supported capacity planning and fed into an annual report on its COVID-19 response.

DARS-NIC-404697-Y7W2M.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 vaccination data, including patient demographics, vaccination appointment and outcome details, and vaccine batch details. It uses the data to support its local response to the COVID-19 pandemic. This includes understanding vaccine roll-out, deciding whether new vaccine sites are needed, and finding areas with low take-up. The main intended benefit is helping to control the spread of the virus.

DARS-NIC-404698-V7Y6F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, allocate resources, identify patients at risk and monitor vaccine take-up, to help commissioners manage demand and respond to COVID-19. The CCG's annual report sets out key achievements in its COVID-19 response that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-404700-Z7J3X.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised GP record data on diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations from the COVID-19 General Practice Extraction Service (GPES) Data for Pandemic Planning and Research (GDPPR). It analyses the data to plan local health care during the COVID-19 emergency, including missed referrals, patient risk stratification and resource allocation. The main intended benefit is better management of demand and capacity.

DARS-NIC-404705-S7F5R.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan health services, predict demand, identify patients at higher risk and allocate resources during the COVID-19 response. The intended benefit is better commissioning decisions and help to control the spread of the virus. The CCGs have published annual reports describing their pandemic response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-404711-R1R3R.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data: GP record data (GDPPR), ethnic category data and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan health care for its local population, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and finding areas with low vaccine take-up. The aim is to help manage demand and support commissioners' decisions. The CCGs have reported that their annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-404715-W5L9M.summary: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough ICB is using pseudonymised GP record data collected for COVID-19 pandemic planning and research, which holds coded health details such as diagnoses, medications, tests and vaccinations. It uses the data to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patient groups at risk of hospital admission and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-404716-G0B7M.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records (GDPPR), ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, predict demand, allocate resources, and identify patients at risk and areas of low vaccine take-up. The aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and control the spread of COVID-19. The CCG's 2020-21 annual report describes key achievements in its COVID-19 response that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-40475-W1M6W.summary: Blackpool Borough Council, a local authority, uses identifiable birth and death registration records and primary care mortality data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, protect public health and support suicide audits, producing aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include analysis supporting commissioning and policy decisions on drug-related deaths, Primary Care Network mortality rates, winter deaths and COVID-19 deaths.

DARS-NIC-404798-C1Z9R.summary: NatCen Social Research is using survey data on the mental health of children and young people in England, from the 2017 survey and a 2020 follow-up of the same young people. It will examine how mental health difficulties and use of services have changed, including during the Covid-19 pandemic, and which groups are affected. The aim is to give service providers and policymakers evidence to plan support and reach the children and young people who need it.

DARS-NIC-40493-G5Y6K.summary: The University of Leeds, working with Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is using hospital records (admissions, outpatient, accident and emergency, critical care) and death registration data for people with heart failure. It is using them in a study linking records to see what happens after hospital discharge, such as readmission or death. The aim is to test whether this data can measure the outcomes of an intervention to support people with their medicines, informing a later clinical trial.

DARS-NIC-405749-N7T3M.summary: The University of Oxford, which coordinates the RECOVERY trial of COVID-19 treatments, is using participants' names and addresses to mail them letters about the trial's results. The aim is to thank participants directly and keep them informed, without the trial team holding their contact details. Results from the trial have already led to treatments being identified that reduce deaths, such as dexamethasone, and to the US FDA revoking an emergency authorisation for hydroxychloroquine.

DARS-NIC-406158-Q2J0X.summary: The Renal Registry, a charity that runs the UK Renal Registry, is using hospital records (admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and civil registration death records linked to its kidney disease data. It uses them for research into risk factors, outcomes, inequalities and costs for people with kidney disease. The aim is to improve their care and outcomes. Published work includes papers and conference presentations on acute kidney injury, children's kidney transplants and seasonal mortality.

DARS-NIC-406632-X0L2M.summary: Peninsula Cancer Alliance, with NHS England as the legal data controller and NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit as processor, uses Cancer Waiting Times data (the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring DataSet). It analyses waits and variation between hospital trusts and commissioners to guide discussions on improving cancer patient pathways. The aim is faster diagnosis and treatment, better survival and a better patient experience. Reported benefits include local analysis that identified outliers, with performance and patient care improving as a result.

DARS-NIC-406871-Q9G2Q.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care, through the UK Health Security Agency (the former Joint Biosecurity Centre analysts), uses COVID-19 test results, death registrations and hospital spell data. It uses them to analyse what drives the spread of COVID-19 and to help national and local decision makers target testing, contact tracing and action on local outbreaks. The intended benefit is earlier warning, limiting transmission and reducing the burden on the NHS.

DARS-NIC-407121-Z8K8K.summary: Ipsos (Market Research) Ltd, which co-ordinates the NHS Patient Survey Programme for the Care Quality Commission, is using record-level pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data for a sample of 180,000 hospital patients. It will compare this sample with the ones trusts currently provide for the Adult Inpatient Survey. The aim is to test whether centralised sampling could reduce the burden on trusts while keeping survey data reliable.

DARS-NIC-407274-Q4N0X.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland ICB, working with local councils, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, along with vaccination status and ethnic category data. It uses the data to plan demand for services, monitor the effects of COVID-19, identify vulnerable patient groups and areas of low vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is better decisions on services and help in controlling the spread of the virus. Work has begun on reporting for several conditions, and annual reports describe pandemic response.

DARS-NIC-407929-Q6Z6L.summary: NHS Somerset ICB, a sub-ICB location, is using pseudonymised GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health care during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patient groups at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-408171-X7F8W.summary: University College London is using hospital admission, accident and emergency, death registration and demographic data, linked to North London NHS Foundation Trust's mental health clinical records. The research looks at physical health, including premature death and access to physical healthcare, in people using secondary mental health services. It aims to provide information that helps narrow the mortality and physical illness disadvantage faced by people with diagnosed mental and behavioural health disorders.

DARS-NIC-40819-K5R4W.summary: Suffolk County Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable details, along with primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, protect public health and plan services, including suicide prevention work, with results published only as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, to reduce mortality and health inequalities. The data has already fed into the council's annual suicide audit, its suicide prevention strategy and the State of Suffolk Report 2022.

DARS-NIC-408892-F1R1Y.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses identifiable demographics data, specifically updated addresses, for about 14,100 members of the Millennium Cohort Study, which follows people born in the UK in 2000-02. It uses the addresses to trace participants it has lost touch with and invite them to rejoin the study and take part in the age 22 survey. The aim is to keep the study sample up to date and representative. The addresses have been used to invite participants to the current survey.

DARS-NIC-408951-K3C1Y.summary: PrescQIPP CIC, a community interest company, is using pseudonymised patient-level data on medicines dispensed in primary care. It will build dashboards and scorecards of aggregated indicators, with small numbers suppressed, for NHS commissioners and prescribers. These aim to improve medicines optimisation and safety, including prescribing changes linked to COVID. It reports producing decision aids and clinical snapshots that help identify oversupply of medicines and appliances.

DARS-NIC-409280-J6T3M.summary: Janssen-Cilag Limited, a pharmaceutical supplier, is using Permission to Contact data from people who signed up on nhs.uk to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. NHS Digital processes the data to help recruit participants to a phase 3 trial of the Ad26.COV2.S vaccine in adults aged 18 and over. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment of suitable volunteers, helping speed the delivery of an effective COVID-19 vaccine.

DARS-NIC-409290-L1F3L.summary: AstraZeneca UK Limited is using contact details and screening information (such as age, sex, location, type of employment and some health questions) from people who signed up to the NHS "Permission to Contact" service. The data will be used to invite potentially eligible adults to take part in a Phase III trial of AZD7442, which is being tested to prevent COVID-19. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment to the trial, with less burden on research staff.

DARS-NIC-409296-H4X9J.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using linked hospital, community services, emergency care and death registration data. It is studying how adults use community health services, how that use varies by patient group and area, and how these services interact with hospital care. It also plans to project demand over the next 10 years. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence to inform national and local planning of community health services.

DARS-NIC-409610-J6L1F.summary: The University of Oxford, an academic organisation, is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, death registration, COVID-19 hospitalisation and dispensed medicines data. It links these to CT scans of study participants to develop tools that assess the risk of heart attack and stroke, including after COVID-19 infection, with the aim of earlier detection and better patient care. Reported results include a published paper predicting in-hospital COVID-19 mortality from CT scans and an AI risk tool that predicted heart attacks recorded in the NHS England data.

DARS-NIC-41001-J7C4Q.summary: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council uses identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and protect public health, including suicide audits and prevention. The main intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. So far, the data has informed the local suicide prevention strategy, changes to end of life care services, and the Director of Public Health's October 2023 annual report.

DARS-NIC-41017-C4N3X.summary: Barnsley Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with published results being aggregated statistics. The aim is to adjust local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. Reported results include life expectancy and excess winter death analysis in local health profiles, a deep dive into COVID-19 excess mortality, and school admissions projections.

DARS-NIC-41104-C0Y4K.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, plus birth and death records. It uses them to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and to plan and monitor local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-411161-G4K7X.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England data on people in England, including COVID-19 test results, GP records, hospital admissions, deaths and dispensed medicines. It uses them to run the PRINCIPLE trial, which tests treatments for COVID-19 given in the community, and to contact and follow up participants. The aim is to find out whether early treatment speeds recovery and reduces hospital admission. The trial has identified budesonide as an effective treatment and found azithromycin and doxycycline are not generally effective.

DARS-NIC-41125-L4F2X.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, acting for the former Sandwell and West Birmingham CCG, uses hospital, mental health, community, maternity, ambulance and other care activity data, mostly pseudonymised, with some NHS-number-level data for risk stratification. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and support planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted, more effective care for the local population.

DARS-NIC-41140-T4H0T.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, acting for the former NHS Walsall CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other patient-level health data, mostly pseudonymised. It uses the data for risk stratification, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care, and for commissioning, to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-41158-X3V7D.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, acting for a sub-ICB location formerly NHS Wolverhampton CCG, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and primary care activity data, plus birth and death records. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health using risk scores, and to support planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned more effectively, improving patient care.

DARS-NIC-411785-Z6X7M.summary: NHS England is using linked national health data in a Cancer Trusted Research Environment. This includes cancer registrations, cancer waiting times, hospital records and death registrations, together with information collected from Rapid Diagnostic Centres. The data will be used to evaluate how well these centres work for people with symptoms that could indicate cancer, and to feed a dashboard for Cancer Alliances. The main stated benefit is less data collection for local providers, as existing national data can be reused.

DARS-NIC-411795-X5N2V.summary: Our Future Health, a charity running a large UK health research programme, is using linked NHS England hospital, cancer, death, diabetes audit and dispensed medicines records for its consenting participants. It will make the linked data available to approved researchers in its Trusted Research Environment, to study how to predict, detect and treat diseases such as dementia, cancer and diabetes. So far, 17 of 71 study applications have been granted access to the environment.

DARS-NIC-411813-H0T2W.summary: Genome Research Limited (the Wellcome Sanger Institute), a research charity, is using COVID-19 UK non-hospital antigen testing results (Pillar 2). It is linking a subset of this data to viral genome sequences to help public health agencies map geographic hotspots of coronavirus strains. The main intended benefit is faster detection of super-spreading events and of mutations that evade vaccines. The title says the request is to hold and not process the previously approved data.

DARS-NIC-41188-J4C7J.summary: Herefordshire Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. The council reports that the data informed its Suicide Prevention Strategy and a Mental Health Needs Assessment, and was used to target public health campaigns.

DARS-NIC-412777-Z2J9N.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB (Portsmouth area) uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data at NHS number level, for risk stratification. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services, so GPs and commissioners can plan and target care. The stated aim is to prevent worse outcomes, including by reducing avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-413717-C8Y6K.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) uses Personal Demographic Service data, which holds basic personal details used to identify people. It uses these to add missing NHS numbers to the Coronavirus Infection Survey and School Infection Survey records. This lets those records be linked reliably with other health data for COVID-19 analysis requested by SAGE. The intended benefit is robust, quality-assured linked data to inform government policy decisions.

DARS-NIC-414067-K8R6J.summary: Our Future Health, a charity, uses NHS England data that identifies potential participants so it can post them invitations to join its health research programme. The aim is to recruit up to 5 million UK adults into a long-term cohort that researchers can use to find better ways to prevent, detect and treat diseases. As of January 2024, about 18.3 million invitation letters had been sent through the NHS DigiTrials Recruitment service, and about 1.146 million people had consented to take part.

DARS-NIC-414309-R7H4W.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, outpatient, critical care, cancer registration and death records for 497 English patients who joined the EUROGOLF study in 1998 to 2000. It is a follow-up study of how well the enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF) blood test predicts liver-related outcomes and deaths over about 23 years, and what chronic liver disease costs. The findings are intended to inform decisions by NHS planners, doctors and patients.

DARS-NIC-41477-N2G4S.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (for the former Blackburn with Darwen CCG area) uses hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and support planning of health services. The main intended benefit is more accurate payments and more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-414909-M5W6W.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admissions records and death registration records for a pilot clinical trial called ATEMPT. The trial involves about 200 people aged 65 or over with several long-term conditions or many medicines. It compares having more or fewer blood pressure-lowering drugs, to see how well this works, how safe it is and how acceptable it is to patients. The main intended benefit is better understanding of blood pressure management in this group, helping to plan a larger trial.

DARS-NIC-415025-V8S5S.summary: The Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, a network of local health leaders, is using national Cancer Waiting Times data, which tracks how long patients wait for cancer diagnosis and treatment. It will analyse waiting times and variation between providers to improve cancer pathways, with the aim of better survival and patient experience. Reported benefits include reports on delays in referrals between hospital trusts and on compliance with the 28-day faster diagnosis standard.

DARS-NIC-41506-S6K3P.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (for the former Cannock Chase CCG area) uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), with Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit carrying out the work. The data is used to check that provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for, and to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better targeted care, reducing avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-41508-M6M3K.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (North Staffordshire area) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services, which is pseudonymised for invoice checking and linked to GP data using NHS numbers for risk stratification. It uses the data to check that providers' invoices are the commissioner's responsibility and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better targeted support for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-41522-S6G4K.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital activity data, which is linked with GP data for risk stratification. It uses the data to check that provider invoices are valid and to identify and recover overpayments. It also uses the data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, so that care can be planned and targeted. The stated aim is to ensure accurate payments and improve care through better commissioning.

DARS-NIC-41524-N9J9N.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (for the former Greater Preston CCG area) uses hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, some pseudonymised and some identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and to support the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-41525-H2P4B.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB, on behalf of the former Chorley and South Ribble CCG, uses health and care data from hospitals, community, mental health and GP services, mostly pseudonymised. It is used to check that invoices from care providers are correct, to identify patients at high risk of poor health, and to support the planning of health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-41530-F9D6Z.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (Stoke-on-Trent area) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, which is pseudonymised for invoice checking and identifiable by NHS number when linked with GP data for risk stratification. It uses the data to check that invoices from care providers are for patients it is responsible for, and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted care that reduces avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-41531-X2G5C.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-41534-Q5K9G.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, along with births and deaths records, mostly in pseudonymised form. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be managed earlier, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better-targeted care and accurate payment for treatment.

DARS-NIC-41540-K2N7Z.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB, for the former East Staffordshire CCG area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), pseudonymised for invoice checking and identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification. It uses the data to validate provider invoices and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better-targeted support for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-41549-G2V6J.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (for the former Fylde and Wyre CCG) uses pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community, ambulance, maternity and other health activity data, plus GP data for one purpose. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor commissioned services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately, care is better targeted and services are commissioned more effectively.

DARS-NIC-41556-H6V2V.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (a sub-ICB location, formerly NHS Blackpool CCG) uses hospital, mental health, community and other health service data, mostly pseudonymised, with some identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care, and to plan and commission health services. The stated aims include accurate payment of providers, better targeted care in primary care and more effective commissioning.

DARS-NIC-41581-C1G4F.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, pseudonymised for invoice checking and identifiable by NHS number for risk stratification. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, so only patients it is responsible for are paid for, and to identify patients at high risk so GPs and commissioners can plan their care. The stated aim is to improve commissioning and prevent worse outcomes.

DARS-NIC-41585-Z7Q7Q.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other NHS activity data, including pseudonymised and some NHS-number-level records. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration so GPs can target care, and support the planning of local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-41596-N5Q8N.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent ICB (Stafford and Surrounds area) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+), which is pseudonymised for invoice checking and linked with GP data for risk stratification. It uses the data to check that provider invoices are the commissioner's responsibility, and to identify patients at high risk so care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and earlier support for at-risk patients.

DARS-NIC-41597-J6M1R.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand local health needs, plan public health services and support work such as suicide prevention audits. The aim is for health and care services to be tailored to areas of greatest need, helping to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports that the data informed its Director of Public Health's 2022 annual report and an analysis of causes and place of death after COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-41605-Q7C3C.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB (a sub-ICB location, formerly West Lancashire CCG) uses hospital, mental health, community and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration so GPs can target care, and to plan and commission health services. The stated aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and to improve care through better-targeted commissioning.

DARS-NIC-41615-K7Y2P.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB, acting for the former Wyre Forest CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health and other care activity data, mostly pseudonymised, with some linked to NHS numbers. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor local health services. The stated aim is to pay providers accurately and commission services that improve patient care.

DARS-NIC-416308-H6X4N.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB is using pseudonymised GP record data, covering diagnoses, medications, tests, treatments and vaccinations, collected for pandemic planning and research. It is using the data to support the local COVID-19 response, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission and planning how to allocate resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions to support patients.

DARS-NIC-41646-V9N9J.summary: NHS North East London ICB (Redbridge area) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices, so it pays only for care it is responsible for. The second is risk stratification: linking the data with GP records to score which patients are at high risk, so GPs and commissioners can target care and reduce avoidable admissions.

DARS-NIC-416549-K7D3J.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (a Sub ICB Location) uses pseudonymised GP record data, ethnicity data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health services, model patient risk, allocate resources and monitor the effects of COVID-19, including vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is better decisions on demand, capacity and resources. The CCGs have published annual reports describing their pandemic response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-41691-F5D8L.summary: London Borough of Merton uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, support public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce aggregated statistics for health assessments and strategies. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. The data has already fed Merton's health needs assessments, Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, ward health profiles and a suicide and self-harm profile.

DARS-NIC-41730-G3J5W.summary: Wakefield Metropolitan District Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support work such as suicide prevention audits, with the aim of tailoring services to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include analysis of seasonal and extreme heat deaths, which led to proactive work promoting ways to deal with extreme heat.

DARS-NIC-418208-J1Y6J.summary: Valneva Austria GmbH, a commercial company, is using Permission to Contact data: details of people who signed up on nhs.uk to be approached about COVID-19 vaccine trials. NHS Digital, acting as data processor, will use it to invite potentially eligible people to join Valneva's trial comparing its VLA2001 vaccine with the AZD1222 vaccine in adults. The main intended benefit is faster, more transparent recruitment, helping speed the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-418444-H4X4L.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, working with Bury Metropolitan Borough Council, uses pseudonymised health and adult social care data, including hospital, community, mental health, maternity and death records. It links this data to plan, commission and monitor joined-up health and care services across Bury, aiming to improve population health outcomes. Reported benefits include commissioning data being used to plan a new Urgent Treatment Centre at Fairfield General Hospital, and NHS Digital data informing the response to endoscopy waiting times.

DARS-NIC-419335-H5P8T.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked hospital, emergency care, maternity, vaccination and death registration records for patients treated in intensive care units (ICUs). It is studying the risk of death, emergency hospital readmission, heart attacks and strokes in the year after discharge for people treated for COVID-19, compared with those treated for other conditions. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand long-term risks and how follow-up care might improve. So far, the study found that survivors of COVID-19 in the first wave were less likely to die or be readmitted than pre-pandemic ICU patients.

DARS-NIC-419453-G3G1G.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data. The team is comparing methods for creating synthetic datasets, which are artificial data that resemble the original but contain no real individuals. The main intended benefit is evidence and guidelines to help data providers decide whether synthetic health data could speed up and streamline researchers' access to data.

DARS-NIC-41957-W5S6T.summary: The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, a local authority, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital admissions, A&E, outpatients and critical care. Its public health team uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners, so that it can analyse local health and inequalities. Previously, the data fed into locality profiles on emergency admissions, which were shared with the local Integrated Care Steering Group.

DARS-NIC-420105-M8Y5X.summary: Novavax, Inc., a private healthcare company, is using identifiable details of its UK vaccine trial participants, which NHS Digital links to non-hospital (Pillar 2) COVID-19 test results. The aim is to match each participant's self-swab PCR result to them accurately, so the trial can measure how well the Novavax vaccine prevents COVID-19. The stated benefit is faster, more reliable evaluation, helping bring another effective vaccine to the UK population.

DARS-NIC-420168-K4N1F.summary: The University of Bristol, through the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration, is using linked NHS health records, including hospital, GP, mental health, COVID-19 testing, vaccination and death data, alongside data from UK longitudinal population studies. It is using them for Covid-19 research on the pandemic's effects on health and wellbeing. The aim is to give policy makers rapid evidence. Findings have already informed NICE long COVID guidance, an NHS enhanced service specification for GPs and SAGE reports.

DARS-NIC-420229-G9H9S.summary: The University of Bristol uses linked NHS health records, including hospital, GP-related, mental health, maternity, cancer, death and COVID-19 data, to run the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration. This secure research database links records to long-running population study data, for health research that relies on section 251 support rather than consent. It aims to provide evidence for health and care policy. Published research from it has been presented to NICE and SAGE and has informed Health & Safety Executive policy.

DARS-NIC-420710-X0H1P.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using linked hospital, GP, emergency care and COVID-19 vaccination records, combined with 2011 Census and death data. It is creating an anonymised version of this dataset for approved researchers to use in a secure environment for COVID-19 research. The aim is better evidence for public health decisions. Reported results include Cabinet Office findings on ethnicity and deprivation that informed pandemic service decisions, and research that led to policy recommendations.

DARS-NIC-421524-R0Y3P.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using patient-level pseudonymised NHS data on Covid-19 testing, hospital care, deaths and the COVID Oximetry @ Home (CO@H) remote monitoring service. It is evaluating how safe, effective and equitable CO@H is, to inform national policy on home oximetry. So far, monthly interim reports have guided the programme's rollout, and preprint papers and a conference presentation have been produced.

DARS-NIC-421528-J6S3N.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is using linked NHS data on COVID-19 tests, GP records, hospital and emergency care, deaths and the shielded patient list. It is evaluating the national COVID Oximetry at Home programme, in which patients monitor their own oxygen levels at home. The aim is to show the programme's health and safety outcomes and fairness of access, to guide how it is run and improved. So far, interim analyses have been shared internally with partners in NHSX, NHS England and NHS Digital.

DARS-NIC-421602-N3B0X.summary: Northwest Ehealth Limited, working for Novartis Pharmaceuticals UK Limited, holds hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for a primary care study of inclisiran, a cholesterol-lowering treatment given in a vaccine-like way. The records are used to analyse NHS costs and hospital use, and to check the published findings if they are challenged. The study aims to show the best way for the NHS to deliver inclisiran. Findings have so far improved understanding of point of care testing and its limits.

DARS-NIC-42177-M7K0J.summary: Nottingham City Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to measure local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. It reports using the data in its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment dashboards and when commissioning a new integrated wellbeing service.

DARS-NIC-422044-Z5K5Q.summary: Health IQ Ltd, a commercial research consultancy, is using civil registrations of death data linked to hospital records for patients diagnosed with beta-thalassaemia or myelodysplastic syndromes between 2015 and 2019. Funded by Bristol-Myers Squibb, it will describe patient treatment pathways, healthcare use, costs and survival, including cause and time of death. The intended benefit is evidence to inform treatment policy, resource allocation and a regulatory review of a drug.

DARS-NIC-422183-C3K9L.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB uses hospital, community, mental health and other health and social care data, including identifiable NHS number-level data and pseudonymised data, to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payments and better patient care. Reported results include a review of people with diabetes at highest risk during the Covid-19 pandemic and choosing the location of a new health centre.

DARS-NIC-422189-G8H5X.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care and other health data about patients in its area. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and to support the planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned more effectively. The CCG has also produced an annual report describing developments its data processing supported.

DARS-NIC-422195-G1Y7D.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health datasets, some identifiable and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and commission health services. The aim is accurate payment and more targeted, effective care. The CCG has produced an annual report outlining developments and achievements the data supported.

DARS-NIC-422200-Q1K7S.summary: NHS North East London ICB uses patient-level hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS data, some identifiable and some pseudonymised, for invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning. It checks that providers are paid correctly, identifies patients at risk of worse health so GPs can target care, and plans health services for the local population. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. Reported results include fewer undiagnosed diabetes cases in Barking and Dagenham and shorter hospital stays in Waltham Forest.
