DARS-NIC-422205-F2Y2V.summary: NHS North West London ICB, which took over from the area's clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care, social care and civil registration data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor local health services. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. Reported results include setting up three Covid-19 vaccination sites in areas with low uptake and introducing a mental health placements system.

DARS-NIC-422207-N1D1V.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, mental health, community, maternity, GP-linked and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and commission health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payments, earlier help for at-risk patients and better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-422211-Q0Y4D.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, primary care medicines and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-422218-V6L8T.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other patient-level health data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better matched to local needs. The register reports that the data has helped services meet population requirements and supported monitoring of in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-422221-W0P7K.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and monitor the commissioning of health services for its population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payment of providers and better targeted care.

DARS-NIC-42272-S9J3L.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research, an academic body, is using hospital-level Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data. It will compare these figures with the records hospitals submit to the National Heart Failure Audit, to check how fully each hospital takes part and to support the audit's annual report. The audit aims to improve the diagnosis, treatment and outcomes of heart failure patients. NHS England already uses the audit data to support the Best Practice Tariff, a payment incentive for specialist heart failure care introduced in April 2015.

DARS-NIC-422971-B8P2V.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using COVID-19 General Practice Extraction Service (GPES) Data for Pandemic Planning and Research (GDPPR). The work is a service evaluation for NHS England. It examines whether open invitations to book breast screening, introduced in London during COVID-19, affect attendance and widen inequalities compared with timed appointments. The aim is to help screening services tailor resources and decide whether to change their invitation policy.

DARS-NIC-423551-K2C4H.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, covering the former Halton and Warrington clinical commissioning groups (CCGs), uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care, prescribing and death and birth records. It uses them to plan and commission health services for the local population, including spotting patients at risk of admission and reviewing service demand. The aim is better-designed services and outcomes. The CCGs reported using the data to find duplicated or missing services and published 2020/21 annual reports.

DARS-NIC-423553-H8D6H.summary: NHS Sussex ICB is using pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance, primary care and civil registration data, containing both clinical and financial information. It uses this data to plan and commission health services for the population of the former Brighton and Hove, East Sussex and West Sussex CCG areas. This includes reporting on providers, predicting demand and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better-informed commissioning decisions that improve service quality and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-423859-V7S0R.summary: NHS England, with the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership, uses pseudonymised hospital admission and death registration data for the National Gastrointestinal Cancer Audit, covering bowel and oesophago-gastric cancer. It uses the data to assess the quality of cancer care in England and Wales, give hospital trusts timely feedback and study the impact of COVID-19. The aim is to improve care. Reported results include more bowel cancer patients receiving adjuvant chemotherapy and more high-grade dysplasia patients being discussed by specialist teams.

DARS-NIC-423900-L1L7X.summary: North Tyneside Council uses hospital data, covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care, outpatients and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses this for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reports it previously used the data to help develop a Local Health Index with partners.

DARS-NIC-424336-T7K7T.summary: The University of Exeter, working with the University of Cambridge and NatCen Social Research, is using survey data on the mental health of children and young people from 2017 and a 2020 follow-up. They are examining how mental health, and use of mental health services, changed during the Covid-19 pandemic. The aim is to give evidence to those planning and commissioning child and adolescent mental health services, and to schools, so they can target support at the groups most affected.

DARS-NIC-424723-D5Q9W.summary: The Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), part of the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), receives a minimal extract of hospital data from the Secondary Uses Service (SUS) for COVID-19 surveillance. It is used to monitor the safety and quality of COVID-19 vaccines until routine GP data flows can be used, and to produce reports for the Yellow Card scheme. The data has already supported assessment of myopericarditis and menstrual disorders after vaccination.

DARS-NIC-42507-N1M8Z.summary: South Gloucestershire Council uses identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs and protect public health. It produces aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics for needs assessments, public health reports and suicide prevention work. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include local analysis showing no excess deaths among residents, and a needs assessment now used in council planning.

DARS-NIC-42575-X8G6W.summary: Southend-on-Sea Borough Council, a local authority, uses civil registration births data, primary care mortality data and Vital Statistics Service data, including identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan and monitor services, and protect public health, for example through suicide audits and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. So far, its Joint Strategic Needs Assessments are being used to develop pilots of community-based support.

DARS-NIC-42679-H5B1D.summary: Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, support suicide audits and protect public health, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. The council reports it has used the data to compile a report on Excess Winter Deaths.

DARS-NIC-426830-M1C1K.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, through its commercial arm ARCTEC, is using Pillar 2 (non-hospital) COVID-19 test results, including test outcomes, symptom start dates and PCR cycle thresholds, for about 900 study participants. It is using them to check how accurately medical detection dogs identify SARS-CoV-2 infection, including with new viral strains, low viral loads and no symptoms. The intended benefit is a quick screening tool for places such as airports.

DARS-NIC-426970-Y8V6T.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire ICB uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data, covering GP record codes, ethnic category and vaccination status, to plan local health services. It uses the data to analyse missed appointments, identify patients at risk of hospital admission, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and respond to the outbreak. The CCG's annual report describes COVID-19 achievements that this data supported.

DARS-NIC-427822-X5G6N.summary: NHS England is using pilot ambulance service data from across England. It is testing and evaluating a trial collection of this data, with the aim of improving its quality and consistency, as directed by the Ambulance Services Data Set Discovery Directions 2020. The pilot supports a Long-Term Plan commitment to follow patient journeys from ambulances into other urgent and emergency care. The intended benefit is better commissioning of emergency care services, leading to better outcomes for users.

DARS-NIC-427962-M3K1W.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC), a research organisation, is using civil death registrations and hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records. The data provide outcome information for the UK-ROX trial, which compares conservative with usual oxygen therapy in adults on mechanical ventilation after an unplanned intensive care admission. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on the best amount of oxygen to give, to inform national guidance and improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-42818-F4R1T.summary: Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council uses identifiable births and deaths records, including primary care mortality data, to understand local public health needs. It uses them for needs assessments, health protection monitoring and suicide prevention work, with aggregated outputs. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Under the previous agreement, the data fed an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, a substance misuse needs assessment and a Falls Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-428459-V7Q8M.summary: The University of Oxford is using Permission to Contact data, which is contact and eligibility details given by people who have volunteered to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. NHS Digital, acting as data processor, will use it to email potentially eligible people about the Com-COV trial, which compares different COVID-19 vaccine schedule combinations. The main intended benefit is faster, less burdensome recruitment of suitable volunteers, helping speed up the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-430380-F7L4Z.summary: The University of Bristol is using Maternity Services Data Set records from England to study inequalities in stillbirth and preterm birth, and the risk factors behind them. The aim is to help the NHS find units needing support, judge whether interventions work, and develop tools to identify high-risk pregnancies early. So far, the team has found risk factors for both outcomes among first-time mothers, but no stillbirth prediction tool.

DARS-NIC-43048-T5S9D.summary: The London Borough of Enfield, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable primary care mortality data. It uses this data to understand local health needs, plan public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce reports with small numbers suppressed. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. Enfield reports using the data to show health inequalities to the council and voluntary sector, and in its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and Pharmaceutical Needs Assessment reports.

DARS-NIC-43059-H1N6M.summary: Sheffield City Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including through suicide audits. The main intended benefit is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported outputs include an updated Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, Director of Public Health reports and several health needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-430963-R7T2B.summary: The University of Leeds, working with University College London, is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, death and cancer registration records for 1,279 people who consented to take part in a trial. It is a long-term follow-up of the ELUCIDATE trial, which tests whether the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) blood test can give early warning of cirrhosis and reduce serious liver complications. The aim is to inform decisions on whether wider use of the test would improve patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-431352-G7F1M.summary: Imperial College London is linking consenting participants in its REACT COVID-19 study to their NHS health records, including hospital, cancer, mental health, death, testing and vaccination data. It will use the linked data to study the risks of COVID infection and reinfection and people's later health, aiming to help plan healthcare for conditions such as Long COVID. The register reports that earlier REACT findings fed into government policy and were published in journals such as Science.

DARS-NIC-431355-B1L8W.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked NHS data on COVID-19 tests, vaccinations, adverse reactions, hospital care, maternity and deaths. The data is used for studies of COVID-19 vaccine safety and effectiveness, including vaccine uptake and the risk of adverse events after vaccination. The stated main benefit is better public health knowledge about vaccine safety and how well vaccines reduce COVID-19 infections.

DARS-NIC-431565-K9V9N.summary: University College London's Centre for Longitudinal Studies uses identifiable civil registration death records and demographic data for the 15,770 people in the Next Steps cohort. It uses them to keep participant records up to date, avoiding contact with people who have died or emigrated, and to research mortality and its links to health behaviours and social factors. Reported benefits include 21 deaths notified, which prevented unwanted contact with families.

DARS-NIC-431736-X6C4F.summary: Kingston University is using pseudonymised patient-level records from emergency departments and urgent treatment centres in England, drawn from two NHS England datasets: the Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics Accident and Emergency. The research looks at how different mixes of non-medical practitioners and other staff affect patient outcomes, care quality, activity and costs. It aims to inform workforce decisions by clinicians, managers and commissioners.

DARS-NIC-431881-N8B0N.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked NHS hospital, emergency care, mental health, COVID-19 test and death registration data, alongside GP records from the Royal College of GPs surveillance network. It is developing and validating an early warning score to help GPs assess COVID-19 in remote consultations, using hospital admission as a measure of deterioration. It also aims to compare recovered and long COVID cases. So far, two predictive risk scores and a long COVID phenotype have been developed, and manuscripts have been written and submitted to a journal.

DARS-NIC-432598-Q6S0C.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics), linked to death registration data, to study shoulder replacement surgery in England. It is looking at trends over time, differences in access across areas, complications after surgery and the likely future demand on the NHS. The aim is to help NHS planning of services, costs and staffing. A paper on rising demand, unequal provision and varying outcomes was published in BMC Medicine in 2023.

DARS-NIC-433152-N2N7C.summary: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and population data, containing clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, including analysing population needs, predicting demand and monitoring provider performance. The main aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and improve services and health outcomes. So far, it has let the CCGs benchmark performance across West Yorkshire, starting with mental health, community and maternity data.

DARS-NIC-433156-Q9X6Z.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, prescribing and population data, containing both clinical and financial information. It is used to plan and commission health services across the Hampshire and Isle of Wight partnership area, including activity and budget reporting, demand planning and identifying patients and groups with the greatest need. The main intended benefit is better-planned services and improved patient flow.

DARS-NIC-433158-L7X7P.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB receives pseudonymised COVID-19 data covering GP record codes (GDPPR), ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, predict demand, allocate resources, identify patients at risk and find areas with low vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners make better decisions and respond to the outbreak. The CCG has published an annual report describing its pandemic response achievements, which the data supported.

DARS-NIC-433163-Y2V0K.summary: NHS Black Country ICB uses pseudonymised community, mental health and hospital activity data, which includes clinical and financial information. It is processed by Pi Limited (trading as Predict X) to plan and commission health services and to profile health and social care use across the Black Country and West Birmingham area. The aim is to find where care can be improved, such as emergency admissions and transfer of care delays. Reported results include dashboards showing pressure points in the care system for Wolverhampton City Council.

DARS-NIC-433166-T6N9F.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) GP record data, COVID-19 vaccination data and ethnicity data. It uses them to plan local health services, assess risk among patients, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and make better decisions for patients. The CCG has published an annual report describing its COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-433167-R3Q1Z.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, a Sub ICB Location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, ethnic category data and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health services, model patient risk, allocate resources and monitor vaccine uptake. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and respond to COVID-19. The CCGs have published an annual report describing their COVID-19 response, which this data supported.

DARS-NIC-433176-J8Q2S.summary: AstraZeneca AB is using death records, hospital admission records and heart attack audit data to run a trial of dapagliflozin, given daily alongside standard care after a heart attack. It aims to see whether the drug prevents hospitalisation for heart failure or cardiovascular death. The main results were published in NEJM Evidence in 2024, with further published analyses of patient subgroups.

DARS-NIC-433181-W6M0J.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB uses pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination data. It uses them to plan local health services, model which patients may need hospital care, allocate resources and monitor vaccine take-up during the COVID-19 response. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and make better decisions for patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-433257-K6Q2Y.summary: The University of Liverpool, working with the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is using identifiable NHS England data on hospital care, emergency care, deaths and medicines dispensed in primary care. It supports a national trial, HEAL-COVID, which tests treatments for people after hospital discharge with COVID-19. The data helps measure survival, hospital readmission and NHS resource use. The main intended benefit is knowing how best to treat patients in the post-acute phase of COVID-19.

DARS-NIC-43362-G7T9X.summary: NHS Somerset ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some of it identifiable and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of deteriorating health, and plan and monitor commissioned services. The main intended benefit is that services are paid for accurately and planned to meet local needs. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements such as a diabetes advice service and a COVID-19 recovery service.

DARS-NIC-433629-H3M0G.summary: NHS England is using routinely recorded GP data on physical health checks for people with severe mental illness, covering alcohol, blood lipids, blood glucose, smoking, BMI and blood pressure. It is using this to monitor delivery of the NHS Long Term Plan ambition for 390 thousand people to receive a comprehensive check and follow-up. The aim is to reduce premature mortality by supporting local quality improvement and tackling inequalities in access to checks.

DARS-NIC-433923-Z0V8D.summary: The University of Glasgow is using NHS England cancer registration, death registration and hospital admission records for people in the IRONMAN trial, which involves 1,400 people with heart failure and iron deficiency. The data will help the researchers capture hospitalisations, cancers and deaths, to test whether adding intravenous iron to standard care reduces illness and death and is cost-effective. The initial linkage has already identified previously unreported clinical events.

DARS-NIC-43421-F1R6G.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This applies an algorithm to produce risk scores that identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services. GPs and commissioners can use the scores to target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-43431-N0G4J.summary: NHS South West London ICB (for the former Croydon area) uses hospital activity data, linked with GP data, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or repeated service use. The Sollis Partnership Ltd carries out this risk stratification, which helps GPs and commissioners target care and plan services for vulnerable patients. The main intended benefit is fewer avoidable emergency hospital admissions through earlier intervention.

DARS-NIC-43435-D8M8Z.summary: NHS North West London ICB (a sub-ICB location) is using Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, which checks that provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is better-planned care and accurate payment.

DARS-NIC-43450-C7M7C.summary: NHS South West London ICB is using hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP records, for risk stratification. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or of using multiple services, so that care can be planned and GPs can target support. Sollis Partnership Ltd carries out the processing. The main intended benefit is better planning and more effective commissioning of services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-434738-K7Z9L.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using demographic data from NHS Digital to select and invite a sample of people aged 80 or over to take part in a COVID-19 vaccination survey. The survey will gather views and behaviour of people likely to have been offered the vaccine, including why some did not accept it. The results go to the Department of Health and Social Care to help plan vaccination policy and increase uptake.

DARS-NIC-434767-Z4P3N.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data on GP record information, ethnic category and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, forecast demand, allocate resources, identify patients at risk and track vaccine uptake. The main aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and respond to the outbreak. The CCG has published an annual report on its COVID-19 response, which the data supported.

DARS-NIC-43481-Y2L3X.summary: NHS North West London ICB uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked at NHS number level with GP data. It uses this data for risk stratification, which means identifying patients at high risk of health deterioration so that care can be planned and GPs can target interventions. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-43492-M8R1G.summary: NHS North West London ICB, covering the former Hammersmith & Fulham CCG area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. It links this with GP data to give patients risk scores, so GPs and commissioners can target care at those likely to get worse and reduce avoidable emergency admissions. It also checks provider invoices so that payments are accurate and public money is properly controlled.

DARS-NIC-43499-C1H9Y.summary: NHS North West London ICB, for the former NHS Harrow Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers' invoices are for patients the CCG is responsible for. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better-targeted care.

DARS-NIC-435152-C0H4N.summary: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is using COVID-19 vaccination status data for the CLARITY IBD study of people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who take immunosuppressive drugs. The study examines how these drugs affect COVID-19 infection and immunity after infection or vaccination, to help guide prescribing and vaccination advice. Published papers from the study are cited in UK and Canadian vaccination recommendations for people on these drugs.

DARS-NIC-435161-Z0W9W.summary: NHS North West London Integrated Care Board uses pseudonymised GP record data, COVID-19 vaccination data and ethnic category data. It uses them to plan local health services during the COVID-19 emergency, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, and allocating resources. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and make better decisions to support patients. The CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-435164-Y9N2N.summary: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board (a sub ICB location) uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data from GP records, along with ethnic category and vaccination status data. It uses this data to plan local health care, forecast demand, allocate resources, identify patients at higher risk of hospital admission, and monitor vaccine rollout and areas of low take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and capacity and respond to the outbreak. Its former CCGs' annual reports describe pandemic response work supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-435166-T9S8X.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised COVID-19 data on ethnic category, GP record information (GDPPR) and vaccination status. It uses the data to plan local health care, including analysing missed appointments, identifying patients at risk of hospital admission, allocating resources and monitoring vaccine take-up. The main intended benefit is helping commissioners manage demand and make better decisions for patients. The CCG has published an annual report on its COVID-19 response achievements.

DARS-NIC-435173-Z6K9J.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses pseudonymised (identifying details replaced) GP record data, ethnic category data and COVID-19 vaccination status data. It uses them to plan local health services, predict demand, allocate resources and identify patient groups at risk during the COVID-19 emergency. It also uses them to monitor vaccine rollout and find areas of low take-up. The stated aim is to help commissioners make better decisions and to control the spread of the virus.

DARS-NIC-43519-Q8P5N.summary: NHS North West London ICB (for the former Hillingdon CCG) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services, which is identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking invoices from care providers so that only activity the CCG is responsible for is paid. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aim is better targeted care and more effective commissioning of services.

DARS-NIC-43522-H5N2S.summary: NHS North West London ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data that can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data for risk stratification, which links it with GP data to predict which patients are at high risk so care can be targeted and planned, and for invoice validation, which checks that providers' invoices are correct and are the commissioner's responsibility. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and accurate payment for treatment.

DARS-NIC-435236-H4X4N.summary: The University of Bath is using hospital, emergency care and death registration data to study how urban development, such as air pollution, housing, transport and green spaces, affects health and wellbeing. The aim is to evaluate urban planning interventions and their costs and benefits, so planners can better prevent non-communicable diseases. So far, the work on Low Emission Zones has produced a policy brief, media coverage and results used in a cost tool for local authorities.

DARS-NIC-43531-D9G5J.summary: NHS North West London Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, linked to GP data and identifiable by NHS number, for risk stratification and invoice validation on behalf of the former Hounslow clinical commissioning group. It identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration so care can be planned and targeted, and checks that provider invoices are accurate and the commissioner's responsibility. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient care.

DARS-NIC-43547-B4R5Q.summary: NHS South West London ICB (Richmond area) uses hospital activity data from Secondary Uses Service (SUS+), linked with GP records, with Sollis Partnership Ltd carrying out the work. It is used for risk stratification: predicting which patients are at high risk of health deterioration so that GPs and commissioners can plan and target their care. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and earlier intervention, reducing avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-43558-V8K7Z.summary: NHS Frimley ICB, acting for the former NHS Surrey Heath Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including births and deaths records. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better-targeted, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-435753-D4J0Y.summary: Imperial College London is using hospital admission records from England, covering COVID-19 related diagnoses, admission and discharge dates, and patients' local areas. The team will combine these with wastewater treatment plant catchment areas to produce summary statistics, which will be used to calibrate models based on virus traces in sewage. The intended benefit is better estimates of how many people are infected and better predictions of hospital demand, so resources can be allocated more effectively.

DARS-NIC-436453-C4N4Z.summary: Medicago R&D Incorporated, a research company, is using "Permission to Contact" information from people who signed up through NHS Digital's online service to say they were willing to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The data is used to invite potentially eligible adults to be screened for Medicago's Phase 2/3 trial of a coronavirus-like particle COVID-19 vaccine. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment of volunteers, helping a safe and effective vaccine be developed sooner.

DARS-NIC-437579-V8J5V.summary: The University of Nottingham is using linked NHS hospital, emergency care, COVID-19 testing, vaccination, death and demographic records for people taking part in a trial in care homes. The data will help assess whether treatments given to care home residents can prevent COVID-19 infection, severe illness, hospital admission and death, and whether they are cost-effective. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform changes to clinical practice and guidelines.

DARS-NIC-43771-N0W3Q.summary: The University of Cambridge is using identifiable participant data (current address, GP details and mortality information) from NHS Digital for the Fenland study, a long-running study of obesity, diabetes and related conditions. It will use the data to invite participants to phase 2 and avoid contacting relatives of those who have died. The aim is to keep more participants in the study. Fenland evidence has been given to a House of Commons Select Committee, and Fenland research on takeaway outlets has influenced NICE diet recommendations.

DARS-NIC-438547-B6Y8V.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight ICB uses pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) clinical and financial data from hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and primary care services. It uses this to plan and commission health services for the population of the former Hampshire, Southampton and Isle of Wight and Portsmouth CCG areas. The aim is to match services to local needs, target care better and support service redesign. The register reports that services have been delivered to match population needs, and that the CCGs' 2020/21 annual reports describe achievements.

DARS-NIC-438551-P4C0G.summary: The University of Nottingham is using linked hospital admission records and civil registrations of death for about 6,000 older surgery patients in the third Sprint National Anaesthesia Project (SNAP 3). The study looks at how frailty, multiple health conditions and delirium relate to outcomes after surgery, including readmission and death. It aims to improve the care of older surgical patients, including through a tool to identify patients at risk of delirium.

DARS-NIC-443107-J3T0L.summary: Essex County Council's public health team uses hospital records, covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients, to support its public health duties. It uses them to produce needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, and to analyse health inequalities locally. Reported uses so far include analysing where self harm and substance misuse admissions occur, to inform mental health and substance misuse services, and examining differences in avoidable admissions.

DARS-NIC-44324-R3G0Q.summary: North East Lincolnshire Council, a local authority, is using civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan public health work such as suicide prevention, and produce summary statistics for reports like its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment. The main intended benefit is local services better targeted to reduce deaths and health inequalities. So far, the data has helped identify health patterns and inequalities at ward level and has fed into a children's health needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-44356-Y8N6R.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists runs the National Maternity and Perinatal Audit, using NHS England maternity, hospital admission, mental health, birth notification and death registration data. It uses the data to report on maternity care and outcomes in England, Wales and Scotland, so units can compare themselves and improve care. Published reports have led to changes such as Stockport's new perineal care bundle, and have been cited in a House of Commons committee report.

DARS-NIC-44378-T7F0X.summary: Brighton and Hove City Council uses identifiable births and deaths registration data, along with primary care mortality data, to assess local health needs, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health, including suicide audits and prevention work. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. Reported uses include analysis supporting the pandemic response, a Joint Strategic Needs Assessment on adults with multiple complex conditions, and primary care network profiles.

DARS-NIC-44383-L6C0X.summary: King's College London, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital admissions and death registration records to study people who frequently attend hospital because of alcohol. It aims to understand their characteristics, health outcomes, deaths and NHS costs, and to build a risk stratification model estimating how many could benefit from specialist outreach services. Reported results include national figures on their numbers and costs, and the work's inclusion in PHE's menu of preventative interventions.

DARS-NIC-445543-W0D4N.summary: AstraZeneca UK Limited is using national NHS records on COVID-19 testing, vaccinations, adverse reactions, hospital care and deaths. It is studying how well the Oxford/AstraZeneca and other COVID-19 vaccines work in England, including booster doses. It is also studying how often rare blood clotting with low platelets occurs after vaccination. The aim is to show real-world effectiveness and safety to inform vaccination policy. So far, the University of Oxford has shown vaccine effectiveness in people over 65.

DARS-NIC-445821-L3B2N.summary: Gateshead Metropolitan Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable information. It uses this to understand local health needs, plan services, and support work such as suicide prevention and public health reports, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. It reports that the data has informed its understanding of need after the pandemic and helped it target activity in the most deprived communities.

DARS-NIC-445826-K3H7D.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB uses identifiable hospital activity data (SUS+) and patient demographic data to check that provider invoices are correct and that it is the responsible commissioner. It also links hospital data with GP data to produce risk scores that identify patients likely to need high levels of care. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better targeted care. Reported benefits include services matched to population needs and monitoring of in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-448252-L2R6Q.summary: NHS England is using linked, pseudonymised patient-level data on hospital care, GP records, antibiotic prescriptions dispensed in primary care and deaths. It is using them to build a dashboard on infections and antibiotic use for programme stakeholders, supporting the UK's antimicrobial resistance (AMR) action plan. The long-term aim is to show what affects infection outcomes and guide better prescribing. An initial dashboard launched in February 2022, showing infection trends and changes in antibiotic course length during the pandemic.

DARS-NIC-448303-Z7H5R.summary: The University of Oxford is using details from NHS Digital's Permission to Contact service, which holds information from people who have volunteered to be contacted about COVID-19 vaccine trials. It will use the data to invite potentially eligible people to join a trial comparing different combinations of COVID-19 vaccine doses. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment into the trial, helping to speed up work on an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-44840-S2Q7M.summary: Essex County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan public health work such as suicide audits, and produce aggregated, small-number-suppressed statistics. The aim is to adjust local services to reduce mortality and health inequalities. So far, the council has combined death counts with census estimates to produce small-area healthy life expectancy figures shared with partners.

DARS-NIC-44845-W4G8Y.summary: St Helens Council uses identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of people in its area, plan immunisation programmes and protect public health. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local need, helping to reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has already been used to produce a Mortality JSNA (Joint Strategic Needs Assessment) and a Children's JSNA, and to identify suicide hotspots that informed the local suicide prevention strategy.

DARS-NIC-44904-K0Y9V.summary: Cheshire East Council is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local public health needs, including suicide audits and health needs assessments, and to publish summary statistics. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce health inequalities. So far, the data has fed completed Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, including a place-based analysis of Crewe, and a ward-level health profile shown to councillors.

DARS-NIC-449801-W5J4M.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using linked NHS hospital, GP, prescribing, COVID-19 test, vaccination and death records for participants in the COVIDENCE UK study and the CORONAVIT vitamin D trial. It will link these to participants' questionnaire and antibody test answers to study risk factors for COVID-19, recovery, long-term effects and responses to vaccination. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide public health advice and clinical care, including on vitamin D.

DARS-NIC-449860-L0D6W.summary: The University of Oxford's EMPA-KIDNEY study team is using demographics data, specifically fact and date of death, for UK participants in a clinical trial of empagliflozin versus placebo in people with chronic kidney disease. It will identify deaths missed because trial follow-up was disrupted, for example by COVID-19. The intended benefit is more complete, higher-quality trial data on whether the drug slows kidney disease or prevents cardiovascular death.

DARS-NIC-45168-S6S7W.summary: The Royal Borough of Greenwich, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable records and primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include the suicide audit, which is updated each year, and births data used in children's centre datapacks.

DARS-NIC-454210-X7N1F.summary: NHS Devon ICB (formerly NHS Devon CCG) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor commissioned health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. The CCG's annual report describes projects supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-454217-D9J5X.summary: NHS Lincolnshire ICB, working with Lincolnshire County Council, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, social care, prescribing and births and deaths data. It is used to plan and commission health services for the local population, and to redesign services with the council. The aim is to improve population outcomes. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report shows the data supported emergency response planning, contract planning and urgent care board decisions.

DARS-NIC-454669-H0H4X.summary: NHS England, jointly with the Healthcare Quality Improvement Partnership, uses pseudonymised hospital admission, death registration and demographic data on adults with oesophago-gastric cancer or pre-cancerous oesophageal high-grade dysplasia. It supports the National Oesophago-Gastric Cancer Audit, which assesses the quality of their care in England and Wales. The aim is to help hospitals compare themselves and improve care. Annual reports show improvements, such as more patients with high-grade dysplasia being discussed by a specialist team.

DARS-NIC-45468-Z9T9F.summary: London Borough of Hackney, a local authority, uses civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, which include identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan public health services and support work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has already contributed to reviews of substance misuse deaths, end of life care and infant mortality, and to analyses of COVID-19 deaths and birth rates.

DARS-NIC-45562-G1X9H.summary: The London Borough of Lewisham uses identifiable birth and death registration records, plus Primary Care Mortality Data. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits and prevention. The aim is to tailor services to local needs and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has been used in Lewisham's joint strategic needs assessment, a cancer mortality dashboard and Child Death Overview Panel reports.

DARS-NIC-456088-R0H0V.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using Permission to Contact data, which is contact and basic health details from people who have volunteered to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. It uses the data to invite potentially eligible people to take part in the Covboost booster vaccine trial. The aim is to recruit participants faster and help develop safe, effective vaccine combinations. Results from the study have been published in three journals and helped inform government and JCVI booster decisions.

DARS-NIC-456778-J0G3H.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd and King's College London, as joint data controllers, are using demographic data to identify and write to people in the areas of eight Cancer Alliances in England who may be eligible for the NHS-Galleri trial. The trial tests whether a blood test that can detect many types of cancer (a multi-cancer early detection test) finds cancers earlier than current NHS tests. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform whether the NHS should adopt the test.

DARS-NIC-457686-H6K6R.summary: Worcestershire County Council is using NHS community services, maternity, mental health and hospital data (SUS for Commissioners) linked with social care data. It is using this to understand demand for health and social care across its area, with results shown in a dashboard for council analysts. The aim is to help plan services and the workforce, and to focus resources on those most in need.

DARS-NIC-459114-J3C1F.summary: The University of Oxford, working with AstraZeneca UK, holds linked NHS England hospital, emergency care, testing, vaccination, adverse reaction and death records for people in England. They used them to study how well the Oxford/AstraZeneca and Pfizer COVID-19 vaccines work, including booster doses, and to examine blood clots with low platelets after vaccination. The aim is to show how effective the vaccines and roll-out are. A study report was submitted to the MHRA and European Medicines Agency in March 2023, and it received a positive opinion from the CHMP in July 2023.

DARS-NIC-459340-M8R2R.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital, emergency care and death registration records for people who took part in the OPTiMISE trial of reducing blood pressure medication in adults aged 80 and over. It will follow them for three years after randomisation to see how stopping or reducing these medicines affects cardiovascular disease, falls and death. The aim is to show whether deprescribing is safe in the longer term and to inform clinical guidelines.

DARS-NIC-45990-Q6G6S.summary: Kirklees Council uses identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs and protect public health. It uses them for suicide audits, needs assessments and annual public health reports, so services can be tailored to local needs and health inequalities reduced. Reported uses so far include updating the Director of Public Health Annual Report, supporting a suicide reduction project and calculating local life expectancy.

DARS-NIC-460641-M8X4D.summary: The UK Health Security Agency, an executive agency of the Department of Health and Social Care, is using pseudonymised COVID-19 community (Pillar 2) antigen test results. It links them to voice and cough recordings from volunteers to build and test algorithms that could detect COVID-19 from audio. The aim is a rapid, minimally invasive, lower-cost screening tool that could reduce the need for swab-based testing.

DARS-NIC-460711-S8W6S.summary: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, prescribing and death records for patients who had a heart CT scan between 2018 and 2020. It is studying whether adding an AI-based blood flow analysis (FFRCT) to chest pain diagnosis is safe, reduces unnecessary tests and saves NHS costs. The primary results have been published in Nature Medicine (April 2025), showing fewer diagnostic tests at two years.

DARS-NIC-46086-Z7N9L.summary: Surrey County Council, a local authority, is using civil registration data on births and deaths, plus Primary Care Mortality Data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and protect public health, including suicide audits. The main intended benefit is local services adjusted to reduce mortality and health inequalities. So far, the data has supported parts of the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and suicide, drug and alcohol death surveillance.

DARS-NIC-461060-D7X5H.summary: The University of Birmingham's Centre for Childhood Cancer Survivor Studies is using aggregate hospital, mental health and primary care medicines data for the general population of England. It will compare these with the health problems and NHS use of people who survived childhood, teenage and young adult cancer, to identify survivors at higher risk and needing more support. Earlier publications from this work were used as key evidence in NHS England's review of its service specifications.

DARS-NIC-46116-N5L4J.summary: Cumberland Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention, with results published only as aggregated statistics. The intended benefit is local services tailored to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Analysis of drug and alcohol deaths informed the 2022 Drug and Alcohol Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-461283-Q3R7K.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care records on maternity care in England. It is studying how COVID-19 and changes to maternity services affected ethnic and socioeconomic inequalities in outcomes such as stillbirth, preterm birth and caesarean section. The aim is to inform guidance on reducing these inequalities. Findings have been presented at a conference and a paper was accepted by BMJ Open in 2024.

DARS-NIC-46180-X4X8N.summary: Lincolnshire County Council uses birth and death registration records, including identifiable details, to understand local health needs and plan public health services. The data supports needs assessments, suicide audits and advice to NHS commissioners, with published outputs being aggregated statistics. The aim is to target services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. It has already supported suicide audits and strategies, a suspected cancer cluster investigation in East Lindsey, and a Power BI analysis tool created in 2021.

DARS-NIC-46283-S8Z4X.summary: Harrow Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, along with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention and immunisation programmes. The main intended benefit is local services that are better targeted to reduce mortality and health inequalities. The council reports using the data to target public health resources and campaigns, and to support maternity service planning.

DARS-NIC-46287-C8S9C.summary: NHS Devon ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which is identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is invoice validation, which checks that hospital and other provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. The second is risk stratification, where the data is linked with GP data to identify patients at high risk of poor outcomes. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-463165-H3R4K.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care is using pseudonymised NHS commissioning data, including hospital data, linked with adult social care client-level records. It uses them to quality assure the social care data collection, produce official statistics and outcome measures, and support national oversight and local improvement. The stated aim is better outcomes for people using adult social care. So far, an outcome measure on reablement after hospital discharge has been developed, and councils receive dashboards of their own data.

DARS-NIC-463167-T3K0S.summary: NHS Black Country ICB, working with local authorities, uses pseudonymised hospital, mental health, community and other service data that combines clinical and financial information. It uses the data to commission health and care services, monitor providers and support public health duties. The main aim is to match services to local need, improve quality and reduce inequalities. It reports that services have been delivered to match population needs, and that it has monitored in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-463170-V2K1Y.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board uses pseudonymised patient-level NHS data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity, prescribing and adult social care records. It uses this to plan and commission health services, understand population health needs, validate provider activity and manage budgets and contracts. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care, reduced health inequalities and improved patient flow. It reports that the data is already informing its Joint Strategic Needs Assessment and Quality Improvement projects.

DARS-NIC-46451-N5X1R.summary: London Borough of Tower Hamlets uses identifiable birth and death registration data, plus primary care mortality data, to understand local public health needs. It uses them for suicide audits, planning health services and producing aggregated statistics, with the aim of tailoring local services and reducing health inequalities. The council reports using the data to examine life expectancy differences by sex and ethnic group, and to estimate local curves that inform prioritised screening programmes.

DARS-NIC-465144-J4C3T.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust is using hospital admission, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration data to study head injury and traumatic brain injury across England. The aim is to measure how common these injuries are, and how often they lead to brain bleeds, neurosurgery or death within 28 days, including for different age, sex, ethnic and deprivation groups. The main intended benefit is to help healthcare planners and policy makers focus services and prevention on higher-risk groups.

DARS-NIC-46517-P9Y7P.summary: Lancashire County Council, a local authority, uses civil registration births and deaths data and primary care mortality data, including identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and investigate issues such as suicide hotspots, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. Reported benefits include infant mortality analysis supporting the council's Early Years Strategy, and births data analysis that formed part of that strategy and informed service planning.

DARS-NIC-46741-M5T3F.summary: London Borough of Islington uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and immunisation programmes, and protect public health, including suicide prevention work. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. Reported outputs for 2022-2024 include a local births profile and analyses of cardiovascular, alcohol-specific and homeless-hostel deaths.

DARS-NIC-467721-N7C0L.summary: King's College London is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) to study whether X-ray guided endovascular aortic aneurysm repair is linked to a higher risk of later cancer than open repair. The researchers also want to identify which cancers develop and how long after the procedure. The aim is to help patients and clinicians weigh the risks when choosing between the two types of repair.

DARS-NIC-46844-W5V5G.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) uses NHS Digital reports on whether trial participants have died and which GP practice they are registered with. It uses them for the POPPI trial, which tested a nurse-led psychological intervention for critically ill patients, and it is keeping the data to finish writing up and analyse the results. The reports helped stop follow-up questionnaires going to families of participants who had died. The trial results have been published in the Journal of the American Medical Association and in a final report to the National Institute for Health Research.

DARS-NIC-468622-L9V8Z.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London, which manages the National Hip Fracture Database, uses civil registration of death, demographic and list cleaning data. It uses them to identify when patients with a hip, femoral or pelvic fracture have died, and to improve risk adjustment when comparing hospital performance. The aim is better care and outcomes for patients. An independent evaluation reported that the database has reduced deaths in the month after hip fracture, and mortality fell from 11% in 2007 to 5.3% in 2024.

DARS-NIC-470203-Y2L7J.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked NHS data for people who consented to the AMALFI trial, including hospital, emergency care, outpatient, medicines dispensed and death records. It is using the data to follow participants and measure whether screening older people at risk for undiagnosed atrial fibrillation, using a two-week heart monitor patch, improves outcomes compared with usual care. The main intended benefit is reliable evidence on whether this screening works and is cost-effective, which could inform future UK screening guidance. So far, the data has helped shape the analysis plan and identify participants who had died, so that contact with them could stop.

DARS-NIC-47108-H0V7G.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This applies an algorithm to identify patients at high or rising risk, so that GPs and commissioners can plan and target care. The main intended benefit is improved planning and more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-47118-L9M1G.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB (Milton Keynes area) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and other NHS activity data, including births and deaths records. It uses the data to check provider invoices are correct and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-47129-G8W4Q.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former St Helens CCG, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. It is used to check provider invoices and to recover overpayments through Liaison Financial Services Ltd. It is also used for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so GPs and commissioners can target care and reduce emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-47139-R5G3C.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is risk stratification: linking it with GP data to predict which patients are at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted. The second is invoice validation, checking that provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility and recovering overpayments. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient care.

DARS-NIC-47141-V2B4Q.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for its Oldham area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) linked with GP data at NHS number level. It uses this for risk stratification, which applies an algorithm to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is fewer avoidable emergency admissions and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-47142-P7B7Q.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (Vale Royal area) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, linked with GP data. It uses this for risk stratification, which gives patients risk scores so that those likely to deteriorate or need multiple services can be identified. GPs and commissioners can then target care and plan services. The main intended benefit is better-planned care and fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-47156-Y6P2L.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (South Cheshire area) uses hospital activity data from SUS for Commissioners, linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This applies an algorithm to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy use of services, so that GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services. The stated aim is earlier intervention, fewer avoidable emergency admissions and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-47174-R9S4W.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former NHS Bury CCG, uses hospital, ambulance, community, diagnostic and emergency care activity data, including Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better planned and targeted.

DARS-NIC-47180-P3Z1Q.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former Bolton CCG, uses hospital activity data (Secondary User Services data for commissioners) that can be identified by NHS number. It is used to check provider invoices and recover overpayments, and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to score patients' risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are sound financial control and better-targeted care that reduces avoidable hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-47184-P3G4K.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is risk stratification: linking it with GP data to score which patients are at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted earlier. The second is invoice validation: checking that provider invoices are the commissioner's responsibility and recovering overpayments. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-47189-W3X0L.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former Tameside and Glossop clinical commissioning group (CCG), uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and care activity data. Most is pseudonymised, but risk stratification uses data identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to identify patients at high risk of poor health and to plan, monitor and redesign local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-47190-V7H9B.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses health and care data covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times, social care, and birth and death records. It uses the data for risk stratification, which identifies patients likely to be at high risk, and for commissioning tasks such as planning, reporting and contract management. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning of services, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-47191-D9X6J.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, working with the local authority, uses pseudonymised health data covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and social care activity, plus births and deaths records. It uses the data to plan and commission health services and to understand local people's needs. The main aim is better joined-up, higher-quality care. Reported benefits include collating national outpatient data, monitoring the 2-hour crisis response target and work with providers to improve ethnicity coding.

DARS-NIC-47215-M5Y5Q.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for the former NHS Trafford CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including civil registration records of births and deaths. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor outcomes, and plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment and better-planned, more effective care for the local population.

DARS-NIC-47221-T6B6Y.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for the former Wigan Borough CCG area, uses hospital, community and mental health service data. It uses the data for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration so GPs can target care. It also uses it for commissioning, to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is better-planned, more effective services and improved patient experience.

DARS-NIC-47225-D8S4S.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB (for the former NHS Warrington CCG) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check invoices and recover overpayments, to identify patients at high risk so their care can be planned, and to plan and monitor commissioned services. The stated aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-47228-R3R3R.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside ICB, for the former NHS Wirral CCG, uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services (SUS+) for commissioners. It uses the data to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, including a review by Liaison Financial Services Ltd to recover overpayments. It also uses the data for risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk so GPs and commissioners can target care and plan services.

DARS-NIC-474087-R4S6D.summary: Norfolk County Council, a local authority, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering A&E, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient care. It uses them in its public health work, including needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. Reported results include electoral division health profiles, a falls dashboard and a tool to support alcohol licensing decisions.

DARS-NIC-474218-V7G7L.summary: AstraZeneca UK Limited, a commercial company, is using Permission to Contact data from people who have volunteered through an NHS service to hear about COVID-19 vaccine trials. The aim is to identify and respond to local health challenges, particularly for disadvantaged groups. Reported examples include a needs assessment on adolescent risky behaviours and a review of children's injury admissions that informed talks with NHS partners.

DARS-NIC-55670-P9Z0Z.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes ICB (for the former NHS Luton CCG) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including NHS-number-level activity data for invoice checks and pseudonymised data for planning. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care, and support commissioning and planning of local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient care.

DARS-NIC-55679-K9X4J.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board (ICB) is using hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, maternity, births and deaths data for the former East and North Hertfordshire area. It is used to check provider invoices and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and to improve care pathways. Reported results include local analysis behind new savings schemes for 2019/20 and monthly practice-level budget reports.

DARS-NIC-55684-W3H2F.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex ICB uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices for patients it is responsible for, and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and earlier, better-targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-55697-J3L9V.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex ICB (for the former NHS Southend CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that the CCG is only paying for activity it is responsible for. Risk stratification links this data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted earlier. The stated aim is to improve commissioning and patient care.

DARS-NIC-55709-D8W3P.summary: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board (a sub-ICB location, formerly NHS Waltham Forest CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data, linked with GP data, for risk stratification. This identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or heavy service use, so GPs and commissioners can plan and target care. The main intended benefit is better case management and more effective commissioning, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-55710-W8F8C.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB (West Essex area) uses NHS hospital, community, mental health, ambulance and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It is used to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be prioritised, and to plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned more effectively, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-55752-D6X5Y.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, social care and other health data, mostly pseudonymised, to check invoices from care providers and to plan and commission local health services. This supports payment accuracy, financial control and better planning around population needs. Reported results include helping GPs support frequent A&E attenders, which reduced attendances, and informing the redesign of the Integrated Diabetes Service.

DARS-NIC-55950-Y5Y2Y.summary: Queen Mary University of London, an academic organisation, holds hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registration death records linked for the EPOCH trial. The trial studied whether a quality improvement programme could improve care and survival for high-risk patients having emergency abdominal surgery (emergency laparotomy). This agreement covers only secure retention of the data, with the aim of helping hospitals make evidence-based improvements. The trial's main report was published in The Lancet in April 2019.

DARS-NIC-561357-X0F3N.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research organisation working for AstraZeneca UK Ltd, is using linked hospital, GP, prescribing, vaccination, COVID-19 test, cancer and death records. It is studying how much COVID-19 affects vulnerable groups such as immunocompromised and older people, and how much healthcare they use. The aim is to give regulators and health bodies evidence for decisions on COVID-19 prevention and treatment. Results have already appeared in a Lancet Regional Health-Europe paper, conference presentations and submissions to health authorities.

DARS-NIC-564296-L7V1M.summary: The Renal Association, a charity that runs the UK Renal Registry and the National Registry of Rare Kidney Diseases (RaDaR), is using hospital, emergency care and death registration records. It is linking them to RaDaR to study risk factors, future outcomes, inequalities and costs for adults and children with rare kidney disease, and to check the accuracy of registry data. The main intended benefit is better evidence to improve care, treatment and service planning for people with rare kidney disease.

DARS-NIC-56872-T9B0J.summary: The University of Warwick, an academic organisation, is using hospital records (including accident and emergency, inpatient, critical care and outpatient data), death registration data and a list-cleaning report. The data support the PARAMEDIC2 trial, which tests whether adrenaline is safe and effective for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. It will measure survival, hospital and intensive care stays, and cost-effectiveness, to inform resuscitation guidelines. The main results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2018.

DARS-NIC-568980-P9W7B.summary: The University of Edinburgh is using identifiable NHS England data on deaths, hospital admissions and medicines dispensed in primary care for a UK-wide study of stroke survivors. The study looks at memory, thinking and mood problems and vascular dementia after stroke, including links with COVID-19. It aims to improve prediction of who will develop these problems, so patients can be better informed and reach earlier treatment and care.

DARS-NIC-57238-Z1H5H.summary: Warwickshire County Council is using identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand and respond to local public health needs. The data supports needs assessments, suicide audits and hotspot mapping, and monitoring of deaths, with the aim of tailoring local services and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include analysis used in the Healthy Aging and 0-5 needs assessments, a bespoke mortality report, and drug-related death surveillance analysis.

DARS-NIC-577815-R9L1J.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, through its PIONEER data hub, is using COVID-19 vaccination status and vaccine adverse reaction data, linked to its own hospital patient records. The aim is to support research on vaccine safety and effectiveness, including rare blood clotting events after vaccination. The main intended benefit is more detailed information for researchers, policymakers and NHS managers on which patient groups may be at risk of adverse reactions.
