DARS-NIC-578994-N0J1X.summary: The Department for Education will use linked, pseudonymised health and education records for children and young people, held in the Office for National Statistics Secure Research Service. It will study how education and health affect each other, including the long-term effects of COVID-19 and lost learning, especially for vulnerable children. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform government policy and better health and social care services for these children.

DARS-NIC-579513-Z7S7N.summary: The University of Kent is using record-level, pseudonymised data from the Personal Social Services Survey of Adult Carers in England, which collects information about unpaid carers of adults using social care services. It will use the data to put findings from its project on carers' experiences over time into a wider national context. The aim is to show what support helps carers keep a good quality of life, so that local authorities can better plan and commission services.

DARS-NIC-580880-D9Q9P.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB, working with the local authority, uses pseudonymised health and social care data, covering hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing and births and deaths records. They use it to plan and commission health and care services for people in the Newcastle area. The aim is to meet patient need, reduce inequalities and improve outcomes. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report says this data supported integration analysis and its work on hospital discharge and services for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

DARS-NIC-580883-G7N1K.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for Stockport's clinical commissioning group (CCG) and council, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care, prescribing and mortality data. It uses this to plan and commission health and care services for the local population, including service redesign, spotting patients at risk and managing demand. The stated aim is better decisions and better quality of care. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report records lower emergency admissions for several groups and reduced spending on procedures of limited clinical value.

DARS-NIC-580892-L7J0N.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB is using pseudonymised (identifiers replaced) hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and death and birth registration data. It uses this to plan and commission health services for its local population. This includes identifying patients at risk, understanding health needs, monitoring provider activity and redesigning care. The main intended benefit is better-planned services that reduce avoidable hospital admissions and improve the quality of care.

DARS-NIC-583534-X7S2N.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records for patients admitted in an emergency with five acute abdominal conditions, including appendicitis and diverticulitis. It is comparing emergency surgery with non-emergency care at different stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, looking at effectiveness and cost-effectiveness. The intended benefit is to help NHS England and hospitals plan and prioritise care during COVID-19 recovery.

DARS-NIC-58603-S6Z1B.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, a research organisation, is using cancer registration, death registration, demographic and follow-up status data on women in the Manchester Study and ARTISTIC trial cohorts. It will estimate long-term cervical cancer risk following human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, to inform cervical screening policy. Findings from the ARTISTIC cohort have already been cited as evidence for England's move to primary HPV screening.

DARS-NIC-589868-W0K1B.summary: The University of Sheffield is using linked NHS data on emergency care, hospital admissions, outpatient care, mental health services, dispensed medicines and deaths. It is building a research database, CUREd+, to study how patients use urgent and emergency care in England. The main intended benefit is evidence to make these services more efficient, safer and better for patients. So far, four research studies have been approved to receive data extracts, but no results are reported yet.

DARS-NIC-58999-K6P8B.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company, holds hospital data (Hospital Episode Statistics accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) to check its published findings on pulmonary arterial hypertension if questions are raised. The research looked at how patients with this lung condition are diagnosed, aiming to support earlier diagnosis and better treatment. Findings have already been published in the Journal of Pulmonary Circulation and the European Respiratory Journal in 2018, and presented at two international conferences.

DARS-NIC-594012-C9R9H.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne, an academic organisation, is using NHS hospital, emergency care, outpatient, mental health and death registration records. It is studying how disabled children's contacts with NHS services changed between April 2019 and September 2021, across different COVID-19 lockdown periods. The aim is to inform policy on recovering services and planning a minimum service for future emergencies.

DARS-NIC-594129-R0M3W.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using contact details and screening information (such as age, sex, location, job type and health questions) from people who signed up to be contacted about COVID-19 vaccine trials. NHS Digital processes this data on the Trust's behalf to recruit volunteers to a phase I trial of the pEVAC-PS vaccine. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping speed up the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-595090-W5R3K.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS hospital, emergency care and death registration records to carry out a health economic analysis for the FAME trial. The analysis compares close contact casting with surgery in younger adults with unstable ankle fractures. It looks at whether ankle function with casting is not worse than with surgery. The main intended benefit is evidence to update NICE fracture guidance and inform commissioning decisions.

DARS-NIC-595667-K4S9R.summary: The University of Bristol, an academic organisation, is using pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and chemotherapy-type records for about 300 consenting patients in the ROMIO trial. The trial compares combined keyhole and open surgery with standard open surgery for oesophageal (gullet) cancer. It looks at recovery, complications, survival, quality of life and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to help inform the best surgical practice in future.

DARS-NIC-596002-V3N9J.summary: Harvey Walsh Ltd, a supplier working on a University of Bristol study, is using GP records from the COVID-19 GP data extraction (GDPPR) for people registered with GP practices in the Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire area. It will use them to calculate population denominators by risk group for the Avon Community Acquired Pneumonia study of hospitalised lower respiratory illness. The intended benefit is accurate disease incidence figures to help guide healthcare resourcing and vaccination policy.

DARS-NIC-596409-F0T3M.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on mothers and babies. It is working for the Department of Health and Social Care to estimate how many obstetricians and anaesthetists maternity units in England need, taking account of how complex each unit's births are. The results will feed an online workforce tool, a report and publications. The aim is to help plan staffing that supports safer maternity care.

DARS-NIC-59669-F6Y3W.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England is using patient-level hospital admission records and civil registration death records for the National Vascular Registry, an audit of NHS vascular surgery. The data will be linked to the registry's records to show longer-term outcomes, such as 90-day mortality and readmissions, and to check how complete the registry's case numbers are. The aim is to help NHS vascular units improve care and patient outcomes. The registry's outputs have already been used by surgeons for revalidation, by NHS trusts for quality improvement, and in the NHS England CQUIN process.

DARS-NIC-597255-J9M1H.summary: The University of Manchester is using cancer registration and civil death registration data for about 500 people who took part in the RAPID clinical trial for early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma. It will follow their survival, causes of death and second cancers, comparing those treated with chemotherapy alone against chemotherapy plus radiotherapy. The hoped-for benefit is better evidence on late effects of treatment, which could change how early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma is managed.

DARS-NIC-59807-V1B8W.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB (North East Lincolnshire area) uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and social care data, including identifiable and pseudonymised records. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-59873-D8C6G.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit uses cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on men taking part in the STAMPEDE trial of added treatments for high-risk prostate cancer. The data is used to follow participants' survival over the long term and to check how well death records match trial data. The aim is better evidence on which treatments help men live longer. Death registration data let the metformin comparison report its main result sooner.

DARS-NIC-60215-F1S2G.summary: Cheshire West and Chester Council uses civil registration births and deaths data, including identifiable records, along with primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, support suicide audits and prevention, and plan public health services, with the aim of tailoring services and reducing health inequalities. Reported results include informing the Place Plan 2024, Children's centre dashboards, and the 0-19 JSNA published in 2024.

DARS-NIC-602345-C6S4M.summary: The University of Cambridge is using NHS England cancer registration and civil registration of death data for the EMBED study. The study aims to develop sensitive blood tests that detect tiny amounts of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), so breast cancer can be found earlier in women at increased risk. The main intended benefit is a simple blood test that improves early diagnosis and may reduce the need for repeated scans, biopsies and preventive surgery.

DARS-NIC-604129-X4D1K.summary: The University of Bristol is using the 2014 Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey, a population survey of adults in England covering mental health and use of support services. The research looks at which social and demographic factors are linked to older men using community support groups for mental health difficulties. The main intended benefit is to help support services and community groups target help at particular groups of older men.

DARS-NIC-604847-S4B5L.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, a commercial company, and Queen Mary University of London are using pseudonymised patient-level NHS data on cancer registrations, cancer treatments, hospital care and emergency care. They are following up people recruited to the NHS-Galleri trial, which tests whether a blood test that can detect many cancers finds them earlier than current NHS tests. The aim is to inform whether the NHS adopts the test to help detect cancer earlier.

DARS-NIC-604851-W0M3S.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, a commercial company working jointly with the University of Oxford, is using linked NHS cancer registration, hospital, emergency care and cancer waiting times data for people who consented to the SYMPLIFY study. The study assesses how well the Galleri blood test detects many types of cancer in people referred with possible cancer symptoms. The main intended benefit is to show whether such a test could help diagnose cancer earlier and with fewer diagnostic procedures.

DARS-NIC-605115-L0W3V.summary: The University of Oxford (Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences) uses NHS England data on COVID-19 test results, hospital care, emergency care, deaths and dispensed medicines. It uses them in the PANORAMIC trial, which tests antiviral treatments for higher-risk people with COVID-19 in the community. The aim is to see whether the treatments reduce hospital admissions and deaths. The trial has produced four publications, including a 2023 results paper on molnupiravir.

DARS-NIC-606084-D1D6T.summary: University of Cambridge is using NHS England death registration records and hospital admitted patient and outpatient records to follow up people with cerebral small vessel disease, a disease of the small blood vessels in the brain. The research aims to find genetic risk factors for the disease and to identify who goes on to develop dementia. The main intended benefit is better prediction of dementia after lacunar stroke and a better understanding of the disease's causes, which could support new treatments.

DARS-NIC-60624-B1R2Q.summary: IQVIA Ltd, a commercial company working with the National Amyloidosis Centre at the Royal Free, is using hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatient and A&E) on people with amyloidosis, a rare disease. They are studying how patients are diagnosed and treated, to support earlier diagnosis and a more efficient care pathway. One paper on cardiac transthyretin amyloidosis has already been published in the journal Circulation.

DARS-NIC-606839-V5X2P.summary: The Boston Consulting Group UK LLP, a consultancy, uses pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, mental health, community services and patient-reported outcome data. It uses the data to give NHS and public sector clients benchmarking, performance analysis, demand and capacity modelling and care pathway analysis. The main intended benefit is helping clients find improvements in patient care and experience. In 2025 it used hospital data for an integrated care system's productivity analysis and to build a productivity benchmarking tool.

DARS-NIC-60714-M4T1M.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, with Queen Mary University of London, is using hospital admission, critical care and death records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. The trial tests a fluid treatment for people having emergency bowel surgery. The aim is to show whether it helps or harms patients and what it costs. Data have been used in four safety reports, and the 2019 report led the trial team to change the primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-608743-H5X9Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS hospital records, demographic details and death registrations for children with certain surgical conditions. It is building a research database to compare hospitals' observed outcomes with those expected from the children they treat. This aims to identify unwarranted variation in care, with feedback to hospitals and a public dashboard. The intended benefit is better health outcomes and care for children with these conditions.

DARS-NIC-609893-N5P5L.summary: Imperial College London's Neonatal Data Analysis Unit is using demographic data (names and up-to-date postcodes) to link records of very preterm and surgical babies in the National Neonatal Research Database with education and health records. The aim is to understand the long-term health and educational outcomes of these children, so that neonatal care and service planning can be improved. Reported results include a peer-reviewed paper on survival of extremely preterm babies that changed national guidance.

DARS-NIC-609903-V6Q7S.summary: NHS England is supplying demographic data from the Patient Demographic Service for a cohort of adults with autoimmune diseases or cancers who are immunosuppressed. Imperial College London is using it for the MELODY study, so that Ipsos MORI can send invitations, confirm identities and post home antibody test kits after a third COVID-19 vaccine dose. The study aims to show how many immunosuppressed people develop detectable SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, to help inform health policy and targeted protection.

DARS-NIC-61042-K9Q3G.summary: Hull York Medical School is using hospital admissions records linked to death registration data to assess how national head injury guidelines (from NICE) affected deaths from traumatic brain injury and hospital admissions for head injury. The aim is to judge whether the guidelines have been clinically effective and whether they added to NHS admissions and costs. Analysis so far found that only the guideline recommending specialist centre care was linked to lower mortality, limited to ages 16 to 65.

DARS-NIC-610798-N0G8Z.summary: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) is using NHS England hospital, death registration, mental health, maternity, cancer and primary care dispensing data in the Secure Data Environment. It uses this to understand NHS activity and costs, and to develop and update its guidance. The aim is for guidance to reflect real-world patient care. NICE reports completing eight data requests for 2025/26, including hospital data to support resource impact tools for guidelines.

DARS-NIC-61090-T9Y0G.summary: The University of Oxford, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital admission records, death registration data and the National Hip Fracture Database. It is studying whether total hip replacement gives better outcomes than partial (hemiarthroplasty) replacement for independently mobile older adults with a hip fracture. It will also look at whether treatment that departs from NICE guidance leads to worse outcomes. The aim is to inform future updates of NICE and British Orthopaedic Association guidance.

DARS-NIC-612092-Q0Y6F.summary: The Home Office is using detailed, unsuppressed tables of hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for assault injuries in England. It uses them to monitor serious violence, evaluate policies and decide where to allocate funding. The aim is to target money at the areas with most need and reduce serious violence. A published evaluation of Violence Reduction Units reportedly showed a statistically significant reduction in violence.

DARS-NIC-61265-Q4L9V.summary: Wirral Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work and needs assessments. The aim is to tailor local services to areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. Reported results include analysis that found high COPD mortality in two deprived wards and led to joint work with the ICB and Community Trust on early intervention.

DARS-NIC-613522-Q7Z8N.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using NHS hospital, emergency care, community and mental health service records, including psychological therapy data. It is studying how people from ethnic minorities in North East and North Cumbria used mental health services before and after the pandemic, and how this relates to their health outcomes. The aim is to inform evidence-based decisions and services that better meet the needs of ethnic minority communities.

DARS-NIC-614954-G8P7P.summary: The University of Edinburgh, an academic organisation, is using identifiable NHS England data, drawn from hospital admissions, demographics and dispensed medicines records, to find and invite people who survived a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain to join the ASPIRING study. The study tests whether starting antiplatelet drugs reduces later major cardiovascular events. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on whether this treatment helps stroke survivors.

DARS-NIC-615890-Q8N9R.summary: NHS Hertfordshire and West Essex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include patient-level health and financial data. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and manage local health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. Reported results include a frailty service evaluation that led the provider to refine the service, and an urgent and emergency care analysis that informed an approved strategy.

DARS-NIC-615897-K1Z9C.summary: NHS North East London Integrated Care Board uses invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices are correct, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is better-targeted care and more effective commissioning of services. The board says its analysis already helps it identify unmet need and inequalities.

DARS-NIC-615958-F7Q7Z.summary: NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board uses commissioning datasets, containing pseudonymised clinical and financial information, and invoice validation datasets. It uses them to plan health services for its local population and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that services are planned and paid for accurately and appropriately.

DARS-NIC-615960-G7W1L.summary: NHS Kent and Medway Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients, to plan health services, check provider invoices and identify patients at high risk. The aim is to commission services more effectively, control budgets and improve patient outcomes. It reports using the data for board performance reports, contract monitoring, invoice queries and disputes, and an evaluation of social prescribing in Kent and Medway.

DARS-NIC-615969-D3K1X.summary: NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board uses commissioning and invoice validation datasets, including pseudonymised clinical and financial data about patients. It uses them to check that providers' invoices are correct and the patients are its responsibility, and to plan and manage health services for its population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned to meet local health needs.

DARS-NIC-615972-B8C0H.summary: North Tyneside Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits. The main intended benefit is local services that are better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. Reported results include identifying clusters of disease and of suicide, and an end of life care needs assessment.

DARS-NIC-615974-Y3R7Q.summary: NHS North Central London Integrated Care Board uses identifiable and pseudonymised data on invoices, patient risk and commissioned health services. It uses the data to check that providers' invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to analyse population needs so services can be planned. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with better patient outcomes and accurate payment of providers. The reported benefits section lists general aims but no specific completed outcome.

DARS-NIC-615980-P3Y7N.summary: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board is using commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-615981-K2W5D.summary: NHS South East London Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data and invoice validation data, including pseudonymised patient-level clinical and financial information. It uses them to check that provider invoices are correct and to analyse population health needs, so health services can be planned, commissioned and redesigned. Some results may also go to health and care professionals for direct care. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services better meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-615983-Y9Q5G.summary: NHS Bedfordshire, Luton and Milton Keynes Integrated Care Board uses invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some of which can identify patients. It uses them to check that providers' invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and monitor health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-615985-Y6L2H.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire Integrated Care Board, uses commissioning and invoice validation datasets, including pseudonymised clinical and financial data. It uses them to plan and commission health services for the local population, to check that provider invoices are correct and to support direct care. The main intended benefits are better-planned services and accurate payment of providers for patient treatment.

DARS-NIC-615995-K0R4H.summary: NHS Northamptonshire Integrated Care Board uses patient-level health and financial data, including commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which are mostly pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and manage health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-615997-B5S2L.summary: NHS Herefordshire and Worcestershire Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Coventry and Warwick Integrated Care Board for some purposes, uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with providers paid accurately and care better targeted. The reported benefits are general, covering statutory duties, invoice validation, better understanding of the local population, and improved planning.

DARS-NIC-615998-S4B4H.summary: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients by NHS number. It uses them to check that provider invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and monitor local health services. The main aim is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. It reports that Eclipse risk stratification services saved up to £42 per patient per year across GP practice populations.

DARS-NIC-616004-J8K1K.summary: NHS South Yorkshire Integrated Care Board uses invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at risk of health deterioration, and plan and manage health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient care and outcomes. The board reports that it has queried inaccurate invoices from acute trusts and given senior staff cost breakdowns by area.

DARS-NIC-616005-Z0T0F.summary: NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include patient-level and pseudonymised health and financial data. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616007-R3H0G.summary: NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data (pseudonymised, with clinical and financial information) and invoice validation data. It uses them to plan health services for the local population, and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility. The main intended benefit is that services are planned and paid for accurately and appropriately.

DARS-NIC-616019-B4C8W.summary: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board uses commissioning and invoice validation datasets, including pseudonymised clinical and financial data, to plan health services for its population and to check that provider invoices are accurate and payable. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid correctly and services are planned around local needs. Reported results include improved discharge planning for people with a learning disability or autism, and a completed evaluation of Luscii remote monitoring in Leeds.

DARS-NIC-616027-W7K5H.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney Integrated Care Board uses national hospital and emergency care records, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. The data is pseudonymised before it is supplied. The board uses it to meet its legal duties on commissioning health services, improving quality and reducing inequalities. This includes benchmarking against other areas, planning capacity and redesigning services. The main intended benefit is better local commissioning decisions based on national comparisons.

DARS-NIC-616029-Y7G7K.summary: NHS Derby and Derbyshire Integrated Care Board uses invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some of which can identify patients and some of which are pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The stated aim is more effective commissioning, with better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616031-W6R2C.summary: NHS Somerset Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data and invoice validation data about patients' care. It uses them to check that providers are paid correctly for patient treatment and to plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that payments are financially validated and services are better planned and managed. The agreement reports that invoice validation has ensured care was financially validated, and that commissioning data has supported quality improvement work with providers.

DARS-NIC-616034-Y7S7M.summary: NHS Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Integrated Care Board, uses commissioning datasets (pseudonymised clinical and financial data) and invoice validation datasets. It uses them to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility, and to plan and review health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned to meet local health needs.

DARS-NIC-616037-P7H6X.summary: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Integrated Care Board, uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include pseudonymised and NHS-number-level patient data. It uses them to plan and commission health services, check that provider invoices are correct, and identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616038-B3P3X.summary: NHS Suffolk and North East Essex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at risk of poorer health, and plan health services for its population. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. It reports that the data now supports a population health management platform and board reports used by transformation groups.

DARS-NIC-616039-L2R9G.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data, which is pseudonymised and holds clinical and financial information, and invoice validation data. It uses them to plan health services for its local population, check that provider invoices are correct and the patients are its responsibility, and identify patients at risk. The main intended benefits are better planning and quality of services, and accurate payment of providers.

DARS-NIC-616043-S9R4P.summary: NHS England is using patient-level acute hospital activity data (inpatients, admissions, discharges and outpatients), which is pseudonymised before it is shared. It is collected daily into the NHS National Data Platform (Foundry) to help reduce elective waiting lists and support planning of services by integrated care boards, acute providers and community providers. The main intended benefit is more timely data for commissioners and less manual reporting for providers.

DARS-NIC-616045-Q5Y4G.summary: NHS Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin Integrated Care Board, uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of them pseudonymised. They use them to plan and commission health services, check that providers' invoices are correct, and identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616046-J1Q0N.summary: NHS Norfolk and Waveney Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, including patient-level data. It uses them to plan and commission health services for its population, check that provider invoices are correct and identify patients at high risk so GPs can target care. The main stated benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. Reported examples include elective recovery reporting supporting contract management and planning.

DARS-NIC-616054-M4C8K.summary: NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include patient-level health and payment data. It uses them to plan and commission health services, check provider invoices before payment, and identify patients at high risk so care can be targeted. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. It reports that board reports are already used by programme groups to act on services and inform new care models.

DARS-NIC-616059-F9B3T.summary: NHS Mid and South Essex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include pseudonymised clinical and financial data and some identifiable NHS number data. It uses them to check provider invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616065-S6L4Q.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board is using commissioning data, which is pseudonymised and holds clinical and financial information, and invoice validation data. It uses them to plan and commission health services for its local population and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility. The main intended benefits are better-informed service planning and accurate payment for patient treatment.

DARS-NIC-616080-P7S9X.summary: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. It reports that practices have used the risk tool to identify patients and give them additional care.

DARS-NIC-616081-Z8H5D.summary: NHS Frimley Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data, which contains clinical and financial information in pseudonymised form, and invoice validation data. It uses them to plan health services for its local population and to check that providers' invoices are correct before payment. The main intended benefit is that services are planned and paid for accurately, supporting better care and sound use of public money.

DARS-NIC-616082-B5F6M.summary: NHS Bath and North East Somerset, Swindon and Wiltshire Integrated Care Board uses invoice validation, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check that providers' invoices are correct, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and commission health services for its local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616083-J8W7P.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can be identified by NHS number and some of which are pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices before payment, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and analyse clinical and financial information to plan health services for its population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-616088-L5G0W.summary: NHS Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Black Country Integrated Care Board, uses commissioning data and invoice validation data. The commissioning data is pseudonymised and holds clinical and financial information. It is used to check that providers' invoices are correct and to plan health services around the needs of the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned and managed.

DARS-NIC-616929-K6X7D.summary: NHS Lincolnshire Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include patient-level health and financial data. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at risk of worse health, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and outcomes. Reported benefits include risk stratification being used in annual planning and in proactive primary care work to reduce emergency readmissions.

DARS-NIC-616940-N5K1W.summary: NHS North West London Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data, which is pseudonymised and holds clinical and financial information, and invoice validation data. It uses them to plan and commission health services for its local population and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patients are its responsibility. The main intended benefits are better-planned services and ensuring providers are paid accurately for patient treatment.

DARS-NIC-616944-B6M7X.summary: NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include pseudonymised and NHS-number-level patient data. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes. It reports that the data has helped identify health inequalities and guide new commissioning programmes.

DARS-NIC-616945-T7V7D.summary: NHS Devon Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly ICB, uses commissioning datasets (pseudonymised clinical and financial data) and invoice validation datasets. It uses them to plan health services for the local population and to check that provider invoices are correct and the patient is its responsibility. The aim is accurate payment and better-planned services. Board reports have already been used by programme groups to take action and guide new models of care.

DARS-NIC-616947-G9K5B.summary: NHS Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Integrated Care Board, jointly with NHS Northamptonshire ICB, uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, with accurate payment and better patient outcomes. The ICB reports the data has helped it validate invoices, understand its population and improve service planning.

DARS-NIC-616950-W5T2S.summary: NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data, which is pseudonymised and holds clinical and financial information, and invoice validation data. It uses them to check that providers' invoices are correct and to plan, manage and redesign health services for the local population. The stated aim is to make sure providers are paid accurately and that commissioning decisions meet the population's health needs.

DARS-NIC-616961-X1J9B.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which are pseudonymised and some identifiable by NHS number. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of emergency admission, and plan health services for its population. The aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. Reported results include supporting the board in surpassing its Elective Recovery Fund target and giving GP practices access to risk-grouped patient information.

DARS-NIC-616967-H6Z6L.summary: NHS Dorset Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients and some of which are pseudonymised. It uses them to check that providers are paid correctly, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-617728-R3S2C.summary: London Borough of Croydon, a local authority, uses civil registration births and deaths data, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide audits, with only aggregated outputs published. The aim is to tailor services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The data has already informed a young people's needs assessment, which led to commissioning of school readiness initiatives.

DARS-NIC-617735-T0Y9F.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some pseudonymised and some identifiable by NHS number. It uses them to plan and commission health services, check that provider invoices are correct and identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The stated aim is more effective commissioning and better patient outcomes. The board reports using the data to assess service performance, ensure enough services meet demand, understand prescribing levels and work with local authorities on the health needs of patients with SEND.

DARS-NIC-617743-X0M9Z.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board is using national hospital and emergency care records: Hospital Episode Statistics (inpatient, outpatient, critical care and A&E) and the Emergency Care Data Set. It will compare services, inequalities, rare conditions and health trends across England with its own area, to inform commissioning, capacity planning and service redesign. The main intended benefit is better local commissioning decisions and improved patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-617755-B4F1L.summary: East Sussex County Council is using civil registrations of death and primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details, on deaths by suicide. It is working with Brighton & Hove City Council and West Sussex County Council to analyse places, methods and trends of suicide across Sussex and to carry out suicide audits. The aim is to inform local services and policies that reduce the risk of suicide in the population.

DARS-NIC-617762-J8X8V.summary: Swindon Borough Council, a local authority, is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is local analysis of health outcomes and health inequalities, particularly for disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-617765-S6H2J.summary: Swindon Borough Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits. Results are published only as summary statistics. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths.

DARS-NIC-61864-C6X2R.summary: South Tyneside Council is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. This includes producing needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups. In 2023, civil registrations were used to analyse covid deaths and drug related deaths.

DARS-NIC-619023-C7K5V.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant, jointly with Imperial College London, is using demographic data on solid organ transplant recipients to invite them to the MELODY study. The study tests whether immunosuppressed people have detectable COVID-19 antibodies after a primary vaccine course, and whether antibodies relate to later infection risk or severity. The main intended benefit is to show which immunosuppressed people have not developed antibodies, so policy makers and clinicians can consider extra protection for them.

DARS-NIC-620484-W0B2K.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised patient-level hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging and death registration records for people enrolled in the EVAREST study. It will follow their heart-related care and outcomes after a stress echocardiogram (a heart test) to assess how accurate the test is and how it is used across the UK. The aim is to find areas for improvement and so reduce unnecessary further procedures. Two manuscripts using the data have already been published.

DARS-NIC-622485-S4F5C.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS hospital, emergency care and death registration records for a clinical trial of a cerebral embolic protection device used during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). It will look at long-term outcomes for trial participants, which groups face a higher risk of stroke, and whether using the device is cost-effective for the NHS. The aim is to help patients make evidence-informed decisions about their care.

DARS-NIC-623799-T2J4F.summary: ModernaTX, Inc, a pharmaceutical and biotechnology company, is using details that people gave through the NHS "Sign Up to be Contacted about Coronavirus Vaccine Studies" service, including age, sex, location, employment and health answers. The data is used to find and contact people who may be eligible for its COVID-19 booster vaccine trial. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping to speed up delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-625841-T2V6N.summary: Cancer Research UK, with the University of Leeds added as a data processor, is using non-identifiable national radiotherapy data collected during the COVID-19 pandemic. They are studying why radiotherapy treatment schedules were changed during the pandemic and how those changes affected patients and UK radiotherapy services. The aim is to give evidence to help health services recover and prepare for future pandemics.

DARS-NIC-626153-S6J6V.summary: King's College London is using cancer registration data from the National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) for YORKSURe, a feasibility trial of urine self-testing for blood in the urine to detect bladder cancer earlier in people at high risk of dying from it in Yorkshire. The data will be used to compare the populations, demographics and cancer incidence of those who complete self-testing and those who do not. The findings are intended to show whether a larger trial is viable, which could lead to earlier detection and better survival.

DARS-NIC-627124-V8Z6Z.summary: Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised civil registration deaths data, linked with local hospital records through its Connected Yorkshire programme. It uses the data to study patient pathways, end of life care and inequalities, so that health services in its Integrated Care System area can be planned and commissioned. The aim is to understand patterns of health need and develop better care. The Trust reports that the linked data let it identify likely palliative care needs in the last year of life and assess inequalities in access to palliative care services.

DARS-NIC-627125-B9N0Z.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, is using pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, prescribing, social care and death and birth registration data covering the South Yorkshire and Bassetlaw area. It uses the data to plan and monitor commissioned health services, including activity and finance reporting, contract management, risk stratification and mortality analysis. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions that improve patient pathways, service quality and health outcomes for the local population.

DARS-NIC-628591-K2Q2V.summary: The University of Bristol is using identifiable hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatients and emergency care) for about 600 people with Parkinson's disease who joined the CHIEF-PD trial. The records will show which hospital stays were caused by falls and what hospital care cost over 12 months. This helps the trial test whether rivastigmine, a cholinesterase inhibitor, prevents falls compared with a placebo and is cost-effective for the NHS. The findings are intended to inform NICE guidance on Parkinson's care.

DARS-NIC-628636-Y3B1N.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust and the University of Cambridge are using identifiable but not directly identifying NHS England cancer data, covering registrations, treatments, scans, waiting times, radiotherapy and patient experience. They are studying survival among people treated for breast cancer at Addenbrooke's Hospital over ten years. The aim is to compare the service with national figures and understand differences by treatment and demographic factors. This is expected to support recommendations to improve breast cancer care.

DARS-NIC-629056-F4L4B.summary: The University of Warwick is using demographic data from NHS Digital to identify and invite adults who were in hospital with COVID-19 and still have symptoms after three months (long Covid) to join the REGAIN trial. The trial tests whether an eight-week online exercise and mental health support programme helps, compared with a single online advice session. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, so results can guide long Covid rehabilitation while still relevant.

DARS-NIC-630656-V9W9M.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS Business Services Authority records of medicines dispensed in primary care, plus basic demographic details (vital status, current address and GP surgery), for ORION-4, a trial of the cholesterol-lowering drug inclisiran. The data will help check how well routine medicines data matches trial records and support contact with participants. The main intended benefit is showing whether inclisiran is safe and effective for people with cardiovascular disease.

DARS-NIC-631605-F2H3M.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using maternity records from the Maternity Services Data Set to produce official statistics. It will use them for research on COVID-19 and pregnancy, child and maternal health, and the future of population and census statistics. The main intended benefit is better evidence for government policy and public health decisions. So far, research has produced admin-based ethnicity statistics for England and Wales.

DARS-NIC-632349-B5F8W.summary: The University of Manchester is using pseudonymised data from the 2017 and 2020 Mental Health of Children and Young People survey. It is researching how children's and young people's mental health has changed over time, including during the COVID-19 pandemic, and how it relates to the mental health of their main carers. The aim is to give policymakers and clinicians evidence to help improve care and support for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-63347-R8J2M.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists is using identifiable hospital admission, critical care and death registration records for adults in the PQIP study who have had major planned non-cardiac surgery. It links them to study data to measure complications, recovery and survival after surgery, and to give hospitals feedback on care quality. The aim is fewer complications and better outcomes. Reported benefits include an enhanced recovery approach that NHS England adopted as a CQUIN financial target for Trusts.

DARS-NIC-633657-S7Z5R.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using the Community Services Data Set, which holds information on community health services. It is using it for research into whether population statistics, including on health and ethnicity, can be produced from administrative data. This research will form part of the evidence for the 2023 National Statistician's Recommendation on whether to hold another traditional Census in 2031.

DARS-NIC-634901-B4H8K.summary: Barts Health NHS Trust is using identifiable hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registration death records for people in England with Marfan syndrome. It is studying the number of these patients who have aortovascular surgery (surgery on the aorta and major blood vessels) and their hospital stays, complications and deaths afterwards. The main intended benefit is better understanding of their care needs, to help guide services and treatment.

DARS-NIC-635697-P0C5M.summary: The Office for Health Improvement and Disparities uses NHS England hospital, mortality, community, mental health and other health records, including some identifiable data. It uses them for public health work on drug and alcohol treatment, mortality and health inequalities, end of life care and local authority public health support. The main aim is to improve the public's health and reduce differences between groups. It reports publishing statistics such as the Excess Mortality in England reports and health profiles on the Fingertips platform.

DARS-NIC-636813-T2D1L.summary: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission and death registration records for about 800 people with autoimmune hepatitis, plus age-, sex- and region-matched people without the condition. It is researching whether people with autoimmune hepatitis have more heart and blood vessel disease, and whether this is linked to corticosteroid treatment. The main intended benefit is evidence to help doctors improve the care and treatment of these patients, for example by limiting steroid doses.

DARS-NIC-637092-P9K6S.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using contact details and screening information (such as age, sex, location, job type and health questions) from people who signed up through the NHS "Permission to Contact" service for COVID-19 vaccine trials. The data is used to invite potentially eligible people to join a phase I trial of the AZD1222 vaccine delivered by aerosol. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, helping speed up the delivery of an effective vaccine.

DARS-NIC-63736-Z7D2Z.summary: Kirklees Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health duties. It uses the data to produce local needs assessments, health strategies and the Director of Public Health's annual report, and to guide public health services. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. Reported uses include analyses supporting the council's healthy ageing report and smoking cessation commissioning.

DARS-NIC-637916-K3L3D.summary: The University of Bristol, an academic organisation, is using hospital admission records and death registration data to follow up people aged 50 and over who were admitted to hospital with pneumonia. It is using them in the ASPECT trial, which tests whether taking aspirin for three months reduces heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths compared with usual care. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide treatment and policy for pneumonia patients.

DARS-NIC-63798-B9T0B.summary: City of Westminster, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to produce needs assessments, health strategies, public health advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Annual public health reports have been published, and mortality data is helping shape local action on health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-63997-N3N7R.summary: London Borough of Bexley, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including through suicide audits. The aim is to tailor services and reduce health inequalities and premature deaths. The council reports using the mortality data in its Suicide Audit to understand risk characteristics and better target suicide prevention.

DARS-NIC-641622-S4C1Q.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using NHS hospital, emergency care, community, mental health and psychological therapy records, plus death registration data. It is studying how COVID-19 and lockdowns changed the use of mental health services by people in the most deprived communities in North East and North Cumbria, and how this relates to their health outcomes. The aim is to help policy-makers and service planners meet the needs of underserved groups.

DARS-NIC-642373-Z3P7N.summary: Imperial College London is using pseudonymised maternity records from the Maternity Services Data Set, covering 2015 to 2023. It is using them to study which factors in maternity care contribute to differences in pregnancy outcomes, including deaths, between ethnic groups, and to assess the quality and completeness of the data. The main intended benefit is evidence to help improve maternity services and reduce excess mortality among women and babies.

DARS-NIC-643421-J9T3M.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable cancer registration, death registration and demographic data on about 1,400 male doctors in the British Doctors Study. It is following them up to examine how smoking, stopping smoking and daily aspirin affect cancer, other diseases and cause of death. The aim is to add evidence on preventing diseases such as cancer and cardiovascular disease. Earlier results from the study are reported to have influenced national and personal decisions about quitting smoking.

DARS-NIC-64474-V4B2D.summary: St George's Hospital Medical School is using linked, de-identified hospital admission, critical care, death registration and demographic records for children born with a congenital anomaly, drawn from five regional registers in England. The data will build a research database for studying these children's long-term survival, health and educational outcomes. The main intended benefit is helping parents understand their children's needs, prospects and life chances.

DARS-NIC-644891-N5T3S.summary: University College London is using identifiable NHS England data on deaths, cancer registrations and medicines dispensed in primary care. The data covers people who took part in the AspECT trial and are included in this follow-up study. It is being used to follow their long-term outcomes, including oesophageal cancer and death, and to see how aspirin and proton pump inhibitor use affected them. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence on preventing oesophageal cancer in people with Barrett's oesophagus.

DARS-NIC-64572-X0Q4D.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research uses tabulated hospital-level Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, which are counts of patients and not patient-level records. It uses them to check how many heart attack patients each hospital submits to the national heart attack audit (MINAP) compared with those coded in hospital records. The main intended benefit is better audit data quality and fairer comparisons between hospitals. Case ascertainment rates have been published annually since 2017, revealing wide variation between hospitals.

DARS-NIC-647363-F3R4R.summary: The University of Oxford's Oxford Vaccine Group is using NHS England's recruitment service, which supplies a mailing list of people matched by age and postcode area, to invite about 4,000 potential volunteers to a malaria vaccine trial. The trial tests the safety and effectiveness of a candidate vaccine, including with volunteers deliberately infected under controlled conditions. The data is used only to identify and invite participants, to help reach the recruitment target. The trial may contribute to a safe, effective malaria vaccine.

DARS-NIC-648118-L0Q2Z.summary: King's College London is using hospital, emergency care and COVID-19 vaccination status records, linked to a South London register of mothers and children called eLIXIR. It will use them for approved research on maternal, child and mental health, including pregnancy complications, long-term health and vaccine uptake among pregnant women. The aim is evidence to inform clinical guidelines, health services and public health policy.

DARS-NIC-648561-Z8L8M.summary: Archus Limited, a consultancy advising the NHS, is using patient-level hospital data covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It uses the data to model future healthcare needs by place and population, supporting service redesign and the planning of hospital facilities. The main intended benefit is better capacity planning and more informed decisions on healthcare buildings and services. So far, it has used the data in a national analysis of robotic assisted surgery, highlighting potential savings and patient outcome improvements.

DARS-NIC-649110-Z5S0L.summary: The University of Birmingham is using pseudonymised hospital records (admissions, accident and emergency, critical care and outpatient data) for people who took part in the CReST2 trial. The trial compares covered and uncovered stents for bowel obstruction caused by colorectal cancer in patients not fit for major surgery. The data will be used to estimate NHS costs for each stent type. The aim is to show which stent offers better value for money and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-650245-T6C6T.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admission records and demographic data, including date of death, for 183 adults who survived intensive care with sepsis and took part in a clinical trial. It will check who was readmitted to hospital with an infection, estimate the hospital costs and measure survival. This will show whether a single pneumococcal vaccine reduces infections and rehospitalisation after sepsis, and whether a larger future trial is worthwhile.

DARS-NIC-650291-P6N5H.summary: The University of Surrey is using pseudonymised data from the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey (APMS), combining the 2007 and 2014 surveys. The research examines how sleep problems, self-harm and suicide are linked, and whether difficulty managing emotions (emotion dysregulation) plays a part. The main intended benefit is a clearer understanding that could support better-targeted care for adults with poor sleep and emotion dysregulation.

DARS-NIC-651348-Z0N4H.summary: Swansea University, an academic institution, is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care, critical care and death registration records for about 550,000 patients who used participating ambulance services. It is comparing ethnic minority and White British people with injuries, looking at the care they receive and their outcomes over six months, and at how complete ethnicity records are. The intended benefit is evidence to help policy makers and care providers improve injury care for ethnic minority populations.

DARS-NIC-651660-J5T6C.summary: Grail Bio UK Ltd, a commercial company working with Queen Mary University of London, is using demographic data (vital status and current addresses) for people taking part in the NHS-Galleri cancer screening trial. It will use this to update the participant list, remove people who have died and send a thank-you letter and follow-up appointment invitations. The aim is to keep participants informed and help them stay in the trial.

DARS-NIC-651858-F5H2J.summary: King's College London is using pseudonymised maternity records for mothers and babies, along with civil registrations of death, covering 2017/18 to 2022/23. The researchers want to understand how maternity outcomes, such as eclampsia, caesarean section and baby deaths, vary by ethnic group, NHS trust and region. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers and clinicians tailor maternity care and reduce unfair differences in outcomes.

DARS-NIC-653950-W8D4Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS England data, including hospital, death, cancer registration and demographic records, for 1,441 consenting participants in the Oxford Vascular Study. The study follows people in eight Oxfordshire GP practices after stroke, TIA, acute coronary syndrome and other vascular events, to measure outcomes and costs of care. It aims to improve prevention, diagnosis and treatment. Study findings have already informed national stroke guidelines.

DARS-NIC-654590-Y0S1H.summary: Cardiff University is using pseudonymised hospital admission records and death registration data for about 3,000 patients who took liothyronine (T3) or similar thyroid treatments. It is studying whether long-term T3 use for underactive thyroid affects survival or raises the risk of heart attacks, heart rhythm problems, heart failure or strokes, compared with patients on levothyroxine (T4). If T3 is shown to be safe, it could widen treatment options for patients who do not feel better on T4 and inform future guidelines.

DARS-NIC-655024-S2H5Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England contact and demographic details, plus aggregate data quality reports, to identify and invite people with type 2 diabetes to join the ASCEND PLUS clinical trial. The trial tests whether the drug oral semaglutide reduces heart attacks, strokes and other diabetes complications, which could change treatment guidelines. Recruitment has reportedly been two to three times faster than the original ASCEND trial, with 9,200 people randomised by November 2024.

DARS-NIC-655446-P9K9Q.summary: Adelphi Group Limited, a consultancy working for Merck Sharp & Dohme (MSD) Medical Affairs UK, is using pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, imaging, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data on adults diagnosed with stage II melanoma between 2015 and early 2018. They are studying patients' characteristics, the treatments they receive and the cost of their care to the NHS. The aim is to fill a gap in evidence on the stage II melanoma patient pathway, to support decisions on care and treatment.

DARS-NIC-656749-G8K4G.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised cancer registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for about 85,000 people who had a solid organ transplant. It is linking these with other existing records to study cancer after transplantation, including cancer types, deaths and hospital care. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform care guidelines and help counsel people before a transplant.

DARS-NIC-656750-K1X5M.summary: Imperial College London's Cancer Screening and Prevention Research Group is using NDRS cancer registration data, linked to bowel screening records for consenting participants. It is testing whether yearly faecal immunochemical tests (FIT) can safely replace three-yearly colonoscopies for people with intermediate adenomas, and examining acceptability and costs. The aim is to inform surveillance guidelines. The study's results have been published, including in the journal Gut in 2019, and report that annual FIT could cut colonoscopies by 71% and reduce NHS costs.

DARS-NIC-656751-H5K0Y.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway, treatment and linked hospital records for more than 100,000 women who have consented to take part in the Generations Study. It is studying genetic and environmental risk factors for cancer, mainly breast cancer, and outcomes after diagnosis. The aim is to add evidence that could shape guidance on prevention and care. Published papers have already appeared, including a large pooled analysis of physical activity and premenopausal breast cancer.

DARS-NIC-656752-G2L2P.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable National Disease Registration Service cancer registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for about 4.5 million women in the AgeX Trial. The trial tests the risks and benefits of extra NHS breast screening invitations at ages 47-49 and 71-73. The findings are intended to help the UK government decide whether to widen the age range for routine breast screening.

DARS-NIC-656754-C6S5Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England cancer registration data, linked to its EPIC-Oxford cohort of 60,642 adults, to study how diet, especially vegetarian and vegan diets, affects long-term health. The aim is to give reliable evidence to inform public and NHS dietary advice. Findings have been published in journals such as the BMJ and used in evidence reviewed by the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition.

DARS-NIC-656755-W4N5C.summary: Queen Mary University of London, an academic institution, is using identifiable National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data on people diagnosed with colorectal cancer in 2012 and 2013. It is using the data in a case-control study evaluating the NHS Bowel Cancer Screening Programme, and wants to carry out further analyses on other disease stages and check for possible biases. The main intended benefit is to estimate the programme's effect on late-stage disease. The team has published results in the Journal of the National Cancer Institute (2022) showing a reduction in Dukes D stage cancer with screening.

DARS-NIC-656757-J8V9D.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using pseudonymised data on cancer registrations, hospital care, diagnostic imaging, treatments and patient surveys. It is studying why inequalities in cancer care and survival arise and persist in England, including the roles of patient, tumour, clinical and healthcare system factors. The aim is to inform strategies that reduce these inequalities. So far, the team reports that differences by deprivation, age or gender were only partly explained by patient factors, which points to barriers within the healthcare system.

DARS-NIC-656758-N4H9Y.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hospital data on women in England diagnosed with breast cancer. It is studying how four breast cancer subtypes vary by age, ethnicity and other characteristics, and how treatment and survival differ. The aim is to identify gaps in care and support tailored treatment. Three peer-reviewed papers have been published, and results have been presented at conferences.

DARS-NIC-656760-F8Y3C.summary: University College London is using NHS England cancer registration data on infants with neuroblastoma to study long-term survival, tumour stage, tumour biology and treatments, comparing England with five other European countries. The aim is to understand why survival in England declined in the 2000s and to help identify best clinical practice. So far, two conference abstracts have been published, and results have been presented at several congresses.

DARS-NIC-656761-R6H7W.summary: The University of Leeds uses cancer registration, death registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data to run the Yorkshire Specialist Register of Cancer in Children and Young People. It supports research on hospital admissions, care pathways, late health effects and survival, aiming to improve care for young people with cancer. Reported results include published papers on long-term health problems, and evidence that supported clinical services in adopting risk-stratified follow-up care.

DARS-NIC-656762-V9J7N.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable NHS England cancer registration data on people diagnosed with invasive or in situ breast cancer, together with control groups. The study is a case-control evaluation of the NHS Breast Screening Programme, looking at its effect on breast cancer deaths and on overdiagnosis. It aims to inform work to improve the national screening programme. Two papers have been published, on the effect on breast cancer mortality and on incidence.

DARS-NIC-656763-K3F9R.summary: The University of Oxford is using national cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data to study women diagnosed with non-invasive breast cancer. It aims to understand their long-term risk of invasive breast cancer, death from breast cancer and further non-invasive cancer, and the factors behind these risks. The main hoped-for benefit is better evidence on screening and treatment for ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). Two published BMJ papers have already been cited in NICE and Association of Breast Surgeons guidance.

DARS-NIC-656767-M5W2L.summary: The UK Health Security Agency is using cancer registration data from the National Disease Registration Service. It is studying cervical cancer in women under 30, comparing rates across birth cohorts by their eligibility for HPV (human papillomavirus) vaccination. The aim is to give evidence for monitoring and evaluating England's HPV vaccination programme and to inform policy. So far, the text reports that surveillance has been established, but not yet any evidence of vaccination impact.

DARS-NIC-656768-C1Z1M.summary: Imperial College London's Small Area Health Statistics Unit uses cancer registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data, some of it identifiable. It uses them for research and surveillance on how cancer and other health conditions relate to environmental, social and geographical factors, aiming to inform public health policy. Reported results include a public online Environment and Health Atlas for England and Wales, launched in 2013, and 20 peer-reviewed publications in the last two years.

DARS-NIC-656770-J1L3N.summary: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust uses identifiable cancer registration, hospital admission, outpatient, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for patients in its MesobanK study. The data is used to add clinical details to tissue, fluid and blood samples, so researchers can pick suitable samples for asbestos-related disease research. The aim is better understanding, diagnosis and treatment of mesothelioma. So far, MesobanK has supplied samples to over 83 research projects.

DARS-NIC-656771-F4K5X.summary: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust holds cancer registration data from the National Disease Registration Service (NDRS), originally supplied by Public Health England. The data supports a study of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in people aged 15 to 25, looking at how common it is, how it is treated and what outcomes follow. The agreement only allows the data to be kept securely. The study aims to identify the most effective treatments for each subtype and help more young people be cured.

DARS-NIC-656773-F5L2T.summary: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is using data on breast cancers diagnosed between routine NHS breast screening appointments, known as interval cancers. The Centre for Cancer Prevention is carrying out an independent audit for the cancer screening programmes, reporting interval cancer rates for each screening service and supporting discussions with services. The stated benefit is better information on how well the programme performs, to support quality analysis and planning.
