DARS-NIC-695075-J7Y2H.summary: The University of Manchester, working with the University of York, is using pseudonymised hospital admission, emergency care and civil registration of death data from April 2013 onwards. The research compares the quality and safety of care in NHS and independent hospitals and looks at how clinical governance works across both. The main intended benefit is better evidence for policy-makers, clinicians and patients choosing where to receive care.

DARS-NIC-696708-J3L1R.summary: King's College London, with Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, is using civil registration death data (date and cause of death) for people in the South London Stroke Register. They will link it with existing register data to study the long-term outcomes, needs and care costs of stroke survivors. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers and services plan future stroke care.

DARS-NIC-69707-G0Q7Z.summary: RM Partners, an independent sector healthcare provider running a cancer alliance in West London, uses Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital, outpatient, critical care and A&E activity. It uses them to produce comparative performance reports on cancer services, to find areas needing improvement and variation between providers. The aim is better cancer care and less variation. Reported results include redesigned prostate, colorectal and lung pathways and published two-week-wait volumes.

DARS-NIC-69751-C0M8P.summary: Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and death registration data for patients admitted to or discharged from Arnold Lodge Medium Secure Unit in Leicester. The research looks at deaths and readmissions to psychiatric care among these patients, extending an earlier study to cover admissions up to June 2013 and a longer follow-up. The aim is to improve understanding of outcomes after medium secure care, so that services can plan support for people who may be particularly vulnerable.

DARS-NIC-698157-B0L5B.summary: Certara UK, a commercial company, is using National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data (the NDRS Cancer Consolidated Data Set). It is assessing whether the data is good enough to support research into CAR-T cell therapy, a treatment for blood cancers, by checking its quality, completeness and reliability. The main intended benefit is more efficient, robust research that helps inform regulators, clinicians and patients about the safety and effectiveness of these therapies.

DARS-NIC-698171-K4M0B.summary: The Home Office, a ministerial department, is using aggregated hospital admission counts from Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care. These cover people admitted to hospital in England because of drug misuse or poisoning, the mental and behavioural effects of drugs or alcohol, or assault by a firearm or sharp object. It uses them to monitor drug use, drug-related harm and serious violence, and to assess policies such as the County Lines Programme and Project ADDER. The main intended benefit is better drug policy and fewer drug-related harms.

DARS-NIC-699963-K1C6T.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable details of adult women in England, taken from the Personal Demographics Service, to invite people to join the PROTECT-C study. The study will test women for inherited cancer-risk genes and assess personalised breast and ovarian cancer risk. The main intended benefit is to give evidence on whether population-wide genetic testing could help prevent cancers.

DARS-NIC-700125-B2Z7J.summary: Young Epilepsy, a charity, is using identifiable demographics data about 112 children who took part in the EPIPEG study. It will find their up-to-date addresses and check whether any have died. This lets it send invitations to the Turning6 follow-up study at 60 months to parents and carers, and avoid contacting families whose child has died. The aim is to reach enough participants for the study to produce meaningful results.

DARS-NIC-700547-S2M9L.summary: Corevitas, a consultancy, is using national cancer registration, treatment, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hospital records for people in England with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. It is studying how the disease progresses from early to metastatic stages, which treatments people receive, whether age, ethnicity or deprivation affect access, and how often CDK4/6 inhibitor doses are reduced. The study also looks at hospital resource use. The main intended benefit is better-informed treatment decisions for patients.

DARS-NIC-701654-Q5Z9T.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using linked national cancer registration, hospital admission, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data. It is studying patients who received four chemotherapies that have left the Cancer Drug Fund. The work compares their real-world outcomes with clinical trial results, to test whether routine NHS data can support future National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance. The main intended benefit is to inform national guidance updates for these treatments.

DARS-NIC-701727-S2X0Q.summary: Bristol NHS Foundation Trust, working with the University of Bristol and Change Grow Live, is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for adults prescribed methadone or buprenorphine for opioid dependence. They are studying how the suspension of supervised opioid treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic relates to overdoses, drug-related deaths and how long people stay in treatment. The findings are intended to inform future practice and policy on supervising this treatment.

DARS-NIC-70235-T6P9F.summary: The Met Office uses NHS England hospital data, covering admitted patient care, accident and emergency and emergency care records, for its Health Programme. It uses the data to develop and evaluate health forecasting services and to research how weather, climate and air quality affect health and hospital use. The aim is to help warn people of environmental hazards and help plan health services. Published research papers and heatwave and cold weather planning have already drawn on this work.

DARS-NIC-705741-K8K9G.summary: The Office for National Statistics uses demographic data from NHS England in the ONS Longitudinal Study, which links census and life events records for about 1% of the population of England and Wales. It maintains a pseudonymised research database that approved researchers can use under strict controls. This supports research on topics such as health inequalities and ageing. The study has already supplied evidence for government reports on health inequalities and for National Statistics on life expectancy.

DARS-NIC-705821-P6J0H.summary: ModernaTX, Inc, a pharmaceutical and biotechnology company, is using contact details and basic health information from people who signed up to the NHS England COVID-19 Vaccine Research Registry. NHS England uses this information to invite potentially eligible people to take part in the NextCOVE trial of a COVID-19 booster vaccine. The main intended benefit is faster recruitment, which should speed up the development of effective vaccines.

DARS-NIC-705902-L2J0F.summary: King's College London, an academic institution, is using hospital admissions, accident and emergency, death registration and community prescribing data. It is using them to estimate how many children and young people up to age 25 in England live with a life-limiting condition, and how complex their conditions are, including their use of medicines. The main intended benefit is better planning and funding of children's palliative care and hospice services.

DARS-NIC-706399-T8V0C.summary: The University of Warwick, an academic organisation, is using Civil Registrations of Death data for the ADAPT-Sepsis Trial. The trial tests whether daily blood tests for the biomarkers CRP or PCT can safely shorten antibiotic treatment in hospitalised adults with suspected sepsis. The main intended benefit is reducing antibiotic exposure while keeping patients safe, which could change NHS care and guidance.

DARS-NIC-706484-D0Y6F.summary: The University of Leeds, an academic organisation, is using identifiable hospital records (admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients) and death registration data for people who took part in a stroke trial. It is using them to cost participants' hospital care and to compare this with what participants report themselves. The main intended benefit is to show whether routine data can replace self-reported data in future stroke studies, reducing the data collection burden on patients.

DARS-NIC-706945-F6W2C.summary: York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised hospital admission records and death registration data for about 98,000 people in England with hereditary haemochromatosis, an inherited iron disorder. It will study how many develop cirrhosis (liver scarring) and its complications, and the risk factors involved. The aim is to help services and clinicians review care for these patients.

DARS-NIC-707577-H0F4Z.summary: The University of Leeds is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, death registration and dispensed-medicine data for patients in the ALABAMA trial of penicillin allergy testing in primary care. It will compare patients who had testing with those who had usual care, looking at hospital stays, deaths, antibiotic use and costs. The main intended benefit is more selective use of second-line antibiotics, which would help limit antibiotic resistance.

DARS-NIC-707682-B4H2R.summary: The University of York is using pseudonymised hospital admission, accident and emergency, emergency care and death registration records for children who died aged 18 or under. It is studying differences in emergency hospital care in the last 12 months of life and in place of death, including how these relate to 24/7 paediatric palliative care services. The findings are intended to inform the development of such a service in the Yorkshire region.

DARS-NIC-708052-S1L9J.summary: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, working with King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, is using demographic data on adults with chronic liver disease admitted to hospital as an emergency. It is used to link patients to intensive care records held by ICNARC (Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre). The aim is to study critical care use and regional variation in care, so that services for acutely ill liver patients can be made safer and more effective. A related project's method for identifying first emergency admissions has been published in JHEP Reports.

DARS-NIC-708642-D2Z8T.summary: The University of Hull is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) from NHS hospitals in England. It will study how alcohol care teams affect hospital activity, including 30-day readmissions after alcohol-related admissions, and the costs involved, by comparing the 24 months before and after teams were optimised. The findings are intended to inform how NHS England and other bodies commission these services.

DARS-NIC-709342-K9Z8V.summary: Queen Mary University of London, working with University College London, is using pseudonymised national cancer registry data (the NDRS Cancer Consolidated Data Set) on men diagnosed with prostate cancer in England between 2013 and 2022. They are studying whether survival and treatment patterns, including first treatments and treatment intensification for metastatic disease, differ by ethnic group. The intended benefit is to help identify inequalities and guide interventions that improve treatment uptake and patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-709746-N2T6T.summary: Cardiff University is using hospital, emergency care, outpatient, community and maternity records to follow up women giving birth in 36 UK NHS maternity units taking part in a national trial. The study tests whether a set of bleeding-management steps for childbirth, called the Obstetric Bleeding Strategy, reduces blood transfusions and is good value, compared with standard care. It also looks at women's psychological wellbeing. The main intended benefit is better care for women who bleed heavily after birth.

DARS-NIC-709865-W9X6H.summary: The Royal College of Surgeons of England is using pseudonymised patient data, including cancer registrations, hospital records, treatment, imaging, emergency care and medicines data, for the National Cancer Audit Collaborating Centre (NATCAN). The data supports ten national audits of cancer care delivered by NHS providers, so services can benchmark performance and identify unwarranted variation. The main intended benefit is better care quality, outcomes and equity of care.

DARS-NIC-712819-X8G2J.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admissions, accident and emergency, and maternity services data. It is studying how changes in the way maternity care is delivered, such as continuity of care, visit and scan frequency, and staffing, affect care pathways and health outcomes. The aim is to inform NHS policy and reduce health inequalities in maternity care. So far, the team has built preliminary models that have let them check some of their main hypotheses.

DARS-NIC-714765-G1P5S.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration data from 2016/17 to 2023/24. It is studying whether waiting times in emergency departments differ by socioeconomic status, and whether longer waits lead to worse health outcomes. The aim is to give evidence that helps reduce any inequalities in waiting times. Preliminary results have been presented to the Department of Health and Social Care and NHS England.

DARS-NIC-715080-X0J9J.summary: The University of Manchester is using pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital admission, outpatient, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy data for patients in England. It is studying how socio-economic status and other health conditions affect cancer patients' treatment and outcomes, and mapping the cause-and-effect relationships between them. The main intended benefit is evidence to reduce health inequalities and improve the fairness and quality of cancer care across the NHS.

DARS-NIC-715599-M3G8T.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital admissions, outpatient and national cancer registration data for a PhD research project on people with cystic fibrosis (CF). It aims to measure cancer risk and outcomes in this group and identify who is at higher risk. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform screening, surveillance and educational resources for people with CF.

DARS-NIC-71603-T8C0Q.summary: The London Borough of Islington, a local authority, is using pseudonymised hospital data, covering admissions, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (A&E) attendances. It uses this data for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the annual public health report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. Since May 2023 it has used the data for work on hypertension, alcohol licensing, a London-wide chemsex needs assessment and a review of the local Healthy Start programme.

DARS-NIC-717299-R5H5N.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable NHS England data on hospital admissions, deaths and demographics for children with six surgical conditions. It will use the data to identify and invite eligible children's parents to join the Children's Surgery Outcome Reporting research database, and to check that all eligible cases are captured. The main intended benefit is spotting unwarranted variation between hospitals, so that feedback to hospitals can help improve children's care.

DARS-NIC-717428-M3S8H.summary: The University of Birmingham is using NHS England's emergency care hospital data, covering attendances at type 1 emergency departments from 2018 to 2023. The research applies process mining to map how patients move through emergency departments and compares these patient flows, waiting times, admissions and outcomes across NHS trusts. The aim is to help trusts and policy makers redesign emergency care services and use resources more efficiently.

DARS-NIC-717485-F8L6H.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research organisation working for Sanofi Pasteur, is using NHS England data on hospital admissions, COVID-19 tests and vaccinations, GP records and deaths. It is studying how well the VidPrevtyn Beta® COVID-19 booster protects against hospitalisation with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared with people not boosted in the same period. The main intended benefit is real-world evidence for regulators such as the MHRA and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) to inform future booster campaigns.

DARS-NIC-717493-V2R4K.summary: The National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research is using identifiable civil registration death and demographic data to link with national heart audit and TAVI registry records for Welsh patients. The aim is to report patient outcomes and compare the quality of cardiac care between hospitals, so that care can improve. Reported benefits include annual patient reports, risk models for heart failure and heart attack audits, and findings on how COVID-19 affected cardiac services.

DARS-NIC-717832-F6F3H.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, cancer, death, diabetes audit, imaging and dispensed medicines records for people who joined the ASCEND PLUS clinical trial. The records will be used to follow participants' health, including heart attacks, strokes, kidney decline, dementia and deaths. This will show whether long-term use of oral semaglutide is effective and safe for people aged 55 or over with type 2 diabetes. The results could inform national and international treatment guidelines.

DARS-NIC-719601-J7Z2S.summary: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is using pseudonymised patient data from national heart audits, linked to hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records. It is studying how much diabetes affects survival, stent re-narrowing and repeat heart attacks in people with heart disease, using machine learning. The main intended benefit is finding new links between diabetes and heart disease, to help identify higher-risk groups and target preventative treatment.

DARS-NIC-719879-K6X3J.summary: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust is using pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service cancer registration data on patients diagnosed with upper gastrointestinal cancer after an earlier endoscopy. It is studying why some of these cancers are missed at endoscopy, to help endoscopy units improve quality and reduce missed diagnoses. The study has identified the main reasons cancers are missed and the procedural risk factors involved, and reported these to endoscopy providers.

DARS-NIC-719923-Q5H1S.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using linked hospital, emergency care, cancer registration, death registration and demographic records for participants in the LOLIPOP study of UK South Asians. It is studying how genetic, lifestyle and environmental factors relate to heart disease, type-2 diabetes, cancer and other chronic conditions. The aim is to inform prevention and health policy for this group. The study's resource has already supported over 225 peer-reviewed publications.

DARS-NIC-720122-Y6Q0Y.summary: The University of Essex is using hospital admission, outpatient and death registration records for people in England who have had a stroke. The research, part of a PhD, looks at how factors such as age, gender, ethnicity, deprivation and coastal or urban location combine to affect deaths within 30 days and one year of a stroke, and the care pathways patients follow. It aims to give policymakers evidence to make stroke care more inclusive and improve outcomes.

DARS-NIC-72064-V5V2X.summary: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using linked national hospital, cancer and death records for people in England with liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma) and those who went on to have a liver transplant. The study looks at risk factors, treatment choices and survival after transplant, including the use of donor livers after circulatory death, to help improve patient selection and donor liver allocation. Five papers were published in 2019 and 2020, and the study reports that these donor livers did not worsen survival.

DARS-NIC-721538-N6B1V.summary: King's College London, which runs the Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme (SSNAP), is using identifiable civil registration death records linked to data on about 300,000 hospital-admitted stroke patients. The aim is to report 30-day and longer-term survival rates for hospitals and health boards so services can improve stroke care. Outlier trusts have been contacted and offered peer review visits, and a 2018 Lancet paper on socioeconomic disparities has been published.

DARS-NIC-72180-R2L5Y.summary: The University of Glasgow is using NHS England hospital admission records and mortality and cohort notification data for the FAST trial, which compared the heart safety of two gout medicines, febuxostat and allopurinol. The data was used to find serious adverse events and study endpoints that had not been reported. The main intended benefit is clearer safety information for patients, prescribers and regulators. The main results have been published in The Lancet and a final report has been submitted to the European Medicines Agency.

DARS-NIC-724508-B4V3Q.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using hospital, outpatient, mental health and death registration records for about 10,000 consenting participants in the PREDICT-PD study. The records will be linked to the study participants to follow up who goes on to develop Parkinson's disease, related neurodegenerative conditions or who dies, because following participants directly has become impractical. The aim is to refine predictive algorithms so people at risk of Parkinson's can be identified earlier.

DARS-NIC-726177-R0H8V.summary: The University of Newcastle upon Tyne is using hospital admitted patient, outpatient and national cancer registry data to study head and neck cancer. It is examining how diagnosis, treatment and survival differ by area deprivation and region of England, including before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim is to inform policy and services that reduce inequalities. So far, the work has led to new research collaborations and the basis of a further funding proposal.

DARS-NIC-72626-V4P9B.summary: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust is using hospital, cancer registration, diagnostic imaging, death and demographic records for about 4,264 people with hepatitis C-related liver cirrhosis in a UK research cohort. The data are used to study which patients go on to serious liver complications, including liver cancer, and how outcomes change after a hepatitis C cure. The aim is to help clinicians tailor monitoring and care to individual risk. Published analyses include studies on liver cancer risk, mortality after cure, and uptake of liver cancer surveillance.

DARS-NIC-726391-M6D4Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using civil registration death records, linked to archived health records of about 3,000 veterans treated for head injuries at a Second World War military hospital in Oxford. The study will update the group's mortality information by 21 years. It aims to show the long-term effects of penetrating brain injuries on life expectancy and health. The main intended benefit is evidence on lifelong outcomes, to help shape traumatic brain injury management guidelines.

DARS-NIC-726539-S6T2F.summary: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admission and death registration data for a consented group of 10,007 patients who had heart scans (cardiac magnetic resonance, or CMR) at Wythenshawe Hospital. It will study how CMR findings relate to survival, hospital admission and heart conditions such as heart failure and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The main intended benefit is earlier detection and better risk prediction for heart failure.

DARS-NIC-727325-W4M7T.summary: NHS England and King's College London are jointly using national cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy and chemotherapy data for the PRECISION study. They are examining the risk of breast cancer developing in the opposite breast after ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), a non-invasive breast cancer, compared with invasive breast cancer, and which factors predict it. The intended benefit is to identify patients at higher risk, so that treatment can be tailored and overtreatment avoided.

DARS-NIC-727343-L3N2H.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London is using pseudonymised civil registration death records for adults admitted to Welsh hospitals with asthma attacks. These will be linked to audit data to show whether hospital care led to good or poor outcomes, using deaths within 30 and 90 days. The aim is to improve care standards and reduce readmissions and deaths. A 2023 outcomes report has already informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-727507-W9V7H.summary: Queen Mary University of London (an academic institution) is using pseudonymised hospital admission and civil death registration data for people in the British Spine Registry, plus a comparison group who had routine spinal operations. It will check the accuracy of the Registry and assess outcomes of common spinal operations for low back pain, including the effect of patient and surgical factors. The aim is to help clinicians and patients understand the risks and benefits of each procedure.

DARS-NIC-727537-C3V4G.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London is using pseudonymised civil registration death records for adults in the Welsh COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) hospital audit. It will link them to audit data to measure deaths within 30 and 90 days of admission, to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes. The aim is better COPD care and lower mortality. Outcome reports published so far have been used by services to benchmark performance and plan improvements.

DARS-NIC-727610-S2V3N.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data, covering hospital admissions in England from 1997/98 onwards. Researchers are studying how different ways of paying hospitals affect their efficiency, costs and quality of care, and why providers respond differently. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policymakers design payment models that lead to shorter waiting times and better care.

DARS-NIC-727732-M8C2N.summary: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised national cancer registration data on melanoma in situ in England, covering 2013 to 2023. It is studying how often lentigo maligna occurs, how long patients survive, and how likely it is to progress to melanoma. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better-informed decisions about managing the condition.

DARS-NIC-727954-G5X8B.summary: The Royal College of Physicians of London is using pseudonymised civil registration death records for children and young people admitted to hospital with asthma attacks in England and Wales. The records will be linked to audit data to measure deaths within 30 and 90 days and readmissions. The aim is to show whether hospital care led to good outcomes and to improve care. Outcomes published in 2023 for earlier patients informed recommendations on how services are resourced.

DARS-NIC-729128-M5N1F.summary: King's College London is using identifiable demographic data about people recruited to the South London Stroke Register, a long-running study of stroke in a defined area of London. The data will confirm which participants have died and give current addresses for those still alive, so a newsletter can update them about the study and how to opt out. The intended benefit is to maintain contact with survivors while avoiding distress to families of those who have died.

DARS-NIC-729560-F2F3S.summary: King's College London is using identifiable demographic data from the NHS Population Demographics Service, covering twins born in England and Wales in 1994 to 1996 who take part in the Twins' Early Development Study. It will use current contact details to send information about linking their medical records to the study. The aim is to make the study's health findings more representative, including of people who have lost touch with it. Addresses from an earlier agreement let over 11,000 participants be included in this information campaign.

DARS-NIC-730384-H8G0Q.summary: The University of Birmingham is using NHS England data quality report records, which hold customer contact and mortality details, for the PRISM follow-up research study. It will check whether women who took part in the PRISM trial of progesterone in early pregnancy, and their children, are still alive and confirm their postal addresses. This lets the study team send consent packages for long-term follow-up without contacting families in upsetting circumstances.

DARS-NIC-730458-M8D6M.summary: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for people in England who survived a cardiac arrest and then had a defibrillator implanted. It will estimate how common idiopathic ventricular fibrillation, a rare heart rhythm condition with no identified cause, is in England. The main intended benefit is to guide resources towards diagnosing and managing the condition, and to support further research.

DARS-NIC-732228-T8Q0V.summary: Leeds Institute of Health Sciences, part of the University of Leeds, is using NHS England death registration and cancer registration data on 9,046 people who agreed to take part in the Yorkshire Lung Screening Trial. The trial tests whether inviting smokers and ex-smokers aged 55 to 80 to community-based low dose CT lung screening, compared with usual care, improves lung cancer outcomes. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide the design of lung cancer screening programmes in the UK.

DARS-NIC-733055-Y4J1B.summary: The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) is using pseudonymised heart attack audit data (the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project) and civil registrations of death for adults admitted to hospitals in England and Wales between April 2010 and March 2023. It is evaluating how hospital factors, including mergers, affect quality and safety of care, and whether treatment and care quality differ between patient groups. The aim is to inform policy and treatment decisions and improve outcomes after a heart attack.

DARS-NIC-733084-C6R1J.summary: The University of Warwick is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for 5,945 patients who survived to hospital admission after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in the PARAMEDIC-3 trial. It will use them to compare survival, hospital and intensive care use, and NHS costs between two ways of giving adrenaline: into a vein or into a bone. The intended benefit is evidence that could shape national and international resuscitation guidelines.

DARS-NIC-733503-V0X9Q.summary: Genomics England, a research organisation, receives linked NHS hospital, emergency care, diagnostic imaging, community, maternity and death records for babies in the Generation Study. It uses them in its National Genomics Research Library to evaluate whole genome sequencing of newborns, looking at cost effectiveness, health outcomes and the impact on the NHS. The aim is to find out whether babies with treatable rare genetic conditions can be diagnosed and treated earlier.

DARS-NIC-734202-N9F7P.summary: Cardiff University, with Velindre University NHS Trust, is using identifiable Civil Registrations of Death data (date of death only) for about 900 consenting participants in the PATHOS clinical trial of reduced-intensity treatment for HPV-positive throat cancer. The data will be used to check that NHS sites have reported all deaths, and reported them correctly. The intended benefit is accurate survival data, so the trial can answer its research question reliably.

DARS-NIC-734273-H8R3Q.summary: The Institute of Occupational Medicine, a research organisation, is using identifiable death registration and demographic records for a group of about 15,000 to 22,000 former professional footballers. It is studying whether heading footballs during a playing career is linked to a higher risk of dying from neurological diseases, and how their mortality compares with the general population. The findings are intended to inform policy to protect players' health and could lead to a review of heading in football.

DARS-NIC-73469-F3B9N.summary: The University of Manchester is using aggregated hospital admissions data from Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care, with no identifying details. It is studying whether general practice performance under the Quality and Outcomes Framework, a pay-for-performance scheme, relates to hospital admissions across England between 2006 and 2019. The main intended benefit is evidence for the NHS and policy makers on whether the scheme works and how resources can best be used.

DARS-NIC-734773-Y3P3J.summary: University College London is using identifiable NHS England records on deaths registered in England between 2021 and 2023, together with hospital admitted patient care and critical care records. It is using them to measure how many deaths were linked to antimicrobial resistance (when infections no longer respond to antibiotics) and how this changed over time. The study also aims to set up a way for public health authorities to calculate these deaths from routine data. The main expected benefit is better evidence for managing drug-resistant infections.

DARS-NIC-736273-V5T6V.summary: Adelphi Group Limited, a consultancy working for Pfizer Limited, is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records. It is studying how often hospitalised children in England (aged 0-17) are admitted with invasive fungal infections, how much hospital care they use and how many die, comparing those with and without a past infection-related admission. The aim is to improve understanding of the risks and the need for better prevention and treatment.

DARS-NIC-736310-S6T1Z.summary: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority is using hospital, emergency care, death registration, demographic and primary care medicines data to look for fraud and other crime in the NHS. It runs exploratory analyses to find cases for criminal investigation and to spot system weaknesses that policy changes could fix. Its analysis has already led to a payment tariff change, with £28m of savings recognised by the Public Sector Fraud Authority Prevention Panel.

DARS-NIC-73678-Y1T0Y.summary: The London Borough of Redbridge, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to study local differences in emergency admissions, especially cardiovascular ones, and their links to NHS Health Check outcomes. It will use the results in its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to identify and address health inequalities in the local population. It reports using the data to support a combined needs assessment with the local integrated care board and to inform local programmes, such as the suicide equity audit and children's health work.

DARS-NIC-736873-X9F8V.summary: Imperial College London's Dr Foster Unit is using pseudonymised civil registration death records, linked to the National Hip Fracture Database, for about 8,000 to 10,000 adults with a fracture around a hip or knee replacement. It will study death rates, time to death and causes of death by hospital and by treatment. The aim is to inform NICE guidelines and quality improvement, so that treatment is more consistent and outcomes improve.

DARS-NIC-737073-H1C6D.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using national NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hospital records for women diagnosed with breast cancer in England. It is studying whether different radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hormonal treatments are linked to later health problems, such as second cancers and cardiovascular disease. The aim is to inform treatment decisions and follow-up care for breast cancer survivors.

DARS-NIC-737123-P6P6G.summary: The University of Oxford is using linked NHS hospital, cancer, medicines, imaging, vaccination and death records for the MyMelanoma study, which follows at least 20,000 consenting melanoma patients across the UK. The data will build a research resource to study what causes melanoma and how patients respond to treatment. The main intended benefit is better prevention, diagnosis and treatment of melanoma.

DARS-NIC-737139-W2B7S.summary: Cardiff University is using hospital, outpatient, critical care and emergency care records from NHS England. They are for a randomised trial (TIPTOE) of a personalised self-management support programme for adults with knee or hip osteoarthritis and other long-term conditions. The records will help measure the programme's effect on use of healthcare services and its cost-effectiveness. The aim is to inform how osteoarthritis care is delivered in the NHS.

DARS-NIC-737333-K2F1T.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care and primary care prescription records for 1,964 primary school children in London and Luton. It is studying whether London's Ultra Low Emission Zone improves children's respiratory health, and it will also assess healthcare costs and value for money. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform government, NHS and city planning decisions on clean air zones and children's health.

DARS-NIC-739358-R1C7S.summary: The University of Leeds is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, mental health, death registration and dispensed medicines data for a randomised trial called FReSH START. The trial compares a psychological therapy for people who repeatedly self-harm with standard care. The data will help measure repeated self-harm, safety and cost-effectiveness. The aim is to provide evidence that could inform NICE guidelines. So far, the data has been used for safety monitoring of trial participants.

DARS-NIC-739463-H4P9N.summary: NatCen Social Research, with University College London, the Institute for Fiscal Studies and the universities of Manchester and East Anglia, uses hospital records (admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and emergency care) linked to the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. They study ageing, health and hospital use, including dementia and social care, to inform health and care planning. Linked data analyses have already featured in the Chief Medical Officer's 2023 annual report and in a Centre for Ageing Better report.

DARS-NIC-739472-P2Y8X.summary: The University of Hull is using pseudonymised hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for about 8,000 women aged 50 to 70 in Hull and the East Riding of Yorkshire. It supports a feasibility trial of free door-to-door transport to breast screening appointments, checking whether this could raise attendance and whether a larger trial is workable. The intended benefit is better access to screening, which could lead to earlier diagnosis of breast cancer.

DARS-NIC-73974-P0L1Z.summary: The University of York, with the University of Liverpool and University College London, is using hospital records (accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients) and date of death data for babies in the PREVAIL trial. The data will help compare two types of central venous catheter, one coated with antimicrobial and antifungal agents and one standard, in very preterm babies, looking at death risk and hospital care costs. The main intended benefit is evidence to help hospitals decide which catheter to buy.

DARS-NIC-739822-Q8R6Y.summary: The University of Manchester is keeping pseudonymised NHS Talking Therapies (formerly Improving Access to Psychological Therapies) patient data from 2020/21 to 2022/23. The completed study examined how provider waiting times affect patients' employment-related outcomes. The data is held securely so the analysis can be repeated if the findings are challenged. The research aims to help improve how Talking Therapies services manage waiting lists and meet patients' needs.

DARS-NIC-740323-Y4T3F.summary: The University of Leeds is using identifiable NHS hospital, emergency care, outpatient, dispensed medicines and death registration data for the PROSPER Trial. The trial tests whether personalised care planning for older people with frailty, compared with usual care alone, reduces hospital use and is cost-effective. The expected benefit is robust evidence on its clinical and cost-effectiveness.

DARS-NIC-740806-W2F6Q.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, cancer pathway and somatic molecular testing data on adults diagnosed with primary lung cancer in England between 2015 and 2022. The data supports a PhD project that describes lung cancer in never-smokers and how factors such as age, gender and ethnicity relate to diagnosis, stage and survival. The aim is to improve understanding and support earlier detection. So far, the team has reported its public engagement work to the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in an annual report.

DARS-NIC-74145-R8B9T.summary: London Borough of Southwark uses civil registration data on births and deaths, including identifiable records, plus primary care mortality data. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services, run suicide audits and protect public health. The aim is to tailor local services and reduce premature deaths and health inequalities. So far, birth data has supported needs analysis and briefings for the Maternity Commission and Children's Services, and mortality data has been used to calculate local life expectancy.

DARS-NIC-741610-V3R1Z.summary: London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to assess local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, protect public health and carry out suicide audits. Results are published as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is local health and care services that are better tailored and targeted to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-742629-H5M4F.summary: London Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using identifiable ambulance records linked to Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS) hospital records. It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, including how resources are allocated and how clinicians' care relates to patient outcomes. The main intended benefit is better care for patients, through targeted clinician training and by helping patients reach the right care pathway.

DARS-NIC-742898-S7N0V.summary: NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is using hospital admission records, death registrations and cancer data on people in England with liver disease, as part of a UCL PhD project. It will examine whether a patient's age, sex, ethnicity, social background and cause of liver disease affect their access to liver transplantation, organ offers and outcomes. The main intended benefit is evidence to help make liver transplant access fairer.

DARS-NIC-742907-Z5F3Y.summary: The University of Southampton, working with University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, is using identifiable civil registration of death records (dates and causes of death) for people taking part in the BRITISH clinical trial. They are using it to test whether implantable cardioverter defibrillators reduce deaths in patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, heart muscle disease not caused by blocked arteries, and scarring on heart scans. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide national guidelines and treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-743125-M0K1Y.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists is using NHS England hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil death registration data. They support the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit's work on patients who need emergency abdominal surgery but do not have it (the "NoLap" group). The aim is to understand these patients' care and outcomes, and to reduce variation in care between hospitals. The overall goal is better care and shared decision-making for this group.

DARS-NIC-743571-K7X4R.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable demographic data from NHS England to find and contact adults in England who have a record of melanoma. The aim is to invite them to join the MyMelanoma study, which is building a large melanoma data resource so researchers can answer questions about risk, treatment and quality of life. Reported so far: about 150,000 invitations sent and about 15,400 participants recruited.

DARS-NIC-743681-L8G9L.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable demographic data from NHS England, covering up to 1,133 people who joined the EMPA-KIDNEY trial in England and Wales. The data will be used to identify participant deaths not already reported, as part of a two-year follow-up of a trial testing empagliflozin in people with chronic kidney disease. The main intended benefit is to show whether the drug's benefits last over the longer term, and to improve the accuracy of the trial data.

DARS-NIC-743987-M7B3P.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) is using pseudonymised Breast and Cosmetic Implant Registry data on people who had breast implants in England between 2019 and 2023. It is testing whether this data can support its monitoring of breast implant safety, including implants of different textures. The main intended benefit is to help MHRA decide whether the registry can be used in routine vigilance, and to improve how it identifies possible links between implants and systemic symptoms.

DARS-NIC-744761-P7S8L.summary: South East Coast Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision and comparing treatment patterns across clinicians and patient groups. The aim is to improve patient care, target training and identify gaps in local services. Results will be internal dashboards of aggregated figures.

DARS-NIC-744993-Z8K2K.summary: Methods Business and Digital Technology Limited, an IT supplier, is using pseudonymised national cancer data covering breast cancer patients in England from 2016 onwards. It is studying how treatment for triple negative breast cancer, including chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy, varies with ethnicity and deprivation. The study aims to improve understanding of the disease and the care patients receive.

DARS-NIC-745735-D8M0S.summary: Lancaster University is using pseudonymised NDRS Cancer Registrations data, which records cancer cases, from 2021 onwards. It will compare cancer incidence, prevalence and mortality across the North West and the rest of England, and look at links with demographic, socioeconomic and environmental factors. The aim is to show where cancer inequalities are greatest, so that North West Cancer Research can target its strategy and funding.

DARS-NIC-74625-S1Q8X.summary: Cardiff University, an academic organisation, is using hospital records for accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatients. These are linked to data on acutely ill children under five seen in general practice. The project, CLASSIC, aims to check an existing clinical tool and develop a new one to help GPs identify serious infections in children that lead to hospital admission. Earlier work from the LUCI study has already produced three published papers, which found that the tools tested were not accurate enough in general practice.

DARS-NIC-746266-S8M6T.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable hospital admission and emergency care records for about 3,500 consenting mothers and children in the Baby Biome Study. It is investigating whether air pollution exposure during pregnancy affects pregnancy, birth and child health outcomes, including respiratory infections. The findings are expected to inform policy on regulating air pollution and advice to pregnant women on reducing their exposure.

DARS-NIC-746522-Y4R7L.summary: The University of Glasgow is using identifiable NHS England hospital admission, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for 139 people in England who joined a registry of microvascular angina, a heart condition affecting the small blood vessels. The aim is to follow their long-term health outcomes and healthcare use, to understand how the condition develops and whether the trial drug zibotentan relates to later outcomes. The findings are expected to inform treatment guidelines and future medicine research.

DARS-NIC-747046-T7C5C.summary: Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust is using cancer registry data and mental health services data for Imperial College London's Indigo trial, which studies people living with and beyond cancer. The trial tests whether patient-reported questionnaires completed online can be linked to national records. The main intended benefit is a practical evidence base on collecting patient-reported outcomes in the community, so care can better reflect long-term unmet needs.

DARS-NIC-747507-C5G6T.summary: The University of Oxford, working with the University of Leicester, is using hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient and death registration records for 1,522 babies in the SurfON trial. The trial compares early surfactant treatment with expectant management in late preterm and early term babies with respiratory distress. The records will help estimate NHS costs and one-year survival. The aim is to inform treatment decisions and reduce intensive care needs and hospital stays.

DARS-NIC-747531-J2Q0W.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using NHS hospital admission, critical care, outpatient and emergency care records, along with death registrations, for a clinical trial called CHIP-BCIS3. The trial tests whether a device that unloads the heart's left ventricle during high-risk coronary stent procedures gives better patient outcomes, quality of life and cost-effectiveness than standard care. The main intended benefit is clearer evidence so patients, clinicians and commissioners can decide whether the technology should be used.

DARS-NIC-748004-M6G9X.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research company working for Takeda Development Centre Americas, Inc., is using pseudonymised cancer registry, hospital, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and molecular test data on adults with advanced non-small cell lung cancer in England. It is studying who these patients are, the sequences of treatments they receive, and how long they survive and go before their next treatment. The aim is to give evidence that helps refine treatment strategies and healthcare planning.

DARS-NIC-748215-Z7K2V.summary: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is using pseudonymised data from the TAVI (transcatheter aortic valve implantation) registry, linked to civil registration death records, for around 43,000 patients treated in England and Wales between 2007 and 2023. It is evaluating whether right bundle branch block, a heart conduction problem, is linked to higher long-term mortality after TAVI, and whether a permanent pacemaker changes this. The findings are expected to inform whether pacemakers should be fitted beforehand.

DARS-NIC-748645-R5G3D.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using NHS England's Diabetes Prevention Programme data, along with hospital and emergency care records, to produce official statistics and statistical research. The statistics will look at how health affects labour market participation, and the reverse. The main expected benefit is better evidence for government departments, which could help improve the design of the programme and help patients back into work.

DARS-NIC-748653-S9J4H.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using NHS England waiting list data, along with hospital, emergency care and psychological therapy records, to produce official statistics. The first project looks at links between adverse health events, NHS waiting lists and employment. The aim is to give government departments better evidence on how health and work affect each other. A published analysis has already examined how waiting times relate to pay and employment after hospital treatment.

DARS-NIC-748729-Z8B3M.summary: The University of Bristol uses linked NHS health records, such as hospital, GP, cancer, mental health, maternity and COVID-19 data, for the UK Longitudinal Linkage Collaboration. It is a research database linking long-running population study participants' data, here relying on participant consent. Approved researchers use it for health research to inform policy and care. Its reported results include published papers on Long COVID and on work-related COVID-19 risk, which informed NICE guidance and Health and Safety Executive policy.

DARS-NIC-748984-C7G9X.summary: Slough Borough Council is using hospital activity data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set, covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and A&E). It uses the data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-749150-S0M7G.summary: Evidera Ltd, a research company working for Takeda Development Centre Americas, Inc., is using pseudonymised cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and molecular testing data. It is studying the characteristics, treatments and survival of adults with metastatic colorectal cancer who have had at least three lines of therapy. The main intended benefit is a better understanding of how these patients are treated and how they fare, to inform clinicians, policymakers and future research.

DARS-NIC-749612-D9M1V.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) on children in England. It is studying how the Soft Drinks Industry Levy affected inequalities in hospital extractions for tooth decay by area deprivation, ethnicity and urbanicity, and assessing its financial and health effects through an extended cost-effectiveness analysis. The findings are intended to inform policy decisions, including the government's obesity strategy and the continuation of the levy.

DARS-NIC-750163-K6F7T.summary: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable cancer registration data, limited to a study cohort, to calculate survival times for teenagers and young adults with cancer. The research compares outcomes for those whose care is wholly, partly or not at all in specialist teenage and young adult centres. It aims to inform NHS policy and service design so these services can improve outcomes for young people with cancer.

DARS-NIC-75079-V7Y7L.summary: Bangor University, an academic organisation, holds Hospital Episode Statistics data covering accident and emergency, admitted patient care and outpatient records. The agreement allows the data to be kept for archiving only, because it is source data for the SANAD-II epilepsy drug trial and analysis is complete. The trial's economic analysis compared the cost-effectiveness of antiepileptic drugs, to help NHS decision-makers choose the most clinically and cost-effective treatments.

DARS-NIC-75133-N8S0N.summary: City of Westminster, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to understand local health needs, plan services and protect public health, including suicide prevention work, with only aggregated figures published. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, reducing health inequalities and premature deaths. It has published annual public health reports and used deaths data to examine inequalities and life-expectancy gaps between boroughs' more and less affluent areas.

DARS-NIC-752432-W7V5T.summary: The University of Leicester is using pseudonymised National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registration data for adults diagnosed with selected cancers since 2000. Its research unit is studying trends in early diagnosis, stage-specific survival and inequalities between patient groups, and developing statistical methods and a monitoring toolkit for NHS England. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help improve early cancer diagnosis and outcomes for future patients.

DARS-NIC-752595-J7L6P.summary: The University of Birmingham is using civil registration of death data, covering the date and cause of death for consenting trial participants. It is for PETNECK 2, a trial comparing PET-CT-guided, patient-initiated follow-up with standard clinical follow-up for advanced head and neck cancer. The death data allows the trial to measure overall survival, its main outcome. The aim is to add evidence to help decide whether this follow-up approach is effective and cost-effective.

DARS-NIC-752925-P6Y2W.summary: The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RCOG) is using a bridging file of person identifiers to link maternity data from the National Maternity and Perinatal Audit with neonatal data from the National Neonatal Audit Programme. The linked data will show neonatal outcomes of maternity care that have not previously been reported, through a snapshot audit and updates to annual reports and a neonatal dashboard. The main expected benefit is better care and experience for women giving birth and for babies.

DARS-NIC-753305-S9Y1C.summary: Cardiff University, working with Velindre NHS Trust, is using civil registration death records for about 400 consenting participants in the SCOPE2 oesophageal cancer trial. The records are used to check and verify deaths so that survival results, the trial's main measures, are accurate. The trial compares a standard and a higher radiotherapy dose, and two chemotherapy combinations. The expected benefit is reliable evidence to inform treatment and NHS policy decisions.

DARS-NIC-753801-J5B3X.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using NHS England's identifiable demographic data, limited to men aged 55-79 and women aged 65-79, to produce mailing lists. These are used to invite people to join the Heartburn Health Programme and, through it, the BEST4 Screening Trial. The aim is to recruit enough participants to test whether a capsule sponge device can screen for Barrett's oesophagus, a precursor of food pipe cancer, and to build a resource for future research on heartburn.

DARS-NIC-754054-P3H3V.summary: King's College London is using civil registration death records for 282 people who joined the NalPORS study and were lost to follow-up after six months. The research checks whether these participants, who were current opioid users, died and whether an opioid overdose was the cause. It forms part of a study of take-home naloxone given to people who witness an overdose. The expected benefit is more knowledge on preventing accidental opioid overdoses.

DARS-NIC-754175-W2Z4T.summary: Imperial College London is using pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient and emergency care records for adults in England between April 2022 and March 2024. It is a PhD project, funded by the NIHR, studying how separating planned and emergency surgery, including through surgical hubs, affects health inequalities and access to planned surgery. It hopes to inform policymakers and guidance on how surgical hubs are used.

DARS-NIC-754519-V1T5M.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) is using NHS England death registration and hospital admission and outpatient records. They support the UK-ROX trial, which compares conservative and usual oxygen therapy in adults on mechanical ventilation in intensive care. The data provide outcomes such as 90-day mortality and length of hospital stay. The intended benefit is stronger evidence on the best amount of oxygen to give, to inform clinical guidelines and improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-75485-J3R9B.summary: The University of Warwick is using hospital admitted patient, critical care and outpatient records (Hospital Episode Statistics) for about 380 people in a trial of exercise after breast cancer surgery. The records will be linked to trial data to check the hospital use that participants reported themselves, supporting a cost-effectiveness comparison with usual care. The main intended benefit is to help NICE decide whether to recommend physiotherapy after breast cancer surgery.

DARS-NIC-755470-G7Y8N.summary: Westmorland and Furness Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand local health needs, plan services and support public health work such as suicide prevention audits. The main intended benefit is local services tailored to areas of greatest need, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-755472-Y7C7F.summary: The Care Quality Commission (CQC) is using pseudonymised NHS England data on community services, emergency care, hospital admissions, critical care, outpatients and mental health services. It uses the data in a pilot of NHS England's Unified Data Access Layer and in its regulation of health and care providers. This includes inspection planning, monitoring the Mental Health Act and national reports such as the State of Care. The intended benefit is better care, treatment and experience for people using health services.

DARS-NIC-755603-Q8Y4Y.summary: Keele University, an academic body, is using hospital, accident and emergency, outpatient and emergency care records for about 2,000 adults with musculoskeletal pain and about 2,500 adults aged 35 and over registered with participating GP practices in North Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent. It is using them to study musculoskeletal health, inequalities and healthcare use. The main intended benefit is a local system of musculoskeletal health intelligence to inform policymakers, practitioners and the public.

DARS-NIC-756432-F0B1L.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using national cancer registration, hospital, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and cancer waiting times data. It is comparing patients who joined its cancer trials with similar patients who did not, looking at their characteristics and overall survival. The aim is to find groups that may be systematically left out of trials. The main intended benefit is more inclusive future trials.

DARS-NIC-756799-M4K3V.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for 3,751 consented trial participants. It is used to check whether patients with chest pain were admitted to another acute hospital within 30 days, in a trial comparing a 1-hour and a 3-hour repeat blood test pathway for ruling out heart attack. The aim is to show whether the 1-hour pathway is safe and can allow faster discharge. The trial's main results have been published in a cardiology journal, and they led to a regional switch to the 1-hour pathway.

DARS-NIC-756900-Q2J3K.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records to evaluate the National Perioperative Screening and Optimisation Programme, which sets up teams to assess patients' health needs before and after surgery. The aim is to measure its effect on patient-centred outcomes, with the hope of showing whether it leads to fewer complications and better recovery. So far, UCL has built a baseline of days alive and out of hospital, readmissions and deaths for three types of surgery.

DARS-NIC-757611-Y2B1J.summary: The University of Sheffield, working with University College London, is using pseudonymised NHS data on talking therapy referrals, hospital and emergency care, mental health services, prescriptions and deaths. It is for two studies comparing how effective and cost-effective different talking and digital therapies are for anxiety and depression, including differences in outcomes between groups. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help match patients to suitable therapies.

DARS-NIC-757820-S7F8B.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) is using linked civil death registration records and hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care). It uses them mainly for its national audits of adult critical care and in-hospital cardiac arrest, and secondarily to support approved research. The main intended benefit is better quality, safety and equity of critical care and resuscitation, through audit reports that include longer-term patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-757823-Y6Q1H.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised national congenital heart disease audit records and civil registration death records for about 8,000 people who had a pulmonary valve replacement in England and Wales between 2003 and 2023. It will compare how often different valve types are used, how long they last before further intervention is needed, and survival. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether one valve type is better, to inform a future multi-centre clinical trial and reduce repeat operations.

DARS-NIC-758592-R3M5V.summary: The University of Nottingham, working with Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, uses identifiable hospital, emergency care, community service and mental health service records for children in the STADIA trial. It is using them to follow up 539 participants for at least 36 months and see whether a standardised diagnostic assessment at referral to children's mental health services (CAMHS) affects later referrals, self-harm presentations and hospital admissions. The intended benefit is better evidence on whether the tool helps identify and treat children's emotional difficulties.

DARS-NIC-758630-F8C7Y.summary: South Central Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set pilot and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, reviews of treatments and how resources are allocated. The main intended benefit is better patient care, with improved care pathways and less pressure on busy emergency departments. Results will be shared as aggregated dashboards.

DARS-NIC-759062-F2L6B.summary: NatCen Social Research, with University College London, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, the University of Manchester and the University of East Anglia, uses English Longitudinal Study of Ageing data linked to NHS cancer registration and death records. They use it to study ageing and health in England, including hospital use, social care, health inequalities and dementia, to inform health and care planning. Its findings have already featured in the Chief Medical Officer's 2023 annual report and in NIHR alerts.

DARS-NIC-759203-S1P1T.summary: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records, death registration records and the National Heart Failure Audit dataset. It is studying how kidney impairment affects short- and long-term outcomes, such as death and hospital readmission, in people admitted with acute heart failure over the last 15 years. It also aims to build a tool to predict adverse outcomes. The main intended benefit is service improvements for patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

DARS-NIC-759280-N0Y4F.summary: Slough Borough Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data. It uses this to understand local health needs, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits, health assessments and strategies. Outputs are aggregated statistics with small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, reducing mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-759355-H7B9S.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care is using NHS England data on adult social care, hospital activity, emergency care, cancer waiting lists, continuing healthcare, virtual wards and dental training posts. It uses the data to analyse and develop evidence-based health and care policy and to advise Ministers. The main intended benefit is better-informed decisions that improve patient outcomes. Reporting based on the specialist advice dataset has been automated and fed into elective modelling ahead of the spending review.

DARS-NIC-759654-D8H5M.summary: The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust is using pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, emergency care and diagnostic imaging data covering England from 2021 onwards. It uses the data to run Getting it Right First Time (GIRFT) reviews for NHS and independent sector clients, comparing their results against national benchmarks. The main intended benefit is helping providers check the quality of care and improve it, with learning shared with NHS England.

DARS-NIC-759706-Y0Y3S.summary: Wokingham Borough Council, a local authority, is using pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data: Hospital Episode Statistics (admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care, accident and emergency) and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, especially for disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-761685-K1C1Z.summary: The University of Aberdeen is using hospital admissions and outpatient records for 839 women who took part in the FUTURE clinical trial on refractory overactive bladder. The records will show any further admissions, operations and bladder treatments after each woman joined the trial. The study tests whether routine urodynamics (invasive bladder pressure tests) improves treatment outcomes and is cost effective. The findings are intended to inform patients, clinicians and NHS policy makers.

DARS-NIC-761989-J2G4R.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admission and death registration records for about 20,000 patients who had routine blood tests at the trust in 2017. It is studying whether raised troponin levels, a blood test designed to detect heart attacks, are linked to heart attacks, strokes, heart failure and death over five years. The main intended benefit is helping clinicians interpret troponin results and prompting research into reducing risk. An earlier phase of the study found the test was closely associated with mortality.

DARS-NIC-762732-L6B5X.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using bowel screening, cancer registration and death registration data held by NHS England. It will analyse and model existing faecal immunochemical test and colonoscopy results to estimate bowel pathology at different faecal haemoglobin levels. The work is the first of six stages in a programme on risk-based bowel cancer screening. It is intended to provide evidence to support introducing risk-based screening in the UK.

DARS-NIC-764229-C0C7B.summary: The University of Birmingham is using identifiable hospital, emergency care, outpatient and death registration records for 160 people with permanent atrial fibrillation and heart failure symptoms who took part in the RATE-AF trial. It is following their long-term health outcomes to see whether beta-blockers or digoxin, used to control heart rate, lead to different results. The aim is to help clinicians choose the best heart rate control treatment for these patients.

DARS-NIC-764470-N9W3S.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using NHS England's Hospital Episode Statistics for accident and emergency, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients. Approved researchers will use it in the Health & Labour Market project to study how long-term health conditions, risk factors and treatments affect employment and earnings. The aim is to give HM Treasury and NHS decision-makers better evidence on where to allocate public funds. Initial analysis has already examined the economic effects of bariatric surgery.

DARS-NIC-765236-C7C1B.summary: The University of Oxford's Nuffield Department of Population Health is using identifiable NHS England data on deaths, demographics, hospital admissions, critical care, emergency care and dispensed medicines. The data will follow patients in the RECOVERY trial who were hospitalised with non-COVID-19 pneumonia, to measure death, other outcomes and longer-term effects of the treatments being tested. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve care and reduce deaths for people hospitalised with pneumonia.

DARS-NIC-765257-H7B7S.summary: The University of Cambridge is using identifiable cancer registration and death records for 2,025 consenting trial participants aged 50 and over who take long-term acid suppressants. It is following their long-term outcomes in the BEST3 trial, which compares an invitation to the Cytosponge-TFF3 test with usual care for diagnosing Barrett's oesophagus, a pre-cancerous condition. The intended benefit is evidence on whether this less invasive test could be used in primary care.

DARS-NIC-765457-R1Z0N.summary: University of Bristol is using hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. It is studying how intensive care is used after vascular surgery for blocked or narrowed blood vessels in the neck and legs between 2014 and 2024, and comparing outcomes for patients sent to intensive care with those sent to a normal ward. The main intended benefit is better evidence on which patients need intensive care, to improve outcomes and reduce surgical delays.

DARS-NIC-766571-T4Z2L.summary: The University of Leeds is using identifiable hospital records (admissions, outpatients, emergency care) and dispensed medicines data for about 1.5 million patients registered at GP practices in the 3i-o study. It is using them to assess whether audit and feedback to GP practices, aimed at reducing prescribing of antibiotics, addictive painkillers and gabapentinoids, affects health inequalities, and to analyse cost-effectiveness. The main intended benefit is more selective prescribing across the NHS and evidence on whether the approach widens inequalities.

DARS-NIC-766604-V7D1W.summary: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency department records (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision and checking whether treatment and resources match patients' needs. The outputs are aggregated dashboards for senior leaders. The main intended benefit is better patient care and pathways, with less pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-76770-F0J5W.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, for its Salford area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) linked with GP data to carry out risk stratification, which identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration or repeated service use. NHS Arden and GEM Commissioning Support Unit carries out the work. The aim is to let GPs and commissioners target care and plan services, improving patient outcomes. Reported so far: better understanding of patient flows and identification of high-risk patients who often attend or are admitted to hospital.

DARS-NIC-767874-H5W4P.summary: East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency care data, which records the care patients received from the ambulance crew and in hospital. It will use this for service evaluation and auditing, including clinical supervision, staff development and spotting patterns in treatment. The main intended benefit is better patient care, with improved care pathways that could reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-767882-N1X4D.summary: South Western Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is using linked Ambulance Data Set and Emergency Care Data Set (ECDS) records, which combine ambulance call and patient record data with emergency department data. It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, support clinical supervision and compare treatments and outcomes. The main intended benefit is better patient care, including improved training for clinicians and changes to patient pathways that could reduce pressure on emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-768785-V7L6D.summary: East Midlands Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency care records, which cover the care patients receive from the ambulance service and then in hospital emergency departments. It is using them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision and training for crews, and to check whether treatments and resources are consistent. The intended benefit is better patient care and care pathways, which could also reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-769062-G5F1K.summary: University College London (UCL), working with Care England and The Outstanding Society Community Interest Company, is using linked hospital, emergency care, death and prescribing data on care home residents. They are piloting surveillance of infection and antimicrobial resistance in care homes, producing dashboards and reports for providers and policymakers. The main intended benefit is fewer infections and outbreaks, with better-targeted quality improvement.

DARS-NIC-76968-B0H8X.summary: London Borough of Ealing Council uses hospital and emergency care records from NHS England's secure data environment, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report.
