The aim is more locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports using the access in the last year for needs assessments and other public health analyses.

DARS-NIC-769782-X5C1F.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales is using pseudonymised NHS England hospital data covering admitted patient care, accident and emergency, and outpatient activity from April 2019 onwards. It will use the data to build a benchmarking dashboard that lets Health Boards in Wales compare their metrics, such as mortality, with others across Wales and England. The main intended benefit is improved services in Wales, as Health Boards see how they compare and make changes.

DARS-NIC-771073-N4R2G.summary: Swansea University, an academic institution, is using pseudonymised hospital admission, emergency care, critical care and death registration data for a group of people who had an injury and contacted emergency ambulance services or emergency departments. The data will be linked to survey answers from 250 ethnic minority and 250 white British people. The study compares their injuries, care and outcomes, and explores their experiences of seeking help. The main intended benefit is evidence to help policy makers and services improve care and access for ethnic minority people with injuries.

DARS-NIC-771170-Y3J8Z.summary: The University of Cambridge, working with Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is using pseudonymised hospital admissions and emergency care records from 2013/14 to 2024/25. The research looks at how easily people can reach specialist surgical services, including differences linked to inequality and location, and which surgical pathways are under strain. The main intended benefit is national evidence to help plan specialist surgical services and improve care.

DARS-NIC-771303-G4V1M.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using linked hospital, emergency care and death registration records, along with major trauma registry data, for the Pre-hospital Research and Audit Network (PRANA). The registry follows patients who received critical care outside hospital, to research and audit that care and its outcomes. It aims to give the first national picture of this care in England and Wales. So far, the linked data is being used by the Department for Transport to assess the health effects of road traffic collisions, and PRANA is named in the January 2026 National Road Safety Strategy.

DARS-NIC-771368-F4G0V.summary: The University of Warwick is using pseudonymised hospital, emergency care and death registration records for 151 patients who survived an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and consented to join the PARAMEDIC-3 trial. It will use them to compare survival, hospital activity and NHS costs between two ways of giving adrenaline: into a vein or into a bone. The intended benefit is evidence to inform resuscitation guidelines.

DARS-NIC-77142-Q4D1D.summary: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust is using pseudonymised hospital, death, cancer registration, radiotherapy and systemic anti-cancer therapy records for people who have had a solid organ transplant in England. The study links these records to examine cancer after transplantation, including cancer risk, deaths and hospital care, to help guide care and counselling for transplant patients. Preliminary findings have been presented at two international transplant congresses and submitted to The Lancet as manuscripts.

DARS-NIC-771891-C7B5S.summary: West Midlands Ambulance Service University NHS Foundation Trust is using linked Ambulance Data Set and Emergency Care Data Set records, which follow patients from ambulance care into hospital. It will use them to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, staff training needs and patterns in treatment. The main intended benefit is better patient care and pathways, with less pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-772217-L9G2N.summary: London Borough of Camden uses identifiable civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data. It uses the data to measure local health needs, plan and monitor services, and protect public health, including suicide audits. The aim is to tailor local services to local needs and reduce health inequalities. Under an earlier joint agreement with Islington, it produced mortality profiles for GP practices and informed needs assessments.

DARS-NIC-772232-C4K8W.summary: London Borough of Camden, a local authority, is using pseudonymised hospital and emergency care records, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It will use them for its public health work, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The stated benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-772510-Z1K7F.summary: Yorkshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using Ambulance Data Set (pilot) data linked to Emergency Care Data Set records, which show what happened to patients after they reached hospital. The Trust is using it to evaluate and audit its services, including reviewing clinical care, supporting clinician supervision and training, and checking whether resources are used well. It aims to improve patient care and to help change patient pathways in ways that reduce pressure on busy emergency departments.

DARS-NIC-772615-N4N1V.summary: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for 5,250 Merseyside patients treated with clopidogrel or ticagrelor after acute coronary syndrome. It will test how well tools that estimate bleeding risk on antiplatelet medicines work in this real-world group and identify the best-performing one. The aim is to help clinicians prescribe with more confidence, reducing major bleeding and further heart attacks.

DARS-NIC-772633-Y3K3T.summary: University College London is using hospital, emergency care, critical care, outpatient and death registration records to study young people who move from paediatric to adult intensive care. The data will be linked with national intensive care audit records to show how many young people make this move, what their characteristics are and how they use hospital services. The main intended benefit is evidence to improve care and experience for these teenagers and their families.

DARS-NIC-773525-N5H9R.summary: The University of Cambridge is using survey data on the mental health of children and young people (the Mental Health of Children and Young People 2017 Survey and its follow-up waves). The data will be linked to school attainment records. The research looks at how mental health, mental health service use and educational outcomes relate over time, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim is to show which services work, for whom and why, so that services can be better targeted and improved for children and young people.

DARS-NIC-773720-X4Q2Q.summary: The University of Edinburgh is using identifiable NHS England data on deaths, hospital admissions and medicines dispensed in primary care. It is for a UK-wide study of memory, thinking and mood problems, and vascular dementia, after a stroke, including the effects of COVID-19. The study aims to find who develops these problems and why. The hope is better risk prediction and earlier information, treatment and care for patients.

DARS-NIC-773953-N5L3H.summary: Tolley Ltd, a consultancy, is using pseudonymised hospital admission, outpatient and national cancer registry data on adults in England with non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer that no longer responds to BCG treatment. It will analyse their treatment pathways and outcomes for ImmunityBio, which is seeking a NICE appraisal of its treatment. The intended benefit is evidence on current care to inform NICE decisions and UK clinicians.

DARS-NIC-774097-J9J0C.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic organisation, is using demographic data from NHS England, specifically addresses, for the Medical Research Council National Survey of Health and Development, which follows people born in Britain in 1946. It will use the addresses to re-contact study members who have been lost to follow-up and invite them to rejoin. The intended benefit is keeping the study sample representative of the population being studied.

DARS-NIC-774351-T6M3Q.summary: The University of East Anglia, an academic organisation, is using NHS England data on hospital admissions, outpatient visits, emergency care, deaths and medicines dispensed in primary care. It is using them to test whether the CHARMER training helps hospital geriatricians and pharmacists stop unnecessary medicines for older people. The main intended benefit is to show whether this reduces unplanned hospital admissions and to inform national policy on overprescribing.

DARS-NIC-774448-Q4C6X.summary: Beamtree UK Limited, a consultancy, is using hospital activity data (emergency care, admitted patient, critical care and outpatient records) and the Summary Hospital-level Mortality Indicator. It is using them to run an analytics platform, developed with the NHS Confederation, for NHS acute trusts. Trusts can benchmark their performance against peers, track trends and see predictions up to a year ahead. The main intended benefit is helping trusts target improvements to the safety, quality and efficiency of care.

DARS-NIC-775419-R1N5L.summary: Quality by Randomization Limited (trading as Protas), a research organisation, is using NHS England data, including a mailing cohort and an aggregate recruitment data quality report. It will use the data to identify and invite eligible people to join NATRIX-SBP, a clinical trial of REGN5381, a monthly injection for uncontrolled high blood pressure. The agreement says its sole purpose is recruitment, and the wider trial aims to show whether the treatment safely lowers blood pressure.

DARS-NIC-775420-M7D8Z.summary: Quality by Randomization Limited (trading as Protas), a research organisation, is using NHS England mailing-list data and aggregate data quality reports to find and invite people who may be eligible for the NATRIX-SBP trial. The trial tests REGN5381, a monthly injection intended to lower uncontrolled high blood pressure. The data is used only for recruitment, so no direct health benefit is expected from this agreement; the trial itself aims to show whether the treatment works safely.

DARS-NIC-775459-B7S5G.summary: North West Ambulance Service NHS Trust is using linked ambulance and emergency care data (the Ambulance Data Set and the Emergency Care Data Set, ECDS). It is using the data to evaluate and audit its services, including clinical supervision, clinician training needs, treatments given and patient pathways. The main intended benefit is better patient care and less pressure on busy Emergency Departments. Results will appear as aggregated dashboards for senior leaders.

DARS-NIC-775504-H4Z5Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using pseudonymised hospital admissions, outpatient, emergency care and death registration data for patients who had cardiac surgery at three NHS hospitals between October 2021 and July 2023. It is studying how atrial fibrillation (an irregular heart rhythm) after cardiac surgery relates to longer-term outcomes, and whether prediction models can estimate the risk of those outcomes. The intended benefit is to improve and target follow-up care for patients after cardiac surgery.

DARS-NIC-77560-T5P8Y.summary: East Riding of Yorkshire Council uses identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand local health needs. It uses them for public health work such as needs assessments, suicide audits and monitoring deaths, publishing only aggregated figures. The aim is to tailor local services to the areas of greatest need and reduce health inequalities. The council reports using the data to analyse premature deaths in a deprived coastal town and to inform its 2022/23 Director of Public Health annual report.

DARS-NIC-776114-J7Q9J.summary: University College London is using identifiable NHS England data on deaths, cancer registrations and medicines dispensed in primary care for 300 deceased participants of the AspECT trial. It is following up whether aspirin combined with a proton pump inhibitor (a stomach acid medicine) affects deaths, oesophageal cancer or high-grade dysplasia (precancerous changes). The aim is to inform guidance on preventing oesophageal cancer in people with Barrett's oesophagus.

DARS-NIC-776144-T4V1D.summary: The University of Bristol, an academic body, is using civil registrations of death and hospital admissions data (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) for the ASPECT randomised trial. The trial tests whether aspirin reduces heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths within 90 days in people aged 50 and over admitted to hospital with pneumonia. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide treatment decisions and potentially reduce these events in England.

DARS-NIC-776147-F5N3V.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using identifiable demographic data, specifically NHS Numbers, for people who have consented to join the Heartburn Health Programme. The numbers are needed for the linked BEST4 Screening Trial, which tests a capsule sponge as a screening tool for Barrett's oesophagus and oesophageal cancer. They will be used to label samples, make onward referrals and follow up cancer outcomes. The stated benefit is accurate NHS Numbers for each participant.

DARS-NIC-776195-H7W4D.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using hospital admitted patient care and outpatient records from Hospital Episode Statistics. It is studying how pelvic floor surgery for rectal prolapse, constipation and faecal incontinence has varied across the UK over the past decade, including outcomes and waiting times. The main intended benefit is to identify regions with limited access to specialist treatment, so that policymakers and clinicians can reduce inequalities in care.

DARS-NIC-77633-Y4X1L.summary: Sheffield City Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health inequalities. The council reports it has analysed health inequalities in admissions, outpatient "did not attend" rates by ethnicity, and Covid-19 admissions.

DARS-NIC-776600-D8P6R.summary: Observational and Pragmatic Research International Limited is using NHS hospital, emergency care and death registration records to analyse a trial called PREVAIL. The trial tests whether CONQUEST, a quality improvement programme for GP practices, reduces flare-ups and serious heart or breathing events in people with high-risk chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Practices receiving the programme will be compared with practices giving usual care. If it works, the main benefit would be earlier diagnosis and better-targeted treatment.

DARS-NIC-776952-Z3R9D.summary: The University of Manchester is using pseudonymised hospital, accident and emergency, and death registration data for patients registered with GP practices that use the PATCHS online consultation system. It is researching whether the system's artificial intelligence (AI) triage changes rates of A&E attendance, hospital admission and death compared with practices using PATCHS without AI. The aim is to help the NHS, GP practices and software companies decide whether to use AI triage, so that urgent patients may be helped sooner.

DARS-NIC-777554-J2V4K.summary: University College London (UCL), an academic institution, is using pseudonymised NHS England cancer registration, consolidated cancer and National Cancer Patient Experience Survey data on patients diagnosed with 21 solid organ cancers in England since January 2013. It is studying the causes of inequalities in cancer survival, patient experience, stage at diagnosis, route to diagnosis and first-line treatment. The expected benefit is to identify unusual care patterns so health professionals can investigate them and improve patient care.

DARS-NIC-777868-Z9N1M.summary: The London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham is using hospital and emergency care records from Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It will use them for its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report, advice to NHS commissioners and health impact assessments. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, including for specific groups, so that the needs of disadvantaged residents are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-777919-R7D2B.summary: The University of Leeds, with the University of Sheffield and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, is using identifiable hospital, emergency care and death registration records for about 200 trial participants. The data will help estimate hospital resource use and costs, and the time to events such as melanoma-related hospital care or death. This supports the DANTE trial, which compares a 12-month course of anti-PD-1 treatment with standard-length treatment in advanced melanoma. The aim is to help clinicians choose treatment regimens and allocate resources more effectively.

DARS-NIC-778449-V2L5D.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital, emergency care and death registration records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. It is using them to test whether cardiac output-guided fluid therapy reduces deaths after emergency bowel surgery (laparotomy) and to assess costs. The aim is to show whether the treatment should be adopted nationally. Earlier data supported safety monitoring reports and led the trial team to change its primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-778499-F3Q4L.summary: South East London Cancer Alliance, hosted by Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times and pathways across local hospitals and the ICB, to identify variation and delays. The main aim is faster diagnosis and treatment, supporting better survival and patient experience. Earlier similar analysis is reported to have improved performance and corrected treatment pathways at Guy's and St Thomas'.

DARS-NIC-778520-D7B2M.summary: East of England - North Cancer Alliance, a network of health organisations, is using the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set, which records patients' cancer pathways from referral to treatment. It will analyse waiting times and patient flows across trusts and integrated care boards (ICBs) to find variation, long waits and reasons for delay. The main intended benefit is better cancer pathways, helping services meet national waiting time standards and improving patient survival and experience.

DARS-NIC-778539-F0L7F.summary: NHS England is giving Thames Valley Cancer Alliance, through NHS Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West Integrated Care Board, access to the National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set from the Cancer Wait Times system. The Alliance will analyse waiting times, variation between providers and reasons for delays. The aim is to improve cancer pathways, meet national waiting standards and improve survival and patient experience. Earlier access has already supported local work such as improving faster diagnosis and treatment times.

DARS-NIC-778853-K4R8H.summary: University College London (UCL) is using pseudonymised hospital admission records, death registration data and the national congenital heart disease audit for children in England with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who had surgery to relieve a blocked heart outflow. It will study how many such operations take place, how outcomes vary between centres, and complications, readmissions and survival. The aim is to inform service planning, including whether surgery should be centralised.

DARS-NIC-778927-P3D9Z.summary: Imperial College London, an academic institution, is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patient care and outpatients. The records are for a research project on how cyberattacks could spread between NHS hospitals and how A&E demand would shift if hospitals were disrupted. The team will build a prototype tool to simulate hospital closures and plan how to redistribute patients. The intended benefit is better NHS preparedness and response to large-scale cyberattacks.

DARS-NIC-779200-S6R2D.summary: University College London's MRC Clinical Trials Unit is using linked NHS England data on deaths, hospital admissions and outpatient visits, and cancer registrations for about 8,000 consenting participants in three cancer trials (PATCH, Add-Aspirin and RAMPART). It will track long-term outcomes such as survival, cancer recurrence, new cancers and treatment side effects. It will also test whether health records can replace extra trial follow-up visits. The aim is to make trials faster and less burdensome for patients and hospital staff.

DARS-NIC-779354-C7T9H.summary: Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire Cancer Alliance, hosted by North Bristol NHS Trust, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set data from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waits from referral to treatment, compare hospital trusts and areas, and spot long waits and variation in cancer pathways. The aim is to guide priorities and investment so cancer patients are diagnosed and treated sooner. Earlier access to similar data supported prostate improvement plans and shorter oesophageal cancer treatment waits.

DARS-NIC-779400-J2J4Z.summary: The University of Plymouth is using linked hospital records (emergency care, admitted patient and outpatient data) and death registration data. It is studying end-of-life care in rural and coastal communities of the South West Peninsula, including place of death and how distance from services affects care. The intended benefit is evidence and policy insights to help integrated care boards (ICBs) reduce geographical inequalities in end-of-life care.

DARS-NIC-779433-Q9R8N.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is using hospital and emergency care records from NHS England, including Emergency Care Data Set and Hospital Episode Statistics data. It is using them in the THERM-UK project to measure health risks from heat, cold, air pollution and infectious diseases, and the health benefits of reducing heat exposure. The findings are intended to inform policy, hospital and care home practice, and public guidance on protecting health during hot weather.

DARS-NIC-77953-C4M3T.summary: The University of Leeds is using hospital records on A&E attendances, inpatient admissions and outpatient appointments, linked to GP records, for patients at eight English hospitals without a liaison psychiatry service. It will build patient pathways and calculate their costs to the health service, to assess the cost-effectiveness and efficiency of different liaison psychiatry service set-ups. The main intended benefit is reports to help local and national commissioners make decisions about hospital mental health services.

DARS-NIC-779746-L0Q9T.summary: Wessex Cancer Alliance, a cancer network covering the Wessex region, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times across hospital trusts and integrated care boards to spot variation, long waits and reasons for delay. The main aim is to help improve cancer pathways, so that patients are diagnosed and treated sooner, with better survival and experience.

DARS-NIC-780370-H0H7P.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using records of medicines dispensed in primary care, supplied by the NHS Business Services Authority. It will link them with other data, including Census 2021, to produce official statistics on population, health and disability. It will also study how treatments such as weight loss drugs and menopause medication affect employment, earnings and benefits. The intended benefit is more complete health information to guide government and local decisions.

DARS-NIC-780518-Q7K4W.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is using identifiable NHS England Flag 4 data, which marks people registering with a GP after arriving from overseas. It uses the data to identify who is eligible for latent TB (tuberculosis) infection testing and to monitor and report on the national testing and treatment programme. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform TB screening policy, supporting earlier detection and treatment and reducing TB in England.

DARS-NIC-780525-J4L3S.summary: NHS England and the Department for Health and Social Care (DHSC) will jointly analyse pseudonymised NHS data on elective care, cancer waiting times, diagnostics, urgent and emergency care, and costs. They will use it to give ministers and senior officials timely analysis on waiting lists, waiting times and unit costs. The main intended benefit is better evidence for policy and funding decisions, leading to improved, faster and more efficient services.

DARS-NIC-781290-Q2Q6F.summary: The University of Leeds, an academic organisation, is using NHS England hospital, cancer registration, radiotherapy, systemic anti-cancer therapy and death records. It is linking them with data from about 5,500 people who took part in completed multiple myeloma clinical trials. The aim is to test whether routine health data can accurately support long-term follow-up in trials, and to study frailty, bone disease and who takes part. The main intended benefit is faster, cheaper and more efficient blood cancer trials.

DARS-NIC-782158-W5V8C.summary: Synapsys IQ, a supplier, uses medicines dispensed in primary care, hospital prescribing and administration, emergency care and hospital admitted and outpatient activity data. It builds dashboards, tailored analyses and publications showing prescribing variation across England, to support safer prescribing and planning in the NHS. So far, ICBs have used its bespoke analyses to plan asthma and COPD work, and an asthma analysis supported a conference poster.

DARS-NIC-782177-G5W5G.summary: The University of Oxford is using NHS England data on deaths, diagnostic imaging, hospital admissions and outpatient visits, and national cancer records. It is using them for the DeLIVER research programme, which follows people with cirrhosis or early liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC). The aim is to understand what predicts HCC and to build a risk score. The main intended benefit is detecting liver cancer earlier, when treatment is more likely to work.

DARS-NIC-782449-Z6G3F.summary: University College London (UCL) is using birth notification and civil registration birth records to recruit families to Generation New Era, a long-term research study of about 30,000 babies born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data is used to select families in England and Wales, to target fieldwork and to check how representative participants are. The study aims to show how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-782954-Z6C8Z.summary: The University of Oxford is using identifiable hospital admission, emergency care and death registration records for a small group of people aged 75 or over who lack capacity to consent and are taking blood pressure medicines. The data supports the OPTIMISE2 trial, which tests whether stopping or reducing these medicines is safe, looking at emergency hospital admissions and deaths. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines on treating high blood pressure in older adults.

DARS-NIC-783876-K7N5S.summary: The Royal Borough of Windsor & Maidenhead Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand local health needs, support immunisation and public health work, and carry out suicide audits. Results are published as summary statistics. The main intended benefit is local health and care services that are better targeted, to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-78397-Z1F1Q.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital, mental health and mortality records to follow up people in the Asymptomatic Carotid Surgery Trial (ACST-1), who had narrowed neck arteries. It is keeping this data to study long-term stroke risk and whether carotid surgery reduces dementia. The aim is to help patients and clinicians make better treatment decisions.

DARS-NIC-784100-W4B7T.summary: The University of Manchester is using linked NHS hospital, emergency care, maternity, mental health, death and cancer registration records for the Childhood Arthritis Prospective Study, which follows children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). It will study what happens to them as adults, including ongoing arthritis, mental health, cancer and death rates. The aim is to give patients and families better information on what to expect in future.

DARS-NIC-784425-X2Y5R.summary: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) is using the Mental Health Services Data Set, which covers mental health care, linked with Census 2021 and other administrative data. It will use the data for statistical research on disability and general health, on how mental health and services affect employment, earnings and benefits, and on mental health support for young people. The main intended benefit is better evidence to help target health services and policy decisions.

DARS-NIC-785335-G6D8R.summary: The University of Surrey is using National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) cancer registration data and National Cancer Patient Experience Survey data. The research looks at whether marginalised groups report different experiences of cancer care, and whether those differences help explain inequalities in receiving treatment and in time to treatment. The intended benefit is an evidence base to help policy makers reduce inequalities in cancer care.

DARS-NIC-785339-D9Q2D.summary: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using cancer registration data and the National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) consolidated cancer data set for a research project on lymphoma in people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It aims to identify which types of IBD carry the highest lymphoma risk, whether genetic factors are involved, and which medicines may raise the risk. The main intended benefit is reducing the number of people with IBD who develop lymphoma.

DARS-NIC-786257-W9C8P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using identifiable hospital, emergency care and civil registration (death) records for patients in the FLO-ELA trial. It is testing whether cardiac output-guided fluid therapy during emergency abdominal surgery reduces deaths and is cost-effective, and the aim is to inform national practice. Data from an earlier agreement helped trial monitoring reports spot a fall in the death rate, which led the team to change the trial's primary outcome.

DARS-NIC-786264-W6R5D.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and civil death registration data. It is following up participants from the FORECAST trial, which compared CT coronary angiography with computed fractional flow reserve against standard care for stable chest pain. The aim is to see how the two approaches compare over five years for health outcomes and NHS resource use. The main intended benefit is stronger evidence to guide how chest pain patients are diagnosed.

DARS-NIC-786702-B8R5P.summary: Sanius Health, a commercial health data and technology company, is using NHS hospital, emergency care and primary care prescribing data about people with sickle cell disease. It will describe how they use care and what that care costs across urgent and planned settings, including high-cost drugs and transfusions. The aim is a national costing index, published in a peer-reviewed paper and reports, to help the NHS and NICE plan services and assess new treatments.

DARS-NIC-786843-Y6V6G.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care will use adult social care data collected by NHS England, covering areas such as council spending, safeguarding, carers and user surveys. It will use the data to take over publishing official adult social care statistics, which were previously published by NHS England. The aim is to support monitoring of services, accountability and policy decisions based on current, complete information.

DARS-NIC-786978-Z6K4M.summary: Abiomed Inc, which makes the Impella heart pump, is using data from the National Audit of Percutaneous Coronary Interventions run by NICOR. It is carrying out a descriptive service evaluation of how Impella and intra-aortic balloon pumps are used in high-risk heart procedures in the UK. The aim is to see how far current practice follows NICE guidance and to help design future studies.

DARS-NIC-787003-B1G4C.summary: The University of Bristol is using hospital admissions, outpatient and emergency care data for a research trial called RADICAL. The trial looks at whether radiofrequency denervation, a treatment for moderate to severe long-term lower back pain, reduces hospital use and is cost-effective compared with placebo over 24 months. The findings are intended to inform clinical guidelines and healthcare spending decisions.

DARS-NIC-787006-N2H5C.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using national adult cardiac surgery audit data from the National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (NICOR). It is helping run a UK-wide service evaluation of temporary mechanical devices that support the heart in patients who are very unwell before or after heart surgery. The aim is to show how often and which devices are used and what outcomes follow, and so to help plan the size of the service needed.

DARS-NIC-787009-K8R3B.summary: Imperial College London, an academic organisation, is using pseudonymised patient records from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project (MINAP). These cover about 3,000 people discharged with takotsubo cardiomyopathy, a heart condition that can mimic a heart attack, plus matched controls. The research aims to estimate how common the condition is and identify associated factors such as triggers and existing health conditions. The stated main benefit is better understanding of the condition, supporting more accurate diagnosis and personalised care.

DARS-NIC-787193-Y8W6D.summary: The University of York is using national audit data on percutaneous coronary interventions (procedures to open narrowed heart arteries). The research asks whether a doctor's exam and training appraisal performance relates to how they later practise and to patients' 30-day mortality after these procedures. The main intended benefit is evidence to guide cardiology training policy, including support for doctors who may need it, and ultimately better patient outcomes.

DARS-NIC-787195-R1H2P.summary: University College London is using pseudonymised national records for patients who have had heart rhythm procedures, including NHS hospital, emergency care, death registration and national heart audit data. It aims to find which patients with pacemakers or defibrillators are at risk of problems such as shocks, stroke or heart failure, and to understand differences in outcomes. The main intended benefit is better selection of patients for implants and improved care for those at high risk.

DARS-NIC-787209-F3W7J.summary: University College London is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration data on children and young people with visual impairment or blindness. The study will link this with education and cohort study data to examine their health, healthcare use and educational outcomes. It aims to give policy-makers, service commissioners, families and charities national evidence on what works well and what needs improving in care.

DARS-NIC-787477-W3G5Z.summary: The Renal Association, a charity that runs the UK Renal Registry and the National Registry of Rare Kidney Diseases (RaDaR), is using hospital records (admissions, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and death registration data. It is linking them to its rare kidney disease registry to study risk factors, predict outcomes, examine inequalities, estimate care costs and check the registry's data. The intended benefit is better evidence to improve care and outcomes for people with rare kidney disease.

DARS-NIC-788212-W2D4D.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using NICOR Adult Cardiac Surgery data on adults who had elective cardiac surgery between 2012 and 2022. It will study how smoking affects outcomes around the time of surgery, such as in-hospital death, length of stay and complications, and how this differs by type of operation, region and socioeconomic status. The aim is to identify patients most at risk so that smoking-cessation support can be designed for them.

DARS-NIC-788281-L8X5B.summary: The Regional Drug and Therapeutics Centre, hosted by Newcastle Upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, uses pseudonymised hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) and primary care medicines dispensing data. It links prescribing with hospital activity to help NHS bodies improve how medicines are used and reduce avoidable admissions. It reports that findings led Greater Manchester to change its diabetes formulary and pathway, and COPD and asthma pathways to be redefined.

DARS-NIC-788403-Y9M1G.summary: Leeds Institute of Health Sciences, part of the University of Leeds, is using NHS England cancer registration and death registration data for the Yorkshire Lung Screening Trial. The trial compares inviting current and former smokers to community-based lung cancer screening with usual care, using cancer stage and outcomes data. The main intended benefit is evidence to inform the design of future lung screening programmes and increase uptake, particularly in deprived communities.

DARS-NIC-788591-Z8G5K.summary: The University of East Anglia is using NHS England hospital, emergency care, death registration and primary care dispensing data for the CHARMER study. The study tests whether training geriatricians and hospital pharmacists to stop unsuitable medicines for older people reduces hospital readmissions, deaths and costs. The intended benefit is to inform national policy on managing overprescribing and improve older people's health and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-788663-G4F2D.summary: The Office for National Statistics is using the NHS England Health and Growth Accelerator Programme minimum data set, which records who took part in the programme's interventions. It will link this to its own employment and socio-demographic data to give a preliminary analysis of the programme, which aims to tackle health-driven economic inactivity in three pilot areas. The aim is to support a bid for multi-year funding and show whether interventions keep people in work or return them to work.

DARS-NIC-788684-Y5P8C.summary: The National Centre for Stereotactic Radiosurgery is using cancer registration and death registration data. It is studying patients treated with Gamma Knife radiosurgery over the last 40 years to see whether they develop cancer afterwards, including in the treated area, and whether this is more common than in the general population. The aim is to give doctors, policy-makers and patients better evidence on the long-term risks of this treatment.

DARS-NIC-789345-S3W6T.summary: Milton Keynes City Council, a local authority, uses civil registration data on births and deaths, plus primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses them to measure local health needs, plan immunisation programmes, protect public health and support work such as suicide audits and prevention. Results are published only as aggregated statistics. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-789702-M6C7G.summary: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and civil death registrations for England. It is running a pilot research study on post infarction ventricular septal defect, a rare tear in the heart that can follow a heart attack. The study looks at how often it occurs, who is affected and how patients move through care. The aim is to give better information for planning future clinical trials and a patient registry.

DARS-NIC-789772-N6S1N.summary: The University of Bristol uses linked NHS England health records, including hospital, mental health, maternity, cancer, death and medicines data, for the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), known as "Children of the 90s". The data is added to a research database that approved researchers can use to study health and wellbeing across generations. The aim is to improve understanding of conditions such as depression, psychosis and self-harm. Past ALSPAC research contributed to UK policy change on the "back to sleep" advice to reduce cot death.

DARS-NIC-79018-W9T1D.summary: Halton Borough Council, a local authority, uses hospital admissions, outpatient, critical care and emergency care data to carry out its public health duties. It analyses patterns of illness, access to care and health differences between groups, to inform needs assessments, health strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. It aims to give locally focused analysis, especially for disadvantaged groups. It reports using the data to update internal boards on key indicators and to publish a 2025 analysis of children's hospital admissions and accidental injuries.

DARS-NIC-790414-L6R9T.summary: The Institute of Cancer Research is using identifiable death registration and cohort-tracking records for men with prostate cancer, or a strong family history of it, who joined the UK Genetic Prostate Cancer Study. It uses them to study survival and to find genetic changes linked to prostate cancer risk. The aim is to help identify who is at higher risk and to inform screening and new treatments. So far, the data has helped develop a genetic risk model for personalised prostate cancer risk predictions.

DARS-NIC-791529-K1J8C.summary: The University of Leeds is using NHS England mailing cohort data and an aggregate data quality report to help recruit people to the Digital- My Arm Pain Programme (D-MAPP) clinical trial. The trial is testing whether a digitally delivered self-management programme can be developed for people with musculoskeletal disorders of the arm, to help recovery, long-term function and pain. The main intended benefit is faster, more efficient trial enrolment from a wider pool of potential participants.

DARS-NIC-791694-D2J8T.summary: Cristal Health Ltd, trading as Akrivia Health, is using NHS England's DigiTrials Recruitment Service, which uses personal data to identify and send invitation letters to adults in England with a diagnosis or treatment for major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder or schizophrenia. The letters invite people to join the Global Minds study, which looks at links between serious mental illness and dementia and human biology. The study aims to improve diagnosis and help develop better treatments.

DARS-NIC-791919-T4Y0Y.summary: NHS South West London Integrated Care Board is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients and outpatients across England. It is using them for commissioning and risk stratification, benchmarking itself against other areas to find inequalities in care, such as length of stay, waiting times and readmissions. The main intended benefit is better evidence for planning services and allocating resources more fairly.

DARS-NIC-792066-B5D2T.summary: University College London (UCL) is using demographic data from NHS England to recruit families to Generation New Era, a long-term research study of about 30,000 infants born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data will be used to select families to contact, boost the sample using ethnicity fields, target fieldwork and check how representative participants are. The study aims to understand how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-792991-W4Z6B.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admitted patient care, outpatient and newborn screening data for a clinical trial called the Digital Imaging versus Ophthalmoscopy (DIvO) study. The trial tests whether digital imaging with the Neocam device is more accurate than the standard red-reflex eye test for spotting congenital cataract in newborns. The main intended benefit is earlier detection of cataracts, which could lead to better long-term vision and help inform national screening policy.

DARS-NIC-793230-S7H9P.summary: The University of Edinburgh, working with NHS Lothian, is using NHS England death registration, hospital admission and primary care dispensed medicines data for the ASPIRING clinical trial. The trial tests whether taking a single antiplatelet drug, alongside standard care, delays major cardiovascular events such as strokes and heart attacks in people who have survived a stroke caused by bleeding in the brain. It could show whether this treatment reduces those events.

DARS-NIC-793367-S9D4P.summary: The University of Sussex is using linked NHS hospital, emergency care, mental health and death registration records for a research study. It looks at women who had an adult psychiatric inpatient stay in England between April 2021 and March 2023, comparing mothers with non-mothers on their characteristics, length of stay, readmission and A&E attendance. The main intended benefit is national evidence on inequalities and outcomes for hospitalised mothers, to inform NHS planning and support for parents.

DARS-NIC-793368-F6W8K.summary: West Berkshire Council uses civil registration data on births and deaths, together with primary care mortality data, which includes identifiable details. It uses the data to understand the health needs of local people, support public health work such as suicide audits and immunisation programmes, and produce aggregated reports like Joint Strategic Needs Assessments. The intended benefit is local services that are better targeted to reduce premature deaths and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-793437-Z3C1X.summary: Westmorland and Furness Council, a local authority, is using Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and emergency care. It is using them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, so that the needs of the local population, particularly the most disadvantaged, are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-793709-R9M3D.summary: The University of Warwick, working with University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust, is using NHS England's recruitment service, which draws on personal data to identify and write to adults in England who had a stroke and left hospital 6 to 36 months ago. The letters invite them to join the ReSTORe trial, which tests whether an online, home-based exercise and recovery programme improves well-being after stroke. The service aims to speed up and improve recruitment.

DARS-NIC-793895-J0F7F.summary: Queen Mary University of London is using NHS England data quality reports, which are used to check participants' contact details and life status, for the Heartburn Health Programme and the BEST4 Screening Trial. NHS England will check whether participants have died and update their contact information, so the study team avoids contacting deceased people and can reach participants reliably. The intended benefit is to prevent distressing contact with families and to improve recruitment and retention in the trial.

DARS-NIC-79526-V8F2X.summary: The University of East Anglia is using pseudonymised hospital admissions, A&E, outpatient, critical care and death records for asthma patients at participating GP practices in England and Wales. It is using them in the ARRISA-UK trial, which tests whether flagging at-risk patients' records and training staff reduces asthma-related hospital admissions, A&E attendances and deaths. The aim is to show whether this approach is worth adopting in primary care. The trial's main results have been analysed and submitted to a peer-reviewed journal.

DARS-NIC-795268-S1T4D.summary: The Lampard Inquiry, a statutory investigation into mental health inpatient deaths in Essex between 2000 and 2023, is using Mental Health Services Data Set (MHSDS) data. Its appointed expert health statisticians will analyse the data in a secure environment and publish a report on failings in care, staff practice, and NHS trust culture and governance. The report is intended to support evidence-based recommendations to reduce avoidable deaths and improve patient safety.

DARS-NIC-795405-N6K0D.summary: Stoke-on-Trent City Council is using pseudonymised hospital data, covering emergency care, admitted patient care, critical care and outpatients, for its public health work. It will analyse this to support its statutory duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-795868-X8R6B.summary: The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust, which hosts West Midlands Cancer Alliance, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times across cancer pathways to find variation, long waits and delays, and to inform service discussions and investment. The main intended benefit is better cancer survival and patient experience. Earlier access to similar data is reported to have informed service improvement work.

DARS-NIC-795871-J2G4K.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire Integrated Care Board, on behalf of East Midlands Cancer Alliance, is using National Cancer Waiting Times Monitoring Data Set records from the Cancer Wait Times system. It will analyse waiting times and variation in cancer pathways across providers. The aim is to help the Alliance plan improvements, meet national waiting time standards and improve cancer survival and patient experience.

DARS-NIC-796147-S7T1T.summary: The University of Nottingham is using hospital admission records and death registration data for a study cohort of older surgical patients. It is linking them to its SNAP 3 study, which looks at how frailty, multimorbidity and delirium affect outcomes after surgery, including readmission and mortality. The aim is to improve the care of older surgical patients, including through a tool that predicts the risk of postoperative delirium.

DARS-NIC-796202-M0L0X.summary: The University of Essex is using Health Survey for England data for a research project on school holidays and children's health. It aims to understand how circumstances during school holidays and local food environments contribute to childhood obesity and mental health problems, and how far holidays drive inequality in these outcomes. The findings are expected to help policymakers decide on holiday support, such as food vouchers and holiday clubs, and so reduce health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-796232-C6B3Q.summary: University College London, an academic organisation, is using death registration records, hospital admitted patient care records and dispensed medicines data for a research project on severe aortic stenosis. It will test whether cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) scan measures can predict long-term survival after valve surgery or transcatheter valve replacement better than current risk models. The aim is more accurate risk assessment and better patient selection, which could improve survival and quality of life.

DARS-NIC-796943-G2Q0P.summary: West Berkshire Council, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care and accident and emergency (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use this data to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the annual public health report. The main intended benefit is local analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-797243-P7K9P.summary: University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is using hospital admission records and death registrations for people who took part in the RIPCORD 2 trial. It is following them for five years to see whether routine pressure wire assessment during heart artery investigations is safe and effective compared with conventional angiography. The aim is to inform clinical guidelines. The main trial paper has already been published in the journal Circulation.

DARS-NIC-79728-X2C2X.summary: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust, hosting the Innovation Agency, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) covering the North West Coast. It supports the Connected Health Cities programme, building analysis models and algorithms for alcohol, COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and epilepsy care, to help commissioners and clinicians improve services. Reports have already influenced seizure services, and analysis identified COPD hotspots in Wirral where a GP practice intervention tool was offered.

DARS-NIC-798519-F7X8X.summary: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust is using NHS England bowel cancer screening data on people with Lynch syndrome, with postcodes converted to deprivation scores and dates changed to ages or month and year. It is carrying out a service evaluation of how often these patients develop bowel cancer or polyps, how well colonoscopies detect them, and how many take part in screening. The aim is to inform evidence-based decisions on improving surveillance and care for people with Lynch syndrome.

DARS-NIC-798687-Z0Z8F.summary: University College London's Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Unit is using cancer registration, civil registration of deaths and demographics data for the STAMPEDE trial. The trial tests added treatments for men with high-risk prostate cancer starting long-term hormone therapy, and the data are used to follow participants' survival over the longer term. The aim is to give patients and clinicians evidence on which treatments improve survival. Death registration data let the metformin comparison report its main result sooner.

DARS-NIC-799985-H0F0G.summary: Reading Borough Council is using hospital data from NHS England, covering admitted patient care, outpatients, critical care, and accident and emergency (including the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use the data for its public health duties, such as producing needs assessments, strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-799986-S3L4Q.summary: Reading Borough Council is using identifiable birth and death records, including primary care mortality data, to understand the health needs of its local population. It uses them for public health work such as needs assessments, suicide audits, immunisation programmes and monitoring deaths, publishing only aggregated figures with small numbers suppressed. The main intended benefit is health and care services tailored to local needs, helping to reduce mortality and health inequalities.

DARS-NIC-800347-F4P5X.summary: The University of Oxford is using hospital admissions records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil death registration data. It is researching infections that follow fracture surgery and bone infections managed in the NHS in England. The project will estimate how common these infections are, who is at higher risk, how often repeat surgery is needed, and how care varies between providers. The main intended benefit is better evidence for patient counselling, service planning and the design of future trials to reduce infection risk.

DARS-NIC-800961-W7P2T.summary: University College London is using birth notification and civil registration birth records to recruit families in England and Wales to Generation New Era, a longitudinal study of about 30,000 infants born across the UK in the mid-2020s. The data will be used to select families to contact, boost the England sample using ethnicity fields, and check how representative participants are. The study aims to show how inequalities in early child development emerge over time.

DARS-NIC-800987-T2X1J.summary: NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB is using Cancer Waiting Times data, which records how long cancer patients wait from referral to diagnosis and treatment, on behalf of the Northern Cancer Alliance. The data will be analysed to compare waiting-time performance across hospital trusts and ICBs, find variation and unusually long waits, and look at pathways beyond the national standards. The main intended benefit is to inform cancer service priorities and investment so that waits shorten, survival improves and patient experience improves.

DARS-NIC-801590-G7D7B.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care) and civil registrations of death. The research project, ELATE, compares local and general anaesthesia for endovascular repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms, looking at effectiveness and cost-effectiveness for different patient groups. It aims to give clinicians and policymakers better evidence to guide anaesthetic choices.

DARS-NIC-801642-B0K2B.summary: The University of Southampton is using NHS England bowel cancer screening data from the Screening Research Office. It will study differences in screening uptake across groups such as sex, socioeconomic status, ethnicity and disability, including changes since the FIT test was introduced in 2019 and the COVID-19 pandemic. The main intended benefit is evidence on which groups are underserved, so the screening programme can target efforts and reduce inequalities in uptake.

DARS-NIC-801643-G1K4H.summary: The University of Leeds is using NHS bowel cancer screening data from the Screening Research Office. It is running a randomised trial, BENE-FIT, to test whether a motivation and planning leaflet, a suggested return deadline, or both together help more people complete and return their home screening (FIT) kit. It also looks at which groups benefit most. The main intended benefit is evidence on whether these low-cost measures raise screening uptake and reduce inequalities.

DARS-NIC-802018-Y0J1Y.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data from NHS England: Hospital Episode Statistics (inpatient, outpatient, A&E and critical care) and the Emergency Care Data Set. It will use the data in its public health work, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is more locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities, particularly for the most disadvantaged groups.

DARS-NIC-80304-H6P6R.summary: Imperial College London is using pseudonymised Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care records from 2006/07 to 2015/16, linked to surgeons' simulation-based skills assessment scores. The study examines whether performance in simulated assessments is associated with real-world clinical and patient outcomes. This agreement lets an honorary staff member continue the analysis and write up a peer-reviewed publication. The intended benefit is evidence to improve surgical training and assessment, and so patient care.

DARS-NIC-803151-K2Q8V.summary: NHS West and North London Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify individual patients. It uses them to check that provider invoices are correct and payable, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and redesign local health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted to the needs of the local population.

DARS-NIC-803751-Z3B5K.summary: The University of Liverpool is using national NHS England screening data from the newborn and infant physical examination (NIPE) programme. It is carrying out a service evaluation of developmental dysplasia of the hip in babies. The evaluation will describe how often the condition is found, how screening results compare, and how treatment varies between providers. It aims to show unwarranted variation and support safer, better-quality care.

DARS-NIC-804158-C1F4R.summary: NHS Essex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, some of which can identify patients by NHS number. It uses them to check provider invoices before payment, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804235-N1Y0J.summary: NHS Central East Integrated Care Board uses commissioning, invoice validation and risk stratification datasets, which include pseudonymised and some identifiable patient data. It uses them to check provider invoices before payment, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804237-Y2H9C.summary: NHS Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board uses invoice, risk stratification and commissioning datasets, some of which can identify patients and some of which are pseudonymised. It uses them to check that providers' invoices are correct and payable, to identify patients at risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience and health outcomes.

DARS-NIC-804238-Q6H7C.summary: NHS Thames Valley Integrated Care Board, jointly with Oxfordshire County Council for the commissioning part, uses commissioning data (clinical and financial, pseudonymised) and invoice validation data. The commissioning data is used to plan health services around the needs of the local population, including population health management and service redesign. The invoice validation data is used to check that provider invoices are correct and that the patient is the ICB's responsibility. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned.

DARS-NIC-804239-H4X6K.summary: NHS Surrey and Sussex Integrated Care Board uses commissioning data, which includes clinical and financial information with personal identifiers removed, and invoice validation data. It uses them to check that care providers' invoices are correct and the patients are its responsibility, and to plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are better planned to meet local needs.

DARS-NIC-806125-J8B8J.summary: BCP Council (Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole) uses pseudonymised hospital and emergency care data, including Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set. It uses them for its public health duties, such as needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so that the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-80632-R9D6T.summary: East Riding of Yorkshire Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It will produce aggregated analyses to support needs assessments, health strategies, service commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to show local health inequalities more clearly. The council reports using the data to show higher emergency admission rates in deprived areas and to review outpatient travel distances for local hospitals.

DARS-NIC-808477-T8P0S.summary: The Children's Commissioner's Office is using Emergency Care Data Set and Mental Health Services Data Set records about children detained under the Mental Health Act in hospital wards. It wants to understand how many children are affected, who they are and the nature of their stays, including age, gender, ethnic group, diagnosis and region. Findings will go into a policy report and briefings to help make health and social care policy for these children evidence based.

DARS-NIC-81103-S1W0G.summary: Warrington Borough Council uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to analyse local health needs and inequalities, supporting needs assessments, health strategies, annual reports and advice to NHS commissioners. Reported results so far include adult social care health profiles and a self-harm analysis that informed the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-812033-W7R8C.summary: The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine is using hospital admission records and civil death registration data for a research project called ELATE. It will compare local with general anaesthesia for endovascular repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms, looking at clinical and cost effectiveness for different patient subgroups, such as age, sex and frailty. The aim is to give clinicians and policymakers stronger evidence to guide anaesthetic choices in this emergency surgery.

DARS-NIC-81417-R1V4C.summary: NHS North East London ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former Redbridge CCG area) uses pseudonymised hospital, ambulance, community and emergency care activity data. It uses this data to support the commissioning of health services and to link NHS 111 calls to what happened to callers afterwards. This lets it evaluate the NHS 111 Patient Relationship Manager system and the accuracy of call recommendations. The main intended benefit is better planning of urgent care patient flows.

DARS-NIC-81519-G1T5F.summary: The University of Birmingham holds hospital records (A&E, inpatient, outpatient and critical care) and death registration data for about 75,000 primary care patients at risk of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). The agreement only allows the data to be securely kept, not used further. It supports the TargetCOPD2 study, which looked at whether finding COPD earlier reduces hospital admissions and deaths. The text reports no benefit yet from the study's results.

DARS-NIC-82378-M2B6C.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (a sub-ICB location) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices so that only activity it is responsible for is paid, and for risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and better targeted, more effective care.

DARS-NIC-82396-W4F5T.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire ICB (for the former NHS Warwickshire North CCG area) uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, so the commissioner pays only for activity it is responsible for. The main intended benefit is accurate payment to providers and appropriate use of public funds.

DARS-NIC-82404-V2S5B.summary: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (ICB) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, to check invoices from care providers. The aim is to confirm that the activity claimed is the responsibility of the former South Warwickshire Clinical Commissioning Group, and to review past payments for overcharges. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and money that would otherwise be lost is recovered.

DARS-NIC-82493-P8Y3N.summary: The University of Essex is using school-level, pseudonymised National Child Measurement Programme data on children's weight and body mass index (BMI). It is studying how free lunches for all infant school children in England affect weight in reception class. The aim is to show whether the policy leads to fewer overweight or obese children, helping policy makers decide on funding. Reported findings include a presentation at conferences, a draft report and press coverage.

DARS-NIC-82980-V6D4Q.summary: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data on behalf of the British Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy. It will count hysterectomies each year and show whether they were abdominal, vaginal or laparoscopic, to describe national practice and variation. The aim is to target surgeon training and inform national guidance. Early findings have already helped focus the society's laparoscopic hysterectomy training project.

DARS-NIC-84254-J2G1Q.summary: The University of York's Centre for Health Economics is using pseudonymised, record-level hospital, emergency care, mental health, death registration and patient-reported outcome data. It is using them to study NHS efficiency, provider performance, policy impacts and inequalities in access. The aim is to inform health and social care policy and the use of NHS funding. Published studies have already examined drivers of health care spending and inequalities in waiting times, and an online tool now helps patients and GPs discuss surgery outcomes.

DARS-NIC-84763-L9X2G.summary: Leicester City Council, a local authority, uses hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) for its public health work. It uses them to analyse local health needs and inequalities, and to support needs assessments, strategies and commissioning. The aim is to help identify and respond to local health challenges, particularly for the most disadvantaged. Results have already fed into Joint Strategic Needs Assessments and neighbourhood profiles.

DARS-NIC-85465-H1W9F.summary: The University of Sheffield, an academic organisation, is holding pseudonymised Improving Access to Psychological Therapies (IAPT) data on patients who received high intensity therapy. It is using the data to compare how well Cognitive Behaviour Therapy, Counselling for Depression and other high intensity therapies treat depression. The aim is to help patients, practitioners and commissioners understand how the therapies compare. Early findings have been presented at a Society for Psychotherapy Research conference in July 2022.

DARS-NIC-86054-Q4Y8W.summary: NHS North West London ICB, acting for the former NHS Brent CCG, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data for commissioners, identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to score patients' risk. The main intended benefit is accurate payment of providers and better targeted care, helping reduce avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-86244-P6Y1N.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers are paid correctly for patients the commissioner is responsible for. Risk stratification links this data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted. The reported benefits so far include improved data quality, financial savings and identifying higher-risk patients to prioritise GP work.

DARS-NIC-86246-M3T5X.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, for two purposes. The first is checking provider invoices so the right commissioner pays for each patient's care. The second is risk stratification, which links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk of hospital admission so care can be planned and targeted. Reported benefits include improved data quality, financial savings and better prioritisation of GP and community care work.

DARS-NIC-86250-T2M6F.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (formerly Rushcliffe CCG) uses hospital activity data from Secondary User Services, identifiable by NHS number, to check provider invoices and to identify patients at high risk of hospital admission. The work is carried out by Nottinghamshire Health Informatics Service. The aim is to make sure payments are accurate and to help GPs and commissioners plan and target care. Reported benefits include improved data quality, financial savings and better identification of higher-risk patients.

DARS-NIC-86260-S0V2F.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Mansfield and Ashfield area) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital activity data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers' invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to identify patients at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted. Reported benefits include improved data quality and financial savings.

DARS-NIC-86349-M3B9V.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to check provider invoices are valid and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration. The aim is to make sure payments are accurate and to help GPs and commissioners target care, reduce avoidable admissions and plan services. Reported benefits so far include improved data quality, financial savings, and identifying higher-risk patients so GP practices and community teams can prioritise their work.

DARS-NIC-86409-C4S9S.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB (Nottingham West area) uses hospital activity data from Secondary Uses Service (SUS+), which is identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices before payment and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration by linking it with GP data. The main intended benefits are accurate payment for care and earlier, better targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-86623-P4F4D.summary: The Nuffield Trust, an independent research organisation, is using hospital records covering accident and emergency visits, admitted patient care and outpatient appointments. It is evaluating the Royal Voluntary Service "Home from Hospital" scheme in Leicestershire by comparing hospital use by people who received the service with a matched group who did not. The aim is to give commissioners an independent assessment of whether such schemes affect older people's use of hospital services.

DARS-NIC-86666-V7Z1L.summary: University College London (UCL) is keeping hospital records (admissions and A&E attendances) and linked death registration data for a study of hospital discharge for homeless people in England. The study compares readmissions and deaths between homeless people who used specialist discharge services, those who did not, and non-homeless people in the most deprived areas. It aims to help commissioners and policy makers target services better and reduce readmissions and avoidable deaths. Analysis of the main outcomes has already enabled an economic analysis of the discharge schemes.

DARS-NIC-86861-K1L1N.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, covering the former NHS Doncaster CCG area, uses identifiable hospital activity data to check invoices from care providers, and pseudonymised health, social care and population datasets to support commissioning. The data is used to validate payments, plan and redesign services, assess local health needs and identify patients at risk. The stated aim is to ensure providers are paid accurately and services meet the population's needs. The CCG reports it has published an annual report on its developments and achievements, supported by this data.

DARS-NIC-86954-Y0R2N.summary: University College London uses linked NHS England hospital, mortality, cancer registration and demographic data on members of the 1946 National Survey of Health and Development birth cohort. It uses the data to update study records, re-contact members lost to follow-up, and research how factors across life affect ageing and diseases such as cardiovascular disease. The aim is to show when in life interventions might prevent disease. Published papers include one linking early childhood respiratory infection to premature adult death from respiratory disease.

DARS-NIC-87225-T1V3B.summary: London Borough of Lewisham, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and inequalities. So far, the data has fed analyses of self-harm admissions, children's asthma admissions for an air quality briefing, and an alcohol harm dashboard.

DARS-NIC-88045-R0G8D.summary: Durham County Council is using hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to support its public health duties. These include needs assessments, health strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, using aggregated data with small numbers suppressed. Its reported work so far includes analysis that informed a new Dementia Strategy and an updated Serious Violence Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-88623-F2H1Q.summary: The Royal College of Anaesthetists is using hospital admission, critical care and death registration records for patients who had inpatient surgery in the UK in one week in March 2017.
