It will study how critical care admission after surgery relates to complications and longer-term outcomes, aiming to improve care for surgical patients. Work so far has been published as a PhD thesis and has influenced national policy on critical care provision and perioperative care services.

DARS-NIC-88740-G2Y9Q.summary: Worcestershire County Council's public health team is using hospital records covering emergency care, admitted patients, critical care and outpatients. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports that the data helped it target populations and work with the Integrated Care Board on inequalities and strategic plans.

DARS-NIC-88788-M6F3S.summary: NHS Surrey Heartlands ICB, acting for the former Guildford and Waverley CCG area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, cancer waiting times, births and deaths data. It uses the data to plan and monitor commissioned health services, assess local needs and identify patients at risk. Processing is carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit. The main intended benefit is better planning and quality of services for the local population.

DARS-NIC-89613-L9D8C.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Sheffield clinical commissioning group (CCG), uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and commission services for the local population. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care. The register reports that the data has helped services match population needs and has supported monitoring of in-year projects.

DARS-NIC-90019-Q8P9K.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is using Hospital Episode Statistics data on hospital admissions, outpatient appointments and A&E attendances. It is analysing health inequality in NHS hospital services, A&E waiting times and maternity care by area, deprivation and ethnicity. The aim is to give policymakers and commissioners evidence to target areas for reducing inequality. So far, only preliminary results exist and none have been published.

DARS-NIC-90049-D5S8M.summary: NHS Greater Manchester ICB, acting for the former NHS Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale CCG, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health and social care data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support planning and buying of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and commissioned.

DARS-NIC-90070-F3K4Z.summary: The Health Foundation, a charity, is using Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care data to study the Any Qualified Provider scheme, which lets patients choose between NHS and private providers. It is examining how the scheme affected the volume and quality of planned hospital care, measured through waiting times and hip and knee surgery revisions. The aim is to give policy makers evidence on whether the scheme works. So far, only internal descriptive analysis has been done.

DARS-NIC-90126-D4Z2W.summary: Keele University is using NHS hospital records (admissions, critical care, outpatients) and death registration data for people in England in the BISTRO trial, which involves people newly starting haemodialysis. They are linking this to trial data to capture hospital events and costs, testing whether regular bioimpedance measurements of body fluid help people keep remaining kidney function. The aim is to inform NICE guidance. The data has been used to calculate costs, which showed a 74% chance that bioimpedance was cost effective.

DARS-NIC-90135-P7Z0F.summary: NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria ICB, for the former Morecambe Bay clinical commissioning group area, uses hospital, community, mental health and other health service data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, to identify patients at high risk so GPs can target their care, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and planned.

DARS-NIC-90187-Z0S6Y.summary: South Gloucestershire Council's public health team uses hospital and emergency care records (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set) to analyse local health needs. It uses them to support its statutory public health duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and commissioning, so that services are better targeted at local need. Reported results include injury intelligence used to decide on a home safety equipment scheme, and oral health monitoring that has informed a tooth brushing programme.

DARS-NIC-90638-Q3T5B.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, for the former NHS Bradford City CCG, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data that can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned and targeted. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is commissioned more effectively, with fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-90642-L4S7D.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB (for the former NHS Bradford Districts CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, identifiable by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. It checks that provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility and, by linking the data with GP records, identifies patients at high risk of health deterioration. The main intended benefits are accurate payment of providers and better targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-90647-G3Q4S.summary: NHS South Yorkshire ICB, for the former NHS Barnsley CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, primary care medicines and other health and care data. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and support the planning of health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted, more effective care. The CCG's 2020/21 annual report describes achievements, some of which relied on this data.

DARS-NIC-90651-Q8W4T.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, for the former Calderdale CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity, social care and other health datasets, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses them to check provider invoices are the CCG's responsibility and to plan and commission health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and services matched to local needs. The CCG reports that the data has helped match services to population requirements.

DARS-NIC-90658-F0W4R.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, for the former East Riding of Yorkshire CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and plan and monitor commissioned services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and that care is better targeted and planned for the local population.

DARS-NIC-90661-W2S5Q.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Greater Huddersfield CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health activity data, including births and deaths records. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, with better targeted care and accurate payment for treatment.

DARS-NIC-90665-Z9L7G.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, acting for a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and care is better targeted and commissioned.

DARS-NIC-90668-X5R4Y.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, covering the former NHS Hull Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG) area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including NHS number-level data for some tasks. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, and to plan and commission health services. The main stated benefit is ensuring providers are paid accurately and care is planned and targeted more effectively.

DARS-NIC-90670-W8H6P.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, acting for a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some of it identifiable by NHS number. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk of poor health so GPs can target care, and to plan and commission health services. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-90680-M5B5W.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, for the former NHS North Lincolnshire CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to validate provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be planned, and support the commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are planned around local needs.

DARS-NIC-90691-W4B6F.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, acting for the former Scarborough and Ryedale clinical commissioning group (CCG), uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health, and plan and monitor health services. The stated aim is more effective commissioning, leading to better patient care and experience.

DARS-NIC-90698-W7X6Y.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, for the North Kirklees area, uses pseudonymised hospital, community, mental health, maternity, ambulance and death and birth registration data, which hold clinical and financial information. It uses the data to plan and commission health services, assess population needs, and monitor contracts and quality. The main intended benefit is better planning of services and patient pathways. The benefits reported so far are described as analysis supporting business cases and monitoring of performance and outcome indicators.

DARS-NIC-90700-V8P0C.summary: NHS Nottingham and Nottinghamshire ICB uses hospital, community, mental health, primary care and other health and social care data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of health decline, and plan and commission health services for the Bassetlaw population. The aim is to ensure accurate payment, target care better and reduce avoidable admissions. Reported results include new care pathways, such as home oxygen and blood pressure monitoring, and Long Covid clinics.

DARS-NIC-90708-H6D9L.summary: NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, a sub-ICB location, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other NHS activity data, some of it identifiable by NHS number and some pseudonymised. It uses the data to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of poor health so their care can be targeted, and plan and monitor health services for the local population. The main intended benefit is more effective commissioning of services, leading to a better patient experience.

DARS-NIC-90713-T3K1V.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, covering the former NHS Wakefield CCG area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners), identifiable by NHS number, to check provider invoices and to carry out risk stratification. Invoice checking confirms that the CCG pays only for care it is responsible for and recovers overpayments. Risk stratification links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk, so care can be targeted and planned, with the aim of reducing avoidable hospital admissions.

DARS-NIC-90767-Y3J0B.summary: NHS West Yorkshire ICB, for the former Airedale, Wharfedale and Craven CCG, uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) hospital data that can be identified by NHS number. It is used to check that provider invoices are correct and to recover overpayments. It is also linked with GP data to score patients' risk of health decline. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better-targeted care for vulnerable patients.

DARS-NIC-90989-D6T1T.summary: McKinsey & Company, Inc. United Kingdom, a commercial organisation, is using linked hospital admission and death registration records for Hospice UK and NHS England's HOLISTIC service evaluation. The records are aggregated and de-identified. They are used to compare how much time patients spend in hospital in the last 90 days of life under different hospice-led care models. The aim is to identify which models best reduce hospital use and improve end of life care.

DARS-NIC-91374-Z5V6Y.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable hospital admissions, cancer registration, death and demographic records for 3,870 participants in the SABRE cohort study. It is studying why heart, metabolic and cognitive health in older age differ between ethnic groups and between men and women, aiming to inform better prevention and treatment. The register reports published papers using NHS England data, and findings that informed NICE's BMI thresholds for preventing type 2 diabetes.

DARS-NIC-91376-P5N3X.summary: Bury Metropolitan Borough Council is using hospital admitted patient, outpatient, critical care, accident and emergency, and emergency care records. It uses them for its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, with outputs as aggregated data with small numbers suppressed. So far, it has built a local matrix of alcohol-related A&E attendances to support licensing decisions.

DARS-NIC-91799-G0T9X.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former NHS Coastal West Sussex Clinical Commissioning Group (CCG), uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data to check invoices from care providers, so the CCG can confirm that the activity claimed is its responsibility before payment. NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit carries out the checks. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and commissioners pay appropriately for their own patients.

DARS-NIC-91808-P5Z1F.summary: NHS Sussex ICB (for the former Brighton & Hove CCG) uses identifiable patient demographic data and hospital activity data for commissioners. NHS South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit processes the data in a secure finance environment to check provider invoices and confirm whether the CCG is the responsible commissioner for each patient. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and public funds are protected.

DARS-NIC-91825-W4M1H.summary: NHS Sussex ICB (a sub-ICB location, covering the former Hastings and Rother CCG) uses Secondary User Services (SUS+) data, which can be identified by NHS number, for invoice validation and risk stratification. Invoice validation checks that providers' invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for, so payments are accurate. Risk stratification links the data with GP data to predict which patients are at high risk, so care can be planned and targeted earlier. Both are carried out by South Central and West Commissioning Support Unit.

DARS-NIC-91827-P6J6X.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, for the former High Weald Lewes Havens CCG area, uses Secondary Uses Service (SUS+) data for commissioners, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses the data for invoice validation, checking that the hospital activity providers bill for is the CCG's responsibility. South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit carries out the checks. The main intended benefit is that providers are paid accurately and commissioners pay appropriately for their own patients' treatment.

DARS-NIC-91838-H0B9N.summary: NHS Sussex ICB (Sub ICB Location, formerly NHS Crawley CCG) uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) and Mental Health Services Data Set records, which can be identified by NHS number. It uses them to check provider invoices are correct and the CCG's responsibility, and to predict which patients are at high risk of poor health so GPs and commissioners can plan their care. The main intended benefit is more accurate payments and earlier, better-targeted care, including for mental health.

DARS-NIC-91866-V4R5J.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, for the former Eastbourne, Hailsham and Seaford CCG area, is using Secondary User Services (SUS+) data that can be identified by NHS number. It is used to check that provider invoices are for patients the commissioner is responsible for, and to run risk stratification, which links the data with GP records to identify patients at high risk. The aim is accurate payment and better-targeted care, including fewer avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-91871-D2W1N.summary: NHS Sussex ICB, acting for the former Horsham & Mid Sussex CCG area, uses hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) and Mental Health Services Data Set records that can be identified by NHS number. It uses them to check provider invoices before payment and to identify patients at high risk of health deterioration, linking the data with GP records to produce risk scores. The main intended benefit is more accurate payment and better targeted, earlier care, including for mental health, to reduce avoidable emergency admissions.

DARS-NIC-91972-S9W9T.summary: 3M United Kingdom PLC, a commercial company, uses pseudonymised hospital admitted patient care and outpatient data (Hospital Episode Statistics) to validate and adapt its Clinical Risk Groups software to UK coding standards. The software classifies patients by their burden of illness, to help NHS commissioners and providers plan population health management. A pilot with The Rotherham Hospital NHS Foundation Trust profiled its Same-Day Emergency Care patients, and the trust decided to use the groups to define that cohort.

DARS-NIC-92359-B9Z6Q.summary: London Borough of Bromley's public health team is using hospital records on admissions, outpatient visits, critical care and emergency care, accessed through NHS England's secure environment. It uses them to support its public health duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to give locally focused analyses of health and inequalities. So far, the data has fed into the 2022 alcohol and substance misuse needs assessments and the 2024 suicide audit.

DARS-NIC-92946-H6R5Z.summary: Bury Metropolitan Borough Council will use pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) in its public health and commissioning work. It will use the data to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so the needs of the most disadvantaged residents can be identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-93084-W4B4L.summary: University College London (UCL) is using hospital and mental health records from NHS England, including hospital admissions, accident and emergency attendances, and mental health data covering 2011 to 2016. It is using them in the NIHR-funded AD-CARE study to assess how well Acute Day Units work as a community response to mental health crises. The study compares readmission rates and outcomes for people who do and do not use these units. The intended benefit is evidence on whether the units reduce admissions to acute psychiatric units.

DARS-NIC-93640-K3Z1Y.summary: Leicestershire County Council, a local authority, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties. It uses the data to produce needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, annual public health reports and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities, so that the needs of the local population, particularly the most disadvantaged, are identified and responded to.

DARS-NIC-93829-Q9L5D.summary: Manchester City Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. So far, the data has been used to monitor Public Health Outcomes Framework measures quarterly rather than annually, and to support a review of urgent care across Manchester and Trafford.

DARS-NIC-94250-L8W8T.summary: North Bristol NHS Trust, for the Renal Association's UK Renal Registry, uses hospital records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and civil registration death data. It uses them in national audits of kidney care, to adjust for patient mix when comparing renal centres, and to report hospital admissions and causes of death. The aim is to help identify unexplained variation between centres and improve patient care. Reported results include published annual report analyses, Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) renal reports and peer-reviewed papers.

DARS-NIC-94320-N6Z6H.summary: Oldham Metropolitan Borough Council uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties. This includes producing needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health inequalities, so the needs of disadvantaged groups are identified and addressed. The council reports the data has helped it contribute to its needs assessment and understand secondary care use.

DARS-NIC-94321-Z9K1X.summary: Salford City Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties. It analyses patterns of illness, access to care and health inequalities to inform needs assessments, commissioning and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to make local services better targeted and more responsive. The council reports analyses of children's unplanned admissions, falls in older people and alcohol-related admissions.

DARS-NIC-94322-G8V8K.summary: Rochdale Metropolitan Borough Council is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to carry out its public health and commissioning duties. It uses the data to analyse local health needs, inequalities and service demand, and to produce needs assessments, annual reports and advice to NHS commissioners. So far, admissions data has informed the RAPS accident prevention scheme for children and contributed to the Joint Strategic Needs Assessment.

DARS-NIC-94323-X5R6F.summary: Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties. It uses the data to produce needs assessments, health strategies, the Director of Public Health's annual report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. The council reports using it for the 2022 and 2023 Joint Strategic Needs Assessment deep dives and for regular performance reports.

DARS-NIC-94324-M2Z4H.summary: Tameside Metropolitan Borough Council uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) in its public health and commissioning work. It analyses patterns of disease, hospital admissions and health inequalities to support needs assessments, service planning and public health advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is to make commissioned services more locally targeted. Reported benefits include ward and neighbourhood profiles and locality-based Covid-19 analysis.

DARS-NIC-94326-S9S4H.summary: Trafford Metropolitan Borough Council, a local authority, uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) to support its public health and commissioning duties, including needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. So far, the data has been used to monitor selected Public Health Outcomes Framework measures quarterly instead of annually, and to support an urgent care review across Manchester and Trafford.

DARS-NIC-94327-V0D4V.summary: Wigan Metropolitan Borough Council is using pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners) in its public health work. It uses the data to support its statutory public health duties, such as needs assessments, health strategies and advice to NHS commissioners, and to commission services. The aim is locally focused analysis of health outcomes and inequalities. The council reports using it to investigate youth substance misuse admissions and alcohol-specific admissions, and to inform neighbourhood profiles.

DARS-NIC-94557-Z2T1D.summary: City of Wolverhampton Council's public health team uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (SUS for Commissioners). It uses the data to support its public health and commissioning duties, including needs assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The main intended benefit is locally focused analysis of health status and inequalities, so the needs of the most disadvantaged groups are identified and addressed.

DARS-NIC-94749-Y1R8N.summary: The University of Sheffield, an academic organisation, is using hospital admission records (Hospital Episode Statistics) and death and cancer follow-up records (MRIS) for women over 70 recruited to the Bridging the Age Gap in Breast Cancer study. It uses them to update survival outcomes and to test comorbidity scores, which will revise a statistical model behind a decision support tool. The main intended benefit is better treatment decisions for older women with breast cancer.

DARS-NIC-95040-Y0P3W.summary: NHS Cambridgeshire and Peterborough ICB uses pseudonymised (identifying details removed) health, social care and local provider data, including hospital, mental health, community, maternity and medicines data. It uses this to plan and manage health services, including population health analysis, service redesign, demand forecasting, contract management and identifying patients at risk. The main intended benefit is better commissioning decisions, improving the quality of services and health outcomes for the local population.

DARS-NIC-95658-C4F7D.summary: Powys Teaching Local Health Board uses pseudonymised hospital activity data (Secondary Uses Service, containing clinical and financial information) to plan and commission health services for people in its area. The aim is to understand population needs, redesign services and manage contracts. Reported results include new nurse-led respiratory, ear care and endoscopy services, and a £1m investment in proactive primary and community care.

DARS-NIC-95815-C3W0W.summary: NHS North Central London Integrated Care Board (ICB), covering the former Islington CCG area, uses hospital, community, mental health, maternity and other health service data, including NHS-number-identifiable hospital data and pseudonymised data. It uses the data to check provider invoices, to identify patients at high risk so their care can be prioritised, and to support planning and commissioning of health services. The main intended benefit is accurate payment and better planned, more effective services for local people.

DARS-NIC-95817-Q6V9N.summary: NHS North Central London ICB, acting for the former Haringey clinical commissioning group, uses hospital, community, mental health, ambulance, maternity, cancer waiting times and birth and death records. It uses them to check provider invoices, identify patients at high risk of needing care, and plan and monitor health services. The main stated benefit is that providers are paid accurately and services are commissioned more effectively, improving patient experience.

DARS-NIC-96444-N2B7K.summary: The Intensive Care National Audit & Research Centre (ICNARC) is using NHS Digital's patient status and date of death information to support the 65 Trial. The trial tests whether keeping blood pressure lower while patients receive vasopressor drugs benefits critically ill people aged 65 or over. The data provides 90-day mortality and survival outcomes and avoids contacting families of participants who have died. The trial results have been published in a medical journal and a national report, and the intervention has been included in guidelines.

DARS-NIC-96550-Z8N7V.summary: Cornwall Council, a local authority, is using Hospital Episode Statistics and Emergency Care Data Set records, covering hospital admissions, outpatients, critical care and A&E. It uses them in its public health work, such as Joint Strategic Needs Assessments, health and wellbeing strategies, advice to NHS commissioners and the Director of Public Health's annual report. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. Between 2023 and 2026, the data were used in the statutory Joint Strategic Needs Assessment reporting.

DARS-NIC-97202-W2L3P.summary: Portsmouth City Council, a local authority, is using hospital and emergency care data (Hospital Episode Statistics and the Emergency Care Data Set). It will use them for public health work, such as needs assessments, health strategies, the annual public health report and advice to NHS commissioners. The aim is locally focused analysis of health and health inequalities. So far, the data has supported analysis of cardiovascular hospital admissions for the Portsmouth Joint Strategic Needs Assessment, and ongoing monitoring of alcohol-related admissions.

DARS-NIC-99077-Q0K6Z.summary: University College London (UCL) is using identifiable hospital admissions, death registration, demographic and cohort-tracking data for 69 participants in the SABRE cohort study, with cancer information excluded. It is studying why heart, metabolic, cognitive and physical health in older age differ between ethnic groups and between sexes. The aim is to inform better prevention and treatment. Published papers have used NHS England data, and findings on diabetes helped inform NICE's BMI thresholds for different ethnic groups.
